# Show plugin version in Herdr work item selection list (WL-0MSGKEBFU004T3N3)

## Problem statement

The Herdr Worklog work item selection list gives no indication of which plugin version is running, making it hard to verify installs, spot stale builds, or report bugs accurately. A dimmed, right-aligned version number in the pane header solves this without visual clutter.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who want to confirm which version of the Worklog Selection List plugin is running.
- **Developers/support** who need the version handy when filing bug reports or verifying an updated build is live.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to see the plugin version in the corner of the work item list, so I can confirm which build I'm running.
- As a developer, I want the version visible but unobtrusive, so it doesn't distract from the list content.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The work item selection list header shows the plugin version (`0.1.0` from `packages/herdr/package.json`), right-aligned to the pane width.
2. The version is rendered in the dimmed ANSI style (`\x1b[2m`), matching the existing `[auto-refresh on]` treatment, and does not interfere with the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title.
3. The version is read at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` (not hardcoded in the renderer), so it stays in sync with the manifest version.
4. Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover the header rendering with the version suffix, including a case without a version available (graceful fallback).
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Unobtrusive: dimmed font, right-aligned to the pane edge; must not change existing header content or alignment of the title.
- Use existing patterns: `termSize.cols` for pane width, `ANSI.dim` for dimming, `readFileSync` for reading `package.json` (pattern already used in `worklist.ts`/`shortcut-config.ts`).
- No changes to `herdr-plugin.toml` version unless a version bump is explicitly requested.
- Do not update CHANGELOG.md (managed automatically by the ship skill release pipeline).

## Existing state

- The selection list header is rendered in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (~line 1585): ` Work Items — N item(s)` plus optional `[auto-refresh on]` (dimmed) and `[paused — hidden]` indicators.
- `termSize` (with `cols`) is available in the render function; `truncateLine()` handles width overflow.
- The plugin version is declared in two places: `packages/herdr/package.json` (`"version": "0.1.0"`) and `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` (`version = "0.1.0"`). There is currently no runtime version constant.
- Existing header tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (lines ~86–100) assert `'Work Items'` presence.

## Desired change

1. Add a runtime helper that reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (e.g., parse JSON, fall back to a safe default like `'?'` or omit when unreadable).
2. In the list-mode header renderer, append a dimmed `v<version>` string right-aligned to `cols` (using padding), while keeping the title left-aligned.
3. Add unit tests covering: version suffix present and right-aligned, dim style applied, graceful fallback when the version can't be read.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Header rendering; add version read + right-aligned dimmed suffix (near line 1585).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Header assertions for version suffix, alignment, and fallback.
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — Version source (`0.1.0`); no change expected.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Optional: document the version display.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP** — Create a work item selection list in Herdr: parent feature that produced `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **WL-0MQHYI4E60075SQT** — Fix icon prefix alignment in Pi TUI work item selection list: related header/line formatting work (Pi TUI counterpart).
- **WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ** — Herdr selection list refreshes immediately when its tab regains focus: related Herdr list behavior work.
- **WL-0MQL0T5TR0060AEH** — Add activity-indicator footer to Worklog Pi extension: related footer/status UI precedent (Pi TUI counterpart).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKX5ZV3D0OHIIX2** – Add regression tests for mouse click crash and TUI behavior (completed)
- **WL-0MKZ34IDI0XTA5TB** – TUI: Reparent items without typing IDs (completed)
- **WL-0MQL0T5TR0060AEH** – Add activity-indicator footer to Worklog Pi extension (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/tests/test_ralph_loop.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, src, using, version, work
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2-enforce-git-worktree-usage-for-all-imple/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, using, version, work
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, using, version, work

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: `package.json` is present next to the compiled/tsx module at runtime; the module-dir relative read pattern (as in `shortcut-config.ts`) works for both `npx tsx` and `dist` runs.
- **Risk**: ANSI codes in a right-padded line can misalign padding calculations if padding is computed on raw text length; must compute visible-width padding before applying ANSI styles.
- **Risk**: Very narrow panes could crowd the header; the version suffix should be dropped or truncated if it would overlap the title (guard on `cols`).
- **Scope creep risk**: Bumping the version, adding the version elsewhere (footer/status bar), or showing `wl`/ContextHub versions — out of scope; record as follow-up work items if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1**: "Which version number? I assume the plugin's own version (`0.1.0` from `packages/herdr/package.json` / `herdr-plugin.toml`) — or did you mean the `wl` CLI version or ContextHub's version?"  
  **Answer** (user): "yes the plugins" — the Worklog Selection List plugin's own version. Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2**: "Placement preference? Unobtrusive, dimmed — candidates: (a) right side of the header line, (b) footer hint line, (c) bottom-right corner."  
  **Answer** (user): "a (right aligned to width of pane)" — right-aligned in the header line. Source: interactive reply.

## Summary

`wl sync` fails on every push with `fatal: <path> already exists` because `withTempWorktree()` in `dist/sync.js` invokes `git worktree add --detach <tmp>/wt <ref>` **twice** — once inside a try/catch (added for the unborn-HEAD translation, SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51) and then unconditionally again right after the catch block. When the first call succeeds, the second always fails with "path already exists", aborting the sync.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In any repo with an initialized worklog and a remote (e.g. `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents` or `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`):
2. Run `wl sync` (or any push that triggers the pre-push hook).
3. Observe: `Sync failed: Command failed with exit code 128: git worktree add --detach '<repo>/.worklog/tmp-worktree-XXXXXX/wt' 'refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data'` → `fatal: '<...>/tmp-worktree-XXXXXX/wt' already exists`.

## Root cause

`/usr/local/lib/node_modules/worklog/dist/sync.js`, `withTempWorktree()`:

```js
try {
    await execAsync(`git worktree add --detach ...`);
}
catch (err) {
    // Unborn-HEAD translation (SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51) ...
    throw err;
}
await execAsync(`git worktree add --detach ...`);  // <- duplicate; fails when the first succeeded
```

The second call was likely meant to be the only call, or the catch should re-run only when the first call failed due to an unborn HEAD. Fix: remove the unconditional duplicate call while keeping the unborn-HEAD translation path working (covered by the SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51 tests).

## Impact

- All `wl sync` push operations fail in repos where the temp worktree can be created (the common case). Data is retained locally (SQLite + exported JSONL "retained for retry") but never pushed to the remote worklog ref.
- Blocks collaboration: other agents/operators do not see new work items, comments, effort/risk estimates.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl sync` succeeds and pushes to `refs/worklog/data` in a repo with a remote (regression test).
2. The unborn-HEAD translation error message still works: the single `git worktree add` call in `withTempWorktree()` remains wrapped with the unborn-HEAD translation (`src/sync.ts:937-951`), producing an actionable `Cannot sync: this repository has no commits yet...` message when a repo has no commits yet.

> **AC amendment (variance, 2026-08-07):** AC2 originally referenced `existing SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51 tests remain green`, but no such tests exist in the repo (verified by audit). The criterion is relaxed to verify the behavior directly in code: the translation logic is preserved and single-sourced around the one `git worktree add` call.

Audit trail for the herdr downtime worker (discovered-from:WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K). When the worker auto-dispatches an item during local-LLM downtime, today the only trace is the item's status flip to in_progress (indistinguishable from a manual claim); there is no durable record that the dispatch was automatic.

**User story**
As a producer reviewing the worklog, I want every downtime auto-dispatch to leave an auditable trail, so I can tell which items were advanced automatically and when.

**Expected behaviour**
1. On every successful downtime dispatch, add a comment to the dispatched work item: author 'herdr-downtime', stating it was auto-dispatched by the downtime worker, the UTC timestamp, and the skill run (/skill:plan or /skill:intake).
2. Append a JSONL entry to a rolling log at .worklog/downtime-dispatches.log in the resolved worklog root: timestamp, item id, title, kind, cwd. The log is bounded (keep the most recent ~100 entries) — a rolling log, not unbounded.
3. Both actions are fail-closed: a wl comment failure or log-write failure must never throw/crash the worker or block the dispatch. The .worklog log file is gitignored (matches .worklog/*) so it stays a local artifact; the comment is the durable trail (survives wl sync).

**Implementation approach**
- New deps boundary on DowntimeWorkerDeps: recordDispatch(event) called from dispatchDowntimeWork after a successful spawn (candidate + kind + cwd are all in scope there).
- Small module (downtime-log.ts) for the bounded JSONL append (read existing, append, truncate to N) — pure fs logic, unit-testable with a temp dir.
- createDowntimeDeps wires recordDispatch: wl comment add <id> --comment ... --author herdr-downtime (via the existing getExecFileAsync seam) + the rolling append.
- Document in packages/herdr/README.md under the downtime section.

**Acceptance criteria**
- AC1: dispatchDowntimeWork calls deps.recordDispatch with the item id, kind, ISO timestamp, and cwd on every successful dispatch (plan and intake paths), covered by unit tests.
- AC2: recordDispatch adds a comment to the item via wl comment add with author 'herdr-downtime' and a timestamp (verified via the execFileAsync seam).
- AC3: recordDispatch appends one JSONL line to .worklog/downtime-dispatches.log under the resolved worklog root; the file is bounded at 100 entries (rolling), verified by a test that appends 120 entries and asserts only the last 100 remain.
- AC4: failures are fail-closed — wl comment failure and log-write failure (e.g. unwritable cwd) do not throw; dispatch still succeeds. Covered by tests.
- AC5: README documents the audit trail.
- AC6: full herdr + repo test suite passes; build passes.

# Intake Brief — Insert selected work-item ID into herdr command input forms (WL-0MSGPSEFW006VINF)

## Problem statement

When typing a free-form prompt in a herdr command input form (e.g. the `P-p` chord, which opens a prompt sent to a new Pi agent pane), there is no discoverable way to reference the currently selected work item by its ID. The `<id>` magic token already works inside form field values (both chord and single-key form paths in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` resolve it to the selected item's ID on submit), but the behavior is undocumented, untested, and invisible in the UI — and in one edge case (no item selected, `P-p` path) a literal `<id>` leaks through to Pi.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who open the `P-p` free-form prompt (or any chord form) and want the prompt to reference the work item they currently have selected — without memorising/pasting the ID.
- **Pi agents / operators** who receive the prompt — the prompt becomes self-contained with the item ID, so no follow-up lookup is needed.

User stories:
- As a Herdr user with an item selected in the worklist, I want to type `<id>` in the `P-p` free-form prompt so the selected item's ID is inserted into the prompt sent to Pi.
- As a Herdr user filling any chord command form (e.g. `u-t` title, `u-s` stage), I want `<id>` to resolve to the currently selected item's ID the same way it does in command templates.
- As a new Herdr user, I want the form dialog to hint that `<id>` is available, so I don't need to read the README to discover it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Typing `<id>` in the `P-p` free-form prompt field inserts the currently selected work item's ID into the prompt text sent to Pi (verified by an automated regression test on the form-submit path; no new `wl` spawn needed).
2. The same `<id>`-in-field behavior works in **all** herdr command input forms, for both the chord and single-key dispatch paths.
3. The form dialog renders a discoverability hint (e.g. a footer/help line such as "type `<id>` to insert the selected item's ID") whenever the form is shown.
4. When no work item is selected and a form field value contains `<id>`, the behavior is graceful and consistent across all paths — no literal `<id>` is sent to Pi; the documented decision (see Risks & assumptions) is implemented and covered by a test.
5. `packages/herdr/README.md` documents the `<id>`-in-form-field behavior, including the `P-p` free-prompt example.
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes; new tests cover the free-prompt case, the generic form case, the no-item-selected edge case, and the discoverability hint.

## Constraints

- **No change to `<id>` handling in command templates** — the existing `KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS` / `substituteIdentifiers` mechanism in `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` stays as-is.
- **No changes to the chord definitions** in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` (P-p, P-a, u-*, etc. remain bound exactly as today).
- No modal/UX overhaul of the form dialog — the hint is a minimal addition to the existing form render.
- All work tracked in wl; no changes to work-item tracking tooling.

## Existing state

- `P-p` chord → `/prompt:<prompt>` opens the command input form (`FormState` in `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts`); on submit the resulting command routes through `worklist.ts` and spawns a Pi agent pane with the bare prompt text (`stripAgentPromptPrefix` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`).
- `KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS = {'id'}` in `form-dialog.ts` — `<id>` never triggers an unknown-identifier prompt; `substituteIdentifiers` leaves `<id>` intact in field values.
- Both form onSubmit callbacks in `worklist.ts` (chord-complete path ~line 2353 and single-key path ~line 2464) replace `<id>` with the selected item's ID via `flat[idx].id`.
- No regression test covers `<id>` typed inside a form field value; no UI hint; README documents `<id>` resolution for command templates only, not for field values/free prompts.
- Edge case: in the form paths, when no item is selected and the field value contains `<id>`, `finalCmd` keeps the literal `<id>` and it is sent (visible to Pi in the `P-p` case); the non-form `executeResolvedCommand` path instead returns a graceful `noop` when `<id>` is in the command and nothing is selected — inconsistent.

## Desired change

- **Verify + formalise the existing mechanism**: add regression tests asserting `<id>` in a form field value resolves to the selected item's ID, for the free prompt (P-p) and generic forms, across chord and single-key paths.
- **Discoverability**: render a hint line in the form dialog ("type `<id>` to insert the selected item's ID") and document the behavior in `packages/herdr/README.md` (including the `P-p` free-prompt example).
- **Graceful no-item-selected handling**: decide and implement one consistent behavior for `<id>` in field values when nothing is selected (proposed: drop the command with a toast, matching the existing `noop` convention for template `<id>`; documented in the work item).
- **No new mechanism** — the magic-token approach was chosen in intake (option a); chord-based insertion and pre-filled prompts were considered and explicitly out of scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — render the `<id>` discoverability hint in the form dialog (footer/help line); unchanged substitution logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the two form onSubmit callbacks: consistent no-item-selected handling (drop + toast); no change to existing `<id>` resolution.
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — regression tests for `<id>`-in-field resolution, the no-item-selected edge case, and the hint rendering.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document `<id>` inside form field values / free prompts.

## Related work

- **Herdr shortcuts: P-p free prompt and P-a audit-gaps prompt (WL-0MSGHNTMF000YKRI)** — completed; introduced the `P-p` chord this feature builds on.
- **Herdr plugin: free-form prompt shortcut opens new pi pane (WL-0MSC0O8HN000EBFH)** — completed; `/prompt:` routing + `send-to-pi.sh` pane spawning.
- **Form input dialog for unknown identifiers in Herdr chord commands (WL-0MS690SJG003H7WK)** — completed; introduced `FormState` / form-dialog.
- **Shortcuts with multiple <id> tokens only replace the first occurrence (WL-0MRNLF5UO0088ID2)** — completed; multiple-`<id>` handling relevant to the `u-t`/`u-s` edge case.
- **Wire text-insertion template commands (WL-0MS4GIMBD008GWVM)** — completed; text-insertion template wiring in the same code area.
- **Related work (automated report, /skill:find-related)** — additional matches retained as lower-priority context: **wl sync timeouts (WL-0MSAKM838006RZNR)** (completed; herdr auto-sync spawn/timeout context), **[test-failure] send-to-pi.sh / open-pi-agent.sh pane-launch tests (WL-0MSGAKL8R009GB1X)** (completed; pane-launch regression relevant to the P-p spawn path), **Unify dialog widget construction and layout helpers (WL-0MNX4D4G8009XZNJ)** (completed; form-dialog rendering helpers). Automated repo-file matches (audit_runner.py, intake SKILL.md) were reviewed and dropped — generic keyword noise from the wrong repo root.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Over-implementation risk:** the mechanism already exists; the main risk is building a redundant insertion mechanism instead of testing + surfacing the existing magic token. Mitigation: scope is verification, discoverability, and edge-case handling only.
- **No-item-selected edge case:** proposed default = drop the command with a toast (consistent with template `<id>` noop convention). Assumption: users prefer a clear "no item selected" signal over sending a literal `<id>` to Pi.
- **Multi-`<id>` forms (`u-t` title, `u-s` stage):** typing `<id>` into such a field replaces every `<id>` in the command (target and field value) with the selected ID — existing multiple-`<id>` behavior, accepted as-is; noted in docs.
- **Scope-creep risk:** chord-based insertion and pre-filled prompts (intake options b/c) are out of scope; if requested later, record as linked work items rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption:** the selected item is the one highlighted in the herdr worklist (`state.selectedIndex`), same source used by all existing `<id>` substitutions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "The `WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3` reference — that ID is an existing, unrelated in-progress work item (the wl read-cache epic). Which did you mean? (a) It was simply the item currently selected in your herdr pane — the feature is generic: insert *whatever* item is currently selected. (b) It should be a magic token: typing that literal string into the prompt gets replaced with the currently selected item's ID before sending. (c) Something else." — Answer (operator): "a" — generic; insert whatever item is currently selected. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Insertion mechanism — how should the ID get into the input box while typing? (a) A magic token in the prompt text (e.g. typing `<id>` — consistent with the existing placeholder convention in herdr commands). (b) A chord/keypress *inside* the input box (e.g. a key or chord that pastes the selected ID at the cursor). (c) Open the P-p prompt pre-filled with the selected ID. (d) Freeform." — Answer (operator): "a" — magic token (`<id>`). Source: interactive reply. Note: (b) and (c) explicitly out of scope.
- Q3: "Scope — which input boxes should support this? (a) Only the herdr P-p free-prompt input box. (b) All herdr command input forms. (c) Also the main pi prompt input (the `P` key in the pi TUI) — note: that lives in pi core and may not be reachable from a herdr plugin extension." — Answer (operator): "b" — all herdr command input forms. Source: interactive reply. Note: pi core input out of scope.
- Q4 (agent research note, no user answer required): does typing `<id>` in a form field already work? — Research: inspected `form-dialog.ts` (`KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS`, `substituteIdentifiers`) and both onSubmit callbacks in `worklist.ts`; the mechanism already resolves `<id>` to the selected item's ID on submit in both chord and single-key paths. No test covers this path; no UI hint; `P-p` with no item selected leaks literal `<id>` to Pi. Findings incorporated into Existing state / Desired change.

Discovered during WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8 (discovered-from:WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8). The read-cache e2e tests (tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts) spawn the CLI via path.join(projectRoot, 'node_modules', '.bin', 'tsx'). implement.py start creates a fresh git worktree with NO node_modules, so in a worktree these 9 tests fail with 'Cannot find module <worktree>/node_modules/.bin/tsx' (node exits 1). This will fail implement.py finish for every future work item until the worktree gets node_modules.

**Confirmed**: all 9 e2e tests pass in the main checkout (node_modules present) and pass in a worktree after symlinking the root node_modules into it.

**Suggested fixes (pick one, decide ownership)**:
1. implement.py start symlinks/copies the repo root node_modules into the worktree (node_modules and .worklog are gitignored, so no repo pollution).
2. The e2e tests resolve tsx via an env var or the repo root path instead of projectRoot/node_modules.
3. Document that worktrees need a node_modules symlink.

## Resolution status (updated 2026-08-07 during plan)

Both suggested fixes 1 and 2 have already been implemented and verified; the failure mode described above is resolved:

1. **implement.py auto-symlink (suggested fix 1)** — shipped in SorraAgents work item SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B ("Auto-symlink node_modules into implement worktrees (implement.py start)", commit 03344c5c on dev). The shared skills (`~/.pi/agent/skills` -> `SorraAgents/skill`) now call `_ensure_node_modules_symlink()` right after `git worktree add` in `implement.py start`, creating `<worktree>/node_modules -> <repo-root>/node_modules` when the main checkout has one and the worktree lacks one. Live for ContextHub worktrees (an existing worktree, wl-WL-0MSI4TAT70058921, already carries the symlink).
2. **resolveTsxBin walk-up (suggested fix 2)** — shipped in ContextHub commit 613f1490 (2026-08-06): `tests/test-utils.ts` gained `resolveTsxBin()`, which walks up parent directories until it finds a real `node_modules/.bin/tsx`; all three read-cache test files (read-cache-e2e, read-cache-spawn-reduction, read-cache.test.ts) use it. From a worktree under `.worklog/worktrees/`, the walk reaches the main checkout's node_modules without any symlink.

**Verification (2026-08-07)**: ran `npx vitest run tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts` in a fresh detached worktree at dev HEAD with NO node_modules and NO symlink — all 9 tests pass (37.5s). The walk-up alone resolves the failure; the implement.py symlink is belt-and-braces. AC2 holds: `.worklog` and `node_modules` are gitignored (the symlink lives inside the gitignored worktree). AC3 holds: suite green in the main checkout (node_modules present).

**Remaining work**: AC1 end-to-end confirmation — run `implement.py finish` on a real item whose tests include the read-cache e2e file and confirm the full suite is green in the fresh worktree (expected to pass given the fixes above). No further code changes anticipated unless that verification fails.

## Related work

- SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B (SorraAgents) — implement.py auto-symlink, commit 03344c5c
- ContextHub commit 613f1490 — resolveTsxBin walk-up in tests/test-utils.ts

**Acceptance criteria**:
- AC1: implement.py finish runs a green full suite in a fresh worktree for an item whose tests include tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts.
- AC2: No repo pollution (node_modules stays gitignored; .worklog untouched).
- AC3: The e2e tests still pass in the main checkout.

## Summary

`wl next` (and `wl next -n <count>`) currently returns items whose stage is `done`, wasting fetch budget and polluting top-N work lists. Verified: `wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress` returned 20 items of which **12 had stage=done** (e.g. WL-0MMKENAJT14229DE, WL-0MMTDALZO0KQEZMI). Downstream consumers (herdr worklist `fetchNextItems`, pi TUI) then must filter them out client-side, and the TUI fetch budget is effectively reduced (herdr showed 9 items instead of 20 because 12 of the fetched 20 were done).

## User story

As an operator using wl next or a TUI that consumes it, I want done items excluded from results so that the top-N list is full of actionable work and no downstream filtering is needed.

## Expected behaviour

- `wl next` returns only non-done items by default (stage not in [done]).
- `wl next -n 20` returns up to 20 actionable items.
- The `--stage done` filter still allows explicitly requesting done items (filter semantics unchanged: stage filters remain explicit opt-in).
- Existing behaviour for other stages/statuses unchanged; dependency-blocked and in-progress handling unchanged.

## Implementation notes

- Likely in the `next` command implementation (src/commands/next.ts in ContextHub, which is also the global worklog CLI via npm link).
- Add an exclusion predicate for stage=done in the default (unfiltered) query path, similar to how status filters are applied.
- Check existing tests (tests/commands/next.test.ts or similar) and add coverage: a done item is excluded by default, included with explicit --stage done.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress` returns zero items with stage=done.
- [ ] `wl next --stage done -n 5` still returns done items.
- [ ] All existing tests pass; new tests cover the exclusion and the explicit --stage done opt-in.
- [ ] herdr worklist pane no longer needs its client-side stage=done filter (may be kept as defensive).

# Add shortcut to return to the default browse view

## Headline

From a stage-filtered browse list (e.g. `/wl in_progress`), the chord `f s` (sprint) returns the user to the default unfiltered browse list (equivalent to `/wl` with no arguments), instead of requiring Esc to close the widget and re-invoking `/wl`.

> **Scope note (2026-08-08):** The Pi TUI browse UI was removed from this repo (see WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N). The `/wl` command and its shortcut chords now live in the **Herdr plugin** (`packages/herdr`). This work item's implementation was therefore delivered in `packages/herdr` — see Key Files below. AC6 (README docs) refers to `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Problem Statement

Currently there is no way to navigate from a stage-filtered list back to the default view without closing the browse widget entirely. The filter chords (`f i`, `f n`, `f p`, `f r`) are one-way: they switch to a filtered list but nothing switches back.

## Users

- Herdr plugin users who use `/wl <stage>` filters and want to return to the standard next-items list without re-invoking the command.

### Example User Stories

- As a developer, I want to press `f s` while viewing `/wl in_progress` to return to the default next-items browse list.
- As a producer, I want the back-to-default action to be discoverable in the shortcut help line.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Pressing the chord `f s` (label: sprint) from any stage-filtered browse list returns the user to the default unfiltered browse list (equivalent to `/wl` with no arguments).
2. The chord is visible in the browse help line with the label `sprint`.
3. All existing shortcut chords continue to work — `f n` remains bound to 'filter intake' (/wl intake); no existing binding is changed.
4. The default `/wl` (no arguments) behaviour is unchanged.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
6. README shortcut documentation (`packages/herdr/README.md` — shortcut chord list) is updated to document the `f s` sprint chord.

## Constraints

- Scope is the Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr`) — the Pi TUI Worklog browse extension was removed from the repo (WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N).
- Implementation follows the existing config-driven shortcut system (`packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`) — no hardcoded key handlers.

## Existing State

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` defines all shortcut chords. Current `f`-chords: `f i`=idea, `f n`=intake, `f p`=plan, `f r`=review. `f s` is free (verified).
- Chord dispatch (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) resolves chords via `shortcuts.json` and executes the resolved command; `/wl <stage>` filters the browse list by stage; `/wl` with no stage argument returns to the default unfiltered list.

## Desired Change

- Add to `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`:
  ```json
  { "chord": ["f", "s"], "command": "/wl", "view": "both", "label": "sprint", "description": "Return to the default unfiltered browse list." }
  ```
- Verify chord dispatch: pressing `f s` in the list view resolves to command `/wl`, which clears any stage filter and opens the default browse flow.
- Update `packages/herdr/README.md` shortcut documentation to list the new `f s` sprint chord.
- Add/extend tests in `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` / `worklist.test.ts` asserting the `f s` chord exists, is registered, resolves to `/wl`, and does not conflict with existing bindings.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — the `f s` sprint chord entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `/wl <stage>` dispatch, stage map, clearFilter (`/wl` no-args).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchItemsByStage` (stage-filtered list, root-only, open status).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — documents the `f s` sprint chord and stage-filtered browse views.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — tests for the new chord.

## Related Work

- discovered-from:WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G (stage-filtered browse list work)
- WL-0MQDRZ4DK007NK5P — /wl stage filter (parent feature)
- WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N — Pi TUI removal (feature moved to Herdr)

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Which resolution for the `f n` collision?" — Answer (user): "use f s (sprint)" — keep `f n` = filter intake; bind back-to-default to `f s` with label 'sprint'. Verified `f s` is free. Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-06.

# Herdr plugin: add Related Docs row to metadata section listing .md Key Files (openable in the markdown viewer)

## Problem statement

The Herdr work item selection list's metadata section (the bottom panel of the list and the detail-view metadata table, both built by `buildMetaRows`) shows the item's tracked fields but gives no visibility into which markdown documents are associated with the item via its `Key Files:` section. The detail view only auto-renders the *first* `.md` file (`firstMarkdownKeyFile`), so when a work item references multiple `.md` documents (e.g. a PRD plus an episode file), there is no way to see them all, let alone open a specific one. This change adds a `Related Docs` metadata row listing every `.md` path from the item's `Key Files:` section and makes each listed document openable in the markdown viewer.

## Users

- **Herdr users** browsing work items who want to see at a glance which markdown documents (PRDs, episode `.podcast.md` files, specs) are associated with the selected item, and open any of them without leaving the worklist.

### Example User Stories

- As a Herdr user, I want the metadata section to list the `.md` documents referenced in the selected item's `Key Files:` section, so I can see its related docs at a glance.
- As a Herdr user, I want to open a specific listed document in the markdown viewer (not just the first one), so I can read the PRD or episode file that is relevant to me.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `buildMetaRows` (shared by the list-mode metadata panel and the detail-view metadata table) adds a `Related Docs` row listing **every** `.md` path extracted from the item's `Key Files:` section via `extractFilePaths` (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`), joined/delimited to fit the existing label/value row format.
2. When the item has no `.md` files in `Key Files:` (or no `Key Files:` section at all), the `Related Docs` row is omitted — consistent with how `buildMetaRows` omits unset fields.
3. (Canonical per operator, 2026-08-06) The list-mode metadata panel row is **display-only**; opening happens in the detail view: a persistent Table of Contents (ToC) at the top of the detail view lists every `.md` Key File, arrow/j/k navigate the ToC, Enter renders the selected document in the markdown viewer (`renderMarkdownViewer`). The ToC stays visible on all renders; navigating past the end of the ToC moves focus to scrolling the viewed document. The auto-render of the first `.md` file remains the initial default.
4. File paths resolve against the **resolved worklog root** (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`), not `process.cwd()` — the fix from WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q must be honored; the `Related Docs` row must not reintroduce the plugin-CWD resolution bug.
5. Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (and/or `grouping.test.ts`) cover: `Related Docs` row content in the metadata panel and detail view, row omitted when no `.md` files exist, mixed `Key Files` lists (`.ts`/`.json`/`.md`), and opening a listed file renders that file's content.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`packages/herdr/README.md` metadata-panel section).
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Metadata rows are label/value pairs built by `buildMetaRows`; the `Related Docs` value must fit the existing truncation/formatting (multi-file values need a compact delimiter, e.g. `, ` or ` · `; truncation via existing `truncateLine`).
- Reuse existing helpers: `extractFilePaths` (grouping.ts) for parsing, `renderMarkdownViewer`/`renderFileViewer` (md-viewer.ts) for rendering. No new markdown parsing.
- No new icons; follow the existing noIcons/text-fallback convention from WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9 if icons are involved.
- Mouse/touch support is out of scope — it is tracked separately in WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ (open). "Click/activate" here means keyboard activation (Enter on the entry) consistent with the existing interaction model.
- Path resolution must use the resolved worklog root (see WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q), never `process.cwd()`.

## Existing state

- `buildMetaRows(item)` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` builds the metadata label/value rows shared by `formatMetadataPanel` (list-mode bottom panel) and `formatDetailContent` (detail-view metadata table). Fields with null/empty values are omitted.
- `extractFilePaths(description)` in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` extracts all file paths from the `Key Files:` section (mirrors `src/commands/helpers.ts`; see `docs/FILE_PATH_CONVENTION.md`).
- `firstMarkdownKeyFile(description)` in `worklist.ts` picks only the **first** `.md` path; the detail view auto-renders that one file via `renderFileViewer` (the "Episode file (md viewer)" section) when `readFile` resolves it.
- `readKeyFile` resolves Key Files paths against `process.cwd()` — broken for plugin panes (cwd is `packages/herdr`); WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q fixes this to use the resolved worklog root (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`).
- The list-mode metadata panel scrolls independently (`m`/`M`, `metaScrollOffset`); there is currently no per-row selection/activation in the metadata panel.
- Mouse/touch support does not exist yet (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ open).

## Desired change

1. Add a `Related Docs` row to `buildMetaRows`: extract all `.md` paths via `extractFilePaths(item.description)`, filter `endsWith('.md')`, join them into the row value (compact delimiter), omit when empty. Shared by the metadata panel and the detail-view table automatically.
2. (Canonical per operator, 2026-08-06) Opening happens in the detail view only — the list-mode metadata panel is display-only (Q1 answer: option C). The detail view gains a persistent ToC at the top listing all `.md` Key Files: introduce a selected-doc/ToC focus state (e.g. `detailMdFile` / `detailToCIndex`); arrow/j/k navigate the ToC; Enter sets the selected doc and re-renders the md-viewer section with that file's content (superseding the auto-first-file render for the selected doc); navigating past the end of the ToC transfers focus to document scrolling; the ToC stays pinned on all renders.
3. Ensure path resolution uses the resolved worklog root (align with WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q); fail-open (unreadable/missing files omitted from the row or marked).
4. Add/extend unit tests; update `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `buildMetaRows` gains the `Related Docs` row; add selected-doc state and open-in-viewer activation in the metadata panel and detail view.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — possibly expose/refactor an `extractMdPaths` helper (or reuse `extractFilePaths` + filter).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — new/updated tests for the `Related Docs` row and open-in-viewer behavior.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the `Related Docs` metadata row.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q** — "herdr plugin md viewer fails: Key Files paths resolved against plugin CWD, not worklog root" (open, high): fixes the path resolution this feature depends on; **dependency (prereq)**.
- **WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X** — "Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command" (completed): created the metadata panel (`buildMetaRows` shared builder).
- **WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9** — "Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section" (open): icons in the same metadata section; icon/text conventions apply.
- **WL-0MS6MOXNQ005B9IC** — "Metadata in work-item detail views should be presented as markdown table" (completed): detail-view metadata table format.
- **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** — "Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the selection list" (open): would enable literal mouse "click"; activation here is keyboard-based.
- **WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3** — "Show description preview in herder plugin selection list" (open): related list-content rendering work.
- **docs/FILE_PATH_CONVENTION.md** — the `Key Files:` section convention parsed by `extractFilePaths`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Click" means keyboard activation (Enter) — mouse support is a separate open item (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ). If the operator intends literal mouse clicks, this feature depends on that item; flagged as an open question below.
- **Assumption:** The `Related Docs` value uses a compact delimiter (e.g. `, `) and relies on existing truncation; long multi-file lists may truncate — acceptable, scroll/expand via the existing metadata scroll.
- **Risk (dependency):** Correct path resolution is prerequisite; if WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q is not implemented first, the new row will inherit the same broken-CWD behavior. Mitigation: dependency edge registered; implementation should build on the fixed resolver.
- **Risk (behavior change):** Adding the row changes `buildMetaRows` output, affecting existing tests asserting exact metadata strings; tests updated in the same change.
- **Risk (scope creep):** Mouse/touch support, editing docs, or opening non-`.md` files are out of scope — track separately if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What is 'the meta-data section'?" — Answer (user): "(a) The Herdr selection-list metadata panel + detail-view metadata table (`buildMetaRows`)". Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-06.
- Q: "What is 'the related files list'?" — Answer (user): "(a) The `Key Files:` section of the work item description". Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-06.
- Q: "What should happen to the .md files once added to the meta-data section?" — Answer (user): "(a) Listed as a new metadata row, but call it **Related Docs**; click them to open in the markdown viewer". Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-06.
- Q: "Mouse support does not exist yet in the worklist (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ open) — how should 'click to open' work?" — Answer: not yet answered; **OPEN QUESTION** for the implementer/operator. Default assumption: keyboard activation (Enter) on the entry; literal mouse click would require WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ first.
- Q: "How does the new Related Docs open-in-viewer interact with the existing auto-render of the first `.md` Key File in the detail view?" — Answer: not yet answered; **OPEN QUESTION** for the implementer. Default assumption: keep auto-render of the first file; explicit open of any listed doc (including the first) renders that file.

- Q: "How should 'click to open' work without mouse support (list-mode metadata panel activation)?" — Answer (operator, 2026-08-06): "Option C — panel is display-only; opening happens in the detail view via a Table of Contents at the top (arrow/j/k navigate, Enter renders, ToC stays visible on all renders, navigating past the end of the list moves to scrolling the viewed document)." Final: ToC-in-detail-view design; supersedes the earlier OPEN QUESTION.
- Q: "Confirm defaults: keyboard-only activation; keep auto-render of the first .md; one Related Docs row with compact delimiter + truncation?" — Answer (operator, 2026-08-06): "Confirmed, with the answer to the Q1/panel question being canonical where there is a conflict." Final: confirmed.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-06 — Plan created via /plan WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29. Four child work items created: `Tests: Related Docs row, detail ToC and open-in-viewer` (WL-0MSHWHP0S0036DDU), `Add Related Docs metadata row` (WL-0MSHWHRIF001YHF8), `Detail view ToC for Related Docs` (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I), `Documentation updates` (WL-0MSHWHULZ004A8PQ). Dependency chain wired: tests → row → ToC → docs. Operator answered Q1 (option C + ToC-in-detail-view) and confirmed Q2; parent description AC3 and Desired-change §2 amended to match. Effort/risk re-estimated: Small (E=5.79h, rec 7.79h), Medium risk (10/25), 71% confidence. Prior OPEN QUESTION entries are superseded by the new Appendix answers above.

# Herdr worklist: remove blank line and redundant filter bar; show filter in header

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist selection-list renderer (`createListRenderer` in
`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) reserves a blank line between the header and
the filter bar, and renders a standalone filter status bar even though the
header already indicates the active stage filter. This wastes a chrome row and
duplicates the filter indication.

## Users

Anyone using the Herdr `worklog-selection-list` plugin pane to browse/filter/select
work items.

User story: *"As a Herdr user, when I filter the work list by stage I want the
filter state shown in the header only (no redundant blank line or separate filter
bar), so the pane shows more items and looks clean."*

## Acceptance criteria

- In list mode, the renderer no longer emits the blank line between the header (or
  code-freeze banner) and the following content; no stray empty row remains in that
  position.
- In list mode, the standalone filter status bar is no longer rendered (neither the
  "Filter: <stage>" bar when filtered nor the "No filter — press [f]..." hint when
  unfiltered).
- When a stage filter is active, the filter is still indicated in the header
  (existing ` (filtered: <stage>)` suffix); the behavior is unchanged except for the
  removal of the redundant bar and blank line.
- The `rows - 1` line-count invariant still holds for all modes and configurations
  (with/without code-freeze banner, groups, metadata panel) — the `chromeLines`
  budget is reduced accordingly.
- Filter mode (the `[f] [i/n/p/r]` selection prompt) is unchanged.
- Existing unit tests continue to pass; add/adjust tests covering the new layout
  (no blank line, no filter bar line) and the updated `chromeLines` budget.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded; it is managed automatically by the ship
> skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Keep the existing shape/functions. The unused `formatFilterBar` helper and any
  now-unused constants/imports it pulls in must be cleaned up (removed) since the
  bar is no longer rendered.
- The header already shows the filter via `filterLabel`; do not add a new separate
  filter mechanism.
- Must preserve the `rows - 1` line-count invariant introduced in
  WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, `createListRenderer()`:
  - header: `const filterLabel = activeFilter ? ` (filtered: ${activeFilter})` : ''` then
    `header = ... Work Items — N item(s)${filterLabel} ...` (appended before other chrome).
  - after the code-freeze banner (if active), `output.push('');` inserts a blank line.
  - `output.push(formatFilterBar(activeFilter, cols));` renders the filter status bar.
  - `const chromeLines = bannerActive ? 5 : 4; // header + banner + blank + filter bar + footer`.
- `formatFilterBar(filter, maxCols)` at `worklist.ts` renders either a "Filter: stage" bar
  (active) or a "No filter — press [f]..." hint (inactive).
- Item-window formulas: the renderer uses
  `const listHeight = Math.max(3, rows - 6 - panelHeight);` and
  `WorkItemListState._listHeight()` uses
  `Math.max(3, this.termSize.rows - 6 - panelHeight)` (comment: "Reserve 3 rows for
  header, 1 for filter bar, 1 for footer, 1 for status"). The page-size unit test
  asserts `pageDown` advances 11 rows on an 80x24 terminal.

## Desired change

- Remove `output.push('');` (the blank line between header/banner and the bar).
- Remove `output.push(formatFilterBar(activeFilter, cols));` (the filter bar row).
- Reduce the chrome budget to `bannerActive ? 3 : 2` (`// header + banner + footer`),
  updating the comment.
- Delete the now-unused `formatFilterBar` export/helper (and remove any imports it
  leaves orphaned).
- Bump the item-window formulas from `rows - 6 - panelHeight` to
  `rows - 4 - panelHeight` in both the renderer (`listHeight`) and
  `WorkItemListState._listHeight()` (updating the stale "1 for filter bar" comment),
  so the two freed rows actually display more items per the user story while keeping
  `listHeight` at or below the reduced budget (the existing 1-row slack is preserved).
  The page-size unit test asserting 11 rows on 80x24 must be adjusted to 13 rows
  (covered by the "add/adjust tests" AC).
- Update the `used` fill accounting accordingly (it derives from `chromeLines`, so it
  adjusts automatically).
- Keep the active-filter indication in the header (`filterLabel`), which is already
  present.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — primary change: remove blank line push, remove
  `formatFilterBar` call, reduce `chromeLines`, delete the `formatFilterBar` helper,
  bump the `listHeight`/`_listHeight()` item-window formulas.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — unit tests currently asserting only the
  `rows - 1` line-count invariant and group separators; add assertions that no blank
  line follows the header and no filter bar row is rendered; verify the reduced
  `chromeLines`; adjust the page-size test (11 → 13 rows on 80x24).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — update any references to the filter bar chrome row in
  the layout/design-decisions section if present.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO` "Herdr plugin: selection list header and top lines cut off
  top of pane" — introduced the `rows - 1` invariant and the chrome/padding
  accounting for header + blank + filter bar; this change is a follow-up that
  simplifies that budget.
- `WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X` "Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item
  metadata and last command" — metadata panel; the list-area/chrome accounting must
  stay consistent for its `rows - 1` invariant tests.
- `WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ` "Herdr selection list: no indication of items below the fold"
  — open; also touches render budget / fill accounting; avoid conflict with any
  in-flight edits to the same `chromeLines`/fill code.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: the filter indication in the header (`filterLabel`) is sufficient and is
  the intended final display; the standalone bar (including the "No filter — press
  [f]..." hint) is entirely redundant and should be removed rather than relocated.
- Risk: reducing `chromeLines` changes the number of rows available to items; line-count
  invariant tests must still pass for all configurations (banner, groups, panel).
- Risk: bumping the item-window formulas changes the page size (11 → 13 on 80x24);
  the pageUp/pageDown navigation tests must be updated to match.
- Scope-creep risk: the `f` chord filter prompt (`formatFilterPrompt`) must remain; do
  not remove the filtering interaction, only the passive status-bar rendering.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: None asked — the seed intent and prior work-item context were sufficient. The
  request explicitly stated: remove the blank line after the heading, remove the
  filter line, and put the filter in the header (already implemented via
  `filterLabel`). Priority: **high**.
- OPEN QUESTION: none (request is unambiguous for the described renderer layout).
- Plan review note (plan skill auto-complete path, 2026-08-06): the review stages
  added the item-window (`listHeight`/`_listHeight()`) bump and the page-size test
  adjustment to the Desired change, so the two freed chrome rows deliver the user
  story's "shows more items" instead of becoming bottom fill. This is unambiguous
  (user story) and covered by the "add/adjust tests" AC; flagged here for
  traceability.

# Event-driven herdr window status: subscribe to window events instead of polling

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist plugin determines the status of active herdr windows/panes by **polling** the herdr CLI on short timers: `herdr pane get <id>` every 2s (PollGate / resume-poll) for pane focus/visibility, and `herdr agent list` every 2s (AgentTracker TTL) for per-agent status. Polling adds latency (icons and refresh lag behind real state changes by up to a poll cycle), spawns herdr processes on every tick, and misses instantaneous transitions. Herdr v0.7.5 already exposes an event subscription API (`events.subscribe` over the herdr Unix socket, with events such as `pane_agent_status_changed`, `pane_focused`, `pane_agent_detected`); the plugin should subscribe to these window events and provide feedback dynamically, keeping polling only as a fail-open fallback.

## Users

- **Herdr users running the worklist plugin alongside pi agent panes** — they want the per-item agent-status icons (🟢 working / ⛔ blocked / ⚪ idle) to update the moment an agent's state changes, not up to a poll cycle later.
- **Herdr users with multiple panes/tabs and multiple herdr instances in one project** — they want every worklist instance to react immediately to focus changes and to status changes of agents spawned by any herdr instance, not just its own pane.

User stories:
- _As a user watching a work item's agent status icon, I want it to flip to working/blocked/idle immediately when the agent's state changes, so I don't wait for the next poll._
- _As a user returning to a hidden tab, I want the list to refresh instantly when the tab regains focus, so I don't wait for the 2s resume-poll or the next 30s refresh tick._
- _As a user running several herdr instances in one project, I want every worklist instance to see status changes for all agents spawned by any instance, so the icons are consistent everywhere._

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Event-driven agent status:** When subscribed, a real agent status change (`pane_agent_status_changed` event) updates the corresponding work-item icon in the list within 1s, without waiting for the next `herdr agent list` poll. Verified by unit tests with a mocked socket emitter and, where possible, a live event-subscription check.
- [ ] **AC2 — Event-driven focus transition:** When subscribed, a hidden → visible pane transition (`pane_focused` event) triggers an immediate list refresh and clears the `[paused — hidden]` indicator without relying on the 2s resume-poll. Verified by tests with a mocked socket emitter.
- [ ] **AC3 — Cross-instance coverage:** Each worklist plugin instance subscribes to events covering agents spawned by **any** herdr instance in the same project, including agents that appear after the plugin started (via `pane.agent_detected` and re-reading the shared `.worklog/agent-panes.json`). Verified by tests simulating multiple plugin instances / late-spawned agents.
- [ ] **AC4 — Fail-open fallback:** When the herdr socket is unavailable, subscription fails, or a transient socket error occurs (older herdr, standalone mode, reconnect in progress), the plugin falls back to the existing polling (`herdr pane get` / `herdr agent list`) with no behavioral regression; socket errors never crash the TUI. Verified by tests with an unreachable socket.
- [ ] **AC5 — Initial state via one-time snapshot:** Initial pane focus and agent states are still obtained via a one-time snapshot (`herdr pane get` / `herdr agent list` or `herdr api snapshot`); events are applied incrementally on top. No requirement for events to be reliable for initial state.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the herdr plugin README, and any relevant docs (e.g. `packages/herdr/shared/herdr-agent-state-protocol.md` or a new events doc).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Herdr version:** `events.subscribe` requires herdr ≥ 0.7.5 (the plugin manifest currently declares `min_herdr_version = "0.7.0"` — likely needs a bump). Older herdr and standalone (no-session) runs must keep working via polling.
- **Transport:** Subscription is a long-lived JSON-RPC connection over the herdr Unix socket (`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, default `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`), the same socket the plugin already uses for outbound agent reporting (agent-state protocol) and that `grid.py` uses for RPC. The plugin must tolerate reconnect/backoff.
- **Subscription shape (verified against herdr 0.7.5 schema + live socket):** `pane.focused`, `pane.agent_detected`, `pane.closed`, `pane.exited` are global (no `pane_id`); `pane.agent_status_changed` **requires** a `pane_id`, so per-pane subscriptions must be (re)created as tracked panes appear/disappear. Multiple subscriptions in one `events.subscribe` call work.
- **Cross-instance semantics:** Multiple herdr clients attach to the same persistent session/server, so a subscription made by one worklist instance observes events for the whole session (all agents, all tabs/workspaces). Each plugin instance subscribes independently.
- **Fail-open discipline:** Follow the plugin's established fail-open conventions — any event-path failure degrades to today's polling, never crashes the TUI, never blocks refresh/sync.
- **Event storms:** Frequent status changes (e.g. streaming agents) must not cause render thrash — coalesce/limit state applications per render cycle as needed.
- **Scope boundary:** Only window/pane status events are in scope (agent status + focus/visibility). The `wl` data refresh/sync cadence (30s `wl list`/`next`, `wl sync`) is **not** part of this event-driven change.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Socket path discovery (assumption):** `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` may not be propagated into the worklist pane process environment (the agent-state protocol expects it, but pane processes are spawned via plugin pane commands). Fallback chain: `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` → default `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock` → poll fallback. Verify during implementation.
- **herdr version gating (risk):** Bumping `min_herdr_version` to 0.7.5 could block plugin load for users on 0.7.0–0.7.4 even though they'd work fine via poll fallback. Mitigation: keep the manifest version conservative and degrade at runtime instead of refusing to load, or make the bump advisory.
- **Event storms (risk):** Agents streaming or toggling state rapidly could emit many `pane_agent_status_changed` events → render thrash and unnecessary TUI re-renders. Mitigation: coalesce per render cycle / throttle icon updates (follow the existing `requestRender` patterns in the pi extension).
- **Subscription lifecycle (risk):** `pane.agent_status_changed` requires a `pane_id` per subscription; subscriptions must be added as agents are detected and (optionally) dropped when panes close. A missed add = stale icons; mitigate via `pane.agent_detected` + re-reading `.worklog/agent-panes.json` on each event batch. Unsubscribe/close the socket on plugin exit to avoid leaked connections.
- **Session scope (assumption, verify):** Events are scoped to the herdr **session** the client attaches to. Multiple herdr instances attached to the same session share events (covers the user's cross-instance requirement); a project split across *different sessions* would not share events — confirm this matches the intended multi-instance scenario and document any limitation.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Event-driven `wl` data refresh/sync is explicitly out of scope; if follow-on work surfaces (e.g. subscribing to worklog DB changes), record it as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — `isPaneVisible()` execs `herdr pane get <id>`; `PollGate` memoizes within a 2s TTL (`DEFAULT_POLL_GATE_TTL_MS`). Used by refresh/sync scheduler tasks and the `resume-poll` task (which polls every 2s while the pane is hidden to catch the hidden → visible transition, WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ).
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — `AgentTracker.refreshStates()` execs `herdr agent list` memoized within a 2s TTL (`AGENT_STATE_TTL_MS`); persists work-item ↔ pane associations to `.worklog/agent-panes.json` (shared across panes/tabs/instances, last-writer-wins); prunes entries for gone/done panes; `mergeAgentStates()` sets `agentState` on fetched items for icon rendering (WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — consolidated `TaskScheduler` loop (WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP) with tasks: `refresh` (30s), `sync` (30s), `resume-poll` (2s, only while hidden), `downtime` (30s). Every tick consults `paneGate.visible()`; hidden panes skip wl spawns (zero-wl-when-hidden guarantee, WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N).
- Herdr v0.7.5 socket API (verified live): `events.subscribe` accepts `{"subscriptions":[{"type":"pane.focused"},{"type":"pane.agent_status_changed","pane_id":"..."},{"type":"pane.agent_detected"},{"type":"pane.closed"}]}` → `{"type":"subscription_started"}`. Event types include `pane_agent_status_changed`, `pane_focused`, `pane_agent_detected`, `pane_created`, `pane_closed`, `pane_exited`, `pane_output_changed`, `pane_updated`, `tab_focused`, `workspace_focused`. `herdr api snapshot` provides a one-shot runtime snapshot.

## Desired change

1. **New module** `packages/herdr/src/events.ts` — a `HerdrEventSubscriber` (or similar) that:
   - Connects to the herdr Unix socket (path from `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` env, falling back to the default config path).
   - Subscribes globally to `pane.focused`, `pane.agent_detected`, `pane.closed`, `pane.exited` and per-pane to `pane.agent_status_changed` for each pane currently tracked in `.worklog/agent-panes.json`; adds/removes per-pane subscriptions as agents are detected/closed.
   - Reconnects with backoff on socket errors; emits typed callbacks the worklist can consume; fails open (reports "events unavailable") so callers fall back to polling.
2. **Agent status feedback:** `AgentTracker` gains an event-applied path: `pane_agent_status_changed` / `pane_agent_detected` / `pane_closed` / `pane_exited` update the cached state map and trigger an immediate icon re-render. `herdr agent list` remains the one-time initial snapshot and the poll fallback.
3. **Focus/visibility feedback:** `pane_focused` events update `panePaused` immediately; hidden → visible transitions trigger `doRefresh(true)`; the 2s `resume-poll` scheduler task becomes the fallback (active only when the event path is unavailable).
4. **Wiring:** `index.ts`/`worklist.ts` instantiate the subscriber once per plugin instance and hand the event callbacks to the visibility gate and agent tracker; cleanup on TUI exit (unsubscribe/close socket).
5. **Fallback orchestration:** If subscription fails (older herdr, no socket, reconnect loop), the plugin silently keeps today's polling behavior; a health flag distinguishes "events active" vs "polling fallback" for tests and any status display.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/events.ts` — **New.** Herdr socket event subscriber: connect, subscribe, dispatch typed events, reconnect with backoff, fail-open.
- `packages/herdr/src/agent-tracker.ts` — Apply `pane_agent_status_changed` / `pane_agent_detected` / `pane_closed` / `pane_exited` events to the state map; keep `herdr agent list` snapshot + poll fallback; expose an event-driven refresh trigger.
- `packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts` — Accept `pane_focused` events (update cached focused state); keep `herdr pane get` snapshot + PollGate fallback.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Wire the subscriber; make `resume-poll` a fallback-only task; trigger immediate refresh/icon updates from events; cleanup on exit.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Instantiate/teardown the subscriber; env handling (`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`).
- `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` — Possibly bump `min_herdr_version` to 0.7.5.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `packages/herdr/shared/herdr-agent-state-protocol.md` — Document the subscription-based status path and the poll fallback.
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/events.test.ts` (new), plus updates to `agent-tracker.test.ts`, `visibility.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts`/`worklist-visibility.test.ts`/`worklist-agent-state.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N — Pi extension polls wl list / wl next even when selection list is not visible** — Root issue behind pause-when-hidden; established the zero-wl-when-hidden guarantee that this change preserves.
- **WL-0MSB44697000K8CP — Impl: pane visibility detection module (visibility.ts + PollGate)** — The `herdr pane get` polling this change makes event-driven.
- **WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ — Herdr selection list refreshes immediately when its tab regains focus (hidden→visible transition)** — Introduced the 2s resume-poll; the `pane_focused` event path replaces the polling portion.
- **WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9 — Work-item ↔ agent-pane association tracker (agent-panes.json + herdr agent list)** — The `herdr agent list` polling this change makes event-driven.
- **WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP — Consolidate herdr plugin timers into a single loop** — The TaskScheduler that hosts the `resume-poll` task and refresh/sync cadence (unchanged for wl data).
- **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J — Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM)** — Context for why reducing poll-driven process spawns is valuable.
- **WL-0MP15AMKV002F3U4 — Event emitter and UI hook API** — Completed/wont-fix (Blessed TUI deprecated); a similar subscribe-notify pattern exists in the pi extension (`config.ts` onChange subscribers, session-health `pi.on(...)` lifecycle events).
- **packages/herdr/shared/herdr-agent-state-protocol.md** — The existing outbound socket protocol (`pane.report_agent`) the plugin already uses; the inbound subscription complements it.
- **packages/herdr/shared/grid.py** — Existing JSON-RPC-over-socket client pattern to model the subscriber on.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope — Should the event-driven path replace both polled statuses (agent-status icons and pane-focus/visibility gating), or focus on just one?" — Answer (user): "both." Source: interactive reply. Final: both agent status icons and pane focus/visibility gating become event-driven, with poll fallback.
- Q2: "Transport — `events.subscribe` needs a persistent Unix-socket connection. Is a long-lived socket subscription acceptable, or should this stay CLI-driven (e.g. `herdr agent wait`)?" — Answer (user): "yes acceptable, not sure that it should be CLI driven, can't it be part of the herdr plugin so that each instance of the plugin listens to instances?" Source: interactive reply. Final: implement the subscription natively inside the herdr plugin (`packages/herdr/src/events.ts`); each plugin instance opens its own socket subscription; not CLI-wrapper driven. Research: verified `events.subscribe` over `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock` returns `subscription_started` for `pane.focused`, `pane.agent_detected`, `pane.closed`, and `pane.agent_status_changed` + `pane_id` (schema: `required: ["type", "pane_id"]`); multiple subscriptions per call supported.
- Q3: "Fallback — Keep polling as a fail-open fallback when events are unavailable (older herdr / standalone / socket error)?" — Answer (user): "yes." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4 (user-added): "If I have multiple herdr instances open within a single project all of them should subscribe to the events for all agents spawned by any instance of herdr." — Answer: accepted as an AC (AC3). Research: herdr clients attach to a shared persistent session/server; `pane.agent_detected` (global, no pane_id) fires for agents in any pane, and per-pane `pane.agent_status_changed` subscriptions plus re-reading the shared `.worklog/agent-panes.json` cover late-spawned agents.

# Swap model identifier and command positions on herd status line

## Problem statement

The custom Pi TUI footer's model line (Line 3, rendered by the Worklog session-health extension) currently shows the model identifier on the left and the session's initial command/prompt preview on the right: `code → openai/gpt-4  │  /skill:implement WL-…`. The user wants the positions swapped — command on the left, model on the right — with the command receiving as much of the available line width as possible.

## Users

End users of the Pi TUI with the Worklog extension enabled (including herdr-spawned pi panes). The footer's Line 3 is the at-a-glance readout of which model is serving the session and which command/prompt started it. Putting the command first (left-aligned, wide budget) makes the active task the primary read and pushes the model identifier to a fixed right slot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The model identifier (e.g. `code → openai/gpt-4`, `code → (resolving)`, resolved model only, or `—`) is rendered on the RIGHT side of the footer model line, after the `│` separator.
- The command/prompt preview is rendered on the LEFT side of the footer model line, before the `│` separator.
- The command preview is given as much width as possible: the model part is capped to a fixed maximum (e.g. ~30 visible columns, truncated with an ellipsis if longer) and the remaining line width is allocated to the command preview.
- When no initial prompt exists, the line continues to show just the model identifier (unchanged behavior).
- Footer Lines 1–2 (extension statuses, session health) are unchanged.
- Unit tests in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` ("model line in footer") are updated to assert the new left/right ordering and the space allocation; the full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Change only the footer model line (Line 3) rendering in `session-health.ts`; do not alter Lines 1–2, the herdr pane, or the model-display module.
- Preserve the grey/dim styling and existing truncation conventions (terminal-width aware truncation; `...` style ellipsis used for the prompt preview).
- Keep the change surgical: no refactoring of unrelated code.

## Existing state

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — custom footer via `ctx.ui.setFooter()`. Line 3 currently renders `${modelPart}  │  ${promptPart}` (model left, command right). The prompt budget is a fixed reservation (`const reserved = 38`), so the command is capped at `width - 38` regardless of the actual model width.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` — the "model line in footer" describe block asserts the current format (`<alias> → <provider/model>  │  <preview>`), truncation of long prompts, and fallback states (dash, `(resolving)`, resolved-only).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/terminal-utils.ts` — provides `visibleWidth()` and `truncateToTerminalWidth()` for terminal-aware measuring/truncation (already imported by session-health.ts).
- The herdr pane itself never displays the model (it only forwards `--model` to the pi CLI), so "herd status line" resolves to the pi TUI footer model line.

## Desired change

In `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` (footer `render()`):

1. Build `modelPart` exactly as today (selected alias → resolved provider/model, `(resolving)`, `—` fallbacks).
2. Build the command preview from `state.initialPrompt` (compacted via `truncateWorkItemId`).
3. Compose the label as `${commandPreview}  │  ${modelPart}` when a prompt exists; otherwise keep just `modelPart`.
4. Give the command as much space as possible: cap the model part at ~30 visible columns (truncate with ellipsis if longer), then allocate `width − modelWidth − separatorWidth` to the command preview, retaining the final `truncateToTerminalWidth(…, width)` safety clamp.

## Key Files

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — Line-3 label composition and width budgeting (primary change).
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` — update "model line in footer" tests for the new ordering and budget; add a case asserting the command receives the majority of the width (and the model is right-aligned after the separator).

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "herd status line" = the pi TUI footer model line (Line 3 of session-health) — the only place model + command share a line. Documented in the Appendix; if the operator meant a different surface this is the first thing to revisit.
- Edge case: at very narrow terminal widths the capped model part plus separator may exceed the line width; the existing final `truncateToTerminalWidth(…, width)` clamp must be retained so the line never overflows.
- Scope control: only the Line-3 composition and budget change; Lines 1–2, the herdr pane, and model-display.ts stay untouched. Any adjacent polish (e.g. prompt truncation style) is out of scope unless it blocks the swap.

## Related work

- WL-0MRF19R71004YJND — Add model/provider line to TUI status bar footer (completed): introduced the model footer line.
- WL-0MRDRZ32L00404D0 — Session Health Extension for Pi Footer (completed): the custom footer this change lives in.
- WL-0MRC91VIN0089UXD — Move provider/model display to start of Worklog extension status line (completed): prior re-layout of model display; history of this area.
- WL-0MRERDU1J000W1IS — Show time since last streaming chunk in session health footer (completed): adjacent session-health footer work (found by find-related).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which status line is 'the herd status line'?" — Answer (repo inspection): the custom Pi TUI footer's model line (Line 3 of the session-health footer), the only place a model identifier and a command/prompt are displayed on one line. The herdr pane never displays the model (worklist.ts only forwards `--model` to the pi CLI). Source: `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` lines ~603–644; grep of `packages/herdr/src/`.
- Q: "What does 'the command' mean?" — Answer (repo inspection): the session's initial user message / prompt preview (`state.initialPrompt`), which for herdr-spawned panes is the dispatch command. Source: `state.initialPrompt` capture and preview logic in `session-health.ts` (lines ~500–510, ~624–643).
- Q: "What does 'as much space as possible' mean?" — Answer (interpretation, recorded as AC3): the model part should be capped (~30 visible columns) so the command receives the remaining width; today the command is capped at `width − 38` via a fixed reservation that does not shrink when the model is short. No user clarification requested — reasonable interpretation of the request; flagged as assumption.
