# Objective

Make the worklog-selection-list plugin's chord shortcuts **extensible per project**: the bundled `src/shortcuts.json` provides the default chords, and a **project-local `shortcuts.json`** (discovered from the resolved worklog root) provides additional entries and overrides. Today `loadShortcutConfig()` reads only the bundled file, so projects cannot add project-specific chords without forking the plugin.

## Problem statement

A consuming project (open_source_llm) needs a `w` chord that dispatches `/skill:wiki-podcast-script --doc <path> --force-single` / `--rewrite <path>` to a pi agent pane for podcast episode work items. That chord is project-specific and must **not** be added to the core plugin's bundled `shortcuts.json` (operator decision). The plugin currently loads shortcuts exclusively from `join(__dirname, 'shortcuts.json')` (see `loadShortcutConfig()` in `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts`), so there is no supported way to add or override chords per project.

## Users

Herdr users of the worklog-selection-list plugin, and projects that consume it (e.g. open_source_llm's podcast production workflow).

- As a plugin user, I want the plugin's built-in chords (c, n, p, i, r, s, …) to remain available by default, so I can keep the standard workflow unchanged.
- As a project maintainer, I want to add project-specific chords (e.g. `w` → write podcast script) in a local file without editing the plugin source, so upgrades/rebuilds of the plugin do not lose my chords.
- As a project maintainer, I want a local chord with the same key sequence as a bundled one to override the bundled behavior, so I can tailor defaults per project.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `loadShortcutConfig()` loads the bundled `src/shortcuts.json` as before (backward compatible; no local file → identical behavior to today).
- [ ] When a project-local `shortcuts.json` exists, its entries are merged: new chords are added, and a local entry whose chord sequence (+ view) matches a bundled entry overrides it (local wins). Override semantics are documented and unit-tested.
- [ ] The project-local file is resolved relative to the **worklog root** (the root that `configureWorklogTarget()` / `resolveWorklogRoot()` resolves from `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`, i.e. the directory containing `.worklog/`), so the same plugin install serves different chords in different projects.
- [ ] Local file location and merge order are documented in the plugin README (config section), including the override rule and validation behavior.
- [ ] Malformed local entries are logged and skipped without breaking the bundled defaults (same defensive posture as the bundled parser; invalid values never crash or hide shortcuts).
- [ ] Existing chord behavior is unchanged when no local file is present; full `npm test` suite (shortcut-config tests and others) passes.

## Design notes / open questions

- **Local file location:** proposal is `<worklog-root>/shortcuts.json` (next to `.worklog/`). Alternative: a hidden name (`.herdr/shortcuts.json` or `.pi/shortcuts.json`) to avoid a bare `shortcuts.json` in the project root. The worklog root already has `.worklog/`; a `shortcuts.json` next to it is simple and discoverable. Confirm which location is preferred (see Open Questions).
- **Override key:** chord sequence + view (`'list'|'detail'|'both'`) is the natural key. A local entry with the same chord+view replaces the bundled entry; same chord with a different view coexists. A local `stages` filter narrows availability (already supported by `ShortcutEntry`).
- **Merge mechanics:** `loadShortcutConfig()` currently takes no arguments. Extend it to accept the resolved worklog root (or read `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`), parse both files, and merge (bundled first, local appended/overriding). The registry already de-duplicates by exact lookup; explicit override handling must be added so duplicate chords do not produce ambiguous lookups (`lookupChordEntry` uses `entries.find` — the first match wins, so local entries must replace bundled ones at the same key, not just be appended).
- **`code_freeze`:** local entries may carry `code_freeze` like bundled ones (parser already supports it); no extra work expected.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `loadShortcutConfig()` merge logic, override handling, optional local-path argument.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — new tests: no-local-file (identical defaults), local adds new chord, local overrides bundled, malformed local entry skipped, per-project resolution.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass the resolved worklog root into `loadShortcutConfig()` (note: `loadShortcutConfig()` is currently called before `configureWorklogTarget()` in `main()`; the call order or plumbing must be adjusted so the local file is found).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the local `shortcuts.json` convention, merge/override rules, and location.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/open.sh` — no change expected (already passes `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`); confirm.

## Related work

- Consuming work item (open_source_llm worklog): **Add 'w' chord to write podcast script in ContextHub worklist plugin (OSL-0MSHFQ51L009IUOS)** — needs this extensibility to add its `w` chord without touching the plugin's bundled shortcuts.
- **Model selection per shortcut (WL-0MSD48ZFC0043AO3)** — added the `model` field to shortcut entries; the local-config extension must preserve it (parser already handles it).
- **Code-freeze shortcut visibility (WL-0MSD81VEL009XHWA)** — added `code_freeze` to shortcut entries; preserved by the same parser.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the project-local file should live at the worklog root (or a documented sub-path there) so the plugin can find it with the already-resolved root; exact name to be confirmed.
- **Risk:** duplicate chord sequences between bundled and local files must be resolved deterministically (local wins) or `entries.find` will silently pick the bundled one. Explicit override logic + tests mitigate.
- **Risk (scope creep):** full user-level config files (per-user, per-host), hot-reload of shortcuts, and UI for editing shortcuts are out of scope; track separately if requested.
- **Compatibility:** projects with no local file must see byte-for-byte identical behavior (guard against regressions).

## Open Questions

- **OPEN QUESTION (eng/producer):** Local file location — `<worklog-root>/shortcuts.json` vs `<worklog-root>/.herdr/shortcuts.json` vs `<worklog-root>/.pi/shortcuts.json`? `.pi/settings.json` already exists at the project root of the consuming repo, so `.pi/` has precedent as a project-config location; `.herdr/` is more plugin-scoped. Recommend one and confirm.
- **OPEN QUESTION (eng):** Should the override key be chord+view only, or also stage? (Chord+view is the minimal key; stage is a visibility filter, not an identity.) Recommend chord+view.

# Intake brief — Keep focus on the Herdr selection list when a shortcut command creates a pane

## Problem statement

Executing a shortcut command from the Herdr work item selection list (worklist pane) creates a new pane — a pi agent pane (for `/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:` commands) or a command-output pane (for `!!`/`!` and plain shell commands). The new pane then takes focus, moving the user away from the selection list mid-workflow. The selection list pane should keep focus so the user can continue browsing and dispatching.

## Users

Herdr Worklog plugin users who drive their work-item workflow from the keyboard-navigable selection list.

- As a user browsing the selection list, I want to run `/skill:implement <id>` and keep my place in the list, so I can queue up more work without re-navigating.
- As a user approving/rejecting items (`!!wl ...` audit commands), I want the command to run in a pane I can inspect later without yanking focus away from the list.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Executing an agent command from the selection list (e.g. `/skill:implement <id>`, `/intake <id>`, `/prompt:...`) opens the pi agent pane WITHOUT moving focus; the selection list keeps focus. Verified by a unit test asserting the dispatch passes `--no-focus` to `send-to-pi.sh`.
- [ ] AC2 — Executing a `!!`/`!`-prefixed command from the selection list (e.g. audit approve/reject, priority updates) opens the command-output pane WITHOUT moving focus. Verified by a unit test asserting `run-in-pane.sh` is dispatched with the no-focus option.
- [ ] AC3 — Executing a plain (unprefixed) shell command from the selection list likewise opens the command-output pane WITHOUT moving focus.
- [ ] AC4 — `run-in-pane.sh` gains a `--no-focus` option (parsed before the command, alongside `--cwd`); when set, the final pane zoom is skipped. Without the flag, current focus behavior is unchanged (backward compatible). Covered by a bash test in `scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh`.
- [ ] AC5 — Out-of-scope behavior unchanged: downtime-worker dispatch panes remain `--no-focus`; the `open-pi-agent` herdr action and `open.sh`/`toggle.sh` keep their current focus behavior; the pane still opens and the command still runs (only focus changes).
- [ ] AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` (command routing / design decisions), and script usage docs.
- [ ] AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Shared launchers `shared/send-to-pi.sh` and `shared/open-pi-agent.sh` are reusable by other plugins/consumer projects (see `shared/README.md`) — their defaults must NOT change; the worklist dispatch passes `--no-focus` explicitly.
- `run-in-pane.sh` must remain backward compatible for existing callers/tests that rely on the current focus behavior.
- Only the focus behavior changes — pane creation, command execution, pane naming, and lifecycle (`--exec` wrapper, stay-open behavior) are untouched.
- The new pane must still open in the resolved project root (`--cwd` arg > `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` > `$PWD`), unchanged.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — the `onCommand` callback routes every selection-list command:
  - `agent` route (`/skill:`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:`): spawns `scripts/send-to-pi.sh` with `buildSendToPiArgs(command, targetCwd, model, paneIdFile)` → `['--cwd', <cwd> [, '--model', <model>] [, '--pane-id-file', <file>], <prompt>]`. No `--no-focus`, so `shared/send-to-pi.sh` (default `focus=true`) zooms the new pane at the end (`pane zoom <np> --on` + `--off`).
  - `pane` route (`!!`/`!`): spawns `scripts/run-in-pane.sh` with `['--cwd', targetCwd, <clean-command>]`.
  - `stdout` route (plain): spawns `scripts/run-in-pane.sh` with `['--cwd', targetCwd, <command>]`.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — splits with `--no-focus`, then unconditionally focuses the new pane at the end:
  ```bash
  "$herdr_bin" pane zoom "$np" --on >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  "$herdr_bin" pane zoom "$np" --off >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  ```
  It has no `--no-focus` option.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — already parses `--no-focus`; the downtime worker already passes it (`buildDowntimePaneArgs` in `src/downtime-worker.ts`).
- Command-send feedback is surfaced via Herdr toast notifications (`notify.ts`), so a no-focus dispatch does not leave the user without feedback.

## Desired change

1. `src/index.ts` — agent route: include `--no-focus` in the `send-to-pi.sh` argument vector (in `buildSendToPiArgs`, which is testable and used only by this dispatch).
2. `scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — add a `--no-focus` flag parsed before the command (alongside `--cwd`); skip the final zoom when set.
3. `src/index.ts` — `pane` and `stdout` routes: pass `--no-focus` to `run-in-pane.sh`.
4. Tests: extend `scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh` (bash) for the `--no-focus` flag; extend `src/index.test.ts` for `buildSendToPiArgs`/dispatch args; confirm `shared/tests/test_scripts.sh` `--no-focus` coverage still applies.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `onCommand` dispatch; add `--no-focus` to agent (`buildSendToPiArgs`) and pane/stdout (`run-in-pane.sh`) spawn args.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — add `--no-focus` option; gate the final zoom on it.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — unit tests for the `--no-focus` argument on both dispatch paths.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh` — bash test that `--no-focus` skips zoom and that omitting it preserves current behavior.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — update command-routing / design-decision docs to state that panes spawned from the selection list open without stealing focus.

## Related work

- WL-0MSF49FMW009M06K (Herdr to consume local LLM in downtime) — established the `--no-focus` pattern for `send-to-pi.sh` (`buildDowntimePaneArgs`); precedent for this change.
- WL-0MSDZ6A6M0014SHB (Resize mode in shared launch scripts) — related shared-launch-script option work.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: the no-focus behavior applies to ALL commands dispatched from the selection list (agent, `!!`/`!`, and plain shell) — confirmed with the operator.
- Assumption: `open-pi-agent` (herdr plugin action) and the downtime worker keep their current behavior — confirmed with the operator (scope question; `open-pi-agent` is an unbound action, not part of the selection-list dispatch).
- Risk (low): users may not immediately notice a command pane opened in the background. Mitigation: toast feedback on dispatch (`notify.ts`) and the pane remains visible; the user can focus it manually with herdr pane navigation.
- Risk (low): adding a `--no-focus` option to `run-in-pane.sh` must not break commands whose first token begins with `--` (only `--cwd`/`--no-focus` are treated as options at the head of the argv; everything else is the command).
- Scope-creep guard: no new settings/configurability requested — hard-code no-focus for the selection-list dispatch. If a toggle is wanted later, track as a separate work item.

The underlying `shared/open-pi-agent.sh` is a reusable utility for other plugins/consumer projects. User then confirmed: "proceed" with assumption (a).
  - Final accepted answer: scope = selection-list dispatch paths only (`send-to-pi.sh` agent route + `run-in-pane.sh` pane/stdout routes). `open-pi-agent.sh`, downtime worker, and `open.sh`/`toggle.sh` unchanged. Source: interactive reply, repo/config inspection.

# Herdr metadata panel: drop duplicate ID row from data section

## Problem statement

In the herdr work item selection list, the metadata panel for the selected item shows the work item ID twice: once in the panel title/header line (`── WL-XXXX ──`) and again as the first row of the metadata data table (`ID  WL-XXXX`). The ID row in the data table is redundant and should be dropped, leaving the ID only in the panel title line.

## Users

Users navigating work items in the herdr selection list (`prefix+l`).

**User story:** As a user browsing work items in the herdr selection list, I want the item ID shown once in the metadata panel so the panel is not redundant and the layout is cleaner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The metadata data table in the herdr metadata panel no longer contains an `ID` row.
- [ ] The metadata panel title/header line (`── WL-XXXX ──`) still shows the item ID.
- [ ] Other metadata rows (Status, Stage, Priority, Title, etc.) render unchanged.
- [ ] The detail view (`formatDetailContent`) behavior is unchanged (it already omits ID/Title from its table since they appear in its header).
- [ ] Tests are added/updated covering the metadata panel output (e.g. the `formatMetadataPanel` describe block in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts`).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Fix should follow the existing pattern used by the detail view (`formatDetailContent` filters `ID`/`Title` out of the table since they are in the header).
- No behavior change to the CLI `show` output or other renderers.

## Existing state

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:

- `formatMetadataPanel` (line ~874) renders the panel header separator `── ${item.id} ──` (line ~891) and then the metadata table from `buildMetaRows(item)` (line ~894).
- `buildMetaRows` (line ~828) unconditionally adds the ID as the first row via `addMeta('ID', item.id)` (line ~835).
- The detail view `formatDetailContent` (line ~969) already filters `ID` and `Title` out of the shared table because both appear in its header: `.filter(([label]) => label !== 'ID' && label !== 'Title')`.

So the metadata panel currently shows the ID in both the header line and the first data row — the inconsistency with the detail view.

## Desired change

Remove the `ID` row from the metadata table rendered in the metadata panel, consistent with how `formatDetailContent` handles it. The header line `── WL-XXXX ──` continues to display the ID. The `Title` row should remain in the metadata panel table since the panel header does not show the title.

Likely approach: in `formatMetadataPanel`, filter the `ID` row from `buildMetaRows(item)` output (e.g. `.filter(([label]) => label !== 'ID')`), mirroring `formatDetailContent`. Alternatively, remove `addMeta('ID', item.id)` from `buildMetaRows` — but note `formatDetailContent` relies on `buildMetaRows` including ID then filtering it, so removing it from the shared builder is also safe as long as tests are updated. Prefer the filter-in-panel approach for minimal blast radius.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatMetadataPanel` (~line 874) and/or `buildMetaRows` (~line 828); the ID row is added at line ~835.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — `formatMetadataPanel — field rendering and scrolling` describe block (~line 896); add a test asserting the data table no longer contains an `ID` row while the header still shows the ID. Existing test `expect(joined).toContain('WL-RICH1')` may still pass via the header, but a negative assertion is needed.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X** — "Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command" (completed): introduced the metadata panel and shared `buildMetaRows` (origin of the ID duplication).
- **WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9** — "Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section" (open): also touches metadata section presentation.
- **WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3** — "Show description preview in herder plugin selection list" (open): related to the selection list metadata area.
- **WL-0MNK7CB3F0008YT3** — "Display work item ID in TUI metadata block" (completed): the deprecated Blessed-TUI predecessor; closed as wont-fix/deprecated — not to be used as a pattern.

(Note: an automated find-related scan flagged WL-0MQCU6R6V008JX62, WL-0MRERDU1J000W1IS, WL-0MM0DBM6I1PHQBFI and README worktree copies; these were false positives from keyword overlap and are not genuinely related — excluded per conservative policy.)

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: "metadata section" refers to the herdr selection-list metadata panel (the only place showing the ID both in a title line and as the first data-table row). The CLI `show` output shows ID once in its metadata table with no separate ID-bearing title line, so it is out of scope.
- Low risk: change is localized; detail view and CLI outputs are unaffected.
- Scope creep: do not change icon consistency (tracked by WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9) or add description previews (tracked by WL-0MSFZKQL700381P3) in this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which metadata section is this about?" — Answer (user): "The metadata section has the ID in the title line and in the first line of the data section. Drop it from the data section." Source: interactive reply. Interpretation: the herdr metadata panel, whose title line is `── <id> ──` and whose first data-table row is `ID  <id>`. Verified against `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (lines 891 and 835).
- Q: "Should the Title row remain in the metadata panel table?" — Assumption (agent, Map): Yes — the panel header shows only the ID, not the title, so Title is not duplicated and stays. Source: code inspection of `formatMetadataPanel` header (line 891 shows only `item.id`). Documented in Desired change.

# Objective

Make the herdr worklist plugin's chord shortcut configuration extensible so a **consumer project** (e.g. the LLM wiki project, open_source_llm) can add its own chord entries and override bundled defaults **without modifying the plugin's bundled `src/shortcuts.json`**.

## Problem statement

Today `loadShortcutConfig()` in `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` reads only `join(__dirname, 'shortcuts.json')` — the bundled defaults. There is no mechanism for a consuming project to add project-specific chords. The consumer project (open_source_llm) needs a project-local `w` chord for podcast-script authoring (tracked as OSL-0MSHFQ51L009IUOS in that project's worklog) and the operator has decided that chord must live in a **project-local shortcuts.json**, never in the plugin's bundled defaults.

## User stories

- As the operator of a consumer project, I want to add a local `shortcuts.json` in my project (resolved from the worklog root) so I can define project-specific chords without forking or editing the plugin bundle.
- As a plugin maintainer, I want bundled defaults to remain the base config so the plugin works out of the box unchanged.

## Expected behaviour

- `loadShortcutConfig()` loads the bundled `src/shortcuts.json` first, then a **project-local `shortcuts.json`** if present.
- **Local-wins override semantics:** a local entry with the same `chord` (and `view`) replaces the bundled default; local entries with new chords are appended. The registry produced must be deterministic and deduplicated.
- The local file location is resolved from the **worklog root** (the plugin already resolves this via `configureWorklogTarget` / `setWorklogDir` in `fetcher.ts`). Exact filename/location (e.g. `<worklog-root>/shortcuts.json`) is decided in this item; document it in `packages/herdr/README.md`.
- Existing bundled entries and all existing dispatch behaviour (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:`, `!!`, `/wl`) are unchanged when no local file exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `loadShortcutConfig()` (or a new loader it delegates to) merges a project-local `shortcuts.json` over the bundled defaults when present; without a local file the registry is byte-identical to today.
- [ ] Local entries override bundled entries with the same chord+view; new local chords are added; the merge is deterministic (no duplicate entries in the registry).
- [ ] The local file is resolved from the worklog root the plugin already knows (`getWorklogDir()`); the exact path is documented.
- [ ] Unit tests in `shortcut-config.test.ts` cover: no local file → bundled only; local addition; local override; malformed local file (falls back to bundled, logs error, never crashes).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated (code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`) describing the local file location and override semantics.
- [ ] Full ContextHub `npm test` suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not change bundled `src/shortcuts.json` entries or their semantics.
- Must not change dispatch behaviour in `worklist.ts` / `index.ts` (this item is config-loading only).
- The worklog root must be available at shortcut-load time — `loadShortcutConfig()` is currently called before `configureWorklogTarget()` in `index.ts`; the load may need to move after root resolution or accept the worklog dir as a parameter.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — loader changes (bundled + local merge, override semantics, validation).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — call site: pass the resolved worklog root to the loader (if ordering changes are needed).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — merge/override/fallback tests.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document local `shortcuts.json` location and semantics.

## Related work

- **Add 'w' chord to write podcast script in ContextHub worklist plugin (OSL-0MSHFQ51L009IUOS)** (open_source_llm worklog) — the consumer of this extensibility; its `w` chord is defined in the project-local shortcuts.json this item enables. Dependency edge cannot be recorded via `wl dep` (cross-worklog); tracked via description cross-references on both items.
- **Chord shortcut key system for Pi extension (WL-0MQDZBKO9003CD8K)** — the original chord system this extends.
- **Make shortcuts.json path resolution robust against build output restructuring (WL-0MQDR5IZZ001WCGP)** — prior path-resolution work in this area.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: a single flat local `shortcuts.json` array (same schema as bundled) is sufficient; no per-stage local files or config DSLs are needed. If a consumer needs richer overrides later, track as a separate item.
- Risk: local entries must be validated with the same `parseShortcutEntry` rules; an invalid local entry should be logged and skipped (never crash the plugin).
- Risk (scope creep): per-user keybindings, per-view overrides beyond the existing schema, and a `--no-shortcuts` toggle are out of scope; track separately if requested.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRNW3CZY006K0LD** – [test-failure] shortcut-config.test.ts:loadShortcutConfig > loads valid entries from shortcuts.json — failing test (completed)
- **WL-0MQMFER5N003N1LL** – Chord-based stage filter shortcuts in TUI (completed)
- **WL-0MNX8MASB007TADZ** – Add tests for dialog focus cycling and multiline update comment (completed)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: accept, acceptance, add, added, addition (+128 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — matched: accept, acceptance, add, already, appended (+122 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: accept, acceptance, add, added, addition (+116 more)

# Tests: Related Docs row, detail ToC and open-in-viewer

## Summary

Unit tests for the `Related Docs` metadata row, the detail-view Table of Contents (ToC), and the open-in-viewer behavior described in WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29. Written first (test-first, expected red), then made green by the sibling implementation features `Add Related Docs metadata row` and `Detail view ToC for Related Docs`.

## Expected behaviour under test

- `buildMetaRows` emits a `Related Docs` row listing every `.md` path from the item's `Key Files:` section in both the list-mode metadata panel (`formatMetadataPanel`) and the detail-view metadata table (`formatDetailContent`); the row is omitted when there are no `.md` Key Files.
- The detail view renders a ToC at the top listing the Related Docs with a focus indicator; arrow/j/k navigate; Enter renders the selected doc; navigating past the end of the ToC transfers focus to document scrolling; the ToC stays visible while the document scrolls.
- Opening a listed document renders that specific file's content (not just the first one); missing/unreadable files fail open; paths resolve against the resolved worklog root, never `process.cwd()` (regression coverage for WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `buildMetaRows` tests cover: `Related Docs` row lists every `.md` path from `Key Files:` (via `extractFilePaths` + `.md` filter), joined with the compact delimiter, in both `formatMetadataPanel` and `formatDetailContent` output.
2. Row omitted when the item has no `.md` files in `Key Files:` (or no `Key Files:` section at all) — asserted for both the metadata panel and the detail table.
3. Mixed `Key Files` lists (`.ts`/`.json`/`.md`): only `.md` paths appear in the `Related Docs` row; non-markdown paths are excluded.
4. Detail-view ToC tests: ToC at the top of the detail view lists all Related Docs; a focus indicator marks the selected entry; arrow keys and j/k move selection within the ToC; navigating past the last entry transfers focus to document scrolling and navigating up past the top returns focus to the ToC; the ToC remains visible while the viewed document scrolls.
5. Open-in-viewer tests: activating a ToC entry renders that specific file's content via `renderMarkdownViewer` (supersedes the auto-first-file render for the selected doc; auto-render of the first file remains the initial default); unreadable/missing files fail open without crashing; path resolution uses the resolved worklog root (`HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` / `resolveKeyFilePath`) — a regression test asserting `process.cwd()` is never used.
6. All tests pass as part of the full project test suite once implementation lands (they may be red at creation time — test-first).

## Implementation approach

- Add/extend `describe` blocks in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (and `grouping.test.ts` if an `extractMdPaths` helper is introduced).
- Reuse existing test fixtures (`makeItem`, `makeRichItem`) and the `TERM_80x24`/`panelHeight` helpers already used by the metadata-panel tests.
- Follow the existing pattern of asserting on joined output lines from `formatMetadataPanel`/`formatDetailContent`.

## Related work

- Parent: WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 (Herdr plugin: add Related Docs row to metadata section listing .md Key Files (openable in the markdown viewer))

# Detail view ToC for Related Docs

## Summary

The detail view gains a persistent Table of Contents (ToC) at the top listing the selected item's Related Docs (the `.md` Key Files surfaced by the `Related Docs` metadata row). Arrow keys and j/k navigate the ToC; Enter renders the selected document in the markdown viewer. The ToC stays visible on all renders; navigating past the end of the ToC moves focus to scrolling the viewed document, and navigating up past the top returns to the ToC.

## Expected behaviour

- Opening a detail view for an item with `.md` Key Files shows a ToC (e.g. numbered entries) at the top, with a focus indicator on the selected entry. The first `.md` file is rendered by default (existing auto-render behavior preserved).
- `↑`/`↓` and j/k move the ToC selection. Enter renders the selected document's content via `renderMarkdownViewer`.
- Below the last ToC entry, `↓`/j moves focus into the document scroll area (existing detail scroll keys apply there); `↑`/k at the top of the document returns focus to the ToC. The ToC remains pinned/visible while the document scrolls.
- Items with no `.md` Key Files render the detail view exactly as today (no ToC).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the item has at least one `.md` Key File, the detail view renders a ToC at the top listing every Related Doc with a focus indicator on the selected entry; no ToC is rendered when there are no `.md` Key Files.
2. Arrow keys (↑/↓) and j/k navigate the ToC entries; selection clamps to the list bounds.
3. Enter on a ToC entry renders that file's content in the markdown viewer via `renderMarkdownViewer` (supersedes the auto-first-file render for the selected doc; auto-render of the first file remains the initial default).
4. The ToC stays visible on all renders: while the viewed document scrolls, the ToC remains pinned at the top of the detail view.
5. Navigating past the last ToC entry transfers focus to document scrolling; navigating up past the top of the document returns focus to the ToC. Esc/back and `q` exit the detail view as they do today.
6. Path resolution uses the resolved worklog root via `readKeyFile`/`resolveKeyFilePath` (never `process.cwd()`); unreadable or missing files fail open (detail view falls back to the raw description, no crash).
7. Existing detail keys keep working in the appropriate focus mode (j/k scroll, g/G top/bottom, pgup/pgdn, esc/q); the detail scroll model is reconciled with the pinned ToC.

## Implementation approach

- Add ToC/focus state to the detail view (e.g. `detailToCIndex` / a focus-mode flag alongside `detailScrollOffset`); render the ToC as a pinned header in `formatDetailContent` (or a new helper) with the document region below it.
- Reuse `extractFilePaths` (or the new `extractMdPaths` from the row feature) to build the ToC entries, and `readKeyFile`/`resolveKeyFilePath` for rendering.
- Reconcile the existing single-scroll detail model: the ToC is pinned; the document area scrolls independently.
- Coordinate with `Tests: Related Docs row, detail ToC and open-in-viewer` for expected test names/behavior.

## Related work

- Parent: WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 (Herdr plugin: add Related Docs row to metadata section listing .md Key Files (openable in the markdown viewer))
- Prereqs: `Tests: Related Docs row, detail ToC and open-in-viewer`; `Add Related Docs metadata row`

Extend loadShortcutConfig() in packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts to accept an optional worklog root and merge <worklog-root>/shortcuts.json over the bundled defaults with local-wins override semantics. Bundled defaults remain the base; no bundled entries change.

- Merge via a Map keyed by view+chord (bundled first, then local entries overwrite/add), preserving bundled order for untouched entries; output a deduplicated array.

# Intake Brief: Create `npm run install` routine for install steps and add `install:plugin` rule

## Problem statement

Install steps for the Worklog repo are currently scattered: the herdr plugin install (link plugin + insert `prefix+l` keybinding) runs automatically via the root `postbuild` hook on every `npm run build`, while the pi-extension install exists as a separate manual rule (`install:pi-extension`). There is no single, discoverable `npm run install` routine that performs all install steps, so developers cannot install all integrations with one command and the build doubles as an installer.

## Users

- **Developers installing the Worklog repo from source** who want a single `npm run install` command that performs all install steps (herdr plugin + pi extension), while `npm run build` keeps its current auto-install behaviour.
- **User story:** "As a developer working on the Worklog repo, when I run `npm run install`, I want the herdr plugin linked/keybound and the pi extension installed in one step, so I don't have to remember each install rule — while `npm run build` keeps working exactly as before."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Root `package.json` gains an `install` script that chains the install rules in order, e.g. `"install": "npm run install:plugin && npm run install:pi-extension"`.
2. Root `package.json` gains an `install:plugin` script invoking the existing install script, e.g. `"install:plugin": "bash ./scripts/install-herdr.sh"`.
3. The existing `postbuild` hook (`bash ./scripts/install-herdr.sh`) and the `install:pi-extension` rule are unchanged — `npm run build` still auto-installs the herdr plugin as today (user confirmed: keep).
4. `npm run install` completes successfully (exit 0) in an environment without `herdr` on PATH — the herdr step warns and continues, the pi-extension step completes (verified by running `npm run install` with herdr absent).
5. Re-running `npm run install` is idempotent — no duplicate keybindings and no duplicate links (existing `install-herdr.sh` and `install-pi-extension.sh` behaviour).
6. Unit tests cover the new script wiring — e.g. `tests/scripts/package-scripts.test.ts` reads root `package.json` and asserts `install` chains `install:plugin` then `install:pi-extension`, and `install:plugin` targets `scripts/install-herdr.sh` (matching the `tests/scripts/` convention).
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (root `README.md` Pi agent plugin section and `packages/herdr/README.md` mention the `npm run install` routine as an alternative to `npm run build`).
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Constraints

- `install` is a reserved npm lifecycle script name: in addition to `npm run install`, it auto-runs during `npm install` / `npm ci` in the project (and during a global install of the package). Both chained rules are already safe in such contexts (herdr-missing → warn exit 0; pi-extension symlink creation is idempotent). Use `--ignore-scripts` to opt out of lifecycle auto-runs if ever needed.
- Keep `postbuild` and `install:pi-extension` unchanged (user Q1/Q3 answers) — the diff is additive for the new `install`/`install:plugin` rules.
- No changes to `scripts/install-herdr.sh` or `scripts/install-pi-extension.sh` themselves unless implementation finds otherwise.
- Do not clutter repo root with planning documents.

## Existing state

- `package.json` scripts: `"build": "npm run build:shared && tsc && node ./scripts/generate-version.cjs"`, `"postbuild": "bash ./scripts/install-herdr.sh"`, `"install:pi-extension": "bash ./scripts/install-pi-extension.sh"`.
- `scripts/install-herdr.sh` — idempotent herdr installer (links `worklog-selection-list` plugin, inserts/migrates the `prefix+l` keybinding, warns-not-fails when herdr is absent); invoked by `postbuild`.
- `scripts/install-pi-extension.sh` — creates the `~/.pi/agent/extensions/worklog` symlink; invoked by `install:pi-extension`.
- `README.md` § "Pi agent plugin" documents `npm run install:pi-extension`; `packages/herdr/README.md` § "From source (development)" documents auto-install via `npm run build`.
- No `install` script exists today; no tests reference the install rules.

## Desired change

1. **`package.json`** — add two scripts (additive; nothing removed):
   - `"install": "npm run install:plugin && npm run install:pi-extension"`
   - `"install:plugin": "bash ./scripts/install-herdr.sh"`
   - `postbuild` and `install:pi-extension` stay exactly as they are.
2. **Tests** — new test file (e.g. `tests/scripts/package-scripts.test.ts`) asserting the script definitions and the `install` chaining order, following the existing `tests/scripts/` convention.
3. **Docs** — mention the `npm run install` routine in root `README.md` (Pi agent plugin section) and `packages/herdr/README.md` (as an alternative to `npm run build` for the herdr install); keep existing instructions intact.

**Key Files:**

- `./package.json` — Add `install` and `install:plugin` scripts (postbuild/install:pi-extension unchanged).
- `tests/scripts/package-scripts.test.ts` — New tests asserting the install-rule wiring (location subject to confirmation during /plan, matching `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` / `install-pi-extension.test.ts` precedent).
- `README.md` — Pi agent plugin section: mention `npm run install` routine.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Installation section: mention `npm run install` as an alternative to `npm run build` for the herdr install.

## Related work

- WL-0MSHZR0J2000Q9SW — this item (seed: "Create npm run install routine … add install:plugin rule. Priority: high.").
- WL-0MSAPMGLS0034BTR — "Install script: insert herdr shortcut key into herdr config (runs on npm run build)" (completed): created `scripts/install-herdr.sh` and the `postbuild` wiring; context for the herdr install step this item consolidates.
- WL-0MSG6ODD5002X2OF — "Wire postbuild hook and update docs" (completed): added `"postbuild": "bash ./scripts/install-herdr.sh"`; docs updated there must be kept consistent.
- WL-0MSG6OA2K003GY27 — "Implement install-herdr.sh script" (completed): the script `install:plugin` will invoke.
- `scripts/install-pi-extension.sh` / `install:pi-extension` — existing install rule chained by the new `install` routine.
- README.md § "Pi agent plugin", packages/herdr/README.md § "From source (development)" — docs that reference the install rules.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (lifecycle side-effect):** naming the routine `install` makes npm auto-run it on `npm install`/`npm ci` in the repo (and on global/local package installs), which will touch the user's herdr config and `~/.pi/agent/extensions`. Mitigation: both chained scripts are idempotent and warn-not-fail, so no failures; the behavior is intentional per the requested "npm run install" naming and is documented in the brief so it can be vetoed at review.
- **Risk:** `npm run install` runs `install:pi-extension` which writes a symlink under `$HOME/.pi`; in CI that is a harmless ephemeral side effect (verified: CI uses `npm ci`, herdr absent, both scripts exit 0).
- **Assumption:** `install` chains exactly the two existing rules in the order `install:plugin` then `install:pi-extension` (user Q2: "all").
- **Assumption:** `install:plugin` runs the existing `scripts/install-herdr.sh` (user Q3: "existing"); no new install logic.
- **Assumption:** `postbuild` stays as-is (user Q1: "keep") — `npm run build` keeps auto-installing the herdr plugin.
- **Scope-creep risk:** no changes to the install scripts themselves, no new install steps, no changes to build output — purely additive npm script wiring + tests + docs. Any additional install concerns should be separate work items.

### Related work (automated report)

Automated findings from find_related (WL-0MSHZR0J2000Q9SW): WL-0MQFB8N990056T8P (test-failure: controller-watch re-renders), WL-0MSB445R1004PM3I (Impl: idle-gated auto-refresh/auto-sync in browse widget), WL-0MKXTCQZM1O8YCNH (Core FTS Index) — all keyword matches on generic terms (build/install/add/plugin); weak relevance, informational only. Repo file matches were the draft itself and stale worktree copies of `packages/herdr/README.md`; full report persisted at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MSHZR0J2000Q9SW.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the `postbuild` hook (and thus the herdr install) be removed from `npm run build` so installs only run via the new `npm run install` (build stays pure), or should `npm run build` keep auto-installing as today?" — Answer (user): "keep" — keep the `postbuild` hook; `npm run build` continues to auto-install the herdr plugin. Source: interactive reply (2026-08-07).
- Q: "Should `npm run install` chain all install rules — i.e. `install:plugin` (herdr, from postbuild) plus `install:pi-extension` (existing rule) — or only the herdr/plugin install?" — Answer (user): "all" — `npm run install` chains all install rules: `install:plugin` then `install:pi-extension`. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should `install:plugin` run the existing `install-herdr.sh` script (link plugin + insert keybinding), or is something else expected (e.g. a different plugin, or it should also cover the pi extension)?" — Answer (user): "existing" — `install:plugin` runs the existing `scripts/install-herdr.sh`. Source: interactive reply.
- OPEN QUESTION: none — the npm `install` lifecycle auto-run side-effect (runs on `npm ci`/`npm install`) is documented as a risk/assumption above; flag for user veto at review if unintended.

# Herdr selection list: sort by priority first, then stage (WL-0MSI1LVTJ001M9EY)

## Problem statement

The work item selection list in the Herdr Worklog plugin does not put priority first: a high-priority `in_progress` item lands in the "Other" section while a medium-priority `plan_complete` item sits in an earlier "Group N" section, so the most important work is not at the top. The list should be sorted by priority first, then by stage.

## Users

- **Herdr users** (human and AI agents) who browse the work item selection list and expect the highest-priority work to appear first.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, I want the highest-priority work items to appear at the top of the selection list, so I can see what matters most without scanning.
- As a Herdr user, I want items of equal priority ordered by their workflow stage, so the list stays predictable and mirrors the work item's recorded lifecycle.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Priority is the primary sort key.** Items in the selection list sort by priority in descending order: `critical` → `high` → `medium` → `low` (matching the existing priority ranking `critical=4 > high=3 > medium=2 > low=1` in `src/commands/helpers.ts`). Items with unknown/empty priority sort as `medium` (existing `DEFAULT_PRIORITY` convention).
2. **Stage is the secondary sort key.** Within the same priority, items sort by stage in the order recorded in the work item record / default config (`src/config.ts`): `idea` → `intake_complete` → `plan_complete` → `in_progress` → `in_review` → `done`. Unknown stages sort after known ones. Item `id` is the deterministic tie-break.
3. **Section headers follow priority order.** The existing group-header rendering (`── <label> ──`) is preserved, with one section per priority bucket ordered Critical → High → Medium → Low. No stage sub-headers are rendered (within-bucket stage order is implicit, matching current behavior).
4. **Applies to all rendered lists.** The ordering applies to every list rendered by the plugin: the default worklist, stage-filtered views (e.g. `/wl idea`, `/wl in_review`), expanded child lists, and search results when rendered in-TUI. Implementation may reuse one shared comparator across list types.
5. **Smart-selection guarantee preserved.** All critical items and all `completed`/`in_review` items remain always visible regardless of the `browseItemCount` setting (WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B).
6. **Tests.** Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` (plus any grouping-order assertions in `worklist.test.ts` and `md-viewer.test.ts`) cover the new priority→stage ordering, including unknown priority/stage fallbacks and the smart-selection merge path.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the plugin README's "Stage grouping" feature description, and any relevant docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Scope is the **Herdr plugin selection list only**. Do not change the `wl` CLI ordering, the core grouping in `src/commands/grouping.ts`, or the Pi TUI extension's mirrored copy (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/grouping.ts`) unless explicitly requested. The mirrored copies must remain in sync for whatever is changed (the Herdr copy is intentionally duplicated with zero npm deps — decision Q2c in WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B).
- The plugin keeps using the existing `wl` CLI as its data source; no new fetch paths or `wl` flags are introduced.
- `stage=done` items remain excluded from the default list (WL-0MS94VAII00054L9); child items remain hidden from top-level lists (WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR).
- No new UI features (search-as-a-list, new filters) are introduced by this work item.

## Existing state

- The Herdr worklist fetches via `fetchNextItems(count)` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`): `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` merged with mandatory subsets (`wl list --priority critical`, `wl list --status completed --stage in_review`), then `selectWorkItems` (critical → reviews → others) and `regroupWorkItems`.
- `regroupWorkItems` (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`) calls `assignItemGroups`, which currently produces groups in this order: **Critical Group N** (critical, file-path partitioned) → **Group N** (plan_complete + intake_complete, file-path partitioned) → **Idea** → **Other** → **In Review** (last). Within a group, `compareGroupableItems` sorts by stage sub-order (plan_complete → intake_complete → remaining) then priority (high → medium → low) then id.
- Net effect today: a high-priority `in_progress` item is in the "Other" section (4th), while a medium-priority `plan_complete` item is in "Group N" (2nd) — priority is not the primary ordering.
- Stage filters (`/wl <stage>`, worklist.ts) filter the fetched list client-side, so they inherit whatever order the fetched list has. The `s` key inserts a `!!wl search <search_term>` command dispatched to an external pane; there is no in-TUI search results list today.

## Desired change

- Rework `assignItemGroups` / `regroupWorkItems` / `compareGroupableItems` in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` so the group order is priority-first: one section per priority bucket (Critical → High → Medium → Low), and within each bucket items sort by stage (workflow order: idea → intake_complete → plan_complete → in_progress → in_review → done) then id.
- `selectWorkItems` in `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` keeps its always-show guarantee; its pre-group ordering is superseded by the regroup ordering, so it can be simplified to a stable sort if convenient.
- Because the sort lives at the display-prep step (regrouping), stage-filtered views and any other rendered list inherit it automatically.
- Update the grouping tests and README "Stage grouping" description to match.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — Rework `assignItemGroups` (priority-bucket group order), `compareGroupableItems` (priority → stage → id), and `regroupWorkItems` (unchanged contract, new ordering).
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — Preserve the mandatory-set guarantee; adjust ordering contract only as needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — Update/expand tests for group order, within-group stage order, and unknown priority/stage fallbacks.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Update any assertions that depend on group labels/order in rendered lists.
- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.test.ts` — Update `regroupWorkItems` assertions if affected.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Update the "Stage grouping" feature description to reflect priority-first ordering.

## Related work

- **Create a work item selection list in Herdr (WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP)** [completed] — Parent feature that introduced the selection list this change modifies.
- **Selection list must always show all completed/in_review and critical items regardless of browseItemCount setting (WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B)** [completed] — Defines the smart-selection guarantee (AC 5) and the per-TUI duplication decision.
- **Rewrite assignItemGroups + next.ts ordering (WL-0MSAKPVR9005B6XJ)** [completed] — Authored the current group ordering algorithm this work item reorders.
- **Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order) (WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW)** [completed] — Introduced `regroupWorkItems`/`assignItemGroups`; the group-order logic this change reorders.
- **Exclude stage=done items from default selection lists (both TUIs) (WL-0MS94VAII00054L9)** [completed] — The done-exclusion this change must preserve.
- **Hide child work items from top-level selection lists (Pi and Herdr) (WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR)** [completed] — Root-only behavior this change must preserve.
- **Show plugin version in Herdr work item selection list (WL-0MSGKEBFU004T3N3)** [open] — Another open change to the same selection list; coordinate to avoid merge conflicts in `worklist.ts`/tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption: "sort-order in the work item record"** (user's answer to the stage-order question) means the canonical stage order recorded in the work item config: `idea` → `intake_complete` → `plan_complete` → `in_progress` → `in_review` → `done` (`src/config.ts` defaults).
- **Assumption: smart-selection guarantee stays** (confirmed with the user; AC 5).
- **Assumption: no in-TUI search list exists today** — search is dispatched via `!!wl search <term>`; AC 4 covers "when rendered in-TUI" so future search rendering inherits the sort.
- **Risk: file-path conflict partitioning may be dropped.** The current "Critical Group N" / "Group N" labels partition by file-path conflicts (groups items touching the same files for agent sessions). Priority-bucket sections may drop this partitioning. Preserve the partitioning within buckets if it is still wanted; otherwise document the removal. Flag for implementer review.
- **Risk: algorithm duplication.** `grouping.ts` logic is mirrored in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/grouping.ts` and `src/commands/grouping.ts`. Changing only the Herdr copy creates divergence; a follow-up to align the Pi TUI list is a candidate separate work item (scope-creep guard).
- **Scope-creep guard:** Do not change `wl` CLI ordering, add new `wl` flags, or add new plugin UI features. Record extra opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which selection lists should get the new sort? (A) Default worklist only, (B) Default + stage-filtered, (C) All lists including search results" — Answer (user): **C — All lists including search results**. Source: interactive reply. Note: search is currently dispatched externally (`!!wl search <term>`), so in practice this means the default worklist, stage-filtered views, and any list the plugin renders (search results if rendered in-TUI later). AC 4 captures this.
- Q2: "Within the same priority, what order should stages appear? (A) Workflow order, (B) Most-advanced-first, (C) No preference" — Answer (user): **"sort-order in the work item record"**. Research: the canonical stage order recorded in the work item record defaults (`src/config.ts` stages) is `idea` → `intake_complete` → `plan_complete` → `in_progress` → `in_review` → `done`. Final accepted answer: workflow order as recorded in the record (AC 2).
- Q3: "With priority-first sorting, should the list (A) keep section headers reordered into priority buckets, (B) drop group headers for a flat list, (C) keep current group structure and only fix within-group sort?" — Answer (user): **A — keep section headers, priority buckets first** (Critical → High → Medium → Low sections). Source: interactive reply. AC 3.
- Follow-up (assumption stated, no objection): "the smart-selection guarantee (critical + completed/in_review always shown) should be preserved" — Answer: no objection; captured as AC 5.
- Note: `find-related` was run (WL-0MSI1LVTJ001M9EY). Its automated report returned mostly false positives: its repo-file scan resolved to the wrong repository (SorraAgents `skill/audit/...` and tmp files) and the three ranked items are unrelated (a TUI test-failure, a Local Proxy lease item, and a Pi TUI filter bug). None were added to the curated Related work section per the conservative policy; the curated section above is authoritative.

# Detail view ToC overflows pane — first lines scroll off the top of the screen

## Problem statement

In the Herdr plugin's work-item detail view, when an item has a `Related Docs` Table of Contents (ToC) (i.e. ≥1 `.md` Key File), the rendered output exceeds the pane height: the header (id/title) and the first ToC lines scroll off the top of the screen, so the ToC is not entirely visible. The ToC is also rendered twice and the item header is dropped entirely.

## Users

- **Herdr users** viewing a work item's detail view in the plugin pane, who need the item header and the full `Related Docs` ToC visible at the top of the pane while the metadata/description/document body scrolls beneath.

### Example User Stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to see the item id, title, and the complete Related Docs ToC when I open a work item's detail view, so nothing important is cut off at the top of the screen.
- As a Herdr user, I want the ToC to stay pinned while I scroll the document, so I can always see which documents are linked to the item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When an item has a ToC (≥1 `.md` Key File), the detail view shows the header (id, title, separator) and the **full** ToC at the top of the pane at scroll 0 — no lines cut off. The ToC is rendered **exactly once** (no duplication), and the item header is present.
2. Detail-view output never exceeds the pane: `formatDetailView` returns at most `viewportHeight` lines, and the full renderer (`createListRenderer` detail mode) returns at most `rows - 1` lines — the line-count invariant from WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO holds for detail mode with a ToC present.
3. The header + ToC block stays **pinned** at the top while the body (metadata table, description, md viewer) scrolls beneath it; scrolling is limited to the body region (viewport height minus the pinned block height), and `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` clamps against the same reduced body viewport. No dead/blank region at the bottom when fully scrolled.
4. Items **without** `.md` Key Files (no ToC) keep the existing full-scroll behavior unchanged (regression check — no behavior change for the no-ToC path).
5. Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover: line-count invariant for detail mode with ToC (renderer ≤ `rows - 1`; `formatDetailView` ≤ `viewportHeight`), header + ToC fully visible at scroll 0, ToC not duplicated, pinned-ToC scroll regression (existing `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'` test kept green/updated), and no-ToC behavior unchanged.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant README/docs entries describing the detail-view ToC layout (`packages/herdr/README.md`).
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Preserve the pinned-ToC design from WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I / WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29: the ToC stays visible on all renders; only the body below it scrolls.
- Respect the line-count invariant established in WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO: the renderer must never emit more than `rows - 1` lines, otherwise the terminal scrolls the top of the output off the pane.
- Surgical change: do not alter scrolling behavior for items without a ToC (the pre-existing full-scroll path).
- No new dependencies; reuse the existing `formatDetailToC` / `formatDetailContent` helpers.

## Existing state

- `formatDetailView` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, ~line 1223) builds the detail output as `[...tocLines, ...bodyLines.slice(safeOffset, safeOffset + viewportHeight)]` where `bodyLines = allLines.slice(tocLines.length)`.
- The slicing assumes the ToC occupies the first `tocLines.length` lines of `allLines`, but `formatDetailContent` emits the header first (blank, id, title, separator = 4 lines) and the ToC **after** it. Consequences (verified by reproduction): (a) the header is dropped from the output, (b) the ToC is duplicated (once from `tocLines`, once inside `bodyLines`), (c) total output = `viewportHeight + tocLines.length` lines, which overflows the pane (`viewportHeight = rows - 1` in the renderer). Reproduction: `formatDetailView(item, 80, 0, 20)` with a 2-entry ToC returns 26 lines; the renderer on a 24-row terminal emits 29 lines (max allowed 23).
- Regression introduced in commit `76a52c9f` (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I, "Implementation complete").
- `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` (~line 496) computes `maxScroll` against the full `viewportHeight` instead of the body region, so clamping is also wrong for the pinned layout.
- The existing test `'keeps the ToC pinned at the top while the document scrolls'` only asserts the ToC appears in the first 8 lines — it never checks the total line count, so it passes despite the overflow.

## Desired change

1. In `formatDetailView`, compute a **pinned block** = header (4 lines: blank, id, title, separator) + `tocLines`; the scrollable **body** = `allLines.slice(pinnedHeight)`; the **body viewport** = `max(1, viewportHeight - pinnedHeight)`; `maxScroll = max(0, bodyLines.length - bodyViewport)`. Render `[...pinned, ...bodyLines.slice(safeOffset, safeOffset + bodyViewport)]` and update the scroll-indicator percentage math to use `bodyViewport`.
2. Keep the no-ToC path (`tocLines.length === 0`) identical to the pre-ToC behavior (whole content scrolls, header included) to avoid scope creep.
3. Update `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` to clamp against the reduced body viewport (subtract the pinned height) so `j`/`G` behave consistently with the renderer.
4. Optionally introduce a named constant (e.g. `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES = 4`) documenting the fixed header shape so the slicing is self-explanatory.
5. Add/extend unit tests per AC5; update `packages/herdr/README.md` if it describes the detail-view layout.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatDetailView` pinned header+ToC slicing and body-viewport math; `WorkItemListState.detailScrollDown` clamp; optional header-lines constant.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — line-count invariant tests for detail mode with ToC, header/ToC visibility at scroll 0, no-duplication check, no-ToC regression, updated pinned-ToC test.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the pinned header + ToC detail-view layout if it describes the ToC behavior.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Header-shape fragility:** the fix relies on the header being exactly 4 lines (blank, id, title, separator). Mitigate by introducing a named `DETAIL_HEADER_LINES` constant next to `formatDetailContent` and by an AC1 test asserting the header is visible at scroll 0.
- **No-ToC regression:** altering `formatDetailView` slicing could accidentally change the full-scroll path for items without `.md` Key Files. Mitigate with AC4 regression test asserting the no-ToC path is unchanged.
- **Viewport-height mismatch:** the state class uses `rows - 4` while the renderer uses `rows - 1`; today the renderer's clamp absorbs the difference. The fix must subtract the pinned height consistently in both `formatDetailView` and `detailScrollDown` so `j`/`G` and the on-screen clamp agree.
- **Scope creep:** pinning the header for ALL items (even without a ToC) is deliberately out of scope — it is a UX change beyond the reported bug. Recorded as an assumption; can be tracked as a separate work item if desired.
- **Assumption:** the fix pins header + ToC together (the header sits above the ToC in the content stream, so pinning the ToC keeps the header visible) and scrolls only the body (metadata/description/md viewer) beneath — faithful to the pinned-ToC design intent (WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 AC3) and the user's expectation that the first lines be visible.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I` (completed) — "Herdr: detail-view ToC for Related Docs (arrow/j/k navigate, Enter renders)" — the pinned-ToC implementation that introduced this regression (commit `76a52c9f`).
- `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` (completed) — "Herdr plugin: add Related Docs row to metadata section listing .md Key Files (openable in the markdown viewer)" — defines the pinned-ToC design intent.
- `WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO` (completed) — "Herdr: pane line-count invariant (rows - 1)" — the invariant the detail view now violates.
- `WL-0MS31WX9C008FIQR` (completed) — "Full scrollable detail view" — original detail-view scrolling design (whole content scrolls).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview questions were required for this intake.

- The seed report ("The table of contents on the detail view of work items is not entirely visible — the first few lines are off the top of the screen") combined with repository analysis was conclusive: the root cause was located by inspection of `formatDetailView`/`formatDetailContent` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, confirmed by a reproduction test (26 lines emitted for a 20-line viewport; 29 lines for a 24-row terminal vs. the 23-line invariant), and pinned to the regression commit `76a52c9f` (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I) via `git log -S`.
- Assumption (documented, user can override): the fix pins the **header + ToC** block at the top of the detail view (the header is above the ToC in the content stream, so pinning the ToC necessarily keeps the header visible) while the body scrolls beneath — this is the faithful reading of the pinned-ToC design intent in WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 AC3 ("The ToC stays visible on all renders") and the user's expectation that the first lines be visible.
- Assumption (documented, user can override): items **without** `.md` Key Files keep the existing full-scroll behavior unchanged (surgical scope).

---

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKXJPCDI1FLYDB1** – Prompt input box must resize on word wrap (completed)
- **WL-0MRMCO4WX0073W30** – Arbitrary-depth chords in detail view (completed)

### Repository file matches

- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: first, items, medium, off, priority (+7 more)

# Follow-up: drag-to-scroll in Herdr worklist (WL-0MSI72S0Y0060BRK)

## Problem statement

The Herdr work item selection list already supports click/tap selection, double-click detail, and wheel/touch-scroll navigation, but pointer **drag** gestures (touch drag on touch devices, click-drag on desktop) do nothing: motion with a button held is currently only used to drive the hover tooltip, so users cannot "grab" the content and fling the list or detail view the way they expect in a pointer-first terminal. This item adds drag-to-scroll for the list and detail views without disturbing the keyboard, click, wheel, or hover behaviours delivered by the parent (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ).

discovered-from:WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ

## Users

- **Touch-device users** (tablets, touch laptops, convertible terminals) who have no natural wheel and expect a finger drag to move the list/detail content.
- **Herdr users** who drag the content up/down to browse quickly instead of counting wheel notches or arrow-key presses.
- **Human reviewers/auditors** scanning long lists or long descriptions who want direct-manipulation scrolling.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to drag the list up/down with my finger or pointer so the visible window follows my movement and the selection stays where it was.
- As a Herdr user, I want to drag inside the detail view so the description scrolls without using keys or the wheel.
- As a Herdr user, I want a click (press + release without moving) to keep selecting rows exactly as before, so drag support never turns my clicks into scrolls or vice versa.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **List drag-to-scroll**: with the left button (or touch contact) held over the list area, vertical pointer movement past a small threshold scrolls the list proportionally to the movement, snapped to whole rows; the **selection (`selectedIndex`) does not change** as a result of the drag. Verified by unit tests on the pure drag mapper plus the state scroll method.
2. **Detail drag-to-scroll**: the same gesture inside the detail view scrolls the detail content (`detailScrollOffset`) proportionally to vertical movement (1 terminal row ≈ 1 line), clamped to the content bounds, in both detail focus states (mirroring the existing wheel `scroll-detail-up`/`scroll-detail-down` mapping). Verified by unit test.
3. **Drag never becomes a click / click never becomes a drag**: a press that crosses the drag threshold does not select a row or open the detail view, and its release triggers no action; a press–release that never crosses the threshold still selects (or double-clicks) exactly as today. Verified by unit test.
4. **Hover/drag separation**: button-less motion continues to drive the hover tooltip (`hover-row`/`hover-none`); left-button-held motion drives drag-to-scroll. Verified by unit test.
5. **Threshold and clamping**: drags shorter than the threshold are inert; drags beyond the content bounds clamp at 0 / max without overscroll and without moving the selection. Verified by unit test.
6. **No regression**: all existing keyboard and mouse behaviours from WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ remain intact; the existing `handleKeypress` and `worklist-mouse` suites pass unchanged except for the deliberate motion-branch reinterpretation.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, the package README, and `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` (mouse/touch notes).
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Additive** to the existing SGR mouse path: click/tap, double-click, wheel, filter-tap, hover tooltip, Alt+m toggle, and keyboard navigation must keep working.
- Mouse coordinates from SGR reporting are **1-based terminal cells** (not pixels), so the drag threshold is expressed in cells (default 1 row) and movement is row-granular by nature.
- Must respect the drag-motion guard established by the parent (button & 32 motion bit is never allowed to jump the selection); drag is the *only* sanctioned consumer of held-button motion.
- Drag in **filter mode** is out of scope (the filter prompt is a single options row; wheel is already ignored there). Metadata-panel drag is out of scope.
- Fail-soft: terminals without SGR reporting simply never send motion; keyboard remains fully usable.
- No new runtime dependencies; the drag logic is pure and unit-testable, mirroring `mapMouseToAction`.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (~6,600 lines) owns the worklist TUI. `mapMouseToAction` (≈line 3317) currently returns `{ type: 'hover-row' | 'hover-none' }` for **all** motion events (`button & 32`) in list mode and `null` in detail/filter mode — motion never scrolls.
- `parseMouseEvent` / `consumeMouseChunk` (≈line 3130+) expose the raw SGR button code and handle split chunks; `handleMouseInput` (≈line 3406) contains the single `onData` mouse dispatch, where click/double-click/wheel/filter actions are applied and the `MouseClickState` double-click window is advanced.
- `WorkItemListState` exposes `scrollOffset` (list rows), `detailScrollOffset` (detail lines), `detailScrollUp/Down(amount)` and `moveUp/moveDown`, plus a private `_listHeight()`/`_adjustScroll()` clamp using `maxOffset = max(0, flatCount - listHeight)`. There is no public "scroll by N rows without moving the selection" method yet.
- The enable/disable sequences are `ANSI.mouseEnable = '\x1b[?1000h\x1b[?1002h\x1b[?1006h'` / `mouseDisable = '...l'` (line ~358). Mode 1002 (button-event tracking) reports motion **only while a button is held** — so under the current setup every delivered motion event is a drag candidate, and button-less "hover" motion is delivered only by terminals that report it anyway.
- Hover tooltip (WL-0MT9XRZDK006GMUH) is driven by the same `button & 32` branch; its existing tests treat buttons 32/33/35 as hover candidates.
- Tests: `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` (SGR parser/lifecycle/mapping, drag-motion guard) and `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (keyboard/state). `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` §"Mouse and touch input (SGR reporting)" and `packages/herdr/README.md` §"Mouse and touch" document current behaviour.

## Desired change

1. Add a `MouseDragState` tracker (press origin, fractional accumulator, active flag, pre-press `selectedIndex`/`scrollOffset`) alongside the existing `MouseClickState`, and thread it through `handleMouseInput`.
2. On a left press, record the origin and the pre-press selection. On motion with the left button held (`button & 32` and `(button & 3) === 0`), once movement exceeds `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS`, mark the drag active and **restore the pre-press selection/scroll**, then apply proportional row deltas. A release ends the drag.
3. Add a pure `mapMouseDrag(state, ev, dragState, termSize)` returning `drag-start` / `drag-list` (rows) / `drag-detail` (lines) / null, and dispatch those in `handleMouseInput` — `drag-list` calls a new `state.scrollBy(rows)` that clamps to `[0, maxOffset]` **without** touching `selectedIndex`; `drag-detail` reuses the existing detail scroll clamp (`detailScrollUp/Down`).
4. Route button-less motion (`(button & 3) === 3`) to the existing hover mapping, and left-button motion to the drag mapper; other buttons stay inert.
5. Never let the drag consumer emit `select-row`/`open-detail`; releases remain inert, so a drag-release can never click.
6. Add unit tests in `worklist-mouse.test.ts` for: threshold dead-zone, list drag rows + selection invariance, detail drag lines + clamping, drag-then-release does not select, hover-on-button-less-motion, and drag inert in filter mode.

### Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `MouseDragState`, `DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS`, `mapMouseDrag`, drag dispatch in `handleMouseInput`, `WorkItemListState.scrollBy`; motion branch of `mapMouseToAction` split into hover vs drag (primary change).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-mouse.test.ts` — new drag tests; update the motion-branch guard tests to reflect hover-vs-drag split.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document drag-to-scroll in the "Mouse and touch" section.
- `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` — extend the "Mouse and touch input (SGR reporting)" note (drag-motion is no longer inert).
- `packages/herdr/dist/` — rebuilt artifacts via `npm run build` (tsc), kept in sync with source.

## Related work

- Parent: **Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the selection list (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ)** — defined the SGR parser, dispatch, and drag-motion guard this item builds on; explicitly recorded drag-to-scroll as out-of-scope follow-up.
- **Test: mouse input handling suite (WL-0MSI720DX002E9WC)**, **Implement: mouse tracking lifecycle + SGR parser (WL-0MSI7278X0008XGM)**, **Implement: mouse dispatch and interactions (WL-0MSI72EYW00050N2)** — the parent's child slices that created the mapping/dispatch seam this item extends.
- **Herdr: re-enable terminal drag-select while keeping mouse support (WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN)** — the Alt+m toggle; drag-to-scroll is the in-app counterpart while mouse tracking is on.
- **Herdr worklist: hover tooltip on agent panes (WL-0MT9XRZDK006GMUH)** — the current sole consumer of motion events; this item splits motion into hover (no button) and drag (button held).
- **Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section (WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9)** — same file/rendering area (automated related-work match).
- Historical pointer issues **Mouse click on Work Items tree does not update details (WL-0MLAJ3Z750G25EJE)** and **Critical: TUI closes when clicking anywhere (WL-0MKX2C2X007IRR8G)** — regression tests for inert unknown sequences remain relevant.
- `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` — architecture notes for the worklist input/refresh loop.

### Automated related-work report

- **WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9** – Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section (completed)
- **WL-0MKW0FKCG1QI30WX** – Add N shortcut to evaluate next item in TUI (completed)
- **WL-0MQS2AZD50099JT1** – Establish file-path convention for intake_complete items (completed)

Repository file matches: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CLI.md`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** SGR coordinates are 1-based terminal cells; a 1-row threshold is the natural dead-zone. A "3-pixel" threshold from the Q&A is interpreted as **1 cell / 1 row** (see Appendix correction) — there are no sub-cell coordinates.
- **Risk — click vs drag ambiguity:** the current design selects on **press**, so a press that becomes a drag would momentarily move the selection. Mitigation: remember the pre-press `selectedIndex`/`scrollOffset` and restore them when a drag activates; releases are already inert, so a drag-release cannot click.
- **Risk — hover vs drag confusion under mode 1002:** mode 1002 delivers only button-held motion, so button-less hover may not arrive in practice. Mitigation: split strictly by the SGR button field (`& 3`); if hover is already dead under 1002 that is a **pre-existing** condition, not a regression introduced here. Recorded as a discovered observation, not expanded into scope.
- **Risk — state divergence between renderer and drag clamp:** drag must use the same `maxOffset`/visible-window maths as `_adjustScroll`, otherwise the window can scroll past the fold. Mitigation: reuse `_listHeight()`/`flatCount` via the new `scrollBy` clamp.
- **Risk — double-click interaction:** a double-click is now a press that may be followed by a tiny move; the threshold dead-zone must be large enough that ordinary double-click jitter never activates a drag. Mitigation: threshold test plus reuse of the existing double-click window tests.
- **Assumption:** drag in filter mode and the metadata panel is out of scope (Q1 answer was "both list and detail").
- **Scope-creep guard:** momentum/inertia flinging, drag-select of multiple rows, drag-to-reorder, and horizontal touch gestures are **not** in scope; capture them as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The current description carried placeholder ACs, so an interview was run before drafting this brief.

- **Q1 — Scope of drag-to-scroll (list / detail / both / panel):** Answer (operator): **both list and detail areas**. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-12. Filter mode and the metadata panel remain out of scope.
- **Q2 — Drag detection threshold (any motion / minimum distance / speed-based):** Answer (operator): "your call". Final: **(b) minimum-distance dead-zone**, expressed as **1 terminal row (`DRAG_THRESHOLD_CELLS = 1`)** because SGR coordinates are character cells — an incidental same-row jitter never starts a scroll while genuine movement starts immediately. Source: operator delegated; agent recommendation.
  - *Correction to the earlier Q&A comment:* the original recommendation read "3 pixels"; terminal mouse reporting has no pixel resolution, so the constant is defined in cells (1 row). Recorded here as the authoritative unit.
- **Q3 — Scroll behaviour (proportional / snap-to-row / hybrid):** Answer (operator): "your call". Final: **(a/c hybrid) proportional to drag distance, snapped to whole rows** — a fractional accumulator converts continuous movement into discrete row steps (list) and line steps (detail), so content tracks the pointer with no sub-row rendering artefacts. Source: operator delegated; agent recommendation.
- **Q4 — Touch drag vs click-drag (identical / different):** Answer (operator): **identical behaviour for both**. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-12.
- **Q5 — Interaction with the hover tooltip (replace / coexist / by button state):** Answer (operator): "your call". Final: **(c) hover on button-less motion; drag on left-button-held motion**, keyed off the SGR button field (`button & 3`). This preserves the hover-tooltip contract without conflating it with dragging. Source: operator delegated; agent recommendation.
  - *Research note:* inspected `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the `button & 32` branch of `mapMouseToAction` is the single motion consumer; `ANSI.mouseEnable` uses mode 1002 (button-held motion only), so button-less hover may not be delivered by the current enable sequence. This is a pre-existing condition (parent WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ / hover WL-0MT9XRZDK006GMUH), recorded as a risk, not a blocker.

### Find-related summary

`/skill:find-related WL-0MSI72S0Y0060BRK` identified 3 related work items and 3 repository file matches (see the automated report above); the closest precedent is the parent's mouse-input suite and the hover-tooltip motion consumer.
