# Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added

## Problem Statement

A parent work item cannot be `completed` (status) or `in_review` (stage) while it has uncompleted children — the invariant is "if any child is not completed, the parent cannot be completed". Today, `wl create --parent <id>` and `wl update <id> --parent <new-parent>` add children without re-examining the parent's lifecycle state, so a completed or in-review parent can silently end up with new, uncompleted children. The `wl close` command already has recovery logic for this state ("children were added after the parent was closed"), but nothing prevents it from arising in the first place.

## Users

- **Project managers / producers** who close a parent, then later realize a subtask was missed and add it as a child.
  - *As a project manager, I want adding a child to a completed parent to automatically reopen the parent for planning, so that the parent's lifecycle state always reflects that its subtree is not finished.*
- **Agents / automation** that add child work items during planning.
  - *As an agent, I want the parent's status/stage kept consistent automatically, so I don't have to remember to reset it manually.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a child is created with `wl create --parent <id>` and the parent's status is `completed` (stage `in_review` or `done`), the parent is automatically moved to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`.
2. When a child is created with `wl create --parent <id>` and the parent's stage is `in_review` (status `completed`), the parent is automatically moved to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`. (Covers the same state via the stage axis.)
3. Reparenting an existing item under a parent via `wl update <item> --parent <parent>` triggers the same demotion on the target parent (status `completed` or stage `in_review` → `open` / `plan_complete`).
4. No demotion occurs when the target parent is not in a completed/in_review state (e.g. `open`/`in-progress` status, or stage `idea`/`intake_complete`/`plan_complete`/`in_progress`) — behavior is otherwise unchanged.
5. The demotion is reported: JSON output includes the demoted parent (id, from status/stage, to status/stage) and human-readable output prints a summary line (e.g. `[Parent WL-XXX demoted from completed/in_review to open/plan_complete]`), following the reporting style of the priority-downgrade cascade.
6. Unit tests cover: completed parent in `in_review`, completed parent in `done`, parent in `in_review` stage, non-eligible parent (no-op), the reparenting path, and JSON/human output reporting.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The demoted state must be a valid status/stage combination per the configured compatibility table: `open` / `plan_complete` (status `open` is compatible with stage `plan_complete`; status `completed` is only compatible with `in_review`/`done`).
- Demotion applies only to the direct target parent (the parent the child is being added to). Grandparent/ancestor promotion is out of scope.
- No new config flags. The behavior is automatic, not opt-in.
- Must not interfere with existing recursive-close and recovery-close logic in `wl close`.

## Existing State

- `src/commands/create.ts` (line ~159) sets `parentId` when `--parent` is provided, with no parent lifecycle check.
- `src/commands/update.ts` (line ~198) applies `parentId` updates (reparenting) with no parent lifecycle check.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` has `cascadePriorityDowngrade(parentId, newPriority)` — the established pattern for a parent→child cascade rule, wired in `src/commands/update.ts` (~lines 384–467) with `downgradedChildren` reported in JSON and a human summary line.
- `src/commands/close.ts` implements the inverse: recursive close (deepest-first) and a recovery path for a `done` parent that still has non-closed children (children added after parent closed).

## Desired Change

1. Add a database method on `WorklogDatabase` (in `packages/shared/src/database.ts`, following the `cascadePriorityDowngrade` pattern) — e.g. `demoteParentOnChildAdded(parentId)` — that:
   - Loads the parent by id.
   - If the parent's status is `completed` (any stage) OR stage is `in_review`, updates it to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`.
   - Returns the demoted parent (or `null` when no demotion was needed).
2. Wire the method into `src/commands/create.ts`: after creating a child with `--parent`, call it on the parent id; include the result in JSON output and print a human summary line.
3. Wire the method into `src/commands/update.ts`: when `--parent` is provided, call it on the new parent; include the result in JSON output and print a human summary line.
4. Add unit tests in `tests/` (e.g. `tests/database.test.ts` for the method, plus command-level tests for create/update output).

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — add `demoteParentOnChildAdded(parentId)` method (canonical WorklogDatabase class; `src/database.ts` re-exports it).
- `src/commands/create.ts` — call the method after creating a child with `--parent`; report demotion in output.
- `src/commands/update.ts` — call the method when reparenting via `--parent`; report demotion in output.
- `tests/database.test.ts` (and command-level tests) — unit coverage for the method and the create/update reporting.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR — Auto-downgrade critical children when parent priority is reduced**: established the cascade-rule pattern (`cascadePriorityDowngrade` on the database class, wiring + reporting in `update.ts`). This feature mirrors that pattern in the opposite direction (child addition → parent demotion).
- **WL-0MQQJDQ7M000X2L4 — wl close silently orphans children when no audit result exists**: close-side handling of the parent/child lifecycle invariant; related context for why the invariant matters.
- `src/commands/close.ts` — recursive close + recovery close for parents whose children were added after closing; this feature prevents that state from being created.
- **Automated report note (find-related WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6):** the automated run surfaced only generic keyword matches (WL-0MSA9UHH6005167Y, WL-0MP14ZDJX002KK12, WL-0MLOS7X1C1P82B5J) with no additional strongly-related items; the manual list above contains the true precedents. Full automated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6.md`.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** The demotion applies to both `wl create --parent` and `wl update --parent` (reparenting) — any operation that adds a child to a parent. The user's seed intent covers "when a child is added to parent"; both commands do this.
- **Assumption:** Demoted status is `open` (user answer: "1. a") — the parent is re-opened for planning.
- **Assumption:** Demotion is reported in output (user answer: "2. report"), mirroring the priority-downgrade cascade reporting style.
- **Risk:** A batch `wl update` that reparents multiple items under a completed parent will demote that parent once — harmless and idempotent (subsequent calls are no-ops).
- **Risk:** If `db.update` fails (e.g. file lock), the demotion must not crash the create/update — treat as best-effort, but surface a warning if it fails.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Only the direct parent is demoted; ancestor propagation and child-status validation elsewhere are separate concerns (tracked in existing items where applicable).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: When the parent is demoted from `completed`/`in_review` back to `plan_complete`, which status should it get? Options: a) `open`, b) `in-progress`, c) other. — Answer (user, interactive reply): "1. a" → status `open` / stage `plan_complete`. Source: interactive reply (2026-08-07).
- Q: Should the demotion be surfaced in command output (JSON + human summary line), following the priority-downgrade cascade precedent, or happen silently? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "2. report" → JSON field + human summary line. Source: interactive reply (2026-08-07).
- Note: The user's parenthetical "(sorry status should be en)" was interpreted via the clarifying question above — the demoted status is `open`.
data.title: Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added

# Intake Draft — Add per-shortcut option to control whether a shortcut opens a command pane (WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL)

## Problem statement

Every chord shortcut in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` unconditionally opens a pane when dispatched: shell commands (`!!`/`!`) open a visible "Command Output" herdr pane via `run-in-pane.sh`, and agent commands (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:`) open a pi agent pane via `send-to-pi.sh`. There is no way to configure a shortcut to execute without opening a pane — high-frequency, low-feedback actions (e.g. `a-y` audit approve) force the user to dismiss a pane on every use.

## Users

- **Herdr worklist users** who drive Worklog workflows via chord shortcuts and want quiet, non-intrusive execution for actions that need no visual confirmation (approve, priority changes, etc.).
- **Producers / reviewers** using `a-y` (audit approve) repeatedly across many `in_review` items.

### User stories

- As a user, when I press a shortcut configured with `open_pane: false`, I want the command to run in the background (no pane opens) so I can keep working uninterrupted — and I want its output written to a log file so I can inspect what happened later.
- As a user, when I press any other shortcut, I want the pane to open exactly as it does today (default behavior unchanged).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Schema** — `ShortcutEntry` in `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` gains an optional `openPane` boolean, parsed from the `open_pane` key in shortcuts.json. Missing/invalid values default to opening a pane (backward compatible; invalid values are logged and treated as omitted, mirroring the `code_freeze` pattern).
2. **Dispatch — shell commands** — A `!!`/`!` shortcut with `open_pane: false` executes its command in the background (no herdr pane created) with stdout/stderr captured to a log file for later inspection.
3. **Dispatch — agent commands** — An agent shortcut (`/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, `/prompt:`) with `open_pane: false` runs headless (no pi agent pane created), honoring the entry's `model`, with output captured to a log file. The work-item ↔ pane association (WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9) is skipped when no pane is created.
4. **Default unchanged** — Shortcuts without `open_pane` (all current entries) behave exactly as today: shell commands open a visible command-output pane; agent commands open a pi agent pane.
5. **Test case applied** — The `a-y` (audit approve) entry in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` is set to `open_pane: false`; pressing `a-y` approves the item without opening a pane, and the worklist refresh shows the updated state.
6. **All related documentation is updated** — `packages/herdr/README.md` (shortcut schema section, alongside `model` and `code_freeze`) documents the new `open_pane` field and its semantics.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes, including new unit tests for parsing/validation and dispatch routing (shell + agent, pane vs. no-pane, log-file creation).

## Constraints

- Follow the established optional-field pattern in `shortcut-config.ts` (`model`, `code_freeze`): snake_case JSON key → camelCase TS field, invalid values never break or hide a shortcut.
- Background execution must be detached and non-blocking — the TUI event loop and process lifecycle must be unaffected (mirror the existing `spawn(..., { detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' })` + `child.unref()` pattern in `index.ts`).
- No behavior change for entries without `open_pane` (default = open pane).
- Log file location is an implementation decision; a sensible default is a per-run file under a known directory (e.g. the OS tmpdir or `<worklog-root>`), with the path recorded/logged so it can be located for inspection.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — 22 entries; `a-y` is `["a","y"]` → `!!wl reviewed <id> false && wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close yes --summary 'Approved by manual review'` (view `both`, stages `in_review`).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `ShortcutEntry` interface (command, view, chord, label?, description?, stages?, model?, codeFreeze?) + `parseShortcutEntry` validation + `ShortcutRegistry`; optional fields follow snake_case→camelCase parsing with invalid-value logging.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `onCommand(command, model)` routes: `agent` → `send-to-pi.sh` (pi pane, claims item, optional pane-id capture); `pane` (`!!`/`!`) → `run-in-pane.sh` (visible Command Output pane); `stdout` → `CMD:` prefix fallback.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `processChordInput` resolves chords and stores `resolvedCommand` / `resolvedModel` on `ChordState`; `resolveAndRouteCommand` calls `onCommand(resolvedCommand, model)`.
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` — splits a pane right, runs the command in a shell wrapper, keeps the pane open for inspection.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — opens a pi agent pane with the command as initial prompt; `--model` / `--pane-id-file` options exist.
- Headless pi execution (`pi -p --mode json`) is an established pattern elsewhere (e.g. `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`).

## Desired change

- Add `open_pane: false` support to the shortcut schema, plumbed through `parseShortcutEntry` → `ChordState` → `onCommand`, defaulting to open-pane behavior.
- In `index.ts` dispatch: when a shortcut entry has `openPane: false`, spawn the shell command (or headless pi for agent commands) detached with output redirected to a log file instead of opening a pane; skip pane-id capture for agent commands; keep the worklist refresh cycle so results become visible.
- Set `a-y` to `open_pane: false` in `shortcuts.json` as the proof/test case.
- Document the field in `packages/herdr/README.md`; add unit tests for parsing and dispatch.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — Add `openPane?: boolean` to `ShortcutEntry`; parse/validate `open_pane` in `parseShortcutEntry` (default true, invalid → logged + omitted).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Set `"open_pane": false` on the `a-y` (audit approve) entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Plumb resolved `openPane` through `ChordState` (`resolvedOpenPane`) and `onCommand` signature (`command, model, openPane`).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Branch dispatch on `openPane`: background execution with log-file redirect (shell: `bash -c` detached; agent: headless `pi -p --mode json` honoring `model`) vs. current pane-opening paths; skip pane-id capture when no pane opens.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — Parsing tests: `open_pane: true/false/omitted/invalid`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (or worklist tests) — Dispatch routing tests: no-pane shell + agent, log file written, default still opens panes.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Document the `open_pane` field alongside `model` / `code_freeze` (schema table + behavior notes).

## Related work

- WL-0MS95CEAE0080EB4 — *a-y (audit approve) shortcut does nothing — should run wl command visibly in a herdr pane* (completed): introduced the visible-pane execution for `!!` commands that this feature now makes optional.
- WL-0MS7MFILJ0079283 — *Visible command execution pane for !/!! prefixed commands* (completed): created `run-in-pane.sh`; success/failure pane lifecycle.
- WL-0MS9HIUE0002JAKQ — *Leave command-output pane open after successful !/!! command so output is inspectable* (completed): pane stays open for inspection — the exact behavior `open_pane: false` lets users opt out of.
- WL-0MSD48ZFC0043AO3 — *Add model to the shortcut keys* (completed): established the optional-field schema + `onCommand(command, model)` plumbing pattern this feature extends.
- WL-0MSD81VEL009XHWA — *code_freeze field* (referenced in shortcut-config.ts): the invalid-value→omit precedent.
- WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9 — *Herdr worklist: track agents spawned per work item* (in progress): pane-id capture to skip when no pane is created.
- WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7 — *Evaluate Pi subprocess mechanisms: headless pi -p vs herdr pane* (completed): established headless `pi -p --mode json` as a valid non-pane execution mechanism.
- WL-0MSHIA53D009DJOT — *Keep focus on the Herdr selection list when a shortcut command creates a pane* (open, medium): complementary UX concern for pane-opening shortcuts; related but not blocking.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (low):** Log files accumulate — mitigate by using a per-run filename (timestamp) under a single directory and documenting the location; cleanup is out of scope.
- **Risk (medium):** Headless agent execution (`pi -p --mode json`) may not behave identically to interactive pane execution for all workflows (e.g. `/skill:implement` spawning its own panes, long-running interactive steps). Mitigation: default remains pane-opening; `open_pane: false` is opt-in per shortcut; the a-y test case exercises only a shell command.
- **Assumption:** "Command pane" scope includes both the visible command-output pane (shell commands) and the pi agent pane (agent commands) — confirmed by user (Q2: "all").
- **Assumption:** Background execution must still produce an inspectable record — log file per user (Q1: option b).
- **Scope-creep guard:** Worklist auto-refresh timing, log rotation, and a settings-level default are out of scope; record as separate work items if needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "When a shortcut is set to NOT open a pane, how should the command execute?" — Answer (rgardler): option **b — run in the background but write output to a log file for later inspection**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Should the flag apply only to shell commands (`!!`/`!` → command-output pane), or also to agent commands (`/skill:*`, `/intake` → pi agent pane)?" — Answer (rgardler): **all** shortcut types. Source: interactive reply.

# Auto-downgrade critical priority when item is marked completed/in_review

## Problem statement

A work item that is marked **completed/in_review** can still carry `critical` priority today. Critical is a signal for urgent *open* work — it drives `wl next` ordering, TUI selection lists, and grouping — so a finished item left at critical competes with genuinely urgent items and makes dashboards misleading. When an item transitions to a terminal state (`status=completed` and/or `stage=in_review`), its priority must not remain `critical`.

## Users

- **Operators and agents** who close out work items.
  - *As an operator, when I mark a critical item as completed/in_review, I want its priority automatically downgraded to `high`, so that finished work stops competing with genuinely urgent open items.*
  - *As a developer, I want the automatic downgrade reported in the command output, so that I can verify the change happened.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state — `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` (via `wl update`) or `status=completed` (via `wl close`) — its priority is automatically downgraded to `high`.
2. Priorities other than `critical` (`high`, `medium`, `low`) are never modified by a terminal transition.
3. Command output reports the downgrade: a machine-readable field in `--json` output and a summary line in human-readable output, consistent with the existing `downgradedChildren` reporting in `wl update`.
4. Unit tests cover: `wl update --status completed`, `wl update --stage in_review`, `wl close`, and no-op cases (non-critical priorities unchanged; non-terminal transitions like `plan_complete` leave `critical` intact).
5. Full project test suite passes, and `CLI.md` documentation for `wl update` / `wl close` is updated to describe the auto-downgrade behavior.

## Constraints

- Canonical priorities are `critical | high | medium | low` (see `src/validators/priority.ts`); the downgrade target is `high` per operator specification.
- Only terminal transitions trigger the downgrade — moving `critical` items between non-terminal stages (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must not touch priority.
- Must not conflict with the existing child cascade: `cascadePriorityDowngrade` in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (parent downgrade → children). A completed item is itself terminal, so no child cascade is implied by this rule.
- Prefer reusing existing reporting patterns from `src/commands/update.ts` over inventing new output formats.

## Existing state

- The database allows any priority with any status/stage; there is no rule preventing `critical` on completed/in_review items today.
- Terminal transitions are: `wl update <id> --status completed --stage in_review` (`src/commands/update.ts`) and `wl close <id>` (`src/commands/close.ts` sets `status=completed`, `stage=done`).
- A directly related cascade already exists: `cascadePriorityDowngrade(parentId, newPriority)` in `packages/shared/src/database.ts` (line ~1230) downgrades critical *children* to `high` when a parent drops from `critical`, reported via `downgradedChildren` in `src/commands/update.ts` (lines ~383–408).
- `wl doctor` validates status/stage combinations (`src/doctor/status-stage-check.ts`) but has no priority-vs-stage rule.

## Desired change

1. Add a small helper (e.g., `downgradeIfTerminal(updatedItem)` or an inline check alongside the existing cascade) that, when an item is transitioning to a terminal state, downgrades `critical` → `high`.
2. Invoke it from the terminal-transition paths in `src/commands/update.ts` (stage/status changes) and `src/commands/close.ts` (close path). Decide between explicit call sites vs. enforcement inside the shared `update()` — prefer explicit call sites to avoid side effects on internal cascade `update()` calls unless a guard makes it safe.
3. Report downgraded items in JSON and human-readable output, mirroring the `downgradedChildren` pattern.
4. Add unit tests and update `CLI.md`.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling (`--status completed` / `--stage in_review`); add downgrade enforcement and reporting.
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path sets `status=completed`; enforce downgrade here too.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — home of `cascadePriorityDowngrade`; natural location for the new helper (e.g., `downgradeIfTerminal`) if a DB-layer helper is preferred.
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — canonical priority constants to reuse.
- `tests/database.test.ts` (and/or `tests/cli/*`) — unit tests for the new behavior.
- `CLI.md` — document auto-downgrade in `wl update` / `wl close` sections.

## Related work

- `Auto-downgrade critical children when parent priority is reduced (WL-0MS7YCCLV000YJCR)` — completed; the direct precedent: same `critical` → `high` downgrade rule and reporting pattern, but for parent→child cascades.
- `Add priority normalization to create, update and doctor commands (WL-0MP14WFW6001VE3G)` — completed; priority validation infrastructure (`src/validators/priority.ts`).
- `Bubble up critical items (WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C)` — completed; critical-priority semantics in `wl next`.
- `Exclude in-review items from wl next (WL-0ML2TS8I409ALBU6)` — completed; in_review semantics.
- `Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added (WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6)` — open; sibling rule about terminal-state invariants on parents.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** `wl doctor` detection/fix of legacy `critical` + completed/in_review items is a natural extension but is NOT part of this work item's ACs. If wanted, record as a separate linked work item (`discovered-from:WL-0MSJM4EIV001A0V9`).
- **Over-enforcement risk:** blanket enforcement inside the shared DB `update()` could interfere with internal calls (e.g., the child cascade calls `db.update()`); guard conditions must be precise or enforcement kept at explicit call sites.
- **Assumption:** "completed/in_review" means terminal transitions — `status=completed` and/or `stage=in_review`, plus `stage=done` via `wl close`.
- **Assumption:** the downgrade target is `high`, as explicitly specified by the operator.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: The request ended with `--priority low` — what does it refer to?
  - A (assumed, rgardler): `--priority low` sets the priority of this new work item itself (matching `wl create --priority low` CLI syntax), not the downgrade target — the feature spec explicitly downgrades to `high`. Source: interactive reply; interpretation documented here. If wrong, the item priority is a one-line `wl update` fix.
- No further clarification was needed; the seed context was sufficient to draft the brief (interview skipped per intake skill step 4).

## Problem

The herdr worklog-selection-list plugin pauses auto-refresh/auto-sync whenever the pane is not the keyboard-focused pane. Visibility detection in visibility.ts treats `pane.focused === false` as hidden (the `pause-when-hidden` feature, WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP), so in a multi-pane split tab (e.g. Work Items + several Pi Agent panes side by side) the worklist pane is visible on screen but never refreshes — the list freezes at the last focus-period snapshot.

## User story

As a herdr user working in a split tab, I want the visible Work Items pane to keep auto-refreshing while I work in an adjacent Pi Agent pane in the same focused tab, so the list reflects live worklog state without me having to click into it.

## Evidence (2026-08-08)

- Tab w1:t11 is focused and NOT zoomed; the worklist pane w1:p41 occupies a visible 29-col split, yet `herdr pane get w1:p41` reports `focused: false` (a Pi Agent pane holds focus).
- The pane's own status bar renders `[paused — hidden]`, and its displayed data is stale (LP-0MSF9RUSQ007M346 shown as completed/22:21 while live worklog shows it claimed in-progress at 00:21:58Z).
- The pane only refreshes during brief focus periods (scrollback shows ~14 renders in 7h despite a 30s refresh interval).

## Root cause

`isPaneVisible()` (visibility.ts) conflates keyboard focus with visibility: it runs `herdr pane get <HERDR_PANE_ID>` and reads `result.pane.focused`. Pane focus is a per-split signal; visibility is a per-tab signal. The plugin already has `HERDR_TAB_ID` available — `herdr tab get <tab_id>` reports `focused: true` for the visible tab, which is the correct visibility signal.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The visibility gate treats the pane as visible when its TAB is focused (via `HERDR_TAB_ID` + `herdr tab get`), regardless of which pane in the tab holds keyboard focus.
- [ ] A visible worklist pane in a focused multi-pane tab keeps refreshing on the configured auto-refresh interval.
- [ ] A pane whose TAB is not focused still pauses refresh. Known limitation (approved plan scope): a pane zoomed-over within a focused tab is treated as visible and keeps refreshing — documented in README.
- [ ] Fail-open behaviour is preserved: CLI error/missing env → visible (polling proceeds).
- [ ] Unit tests cover: tab-focused/visible, tab-focused-but-pane-unfocused, tab-unfocused, CLI-failure fail-open.

## Suggested approach

Extend `isPaneVisible()` in visibility.ts: read `HERDR_TAB_ID`; when present, `herdr tab get <id>` → `result.tab.focused` decides visibility. No pane-level fallback (approved plan scope). Verified 2026-08-08: `herdr pane get` exposes no `visible` flag; `herdr pane layout --pane <id>` exposes a `zoomed` flag but zoom-over handling is out of scope per approved plan.

## Plan

Planning completed 2026-08-08 for WL-0MSJNJPRM009RM35 (see Appendix below for decisions).

### Feature plan

1. **Tests: tab-based visibility detection (visibility.test.ts)** — WL-0MSKUANPC000OKR2 (task, high). Rewrite `visibility.test.ts` to exercise tab-based gating: tab-focused/visible, tab-focused-but-pane-unfocused, tab-unfocused, no-`HERDR_TAB_ID` fail-open, CLI-error fail-open, tab-get args + `HERDR_BIN_PATH`, PollGate memoization.
2. **Impl: tab-focus-gated visibility in visibility.ts + docs** — WL-0MSKUAT5D00443GA (task, high). `isPaneVisible()` reads `HERDR_TAB_ID` → `herdr tab get <id>` → `result.tab.focused`; fail-open preserved; no pane fallback; README Pause-when-hidden section updated with tab-based signal and zoom-over limitation. Depends on the tests item (test-first).

### Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-08T20:42Z — plan completed; created child items WL-0MSKUANPC000OKR2 (tests) and WL-0MSKUAT5D00443GA (impl), wired dependency impl→tests.
- 2026-08-08T20:42Z — AC3 updated to reflect approved scope: zoom-over within a focused tab is a documented limitation (treated as visible), not a pause case.
- 2026-08-08T20:42Z — Suggested approach updated: no pane-focus fallback; noted `pane layout` `zoomed` flag exists but is out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Zoomed-over handling: Option A (include `herdr pane layout --pane <id>` zoom check, fully satisfies AC3) vs Option B (tab-focus only; zoom-over documented limitation)?" Answer (operator, 2026-08-08): "1. b" — Option B. Final: zoom-over within a focused tab is a documented limitation; tab-focus is the sole visibility signal. Research: `herdr pane get` has no visible/zoom flag; `herdr pane layout --pane <id>` exposes `zoomed` (tab-level) and per-pane rects, but the layout check was declined for scope.
- Q: "When both HERDR_TAB_ID and HERDR_PANE_ID are present: tab check authoritative with pane-focus fallback when tab metadata is unavailable? Or no fallback?" Answer (operator, 2026-08-08): "2. no need for failover" — no pane-focus fallback. Final: `HERDR_TAB_ID` set → tab get decides; `HERDR_TAB_ID` missing → visible (standalone fail-open, unchanged).
- Q: "README Pause-when-hidden section update in scope?" Answer (operator, 2026-08-08): "3. in scope". Final: yes — README (packages/herdr/README.md:311-334) updated to describe tab-based signal, `[paused — hidden]` on tab-unfocused, and the zoom-over limitation.

## Problem

In the herdr worklog-selection-list plugin, an OPEN detail view is never refreshed. `doRefresh()` → `state.refreshItems(newItems)` replaces `_allItems`/`items`, but `state.detailItem` is set only in `selectItem()` (worklist.ts:482) and cleared in `back()` (:497). While `mode === 'detail'`, render() always draws the same snapshot object. So even with the pane focused and auto-refresh running, the visible detail content (Status, Updated, audit icons, description) stays frozen — user-reported symptom: `I have had it focused and it does not update`.

## Evidence (live, 2026-08-08)

- Pane w1:p41 currently displays the detail view of LP-0MSF9RUSQ007M346: `Status: completed`, `Updated 07/08/26 22:21`, `Audited At 07/08/26 22:18`.
- Live worklog: `status: in-progress`, `updatedAt: 2026-08-08T00:21:58.992Z` (claimed ~5 min earlier via a dispatch from the same pane; agent-panes.json records spawned pane w1:p4W).
- The list portion does refresh while focused (scrollback renders evolve), so the stale detail is not a fetch failure — it is the refresh path never writing to `detailItem`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A refresh while a detail view is open updates the rendered detail content to the freshly fetched item state (without closing the view or resetting scroll/ToC position unless the item identity changes).
- [ ] Selection/scroll restoration semantics from refreshItems are preserved for the list.
- [ ] Unit tests: refresh while in detail mode updates detailItem by ID; item removed from results → detail falls back gracefully (keeps last known or closes).
- [ ] The selected-item metadata panel (list mode) also reflects refreshed data (it already does via items; verify no regression).

## Suggested approach

In `doRefresh` (or `refreshItems`), after swapping items, look up the refreshed object matching `state.detailItem?.id` and assign it to `detailItem` (preserving `detailScrollOffset`/ToC state). If the item disappeared from the fetched set, keep the last snapshot or exit to list mode (decide + test).

## Problem

In the herdr worklog-selection-list plugin, every fetch used by the auto-refresh cycle spawns `wl` via execFile WITHOUT a timeout: `runWl(args)` (fetcher.ts:376) passes `timeout` to execFileAsync only when `timeoutMs !== undefined` (:356), and no caller in the refresh path supplies one (fetchNextItems, fetchItemsByStage, fetchMandatorySubsets, fetchActionableCount). `doRefresh` awaits these inside a `refreshInFlight` single-flight guard (worklist.ts:2497-2503); if a spawn hangs (e.g. waiting on the worklog lock during a long `wl sync`, or a stuck child), the guard stays true forever and EVERY subsequent refresh is skipped — the pane freezes even while focused, with no error surfaced.

Note: runSync (auto-sync.ts:226) already has a 60s spawn safety timeout; the refresh read path does not.

related-to: WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9 (same bug class in the downtime worker path — getNextItem/getNextAuditCandidate in index.ts use direct execFileAsync with no timeout; a single fix adding bounded timeouts to ALL wl spawns would close both).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every wl spawn in the refresh/sync fetch path has a bounded timeout (recommend 30-60s, configurable or aligned with existing constants).
- [ ] A timed-out refresh fails gracefully: toast (`Refresh failed`), guard cleared, next tick retries — never a permanently wedged refreshInFlight.
- [ ] Unit tests: hung execFile resolves to failure after the timeout and the next refresh tick proceeds.

## Suggested approach

Pass a default timeoutMs inside runWl (or runWlInner) when the caller omits one, e.g. `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000`, keeping the option to override. Verify no existing tests depend on unbounded spawns.

## Goal

Root-cause why **zero downtime dispatches** were sent during the night of 2026-08-07/08, despite evidence that multiple clients polled `GET /llama/local/status` continuously — including for the full 7-hour idle window — while the proxy reported an idle local model with free slots. Determine whether any of the pollers were herdr downtime workers that failed to dispatch (wedge, silent wl failure, candidate-selection fail-closed, claim conflict) or whether none of the pollers were dispatch-capable at all.

## Log observations (evidence)

### 1. Continuous status polling all night — including the entire idle window

`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` `status_request` entries (proxy = 192.168.0.199:8000, the herdr downtime worker's `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_PROXY_URL`):

| Window (local) | Poll rate |
|---|---|
| 03:00–04:15 (audit-wave tail) | 15.9/min |
| 04:20–05:00 (idle start) | 15.9/min |
| 05:00–09:00 (idle) | 15.5/min |
| 09:00–11:00 (idle) | 15.9/min |

- Inter-poll gap histogram over 05:10–09:00 (3654 gaps): smooth decay 0–9s, mean gap 3.78s → consistent with **~8 independent periodic pollers at ~30s cadence** (exponential inter-arrival for uniform random phases). Rate did NOT pause during idle (a healthy herdr worker polls regardless, but a *wedged* one stops — WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9).
- The local worklist pane (sole `tsx src/index.ts` on this host) was **wedged since 21:55:26Z** (see item WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9; it ran pre-fix source, HEAD 7ea7cae4) → contributed ~0 polls after 21:55Z. So the ~8 pollers are NOT explained by the local pane.

### 2. Proxy healthy and idle-capable throughout

- `proxy.log.2026-08-08_05` contains ONLY `status_request` (5722) and `lease_released` (51) — no restarts, no watchdog events, no server failures.
- llama-server up with Qwen3 loaded: 104,657 `GET /slots` responses in `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log`; proxy broadcast loop only queries `/slots` when `llama_server_running=true`.
- Zero local model requests 04:18–11:26 local → status would have reported `active_query=false`, `available_slots=3/3` (idle), and fail-open even without a model (LP-0MSI06HPB0043MV1). A ≥4-min idle window existed repeatedly for 7h09m.

### 3. Persistent remote (192.168.0.191) connections to the proxy

- `ss -tnp` at multiple snapshots showed 3–4 concurrent ESTAB `.191 → :8000` connections (ports 44902/64396/59704, then 64396/40258/37498; one with a 276KB in-flight send queue). The remote host also holds 6+ SSH sessions to this host (port 22; herdr TUIs run via SSH — see clients 66/68 in `~/.config/herdr/herdr-server.log` at 02:14/02:55 local).
- **Caveat:** the proxy does NOT log client IPs for `status_request`, so the poller identity is inferred from connection snapshots, not proven. The pollers could be (a) herdr downtime workers on 192.168.0.191 (each worklist pane polls the same LAN proxy URL every 30s), (b) the opencode TUI statusline on .191, or (c) other.

### 4. Zero dispatches anywhere

- Only dispatch log present: `/home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` — last entry `2026-08-07T21:55:26.274Z audit LP-0MSI06HPB0043MV1`. No dispatches after that.
- No `downtime-dispatches.log` in ContextHub/SorraAgents/piman/etc. worklogs.
- No dispatch lease activity during idle: `proxy.log.2026-08-08_05` has no `dispatch_cleanup`, `local_dispatch_denied`, or `lease_renewed` events — only `lease_released` for evicted sessions (leftover audit-wave leases expiring on the 5-min sweep).

## The RCA question

If any of the ~8 pollers were herdr downtime workers (remote or local), they observed a fully idle local model with free slots for 7h09m and still dispatched nothing. Why?

## Candidate hypotheses to evaluate

1. **Wedge bug (WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9):** no-timeout `wl` exec in `getNextItem`/`getNextAuditCandidate` permanently wedges the dispatch task until pane restart. Fix 810afbe1 exists ONLY on `origin/dev` — the local ContextHub checkout was stale at 7ea7cae4 and the pane restarted 2026-08-08 11:53:21 local still loads the pre-fix source (`DOWNTIME_WL_TIMEOUT_MS` absent). Any pre-fix pane would wedge on its first dispatch attempt (e.g., under worklog lock contention from the audit wave).
2. **Pollers are not dispatch-capable** (e.g., opencode statusline) → no dispatch expected; the RCA must identify the pollers first (add client IP to the proxy `status_request` structured log, or tcpdump :8000; check processes/worklogs on 192.168.0.191).
3. **Silent dispatch failure:** wl failures/lock contention, candidate selection fail-closed (`wl next --stage` returns nothing), claim conflict, `send-to-pi.sh` spawn failure. Check what the downtime worker logs on failure vs success (dispatch log only written on success?).
4. **Config/disablement:** downtime worker disabled, paused (no-candidate cooldown), or dispatch window rules on the remote panes.
5. **Worklog-root mismatch:** remote panes write dispatch logs to `.191` filesystems (invisible here); verify on .191 whether dispatches were attempted/logged there.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Poller identity established: each `status_request` poller attributed (herdr worklist pane vs other) with evidence (proxy access-log client IPs, tcpdump capture, or .191 inspection)
- [ ] For each herdr poller that saw an idle window: the exact point of failure determined (wedge / wl failure / fail-closed selection / claim / spawn) with log or repro evidence
- [ ] If the wedge bug is implicated: confirm the fix (810afbe1) is deployed to every running worklist pane (working tree updated + pane restarted), or a follow-up item created for deployment
- [ ] Recommend an observability fix (e.g., client IP in `status_request` structured log) so poller attribution is possible in future
- [ ] Dispatches resume: a dispatch observed in `downtime-dispatches.log` on the next idle window ≥4 min
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9** – herdr downtime worker: hung wl exec (no timeout) permanently wedges the dispatch task until pane restart (completed)
- **WL-0MNC77YBM000ONUO** – Use colour on the audit summary in the meta data. (completed)
- **WL-0MPN6LCLO006N5U8** – In /wl browser, Enter renders wl show markdown in above-editor widget (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSGJDSMJ004128E-herdr-selection-list-shortcut-hint-bar-e/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 168, 192, 199, 2026, 30s (+175 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSKSZBEL0025CN3-test-failure-tests-cli-init-test-ts-shou/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 168, 192, 199, 2026, 30s (+173 more)

data.description:
# Intake Brief — Herdr: filter by priority via f-p-* chords, stage filters become f-s-* (WL-0MSKC8T46006999S) ## Headline Add priority filtering to the Herdr worklist, complementing the existing stage filter: the filter chord gains an axis key — stage filters become `f s ` and new priority filters are `f p ` — with a single active filter (replace semantics), a typed `/wl --priority

` command for parity, and sprint clearing all filters. ## Problem Statement The Herdr worklist currently filters only by stage via single-key chords (`f i`, `f n`, `f p`, `f r`, `f s`). Producers and agents frequently want to see everything at a given priority (e.g. all `critical` items) regardless of stage, which is not possible today. The filter chord needs an axis dimension: `f `. Re-using the existing single-key chords would collide (`f p` currently means "filter plan"), so stage filters move under `f s *` and priority filters take `f p *`. ## Users - Herdr plugin users (producers, developers, agents) who browse the worklist inside a Herdr pane. ### Example User Stories - As a producer, I want to press `f p c` to see every open critical item so I can prioritise review, regardless of stage. - As a developer, I want to type `/wl --priority high` to see all open high-priority work when deciding what to pick up next. - As an agent, I want `f s i` to keep filtering idea-stage items with the same keystroke muscle memory I had for `f i`. ## Acceptance Criteria 1. New priority filter chords work: `f p c` (critical), `f p h` (high), `f p m` (medium), `f p l` (low) filter the worklist to items of that priority. 2. Stage filter chords are remapped under the stage axis: `f s i` (idea), `f s n` (intake), `f s p` (plan), `f s r` (review) filter by stage; the old single-key stage chords (`f i`, `f n`, `f p`, `f r`) no longer trigger filters, and `f s` alone no longer resolves to a command (it is a chord prefix only). 3. Replace semantics (single filter slot): applying a priority filter clears any active stage filter, and vice versa; the list header shows which filter is active. 4. Sprint clears all filters: `f s s` and `/wl` (no arguments) restore the default unfiltered view, clearing both stage and priority filters; a priority-axis clear exists (proposed `f p s`) that returns to the unfiltered view. 5. Typed parity command: `/wl --priority ` filters by priority, accepting canonical names `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`; invalid/unknown priority values fall back gracefully (no crash, no filter change), matching the current `/wl ` behaviour. 6. Priority-filtered views follow the same semantics as stage-filtered views: every open root item with that priority (`wl list --status open --priority

--root-only`) — no `browseItemCount` cap, no `wl next` selection omission, children hidden and reachable via expand, standard sortIndex order. 7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, with new unit tests covering chord registration, dispatch, replace semantics, and the priority fetcher. 8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (Herdr README filter sections, code comments). ## Constraints - **Scope is the Herdr plugin** (`packages/herdr/`): `shortcuts.json`, `worklist.ts`, `fetcher.ts`, tests, and README. The Pi TUI extension and the `wl` CLI are out of scope (the CLI already supports `--priority`). - **No new settings or configuration flags.** The chord scheme and `/wl --priority` command are the only interfaces. - **Single active filter.** Stage and priority filters are mutually exclusive (user decision: replace, not combine). - Keep the existing stage-filter fetch semantics (open, root-only, uncapped, sortIndex order) — the priority filter mirrors them. ## Existing State - Filter chords in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`: `f i` → `/wl idea`, `f n` → `/wl intake`, `f p` → `/wl plan`, `f r` → `/wl review`, `f s` → `/wl` (sprint, unfiltered). - `dispatchChordCommand` in `worklist.ts` maps `/wl ` (via `STAGE_MAP`) to `state.applyFilter(stage)` and `/wl` (no args) to `state.clearFilter()`; `isWlViewCommand` triggers a refetch after a filter dispatch (WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G). - `WorkItemListState.activeFilter` holds the single stage filter; `_applyFilters()` filters `item.stage === activeFilter`; the header renders `(filtered: )`. - `fetchItemsForView(activeFilter, defaultFetcher)` → `fetchItemsByStage(stage)` → `wl list --status open --stage --root-only` (fetcher.ts). - `wl list` natively supports `--priority` (already used by `fetchMandatorySubsets` for the critical subset). - A legacy digit-based filter mode (`state.mode === 'filter'`, `formatFilterPrompt`) exists but is unreachable from the keyboard since the `/` prompt was removed — out of scope unless trivially affected. ## Desired Change 1. **`shortcuts.json`** — Remove the `f i`/`f n`/`f p`/`f r` stage chords and the single `f s` sprint chord. Add stage-axis chords `f s i|n|p|r` (→ `/wl idea|intake|plan|review`) and `f s s` (→ `/wl` sprint, clears all filters). Add priority-axis chords `f p l|m|h|c` (→ `/wl --priority low|medium|high|critical`) and `f p s` (→ `/wl`, clear-priority, returns to unfiltered). 2. **`worklist.ts`** — Add a priority filter slot to `WorkItemListState` with replace semantics (`applyFilter` clears priority; new `applyPriorityFilter` clears stage; `clearFilter` clears both). Extend `_applyFilters` to match stage OR priority. Extend `dispatchChordCommand` and `isWlViewCommand` to handle `/wl --priority

`. Update the header filter label to show the active axis+value. `fetchItemsForView` routes priority filters to the new fetcher. 3. **`fetcher.ts`** — Add `fetchItemsByPriority(priority)` running `wl list --status open --priority

--root-only`, mirroring `fetchItemsByStage`. 4. **Tests** — Update `shortcut-config.test.ts` (chord registration: `f s *`, `f p *`, removal of old single-key chords) and `worklist.test.ts` (dispatch of `/wl --priority

`, replace semantics, clear-all sprint, header label); add `fetchItemsByPriority` coverage in the fetcher tests. 5. **README** — Update the filter-by-stage chord documentation to the `f s *` scheme and document `f p *` priority filters and `/wl --priority

`. ## Key Files (predicted) - `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Replace the single-key stage chords with `f s *` stage chords and add `f p *` priority chords. - `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Priority filter slot with replace semantics, `/wl --priority` dispatch, header label, `isWlViewCommand` update. - `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — New `fetchItemsByPriority` mirroring `fetchItemsByStage`. - `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Dispatch, replace-semantics, clear-all, and header tests. - `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` — Chord registration tests for the new `f s *` / `f p *` scheme. - `tests/herdr/fetcher.test.ts` — `fetchItemsByPriority` mocked-socket tests. - `packages/herdr/README.md` — Filter documentation updates. ## Related Work - **WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G** (in-progress) — "When filtering by stage, show all open work items in that stage": established the stage-filter fetch semantics (open, root-only, uncapped) and `/wl ` dispatch that this work extends to priorities. - **WL-0MSGSE15000746F7** — sprint `/wl` chord returning to the default view; the `f s` chord being remapped here. - **WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR** — root-only top-level lists; semantics reused by the priority filter. - **WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP** — Herdr work item selection list (origin of the plugin's list/filter UI). - **WL-0MSGTSPXK007POB1** — header shows the active filter; the header label changes here for priorities. ### Related work (automated report) Automated report from the find-related skill (full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MSKC8T46006999S.md`). Low relevance — flagged for traceability only: - **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J** – Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM) (completed) - **WL-0MQFB8N990056T8P** – [test-failure] tests/tui/controller-watch.test.ts > TuiController - Database Watch > always re-renders on watch refresh even when dataset appears unchanged (completed) - **WL-0MQF95NCC0024H61** – wl next Stage 3 blocker surfacing still returns child items (completed) ## Risks & Assumptions - **Chord conflict risk (medium):** `f p` changes meaning from "filter plan" to "priority axis leader". Mitigation: remove the old `f p` plan chord; `f p` alone must not resolve (registry prefix semantics already support this); tests assert the old chords no longer resolve. - **Muscle memory regression (low):** existing users of `f i`/`f n`/`f r` must learn `f s i`/`f s n`/`f s r`. Mitigation: README documents the new scheme; `f s` hints show in the chord help line. - **Assumption — priority clear chord:** the exact key for the priority-axis clear is proposed as `f p s` (symmetric with the stage sprint). Final key choice is a product detail; the brief records the proposal (user confirmed a priority-clear exists). - **Assumption — typed command syntax:** `/wl --priority ` mirrors the existing `/wl ` syntax; alternative syntaxes (e.g. `/wl priority:

`) are possible but the `--priority` form matches the `wl list` flag naming. - **Scope creep:** the legacy unreachable digit-based filter mode (`formatFilterPrompt`) is out of scope; any change to it should be a separate work item. ## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers - Q1: "Can a stage filter and a priority filter be active simultaneously (e.g., `f s i` then `f p c` → critical idea items), or does each new filter chord replace the previous one (single filter slot)?" — Answer (user): "replace". Source: interactive reply (this intake session). Final: single active filter; applying one axis clears the other. - Q2: "Should sprint clear *all* filters (stage + priority), and is a way to clear just the priority filter needed (e.g., a `f p` clear chord)?" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply (this intake session). Final: `f s s` and `/wl` clear all filters; a priority-axis clear chord exists (proposed `f p s`, equivalent to returning to the unfiltered view under replace semantics). - Q3: "Should the priority filter also be reachable via a typed command (e.g., `/wl --priority critical`) for parity with `/wl `, or is the chord-only approach sufficient?" — Answer (user): "yes". Source: interactive reply (this intake session). Final: `/wl --priority ` is a supported typed command with graceful fallback for invalid values.

## Summary

Filtering the herdr plugin by in_review using the shortcut `f-r` (which resolves to `/wl review`) results in **0 items** being displayed, even though there are 70 items in the in_review stage.

## Expected behaviour

`f-r` (filter in_review) shows all root work items in the in_review stage.

## Observed behaviour

`f-r` shows an empty list (0 items).

## Root cause (investigated)

`fetchItemsByStage` (packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts) runs:

```
wl list --status open --stage <stage> --root-only
```

Per the project workflow convention (AGENTS.md), advancing an item to `in_review` sets its status to `completed`; some in_review items are still `in-progress`. Live data confirms: stage=in_review → 65 items with status `completed`, 5 with `in-progress`, **0 with `open`**. The `--status open` restriction therefore excludes every in_review item and the filter shows 0 items.

Other stage filters are also lossy (idea: 30/35, intake_complete: 21/33 missing 12 blocked, plan_complete: 10/13), but in_review is the only one that is 100% empty.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the herdr worklist plugin pane.
2. Press `f` then `r` (filter in_review).
3. Observe the list shows 0 item(s).

## Suggested implementation approach

Change `fetchItemsByStage` so a stage-filtered view shows every root item in the stage regardless of status (drop the `--status open` restriction), or map each stage to its conventional statuses (in_review → completed/in-progress). Decision pending user confirmation on scope.

## Acceptance Criteria (draft)

- [ ] `f-r` shows all 70 root in_review items (not 0).
- [ ] Stage-filtered fetch no longer silently drops items whose status does not match `open` for the in_review stage.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the in_review stage-filter fetch (items with completed/in-progress status are returned).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated (code comments, packages/herdr/README.md).

# Intake Brief — Herdr: in_review stage filter (f-r) shows 0 items (WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW)

## Headline

Filtering the herdr worklist by in_review (shortcut `f-r`, resolving to `/wl review`) shows an empty list, because the stage-filtered fetch restricts results to `status=open` while in_review items carry `completed`/`in-progress` status per the project workflow.

## Problem Statement

The herdr plugin's stage filter for in_review (`f-r` → `/wl review` → `STAGE_MAP.review = 'in_review'`) displays **0 items** even though 70 items are in the in_review stage. `fetchItemsByStage` (packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts) runs `wl list --status open --stage <stage> --root-only`; per the AGENTS.md workflow convention, advancing an item to `in_review` sets its status to `completed` (65 items) or leaves it `in-progress` (5 items) — **none are `open`**. The `--status open` restriction therefore excludes every in_review item and the filter shows 0 items.

## Users

- Herdr worklist users (producers, developers, agents) who press `f-r` to review everything awaiting producer review.

### Example User Stories

- As a producer, I want to press `f-r` in the herdr worklist and see every item awaiting review, so I know the full review queue.
- As a developer, I want the in_review filter to list items I have submitted for review (status `completed`) and items being re-worked after review feedback (status `in-progress`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Pressing `f-r` in the herdr worklist shows every root work item in the in_review stage (all 70 in the current dataset), not 0.
2. `fetchItemsByStage('in_review')` issues a `wl list` query whose status filter includes `completed` and `in-progress` (verified by a unit test asserting the exec args), while preserving `--root-only` and the standard list order.
3. Stage filters for other stages keep their existing behaviour unchanged (status=open per WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G) — verified by the existing stage-filter tests.
4. Unit tests cover the in_review stage fetch returning `completed` and `in-progress` items, and a regression test asserts the client-side stage filter (`_applyFilters`) still works for in_review.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- Fix is confined to the herdr plugin (`packages/herdr`); no `wl` CLI changes.
- Do not regress the semantics of the other stage filters (WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G keeps `status=open` for idea/intake_complete/plan_complete).
- Fail-open behaviour preserved: if the stage fetch fails, fall back to the default fetcher (never blank the list).
- `wl list --status` accepts comma-separated statuses (already used by `fetchActionableCount`), so no CLI change is needed.

## Existing State

- `f-r` (shortcuts.json) → `/wl review` → `dispatchChordCommand` matches `/^\/wl\s+(\S+)$/` → `STAGE_MAP['review']='in_review'` → `state.applyFilter('in_review')` → `doRefresh(true)` → `fetchItemsForView('in_review', fetcher)` → `fetchItemsByStage('in_review')`.
- `fetchItemsByStage` (fetcher.ts:510) runs `wl list --status open --stage <stage> --root-only`.
- Live data: stage=in_review → 65 `completed`, 5 `in-progress`, 0 `open`. Other stages: idea 30/35 open, intake_complete 21/33 open (12 blocked), plan_complete 10/13 open — lossy but non-empty; user chose to leave these unchanged.
- The `--status open` restriction originates from WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G (in-progress) whose AC#2 defined "open" as `status=open` — that decision conflicts with the workflow rule that in_review items have `completed` status.

## Desired Change

- In `fetchItemsByStage`, add a status-per-stage override: for the `in_review` stage, query with `--status completed,in-progress` (optionally including `open` for robustness) instead of `--status open`. Other stages keep `--status open`.
- Update/extend unit tests in `worklist.test.ts` (the `fetchItemsForView — stage-filtered fetch` block) to cover the in_review status set.
- Update the code comment in fetcher.ts (and README if it documents filter semantics) to reflect the per-stage status rule.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchItemsByStage` (line ~510): apply the in_review status override in the `wl list` args.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — the `fetchItemsForView — stage-filtered fetch` describe block (line ~676): extend with in_review status assertions; keep other-stage tests green.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — only if the status-per-stage mapping is better placed next to `STAGE_MAP`/`STAGES` (optional; otherwise comment-only).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the in_review filter status semantics if the filter behaviour is described there.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G (in-progress)** — "When filtering by stage, show all open work items in that stage": source of the `--status open` restriction that broke the in_review filter. The fix relaxes that restriction for in_review only.
- **WL-0MQDRZ4DK007NK5P (completed)** — "Add stage-filter arguments to the /wl slash command in the Pi TUI extension": original stage-filter feature this bug extends.
- **WL-0MSKC8T46006999S (open)** — "Herdr: filter by priority via f-p-* chords (stage filters become f-s-*)": will re-map the filter chords; same code path, related-to (not blocking).
- **WL-0MSGSE15000746F7 (in-progress)** — "Add key/chord to return to default browse view": the `f-s` clear-filter shortcut, same shortcut family.
- **WL-0MM0DTK1B1Z0VMIB / WL-0MM0DBM6I1PHQBFI (completed)** — "wl list --stage in_review returns nothing while --json shows content": similar symptom at the wl CLI rendering layer, both closed; this bug is in the herdr plugin's query construction.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope discipline (risk):** the same `--status open` restriction makes idea/intake_complete/plan_complete filters lossy. Per user decision (Q1) those are out of scope; if a follow-up is wanted, record it as a new work item rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption — in_review statuses:** the fix targets `completed` + `in-progress`; including `open` as well is harmless and future-proof (no in_review item is `open` today).
- **Assumption — no wl CLI change:** `wl list --status` already accepts comma-separated statuses; verified via `fetchActionableCount`.
- **Regression risk:** the existing stage-filter tests assert `--status open`; they must be kept green for non-in_review stages (tests will need per-stage expectations).
- **Stale-data assumption:** numbers (70 items, 65/5 split) reflect the dataset at intake time; ACs are stated in behaviour terms so they hold as the dataset evolves.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How should the stage-filter fetch behave? (a) Minimal — fix in_review only: include completed/in-progress statuses for the in_review stage (status-per-stage map), leave other stages as-is. (b) All stages — drop `--status open`: show every root item in the stage regardless of status. (c) Other." — Answer (user): "(a)". Source: interactive reply during intake. Research: confirmed other stage filters are lossy but non-empty (idea 30/35, intake_complete 21/33, plan_complete 10/13); only in_review is 100% empty. Per the user's choice, other stages keep `status=open` semantics.
- Q2 (implicit, documented): Should the 5 in-progress/in_review items appear in the filter? — Resolved by the (a) choice: `completed` and `in-progress` both included; a producer reviewing the queue sees both the submitted-for-review items and those being re-worked after review feedback.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0ML6GP3OQ15UO20F** – Investigate sort-operations performance test timeout (completed)
- **WL-0MKW48NQ913SQ212** – Refactor wl next selection paths (completed)
- **WL-0MQDR5IZZ001WCGP** – Make shortcuts.json path resolution robust against build output restructuring (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F-audit-parent-first-child-pass-through-au/skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — matched: 100, acceptance, agents, also, approach (+71 more)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — matched: 100, acceptance, agents, also, approach (+71 more)
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSKB6VJA005N43F-audit-parent-first-child-pass-through-au/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 100, acceptance, agents, also, approach (+61 more)

# Intake brief — Revisit the templates/AGENTS.md install model (WL-0MSKEJK4G008BMS0)

## Problem statement

`wl init` installs a repo-local `AGENTS.md` copied from `templates/AGENTS.md` (258 lines of work-item tracking, CRITICAL RULES, CLI cheat-sheet, architecture notes). This guidance substantially duplicates the SorraAgents global `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (installed to `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` via `scripts/install_pi.sh`), creating two sources of truth and drift risk — e.g. the recent `docs` issue-type change had to be applied to both files. The install model and the local/global relationship are also undocumented.

## Users

- **Operators / project maintainers** initializing new projects with `wl init` — want clear, non-conflicting agent guidance without duplicated maintenance.
- **Agent authors** who edit AGENTS guidance (e.g. adding an issue type) — want a single place to make the change.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I want to know exactly what `wl init` writes into my project's AGENTS.md and why, so I can predict the result before running it.
- As an agent author, I want to understand how the local AGENTS.md relates to the global `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`, so I can edit guidance in the right place.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Document the current `wl init` → `templates/AGENTS.md` → project `AGENTS.md` install flow (flow description or diagram), including the pointer line, the O/A/M prompt, and idempotence behavior — validated against `src/commands/init.ts` and its tests.
- [ ] Document the relationship and precedence between the local AGENTS.md template and the global SorraAgents `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (including how the pointer line defers to the global file and where duplication/conflict risk remains).
- [ ] Deliver a recommendation on the install model: adopt a single-source-of-truth approach (explicitly referencing WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514 as the implementation vehicle) or document why the current model is kept, with justification.
- [ ] Document how `wl init` interacts with the global AGENTS.md (detection of the global install, no delegation today) and note the drift history (e.g. the `docs` issue-type change).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the findings, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs/wiki entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (no code changes expected; add/extend docs only).

## Constraints

- Investigation/documentation only — implementation of a new install model is out of scope for this item (covered by WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514).
- Do not alter `wl init` behavior as part of this item.
- Findings must be verifiable against the actual code (`src/commands/init.ts`, `templates/AGENTS.md`, `templates/WORKFLOW.md`) and the SorraAgents install (`scripts/install_pi.sh`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`).

## Existing state

- `wl init` (`src/commands/init.ts`, `WORKLOG_AGENT_TEMPLATE_RELATIVE_PATH = 'templates/AGENTS.md'`) copies `templates/AGENTS.md` to `<projectRoot>/AGENTS.md`, prefixed with the pointer line `WORKLOG_AGENT_POINTER_LINE`. If AGENTS.md exists: idempotent no-op when the pointer is present, otherwise interactive prompt O (overwrite) / A (append pointer) / M (manual) or `--agents-template` flag.
- SorraAgents `scripts/install_pi.sh` symlinks `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` → `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` and installs global skills; the global file contains the full agent workflow.
- `templates/AGENTS.md` and `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` overlap substantially: both carry CRITICAL RULES, work-item Types, priorities, and workflow guidance — confirmed drift risk.
- SorraAgents has already adopted the "reference global instead of duplicating" model (SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G, SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W, SA-0MSITKOXI007XD4N — completed); ContextHub's template has not followed.
- Docs coverage of the install is minimal: `docs/tutorials/01-your-first-work-item.md` mentions the AGENTS.md prompt only briefly.

## Desired change

A documented, verified description of the current install model, the local-vs-global relationship, and a recommendation (single-source-of-truth via delegation to the SorraAgents global install, implemented under WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514, vs. keeping the current model with rationale). No behavioral change in this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk**: the natural fix (delegate to the global install) is already tracked by WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514; implementation ideas found during investigation must be recorded as comments/links on that item, not implemented here.
- **Staleness risk**: if the sibling implementation lands before this investigation completes, the documented behavior may no longer match `wl init`; mitigation — cross-reference both items and refresh the doc when either changes.
- **Assumption**: current `wl init` behavior matches `src/commands/init.ts` and its tests (implementer must re-verify against the code, not just this brief).
- **Standalone vs global environments**: document both — machines with and without the SorraAgents global install — since the recommendation only applies when the global file exists.

## Key Files:

- `src/commands/init.ts` — install flow: `ensureAgentTemplateInstalled`, `promptAgentTemplateAction`, `WORKLOG_AGENT_POINTER_LINE`, `WORKLOG_AGENT_TEMPLATE_RELATIVE_PATH`
- `templates/AGENTS.md` — the installed template; compare against `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` for overlap
- `templates/WORKFLOW.md` — workflow template also installed by `wl init`
- `test/` or `tests/` for `init.ts` — validate documented behavior
- `docs/tutorials/01-your-first-work-item.md` — existing minimal docs to extend
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` + `scripts/install_pi.sh` — global install mechanism (reference)
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — check for AGENTS-related install notes

## Related work

- WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514 — "Align wl init with SorraAgents install: delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup instead of duplicating" (open, task) — the implementation counterpart; this investigation informs/validates its direction.
- WL-0MLD6N0GW12MNKK0 — "wl init: prefer global AGENTS.md pointer" (completed) — established the pointer-line behavior this item documents.
- WL-0MKVRI3580RXZ54H — "Add unattended options to wl init" (completed) — `--agents-template` flag behavior.
- SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G / SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W / SA-0MSITKOXI007XD4N — SorraAgents-side dedup/global-reference items (completed, in SorraAgents worklog).
- SA-0MSLK7LGA003J0KP — "Compact AGENTS_GLOBAL.md to ≤8 KB (F4)" (blocked) — relevant to global-file size/drift pressure.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is there a sibling item already proposing the single-source-of-truth implementation?" — Answer (Map, investigation): Yes — WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514 (open) proposes delegating agent-guidance setup to the SorraAgents install. Research: `wl search "wl init"` and `wl search "AGENTS install template"` on the ContextHub worklog. This item is therefore scoped to investigation + documentation + recommendation; implementation is out of scope here.
- Q: "What issue type fits?" — Answer (Map, investigation): `task` (investigation/documentation) rather than the original `bug` — nothing is currently broken; the drift is a maintainability risk. Research: intake skill issue-type decision guide. Applied via `wl update --issue-type task`.
- Q: "Is intake auto-complete justified?" — Answer (Map, investigation): Yes — the item already has a user story, explicit investigation questions, 4 measurable ACs and a suggested approach. Research: intake skill heuristics; auto-completed via `intake.py auto-complete`.
- OPEN QUESTION: "Should this investigation block the sibling implementation WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514, or run in parallel?" — No answer yet; default assumption is parallel (both are `idea` stage; the sibling does not depend on this item's findings to start).

## Related work (automated report)

Generated by find-related (WL-0MSKEJK4G008BMS0): automated keyword search surfaced no strongly-related work items beyond those listed manually above (top matches — WL-0MNX8MASB007TADZ, WL-0MSKSMM5E002O35Q, WL-0MLX62TQH1PTRA4R — concern test/audit/UI topics, not the AGENTS.md install model; repo matches were incidental keyword overlaps). Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MSKEJK4G008BMS0.md` (deleted after intake; see comments for traceability).

## User story

As a producer reviewing work items in the herdr worklist, I want the detail view description and the `Episode file (md viewer)` pane to render real markdown (headings hierarchy, bold/italic, inline code, links, tables, ordered/nested lists, blockquotes) so my episode `.podcast.md` files and GFM-heavy descriptions read properly instead of as raw text.

## Current state

- **Detail view description** (`formatDetailContent`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` ~line 1076): raw line-splitting + wrap + `[NOTE <id>: ...]` link substitution only. No tables, bold/italic, inline code, links, lists, or headings rendered.
- **md viewer** (`renderMarkdownViewer`, `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts`): hand-rolled minimal renderer supporting only YAML frontmatter skip, fenced code blocks, ATX headings (all levels rendered identically), top-level `-*+` bullet lists, and paragraphs. Missing: tables, ordered lists, nested lists, blockquotes, inline code, bold/italic, links, horizontal rules.

## Proposed approach

Replace the hand-rolled parsing with a proper markdown renderer while keeping the existing pure-function, dependency-injectable design (tests inject `readFile`; no terminal/pane harness):

- Add **`marked`** (v18.x — already in the pi agent dependency tree, so compatibility is proven) as a dependency of `packages/herdr`, with a **custom renderer** that emits ANSI-styled terminal lines (headings bold/distinct levels, `codespan`/`code` glyphs, links underlined/colored, tables as aligned columns, blockquotes indented, ordered lists numbered). Alternative: `marked-terminal` if a ready-made terminal renderer fits better. Decide in planning; document the choice.
- Thread the renderer through both call sites: the description section of `formatDetailContent` and `renderFileViewer` → `renderMarkdownViewer`.
- Preserve the existing `[NOTE <id>: ...]` → `<id>↗` link behavior (`renderNoteLinks`) inside rendered output — likely via a marked extension/custom token renderer so NOTE markers stay clickable in both views.
- Keep YAML frontmatter skipping in the md viewer, the `Related Docs` ToC, and the keyboard nav (`↑↓/j:k`, `Enter`, `g/G`) unchanged.
- Note: herdr panes run with cwd = plugin source dir; `marked` must be a declared dependency of `packages/herdr` (installed into `packages/herdr/node_modules` and reflected in `dist/` build), not assumed from a parent node_modules.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts` — `renderMarkdownViewer`, `renderNoteLinks`, `NOTE_MARKER_RE`; the renderer replacement lives here.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatDetailContent` (description section ~line 1076), `renderFileViewer` (~line 1162), `firstMarkdownKeyFile` (~line 1185).
- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.test.ts` — existing Key Files md viewer tests (injected `readFile`); extend with GFM rendering cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — TUI-level tests (chord/smart-selection/needsProducerReview guards must stay green).
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — new `marked` dependency.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — `Markdown viewer` section (line ~425) documents supported constructs; update for full GFM support and the new dependency.

Related: WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q (md viewer Key Files path-resolution fix), OSL-0MSDYOVP6005T1X5 (original md viewer feature).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The detail view description renders GFM: at least tables (aligned columns), bold, italic, inline code, links, and lists — verified by unit tests rendering a sample GFM description.
- [ ] The md viewer renders the full set of GFM constructs used in `.podcast.md` files: heading hierarchy, ordered + nested bullet lists, blockquotes, tables, inline code, bold/italic, links — verified by unit tests.
- [ ] `[NOTE <id>: ...]` markers still render as `<id>↗` links in both the description and the md viewer (regression, existing tests stay green).
- [ ] YAML frontmatter still skipped in the md viewer; `Related Docs` ToC and keyboard navigation behavior unchanged (TUI-level tests pass).
- [ ] `marked` is a declared dependency of `packages/herdr` and the plugin builds/runs with it (repo-root `npm test` = `vitest run` covers `packages/herdr`; `tsc` clean).
- [ ] `packages/herdr/README.md` Markdown viewer section updated to document supported GFM constructs and the renderer dependency.
