# Intake Brief: Add issue-type gating to herdr shortcuts; limit code-focused shortcuts to code work item types

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist plugin's chord shortcut system
(`packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` + `shortcut-config.ts`) gates shortcuts
by chord keys, `view`, `stages`, `model`, and `code_freeze` — but has **no
work-item-type (issueType) gating**. Every bundled shortcut (`n` intake,
`p` plan, `i` implement, `a-a`/`a-y`/`a-r` audit, `r` producer-review,
`u-*` updates, `x-*` close/delete, `P-*` prompts, `f-*` filters) is visible
on every work item regardless of its issue type. Consumer projects that use
non-code work item types (e.g. open_source_llm's `podcast` episodes) see
code-workflow chords (`n`/`p`/`i`) on items where they are the wrong tools —
and podcast-progression chords (defined in the consumer's project-local
`shortcuts.json`, see OSL-0MSKFXM380098LFL) cannot be restricted to podcast
items. This item adds an issue-type allowlist field to shortcut entries and
applies it to the code-focused bundled shortcuts so they appear only on code
work item types.

## Users

Producers and agents using the herdr worklist plugin in projects with mixed
work item types (code + non-code such as podcast).

**Example user stories:**

- As a podcast producer, when I select a `podcast`-typed work item in herdr,
  I want the code workflow chords (`n`/`p`/`i`) to be absent so I cannot
  accidentally run a code intake/plan/implement against an episode.
- As a plugin maintainer, I want bundled defaults to restrict code-focused
  shortcuts to code types (`bug`, `feature`, `task`, `chore`, `epic`) so all
  consumer projects inherit the fix without editing the bundle.
- As a consumer-project operator, I want to add my own chords gated to my own
  issue type (e.g. `podcast`) via the existing project-local
  `<worklogRoot>/shortcuts.json` mechanism — no plugin edits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `ShortcutEntry` gains an optional `workItemTypes` allowlist field
  (JSON key `work_item_types`, parsed to `workItemTypes` following the
  existing `code_freeze`→`codeFreeze` convention); invalid values are logged
  and treated as omitted (never crash, mirroring `code_freeze` handling).
- [ ] AC2 — Registry filtering honors the allowlist when the caller supplies
  the selected item's `issueType`: `lookupChordEntry`, `getEntriesForStage`,
  `getChordByPrefix`, and the footer/help hint paths exclude an entry whose
  `workItemTypes` is present and does not include the item's type. When no
  `issueType` is supplied (or the entry has no allowlist), behavior is
  unchanged from today.
- [ ] AC3 — The selected item's `issueType` (already fetched in
  `fetcher.ts`) is threaded through the `worklist.ts` shortcut lookup/hint
  call sites (currently ~5 sites: lookupChordEntry at 1330/2726,
  getChordByPrefix at 1340/2805, getEntriesForStage at 2924).
- [ ] AC4 — The bundled code-focused shortcuts `n` (intake), `p` (plan), and
  `i` (implement) carry `work_item_types: ["bug","feature","task","chore",
  "epic"]`; `i` keeps its existing `code_freeze: "block"`. All other bundled
  shortcuts (generic `u-*`, `x-*`, `a-*`, `r`, `c`, `s`, `P-*`, `f-*`)
  remain untyped (available on all types).
- [ ] AC5 — Plugin unit tests cover: parsing `work_item_types` (valid,
  invalid, missing), allowlist filtering on all lookup methods, and the
  bundled `n`/`p`/`i` restrictions (extending `shortcut-config.test.ts` /
  `worklist.test.ts`); full ContextHub `npm test` suite passes.
- [ ] AC6 — Plugin README documents the new `work_item_types` field, its
  naming convention, and the bundled code-shortcut restriction.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from the above — it is managed
> automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Backward compatibility:** entries without `work_item_types` behave
  exactly as today; a missing `issueType` at lookup time must not hide any
  shortcut. No consumer project is broken by the plugin change alone.
- **Naming:** JSON uses snake_case (`work_item_types`) matching
  `code_freeze`; the TS interface uses camelCase (`workItemTypes`) matching
  `codeFreeze`.
- **Scope:** this item only adds the gating capability + restricts the three
  bundled code-workflow chords. Consumer-specific chords (podcast) live in
  consumer project-local `shortcuts.json` files (see OSL-0MSKFXM380098LFL).
- **Cross-worklog dependency:** WL ↔ OSL dependencies cannot be recorded via
  `wl dep`; tracked via description cross-references.

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 (blast radius):** a bug in allowlist filtering could hide shortcuts
  globally. Mitigation: AC5 requires unit tests on all lookup paths plus
  backward-compat cases (no allowlist / no issueType); default behavior
  unchanged.
- **R2 (call-site plumbing):** the `issueType` must reach ~5 lookup/hint
  sites in `worklist.ts`; missing one causes inconsistent hints vs dispatch.
  Mitigation: thread it at the same places `stage` is threaded today, with
  tests for hint and dispatch paths.
- **A1:** "code related work items" = explicit allowlist `bug`, `feature`,
  `task`, `chore`, `epic` (per operator decision); `podcast` and `docs` are
  excluded.
- **A2:** the bundled restriction targets only `n`/`p`/`i` — the chords that
  dispatch the code lifecycle skills. Audit/approve/reject (`a-*`), producer
  review (`r`), and housekeeping remain available on all types per operator
  decision (hybrid model).

## Existing state

- `ShortcutEntry` (shortcut-config.ts) supports `chord`, `command`, `view`,
  `stages`, `model`, `codeFreeze`; no issue-type field.
- `fetcher.ts` already parses `issueType` onto fetched work items
  (lines 136/222) — available at selection time in the TUI.
- `worklist.ts` performs shortcut lookups at lines 1330, 1340, 2726, 2805,
  2924, passing `view`/`stage`/`codeFreezeActive` but not `issueType`.
- Bundled `src/shortcuts.json` has no `work_item_types` on any entry.
- Project-local override mechanism landed (WL-0MSHUMX5C004NC4O) — local
  `shortcuts.json` merges over bundled defaults; consumer projects can add
  type-gated chords once this field exists.

## Desired change

1. Add `workItemTypes?: string[]` to `ShortcutEntry`; parse
   `work_item_types` in `parseShortcutEntry` (log + ignore invalid, matching
   `code_freeze` handling).
2. Add an `issueType?: string` parameter to the registry lookup/filter
   methods; exclude entries whose allowlist does not include the type.
3. Thread the selected item's `issueType` through the `worklist.ts` call
   sites.
4. Add `"work_item_types": ["bug","feature","task","chore","epic"]` to the
   bundled `n`/`p`/`i` entries.
5. Extend unit tests + README; run the full test suite.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `workItemTypes` field, parsing,
  registry filtering.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — `work_item_types` on `n`/`p`/`i`.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — thread `issueType` into lookups/hints.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts` / `worklist.test.ts` — tests.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the field + bundled restriction.

## Related work

- `Project-specific shortcuts.json for podcast progression (podcast-type
  gated) (OSL-0MSKFXM380098LFL)` — open_source_llm consumer item this item
  blocks; its podcast chords rely on this item's `work_item_types` support.
- `Extensible shortcuts.json: bundled defaults + project-local overrides
  (WL-0MSHUMX5C004NC4O)` — landed prerequisite providing the project-local
  merge mechanism consumer chords are defined through.
- `Add code_freeze field to herdr shortcuts.json to filter shortcut
  availability during code freeze (WL-0MSD81VEL009XHWA)` — precedent for
  adding a per-entry shortcut config field with parse/filter/tests.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (from OSL intake): "For the ContextHub change, how should 'code related
  work items' be defined?" — A (operator, interactive): **(a) Explicit
  allowlist** — code shortcuts only on `bug`, `feature`, `task`, `chore`,
  `epic` (everything else — e.g. `podcast`, `docs` — excluded). Source:
  interactive reply.
- Q2 (from OSL intake): "Which chords should the podcast progression
  shortcuts use?" — A (operator, interactive): **(c) Hybrid** — podcast-
  specific chords for pipeline skills (`w`, `t`, …) while keeping generic
  ones (`u-s`, `u-t`, `x-c`, `a-a`/`a-y`/`a-r`, `f-*`) available; therefore
  this item restricts only the code lifecycle chords `n`/`p`/`i`. Source:
  interactive reply.
- Q3: "Should the bundled audit (`a-*`) / producer-review (`r`) chords also
  be code-restricted?" — A (operator, via Q1/Q2 answers): no — they are
  generic and remain available on all types. Source: inferred from
  interactive answers (recorded as assumption A2).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQFB8N990056T8P** – [test-failure] tests/tui/controller-watch.test.ts > TuiController - Database Watch > always re-renders on watch refresh even when dataset appears unchanged (completed)
- **WL-0MP0Y4DFG007UBJJ** – E2E Agent Flow Tests & UX Parity Checklist (completed)
- **WL-0MQ3LYSPS006V60H** – TUI does not auto-refresh after CLI audit update (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: add, appear, audit, chord, close, code, config, delete, docs, entries, feature, focused, freeze, gating, herdr, implement, intake, issue, item, json, keys, like, limit, non, packages, plan, plugin, podcast, producer, prompts, result, review, shortcut, shortcuts, src, stages, system, task, type, types, updates, view, work, workflow, worklist

# Auto-revert in_review items to plan_complete when marked not ready to close

## Problem Statement

When a work item in the `in_review` stage (status `completed`) is marked "not ready to close" — via `wl update <id> --audit-text "Ready to close: No"` or `wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no` — nothing happens to the item's lifecycle state. The item remains `completed`/`in_review`, which signals to the heartbeat and release tooling that it is awaiting closure. An item whose audit says it is *not* ready to close should no longer be presented as awaiting closure; its stage should revert to `plan_complete` so it returns to the planning queue for further work.

## Users

- **Producers / reviewers** who audit an `in_review` item, find it lacking, and mark it "not ready to close".
  - *As a producer, I want an in_review item I mark as "not ready to close" to drop out of the ready-to-close queue automatically, so it isn't swept up by heartbeat/release tooling.*
- **Agents / automation** that run audits and write `Ready to close: No` verdicts.
  - *As an agent, I want the lifecycle state to stay consistent automatically when I mark an item not ready, so I don't have to remember to reset status/stage manually.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When `wl update <id> --audit-text "Ready to close: No"` is run on an item with stage `in_review` (status `completed`), the item is automatically reverted to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`.
2. When `wl audit-set <id> --ready-to-close no` is run on an item with stage `in_review` (status `completed`), the item is automatically reverted to status `open` / stage `plan_complete`.
3. The item's priority is unchanged by the reversion (priority is preserved, not reset).
4. No reversion occurs when the item is not in the `in_review`/`completed` state (e.g., `done` stage, or already `open`/`in-progress`), or when the audit verdict is "Ready to close: Yes" — behavior is otherwise unchanged.
5. The reversion is reported: JSON output includes the reverted item's `from`/`to` status and stage, and human-readable output prints a summary line (e.g. `[WL-XXX reverted from completed/in_review to open/plan_complete]`), following the reporting style of the priority-downgrade cascade.
6. Unit tests cover: reversion via `--audit-text`, reversion via `audit-set`, no-op on `done` items, no-op on non-in_review items, no-op on "Ready to close: Yes", and priority preservation.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The reversion must only fire on the "not ready to close" verdict (`Ready to close: No` / `--ready-to-close no`), not on any other audit text.
- The transition must respect `statusStageCompatibility`: `open` status already permits `plan_complete` stage, so the target state is valid per existing rules.
- The audit write must remain best-effort; if the reversion's `db.update` fails (e.g., file lock), the command should not crash — surface a warning (mirroring the sibling demotion item's best-effort guidance).
- The audit text write path must not be blocked by the existing "skip db.update() when no fields changed" safety guard in `update.ts` — the reversion is an intentional lifecycle consequence of the audit verdict, not an accidental field change.

## Existing State

- `wl update --audit-text` writes to the `audit_results` table via `db.saveAuditResult()` in `src/commands/update.ts` (~line 219–246); a safety guard skips `db.update()` when no work-item fields changed (~line 358).
- `wl audit-set` writes the audit result in `src/commands/audit-result.ts` (~line 154–165) without touching status/stage.
- The API-level audit write path in `src/api.ts` (`normalizeUpdateInputWithAudit`, `writeAuditResult`) also persists audit results without lifecycle changes.
- `statusStageCompatibility` in `config.defaults.yaml`: `open: [idea, intake_complete, plan_complete, in_progress]` — `open`/`plan_complete` is a valid combination.
- Sibling item WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6 implements the same demotion pattern (`completed`/`in_review` → `open`/`plan_complete`) triggered by adding a child — same target state, different trigger, and shares the reporting convention.

## Desired Change

Implement the reversion as a shared helper (e.g., `revertToPlanComplete(item, db)` or similar) called after an audit write whenever the verdict is not-ready-to-close and the item's stage is `in_review` / status `completed`:

1. **`src/commands/update.ts`** — after a successful `db.saveAuditResult` when the parsed verdict is `Ready to close: No`, check the item state and revert if `in_review`/`completed`.
2. **`src/commands/audit-result.ts`** — in the `audit-set` action, after `db.saveAuditResult` when `--ready-to-close no`, apply the same reversion.
3. **`src/api.ts`** — decide whether the API audit write path (`writeAuditResult` / `normalizeUpdateInputWithAudit`) should also trigger the reversion for consistency; if yes, apply the same helper.
4. **Reporting** — extend JSON output with a `reverted` field (`{ from: { status, stage }, to: { status, stage } }`) and add a human summary line, following the priority-downgrade cascade style.
5. **Tests** — add unit/integration tests covering AC 1–6 (see `tests/cli/audit-results-cli.test.ts`, `tests/cli/audit.test.ts`, and any update-command test files).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — `--audit-text` write path; add reversion after not-ready verdict
- `src/commands/audit-result.ts` — `wl audit-set` action; add reversion after `--ready-to-close no`
- `src/api.ts` — API-level audit write path; apply reversion for consistency (decision needed)
- `src/audit.ts` — audit parsing helpers (`inspectAuditFirstLine`, `buildAuditEntry`) already produce the ready-to-close verdict
- `src/persistent-store.ts` — `saveAuditResult` / `getAuditResult`; `update` for the reversion write
- `docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md` — document the reversion behavior
- `tests/cli/audit-results-cli.test.ts`, `tests/cli/audit.test.ts` — audit CLI test coverage

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6** ("Demote completed/in_review parent to plan_complete when a child is added", ContextHub, open/intake_complete) — implements the same `completed`/`in_review` → `open`/`plan_complete` demotion triggered by adding a child. This item is the mirror trigger (not-ready-to-close audit verdict). Shared helper and reporting convention; the two should not conflict.
- **WL-0MMS4EUMU15LEU7B** ("Audit Write Path (CLI/API)", ContextHub, completed) — established the audit write paths that this change hooks into.
- **WL-0MPZNK0UW009CI6C** ("Implementation: wl audit set subcommand", ContextHub, completed) — the `audit-set` command this change extends.
- **WL-0MRSGMTYU009OZCF** ("Add --audit-file to wl audit-set", ContextHub, completed) — related `audit-set` surface area.
- **WL-0MNFSCMDU0075BMH** ("Audit parser rejects valid 'Ready to close' audits; improve error message", ContextHub, completed) — the first-line audit parsing that determines the verdict.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: extending the reversion to the API path (`src/api.ts`) may surface API consumers that depend on audit writes not changing lifecycle state. Mitigation: if the API path proves risky, restrict reversion to the two CLI commands and record API consistency as a separate follow-up item.
- **Assumption**: "not ready to close" means exactly the audit verdict `Ready to close: No` (or `--ready-to-close no`); no other audit text triggers reversion.
- **Assumption**: reversion target is status `open` / stage `plan_complete` per user answers; priority is preserved (user answer: "the medium is for this item, for the items being reset the priority should remain unchanged").
- **Assumption**: reversion is reported in output (JSON field + human line), mirroring the priority-downgrade cascade and the sibling demotion item's reporting convention.
- **Risk**: the existing safety guard in `update.ts` ("skip db.update() when no fields changed") must be deliberately bypassed only for the intentional reversion — implement carefully to avoid accidental transitions on other audit texts.
- **Risk**: batch `wl update` over multiple ids where some are in_review will revert each qualifying item independently; must not break non-qualifying items in the same batch.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: What triggers the "not ready to close" flag — a manual `wl update --stage plan_complete` action by the producer, or automated (heartbeat/audit system detecting issues)? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "wl update command".
- Q: What happens to the item's status? Should it remain `completed` (just the stage reverts), or go back to `in_progress`/`open` so work can resume? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "open".
- Q: Priority reset? The seed intent says `--priority medium` — should this override the item's current priority? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "No the medium is for this item, for the items being reset the priority should remain unchanged" → `medium` is the priority of THIS work item; reverted items keep their priority.
- Q: Where does the "not ready to close" trigger live — Option A (setting `--audit-text "Ready to close: No"` or `wl audit-set --ready-to-close no` on an in_review item automatically reverts) or Option B (new explicit flag/command)? — Answer (user, interactive reply): "A".
- Q: When the item reverts to `open`/`plan_complete`, should status also be `in_progress` (so an agent can claim and continue immediately), or leave it `open` so it must be formally claimed first? — Answer (user, interactive reply): status is `open`; the item must be formally claimed again (consistent with the sibling demotion item WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6).


---

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS6AAW3M004JK9U** – Reselect item after list reorder from status change (completed)
- **WL-0MS9HIUE0002JAKQ** – Leave command-output pane open after successful !/!! command so output is inspectable (completed)
- **WL-0MSKCRX730052IIW** – Herdr: in_review stage filter (f-r) shows 0 items because stage-filtered fetch restricts to status=open (open)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-auto-revert-in-review-not-ready-to-close-WL-0MSKHYI5U0069FVV.md` — matched: auto, close, complete, intent, item, items, marked, plan, ready, revert, review, seed, should, stage, when
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSDZ64J8005Q2JJ-grid-rebalance-python-tests-mocked-socke/CLI.md` — matched: auto, close, complete, item, items, marked, plan, ready, returned, review, should, stage, when
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSGAEC5N006W5QA-wire-read-commands-through-cache-spawn-i/CLI.md` — matched: auto, close, complete, item, items, marked, plan, ready, returned, review, should, stage, when

# Intake Draft — Create shortcut to open Pi session without prompt (WL-0MSKIL6P00045UOC)

## Problem statement

The Worklog TUI shortcut palette has `P-p` (free-form prompt via command input form) and `P-a` (audit-gaps prompt), but no way to open a brand-new, blank Pi agent session with one chord. A user who wants a fresh session must either run `pi` elsewhere or trigger a shortcut that injects prompt text. We need a chord that opens a new Pi agent pane with an **empty prompt** — blank, ready to type.

## Users

Operators who use the Worklog TUI to manage work items and want to open a clean Pi session without typing a prompt or attaching a work item.

- As a Worklog TUI user, I want to press `P n` and get a new Pi agent pane with a blank prompt, so I can start a fresh session immediately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A new shortcut entry with chord `P n` exists in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`: command `/prompt:` (empty prompt — no `<prompt>` placeholder, so the command-input form does NOT open), `view: both`, `model: plan`, with a label and description.
- AC2: Pressing `P n` in the Worklog TUI (list or detail view) opens a new Pi agent pane with a blank prompt, ready to type. No form dialog appears and no prompt text is injected.
- AC3: The fresh session carries no work-item context: the command contains no `<id>` placeholder, so no work-item claim happens and no pane↔item association is recorded (consistent with the existing "commands without an ID are not tracked" behavior).
- AC4: The chord is free — no collision with existing chords (`P p`, `P a`, or any other entry) — and `routeCommand('/prompt:')` returns `agent`, dispatching via the agent channel.
- AC5: Existing `P p` / `P a` behavior is unchanged.
- AC6: Unit tests updated: `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` binds test extended to cover `P n` (command, view, model, route), and the "free chord for /prompt: entries" test still passes with the new entry.
- AC7: `packages/herdr/README.md` (Agent-channel / prompt shortcuts section) documents the `P n` shortcut.
- AC8: Full project test suite passes with the new changes (pytest + Node, quiet mode).

## Constraints

- Follow the existing shortcut schema in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` (chord, command, view, label, description, model).
- Do not add net-new mechanisms unless required — an empty `/prompt:` command already routes to the agent channel and strips to an empty prompt via `stripAgentPromptPrefix` (see `buildSendToPiArgs` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`).
- No work-item claim / pane association for this shortcut (no `<id>`).
- Priority: high (user-specified).

## Existing state

- `P p` (`/prompt:<prompt>`) opens the command-input form (the `<prompt>` unknown identifier triggers `FormState`); `P a` (`/prompt:What are the audit gaps reported in the most recent audit for <id>`) injects a fixed prompt with the selected item ID substituted.
- `routeCommand` routes any command starting with `/prompt:` to the agent channel ('agent'), and `buildSendToPiArgs` strips the `/prompt:` prefix so pi receives the bare prompt text.
- The form dialog only opens when the resolved command contains unknown `<identifier>` placeholders (`hasUnknownIdentifiers`). An empty `/prompt:` command has no placeholders → dispatches immediately with no form.

## Desired change

- Add one entry to `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`:

  ```json
  {
    "chord": ["P", "n"],
    "command": "/prompt:",
    "view": "both",
    "label": "new session",
    "description": "Open a new Pi agent session with a blank prompt.",
    "model": "plan"
  }
  ```

- Extend the P-chord binding test in `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` and update `packages/herdr/README.md`.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — Add the `P n` entry (empty `/prompt:` command, model `plan`, view `both`).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — Extend the "binds P-p to the free-form prompt and P-a to the audit-gaps prompt" test (or add a sibling) to assert `P n` binds to `/prompt:`, view `both`, model `plan`, and routes to `agent`.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Document the `P n` shortcut in the agent-channel / prompt-shortcuts section.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — Verify only; `stripAgentPromptPrefix('/prompt:')` yields `''`, which flows through `buildSendToPiArgs` unchanged. No code change expected unless the empty-prompt path needs hardening.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — Verify only; an empty command argument still satisfies the `$# -eq 0` guard and runs `pi ''`.

## Related work

- `Add per-shortcut option to control whether a shortcut opens a command pane` (WL-0MSJLD1I70045ZUL) — open, related-to: controls pane behavior per shortcut, orthogonal to this blank-session shortcut.
- `Chord shortcut key system for Pi extension` (WL-0MQDZBKO9003CD8K) — completed; foundation for chord dispatch this entry builds on.
- Existing `P p` (free-form prompt) and `P a` (audit gaps prompt) shortcut entries in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "No project context" is satisfied by a blank prompt and no work-item association (per user answer Q2: completely fresh — no work-item, no project context). The pane still spawns in the resolved project root (`--cwd` from `send-to-pi.sh`, which requires a working directory) and `pi` will load its normal startup context; the shortcut itself injects nothing and attaches nothing.
- **Risk:** If `pi ''` with an empty quoted argument is treated as a non-empty prompt or errors, the implementation may need to omit the trailing argument in `buildSendToPiArgs`/`send-to-pi.sh` for the empty case. Mitigation: verify behavior of `send-to-pi.sh` with an empty command during implementation; add a unit test for `buildSendToPiArgs('/prompt:', ...)`.
- **Risk (scope creep):** This item is deliberately minimal (one shortcut entry + tests + docs). If a user later wants truly context-free sessions (spawn outside the project root, skip AGENTS.md), that is a separate work item — do not expand scope here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should the fresh session do? (a) Open a new Pi agent pane with an empty prompt (blank, ready to type)? (b) Open a new Pi agent pane and immediately start talking to the model? (c) Something else?" — Answer (user): **(a)** blank pane, ready to type. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What context should the fresh session have? (a) Start completely fresh (no work-item, no project context)? (b) Inherit the currently selected work-item? (c) Include the full project context (like a normal Pi session)?" — Answer (user): **(a)** completely fresh. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should this replace the existing `P p` shortcut, or use a different key combination?" — Answer (user): **use `P n`**. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Which model should the fresh session use? (a) default model, or (b) `plan` model matching existing P-chords?" — Answer (user): **(b)** `plan` model. Source: interactive reply.

## Summary

The shared test runner (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) defines a static `NODE_SUITE_DIRS = ("tests/node", "tests/cli", "tests/unit")`. ContextHub has no `tests/node` directory (git ls-files confirms it was never tracked), so the canonical full-suite command `npm --silent test -- tests/node` always exits 1 with 'No test files found'.

## Impact

The audit skill's automatic full-suite verification (SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W) queries the per-repo test cache for EVERY canonical suite command and requires exit code 0. The permanently-failing `tests/node` entry means the audit runner can NEVER inject automatic green-run evidence for ContextHub audits — execution-dependent acceptance criteria (e.g. 'Full project test suite passes') stay `partial` and block closure.

## Workaround used in release v1.0.9

Operator ran pytest (103 passed) + `npx vitest run` (4117 passed) at the release HEAD and passed `--green-run HEAD` to each audit — honest attestation, but manual.

## Suggested fix

Either (a) filter `NODE_SUITE_DIRS` by directory existence in the shared runner, or (b) make ContextHub's suite definition explicit. Discovered during release v1.0.9 remediation (discovered-from:WL-0MSG80FQ9000C8GE).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The canonical full-suite command set for ContextHub (as resolved by `full_suite_commands()`) matches the suites that actually exist in the repo.
- [ ] `run_tests.py --summary --suite all` reports green for every suite in the canonical set at a green HEAD.

# Herdr: add/remove/edit inline notes on any markdown document

## Problem statement

Herdr's generic markdown viewer renders `.podcast.md` scripts and any `.md` Key File in a **read-only** preview: inline `[NOTE <id>: ...]` markers (PRD §7.1) render as clickable `<id>↗` links, but a human reviewer cannot **add, edit, or delete** a note on a paragraph while reviewing the document. This feature adds an interactive note-edit mode to the markdown viewer so any markdown document can be annotated in place with `[NOTE <id>: ...]` markers — not just podcast scripts.

## Users

- **Podcast producer** — reviewing a `.podcast.md` script; wants to move the cursor onto a paragraph and press a key to add/edit an inline `[NOTE ...]` marker with editorial feedback, without leaving Herdr.
- **General reviewer** — annotating any markdown file (wiki pages, docs, other `.md` Key Files) with the same mechanism.

### User stories

- As a podcast producer, I want to review a `.podcast.md` script, move the cursor onto a paragraph, and press a key to add or edit an inline `[NOTE ...]` marker on that paragraph, so I can give editorial feedback without leaving Herdr.
- As a reviewer, I want to press another key to delete an existing note from a paragraph, so I can withdraw or clear feedback.
- As a user, I want this to work on any markdown file (not just podcast scripts), so I can annotate docs, wiki pages, and other `.md` content with the same mechanism.

## Expected behaviour

1. In the markdown viewer, the cursor can select any paragraph/block of the document (paragraph-by-paragraph or line-based selection within a paragraph).
2. An add/edit key chord on the selected paragraph opens an input form: pre-filled with the existing note text if the paragraph already carries a `[NOTE <id>: ...]` marker (edit mode), otherwise empty (add mode).
3. Saving writes the marker inline in the paragraph at a stable position, following the PRD §7.1 convention `[NOTE <id>: ...]` — `<id>` is a Worklog note-child id when the document is linked to an episode work item; a local placeholder scheme otherwise.
4. A delete key chord removes the existing note marker from the selected paragraph.
5. The edited markdown is written back to the file (surgical edit — all other content preserved), and the viewer reflects the change.
6. Non-podcast markdown documents behave identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Cursor navigation in the markdown viewer can select any paragraph/block of a `.md` document.
- [ ] Add/edit on a selected paragraph with no existing note creates an inline `[NOTE <id>: ...]` marker with the entered text.
- [ ] Add/edit on a paragraph that already has a note opens the form pre-filled with the current note text; saving updates the marker in place.
- [ ] Delete on a paragraph with a note removes the marker from the file.
- [ ] The edited document is persisted to disk and the viewer reflects the change; all other file content is preserved byte-for-byte.
- [ ] Behaviour works identically for any markdown file, not only podcast scripts.
- [ ] Existing inline-note link rendering (`<id>↗`) still works after edits.
- [ ] When editing a podcast script with a known episode id, note-child work items are created/resolved per PRD §7.3 (`wl create --parent <episode>` on add; `DONE` marker + resolution comment on delete/resolve).
- [ ] Automated tests cover add, edit, delete, and persistence for both podcast and generic markdown documents.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (README "Generic md viewer" / "Inline note links" sections, code comments).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing generic markdown viewer (`packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts`), chord/shortcut machinery (`shortcuts.json`, `src/shortcut-config.ts`), and modal form-dialog machinery (`src/form-dialog.ts`).
- Marker format must follow PRD §7.1 exactly: `[NOTE <id>: ...]` inline in the paragraph; resolved notes use `[NOTE <id>: DONE ...]` (§7.3). Note text may span multiple lines and runs to the first `]` (`NOTE_MARKER_RE` in `md-viewer.ts`).
- Note-child sync applies only when the document is a podcast script with a resolvable episode work item id; for generic markdown use a local placeholder id scheme and skip `wl` child creation (never silently skip when an episode *is* resolvable — mirror the podcast-script skill's warning behaviour).
- File path resolution for both read and write-back must follow the existing `resolveKeyFilePath` convention (WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q): resolve against the worklog root, not the plugin process CWD.
- Writer must be side-effect-free/testable like the rest of `md-viewer.ts` (pure functions with dependency-injected file reader/writer where practical).

## Existing state

- `md-viewer.ts` renders read-only: `renderNoteLinks()` rewrites `[NOTE <id>: ...]` markers to `<id>↗` links; `renderMarkdown()` / `renderMarkdownViewer()` produce ANSI viewer lines (frontmatter skipped for file bodies).
- The detail view embeds the viewer via `renderFileViewer()` in `src/worklist.ts`; navigation is currently scroll-based (`[↑↓/j:k] scroll`, `[g/G] top/bot`, `[esc] back`, `[q] quit`) with a focus model (`detailToCFocus`) distinguishing ToC from document scroll region.
- Chord commands already drive modal full-pane form input for unknown `<identifier>` placeholders (`form-dialog.ts`); `<id>` is an auto-resolved known identifier.

## Desired change

Interactive note editing on top of the existing viewer: add a cursor/selection model over markdown blocks, wire add/edit/delete chords through the existing shortcut registry, reuse the form dialog for note text entry (pre-filled in edit mode), persist edits back to the file, and (for podcast scripts with a known episode id) drive the PRD §7.3 note-child lifecycle through the `wl` CLI.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.ts` — NOTE-marker detection/extraction helpers; possible insert/update/remove helpers for markers within a paragraph (or a new sibling module, e.g. `md-note-edit.ts`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — viewer pane integration: paragraph cursor/selection, chord handling, write-back, episode-id resolution and note-child sync.
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — reuse/extend modal form for note text entry (pre-filled in edit mode).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` / `src/shortcut-config.ts` — new chords for add/edit note and delete note.
- `packages/herdr/src/md-viewer.test.ts` (and/or a new test module) — add/edit/delete/persistence tests for podcast and generic markdown.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document the new interactive note-edit mode in the "Generic md viewer" / "Inline note links" sections.

## Related work

- WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29 — Related Docs row + open in viewer (completed) — introduced the md viewer entry points.
- WL-0MSGEA9AY0080V4Q — md viewer path resolution against worklog root (completed) — `resolveKeyFilePath` convention to reuse for write-back.
- WL-0MSKFFJWD002BQJ5 — proper markdown renderer (completed) — the GFM rendering stack being extended.
- WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I — detail view ToC (completed) — focus/scroll model precedent (`detailToCFocus`, ToC vs document region).
- WL-0MSHWHP0S0036DDU — tests: Related Docs row, detail ToC, open-in-viewer (completed) — existing test patterns for the viewer.
- WL-0MSNSZ4R6009AU0N — herdr plugin `npm run build` fails (TS6059 rootDir violations from test files) (open) — **blocker**: build currently fails, so the "full test suite passes" criterion cannot be verified until fixed.
- `.pi/skills/wiki-podcast-script/SKILL.md` (open_source_llm) — `[NOTE <id>: ...]` marker convention (PRD §7.1) and note-child lifecycle (PRD §7.3); reference only, unchanged by this feature.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Keybinding conflict** — the description's suggested `n` chord likely collides with the existing `/intake` chord in the worklist view (`shortcuts.json`). Assumption: implementer verifies the chord registry and picks non-conflicting chords (possibly view-scoped). Flag for decision at implementation, not a blocking question.
- **Local placeholder id scheme** — unspecified for generic markdown; assumption: implementer defines a documented, stable scheme (e.g. `LOCAL-<seq>`), kept idempotent across re-opens where practical.
- **File-write safety** — write-back must be a surgical paragraph-level edit preserving all other file content; recommend a test asserting byte-level preservation of untouched sections.
- **Marker-parsing edge cases** — `NOTE_MARKER_RE` is non-greedy to the first `]`, so note text containing `]` (or `[NOTE`) would parse incorrectly; implementer should document this limitation and, where practical, prevent/escape such content in the editor.
- **Scope-creep risk** — keep note-child sync limited to podcast scripts with a resolvable episode id; generic markdown stays local-only. Extra opportunities (note list panel, cross-file annotation, undo history) should be filed as separate work items, not folded into this one.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Any interview questions? — Answer (intake, `Map`): **No interview required.** The existing work-item description (created 2026-08-08, updated 2026-08-13) already contains a summary, three user stories, expected behaviour, a suggested implementation approach, nine acceptance criteria, and references — sufficient seed context to draft the brief directly. Source: WL-0MSKV6SKK008MMXR description.
- Assumption: keybinding choice and local placeholder id scheme left as implementer decisions (see Risks & assumptions) — flagged, not blocking.

## Summary

`wl sync`'s merge logic can enter a self-sustaining conflict loop that silently corrupts item state. Observed in the field (LP-0MSDRRPV0001TCLX in /home/rgardler/projects/llm): a completed, audit-approved item's local `updatedAt` advanced at every sync (21:36:19Z → 21:53:40Z → 21:57:35Z) and the final sync chose a local `deleted` state (empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason`) over the remote `open` state — soft-deleting the item while the remote `worklog/data` ref still had it `open`/`plan_complete`. No agent ran `wl delete`; the state arose purely from merge behavior. The item had to be manually restored via `StatusLifecycle`.

## Root-cause hypothesis (verified against src/sync.ts)

1. **Same-timestamp merge bumps `updatedAt` unconditionally.** `mergeSameTimestampItems` (src/sync.ts ~L423) sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content (e.g. a `sortIndex` conflict from concurrent `wl re-sort`, or any divergent field). This bump makes the item *newer* than the remote on the next sync, so the local value keeps winning and the timestamp keeps advancing on every sync — a conflict loop with no real user edit behind it. Under auto-sync / multi-pane / multi-agent use this can repeat indefinitely.

2. **Unattributed soft-delete wins over a live remote item.** `deleteSingle` (node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts) sets `status: 'deleted'` but leaves `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` empty. In `mergeDifferentTimestampItems`, `status` is resolved by plain timestamp recency: `status='deleted'` is a non-default value, so if the local copy is (artifactually) newer, `status` flips to `deleted` even though `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` are empty — silently soft-deleting an item the remote still considers open. There is no delete-side equivalent of the close-preservation logic that protects `status='completed'`/`stage='done'`.

## Expected behaviour

- Repeated syncs of the same divergent state must converge: once both sides hold the merged item, `updatedAt` must stop advancing and the item must not flip-flop.
- An unattributed delete marker (status='deleted' with empty deletedBy/deleteReason) must never override a remote item that is open/in-progress/completed. Deletes should only propagate when they are real, attributed deletes (non-empty deletedBy or deleteReason), mirroring the close-preservation model.

## Suggested approach

- In `mergeSameTimestampItems`, only bump `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field (or converge without bumping when the merged result equals one side). Consider whether `sortIndex` conflicts alone should bump at all.
- Add delete-side protection in `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` (and same-timestamp path): treat `status='deleted'` like `status='completed'` — require the delete to be the newer change AND attributed (deletedBy/deleteReason non-empty) before propagating it; otherwise keep the remote live status.
- Add regression tests in tests/sync.test.ts reproducing both failure modes.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing only in `sortIndex` or one metadata field) synced repeatedly converge — `updatedAt` stops advancing after the merged state is present on both sides (no unbounded bumping).
- AC2: Regression test: local `status='deleted'` with empty `deletedBy`/`deleteReason` vs remote `status='open'` — merge keeps the remote `open` state (or at minimum never produces a soft-deleted item with no attribution).
- AC3: Regression test: an *attributed* delete (non-empty `deletedBy`) that is newer than the remote still propagates (delete remains possible when intentional).
- AC4: Full existing test suite (npm test) passes with no regressions.

## Key Files

- `src/sync.ts` — Contains `mergeSameTimestampItems` and `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` functions that need modification
- `src/sync/merge-utils.ts` — Merge utility functions (`isDefaultValue`, `stableValueKey`, etc.)
- `tests/sync.test.ts` — Existing sync tests; new regression tests should be added here
- `node_modules/@worklog/shared/src/database.ts` — `deleteSingle` function that creates unattributed deletes

## Related Work

- **WL-0MSOYWZTH003JFVD**: Sync: regression guard — refuse import of default-value regressions from newer remote state
- **WL-0MT2KZH0I005XUWE**: Deletion propagation in delta exports
data.title: Fix sync-conflict loop: same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt indefinitely and unattributed soft-delete wins over remote open item

## Summary

**Re-scoped** follow-up to the completed twin **WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO** (shipped in
v1.0.13, commit `9e8ca646`, epic WL-0MTFNII4X00632CG), which already delivered this
item's original AC1–AC3 (the unbounded same-timestamp conflict loop and the
unattributed-soft-delete override). Those are now shipped; this item is narrowed to the
**residual** that the earlier fix left in place.

**Residual defect:** `mergeSameTimestampItems` still writes a **fresh wall-clock
`updatedAt`** whenever a non-`sortIndex` field is reconciled and the merged result
differs from local (`src/sync.ts` ~L833):

```ts
if (nonSortIndexMerged && !mergedEqualsLocal) {
  merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString();   // <-- wall-clock stamp on a merge
}
```

A merge is not a user edit. Stamping "now" silently re-timestamps audit-fresh items and
marks valid audits stale, and it feeds further timestamp churn on subsequent syncs.

## Problem

Observed on 2026-09-21: a single sync (`18:35:58 → 18:36:17`) logged **244 conflicts**
and re-timestamped **95 items** to `2026-09-21T18:36:06` (48 of them `completed`).
**14 `completed`/`in_review` items lost audit freshness purely from merge churn** — e.g.
*Sync: regression guard…* (`WL-0MSOYWZTH003JFVD`) was audited 2026-08-31, had no activity
since, yet became "stale" because the merge moved `updatedAt`.

Because `updatedAt` underpins `isAuditFresh` (until the content-fingerprint gate lands,
P1), merge churn drives false staleness → redundant downtime re-audits → more writes →
more churn.

## Expected behaviour

- A merge must **never** introduce a wall-clock `updatedAt`. A same-timestamp merge
  inherits an existing timestamp (the two sides are equal by definition), so repeated
  syncs of the same divergence are **quiescent**.
- Merged content still converges on both sides.
- Audit freshness is unaffected by a merge that did not change user-authored content.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `mergeSameTimestampItems` no longer calls `new Date().toISOString()` for
  `updatedAt`; the merged item inherits the (equal) existing timestamp.
- AC2: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing in one
  non-`sortIndex` field) merged repeatedly are quiescent — `updatedAt` never advances and
  content converges.
- AC3: Regression test: a same-timestamp conflict resolved to remote content leaves
  `updatedAt` unchanged and `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` true for a prior valid
  audit.
- AC4: `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` continues to inherit the winning side's timestamp
  (no wall-clock); an explicit assertion is added.
- AC5: Full existing test suite passes, including the sync convergence + delete-protection
  tests shipped under WL-0MTFNII4X00632CG.

## Notes / open questions

- The original bump existed so the merged side would be unambiguously "newer" on the next
  sync. With both sides writing the merged result, convergence should hold without it;
  confirm via the AC2 quiescence test.
- A same-timestamp `sortIndex`-only conflict already never bumps (unchanged).

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- shipped predecessor (do not re-implement): WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO (completed/done,
  v1.0.13, `9e8ca646`), WL-0MTFNII4X00632CG, WL-0MT2KZH0I005XUWE
- related-to: WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K (P1 — content-fingerprint freshness gate)
- evidence: `.worklog/logs/sync.log` (2026-09-21T18:35:58 → 18:36:17)
data.title: Sync merges must not re-timestamp audit-fresh items (remove wall-clock updatedAt bump)

## Goal

As a herdr downtime worker, I want idle detection to reflect LOCAL model activity only, so that remote provider streams (opencode-go → deepseek-v4-flash) — which consume zero local slots — do not prevent downtime dispatch.

## Background

Follow-up to RCA WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7. The proxy's /llama/local/status `active_query` is the GLOBAL counter = any request in flight (local + remote). herdr's parseLlamaStatus() (packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts) maps `active_query` directly, and isIdleStatus() returns false whenever it is true. Live evidence: status active_query=true with 3/3 slots free, no lease, while the only streams in flight are provider=opencode-go (remote). Local Qwen3 is idle but herdr never sees idle.

The proxy is adding `local_active_query` (derived from its local_active_queries counter) — see LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR (llm-manager worklog). This task makes herdr consume it.

## Expected behaviour

1. parseLlamaPayload accepts `local_active_query` (bool) when present and prefers it for idle evaluation when the field exists; falls back to `active_query` when absent (backward compatible with pre-fix proxies).
2. isIdleStatus uses the LOCAL signal — remote-only traffic no longer blocks dispatch.
3. When `local_active_query` is absent, no behavior change (uses active_query path).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] parseLlamaPayload derives/uses local_active_query when present
- [ ] isIdleStatus returns TRUE with local_active_query=false + 3/3 free slots during remote-only traffic (integration test against a stub status payload)
- [ ] isIdleStatus returns FALSE with local_active_query=true (local busy)
- [ ] Backward compatible: payloads without local_active_query behave exactly as today (unit tests unchanged pass)
- [ ] Docs: the LlamaStatus interface comment documents the field semantics

## Related (cross-repo)

- LLM-manager: LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR exposes local_active_query in the payload (this work item must land together or sequence after it; herdr falls back safely either way)
- Parent RCA: WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7
- related-to:LP-0MSL2ZLLS009RVKR, LP-0MSL1OX51003DOP4

# Intake Draft — Herdr selection list: collapsible group headings with item counts

**Work item:** WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94

## Problem statement

The Herdr work-item selection list renders group separators (`── Group 1 ──`, `── Idea ──`, `── In Review ──`) between items, but these heading rows are pure chrome: they carry no item count, they cannot be collapsed to hide a group's items, and up/down navigation skips over them entirely (the cursor can never land on a heading). With several groups on screen this wastes vertical space and gives the user no way to focus on one group.

## Users

- **Herdr plugin users** (operators running the work-item selection list pane).

User stories:
- "As a producer reviewing the worklist, I want each group heading to show how many items it contains, so I can see at a glance where the bulk of the work is."
- "As a producer, I want to collapse a group by pressing Tab while its heading is selected, so I can hide items I'm not interested in and focus on the rest."
- "As a producer, I want up/down navigation to land on heading rows, so I can reach them to collapse/expand them."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Each group heading row displays the label plus the number of items in that group (e.g. `── Group 1 (4) ──`). The count reflects the top-level items assigned to the group in the current view (post stage-filter), regardless of collapse state.
- AC2: Up/down navigation (j/k and arrow keys) moves the selection onto heading rows as well as items; headings are no longer skipped. Page up/down, first/last, and wrap-around behave consistently with the heading rows included.
- AC3: Pressing Tab while a heading row is selected toggles that group's collapse state: collapsed hides the group's items from both the render and navigation; expanded shows them. Tab on an item row keeps its existing expand/collapse-children behaviour unchanged.
- AC4: Collapsed-group state lives in memory for the session (like `expandedItems`), survives list refreshes, and does not persist across pane restarts.
- AC5: When a heading is selected, the metadata panel shows the group info (label + count) rather than stale item metadata; Enter on a heading is a no-op (only Tab toggles).
- AC6: The `rows - 1` line-count invariant, code-freeze banner, metadata-panel sizing, and stage-filter views keep working; full Herdr test suite (vitest for packages/herdr) passes.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and any relevant docs site entries.

## Constraints

- The change is confined to the Herdr plugin (`packages/herdr`) — the Pi TUI Worklog extension has its own browse implementation and is out of scope.
- `packages/herdr` has zero npm dependencies; the implementation must stay self-contained (the existing duplicated `grouping.ts` pattern).
- Tab already toggles hierarchy expand/collapse for items with children — that behaviour must not regress.
- The renderer must never exceed `rows - 1` lines (pane line-count invariant, WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO).

## Existing state

- Group separators are rendered by `createListRenderer` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` when the `group` field changes between items in the flattened list; they are derived at render time and are NOT rows in any navigation model.
- Navigation (`WorkItemListState.moveUp/moveDown/pageUp/pageDown`, `_clampSelection`, `_adjustScroll`, `flatCount`) indexes into the flattened items list, so headings are never selected.
- Tab maps to the `'toggle-expand'` action (`keyToAction`), which expands/collapses top-level items with children; the main TUI loop fetches children on demand for that action.
- Group assignments come from `regroupWorkItems` (packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts), which stamps every selected item with a numeric `group` and a `groupLabel` (`Critical Group N`, `Group N`, `Idea`, `Other`, `In Review`).

## Desired change

Introduce a first-class **display-rows model** in `WorkItemListState` that interleaves heading rows with item rows:

- New heading entry type (e.g. `{ kind: 'heading', group, groupLabel, count, collapsed }`) produced by a `getDisplayRows()`-style method over the flattened items (children of expanded parents included; items of collapsed groups excluded).
- Navigation, clamping, and scrolling operate over display rows so the cursor lands on headings; `getSelectedItem()` returns `null` for a heading selection (metadata panel then renders group info).
- New collapsed-groups state (`Set<number>` in memory) with toggle on Tab when a heading row is selected; refresh carries the set over (by group number, mirroring `expandedItems` handling).
- `createListRenderer` renders heading rows directly from the display model (label + `(count)` + collapse arrow) and stops deriving separators from group transitions; the visible-window budget logic (`countSeparators`) is reworked for heading rows.
- Tab routing: heading row → toggle group; item row → existing expand/collapse-children path (including the on-demand children fetch in the TUI loop).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — display-rows model, heading type, collapse state, navigation over rows, Tab routing, renderer heading rows + counts.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — heading rendering (counts, collapse arrow), navigation onto/over headings, Tab toggle, metadata panel on heading selection.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts` — collapsed groups survive refresh; Tab-on-item children fetch unaffected.

## Assumptions

- "Headings" = the group separator rows (`── <Group Label> ──`) produced by `regroupWorkItems` group assignments. No other heading type exists in the list.
- Count = top-level items in the group in the current view; children of expanded parents do not add to the count (they never carry group metadata).
- Count is shown whether the group is collapsed or expanded.
- Enter on a heading is a no-op; Tab is the only toggle key (per request).
- Collapsed state is in-memory only, consistent with `expandedItems` (no settings persistence).
- Collapse keyed by group number; if a refresh regroups and renumbers groups, the collapsed set may apply to a shifted group — acceptable in-session, same class of behaviour as `expandedItems`.
- **Scope-creep risk:** extending this to the Pi TUI Worklog extension or persisting collapse state to settings would expand scope — record such follow-ups as separate work items rather than folding them in.
- **Regression risk:** reworking the navigation model from `flatCount` (items only) to display rows touches clamping, scroll adjustment, wrap-around, refresh selection-restore, and the renderer's line budget — the existing expand/refresh and line-count tests must stay green.

## Related work

- WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW — Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order): introduced the render-time group separators this feature builds on.
- WL-0MSAKPVR9005B6XJ — Rewrite assignItemGroups + next.ts ordering: canonical group ordering/labelling used by the headings.
- WL-0MS8XOOMN0022LLH — Pi TUI browse flow: re-fetch + heading count: heading counts exist in the Pi TUI browse widget; Herdr parity for counts.
- WL-0MS4L81QF0013081 — Tab key to expand/collapse children in selection browser: established the Tab expand/collapse pattern this feature extends.
- WL-0MSBVBNGH002RDP5 — Herdr worklist: expanded items momentarily collapse on list refresh (flicker): refresh/children handling this feature must preserve.
- WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO — pane line-count invariant (renderer budget) this feature's heading-row accounting must preserve.
- WL-0MS39YPR5005MJ81 — Feature gap analysis: Pi TUI Worklog extension vs Herdr plugin: prior comparison of the two selection lists (find_related automated match).

Automated find_related report: full (untruncated) version persisted at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Should up/down navigation land on heading rows? — Answer (operator): the request notes "moving up and down does not select the heading lines" as the current gap; selectable headings are required for Tab-on-heading to work, so the feature includes heading selection. Source: interactive request.
- Q: What does the count show? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): top-level items in the group, current view, both collapsed and expanded. Source: reasonable default consistent with the data model.
- Q: Should collapsed state persist across restarts? — Answer (assumption documented, no question asked): no — in-memory like `expandedItems`. Source: consistent with existing hierarchy expand state.

# Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions

**Headline:** The herdr downtime worker re-dispatches the same work item more than once. The audit tier selects an already-dispatched item again because the dispatched `/skill:audit` run reverts the item to `completed`/`in_review` without recording a fresh audit, re-exposing it to the candidate query. Fix: exclude items already dispatched by the downtime worker (durable dispatched-marker) from audit-tier selection.

## Problem statement

The herdr downtime worker (`dispatchDowntimeWork` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`) dispatched the same work item for `/skill:audit` **twice**: `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` at `2026-08-09T01:51:29Z` and again at `2026-08-09T10:59:50Z` (both entries in `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`). The item has no valid audit (`auditResult: None`, `auditedAt: None`), so it remains a candidate. Mechanism: the audit tier selects from `wl list --status completed --stage in_review`; the dispatched audit run's verdict lifecycle transitions the item status back to `completed` (stage stays `in_review`) when it finishes, and with no fresh audit recorded the item re-enters the candidate set and is re-dispatched on the next idle window. The plan (`intake_complete → /skill:plan`) and intake (`idea → /skill:intake`) tiers self-guard via stage transitions, so the duplicate is audit-tier-specific.

## Users

- **Operators running herdr worklist panes with the downtime worker enabled** — want at most one automatic dispatch per work item per skill; duplicate sessions waste local-LLM time and create confusing repeated agent panes.
- **User story:** "As an operator, when the downtime worker dispatches `/skill:audit` on an item, I want that item never to be auto-dispatched again (until a human or a fresh audit resolves it), so I don't get multiple identical agent sessions for the same item."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Durable exclusion (regression for the observed duplicate):** `getNextAuditCandidate`/`selectAuditCandidate` never returns an item that was already dispatched by the herdr downtime worker when no fresh valid audit exists since that dispatch. Verified by a unit test reproducing the `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` scenario: an item present in the shared dispatch log (`.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`) with `auditedAt`/`updatedAt` not fresh is excluded, even though it is `completed`/`in_review`.
- [ ] **Composes with audit freshness:** the marker exclusion only suppresses re-dispatch when the item has no fresh audit since its last dispatch; an item whose most recent audit is fresh is governed by the existing `isAuditFresh` logic (fresh → not a candidate, unchanged).
- [ ] **Marker lookup is fail-safe:** a missing or unreadable dispatch log is treated as empty (audit-tier dispatch still works on a fresh worklog); malformed JSONL lines are skipped without failing the lookup or the dispatch.
- [ ] **Scope:** the exclusion applies to the audit tier only; plan/intake tier selection behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] **End-to-end:** with a single unaudited `completed`/`in_review` candidate and two consecutive idle windows (no audit recorded between), the worker dispatches exactly once.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md` (downtime section), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fail-closed dispatch philosophy** (existing module contract): the worker must never dispatch on ambiguous signals and must never crash; logging/lookup failures must be contained. The marker lookup failure mode is deliberately fail-*safe* (allow dispatch on unreadable log) because a missing log is the normal first-run state — blocking dispatch on it would silently disable the audit tier.
- **Durability across status changes:** the marker must survive the item's status reverting to `completed`/`in_review` (the root cause of the re-selection) — a status-based check alone is insufficient.
- **Shared per-worklog root:** all panes using the same worklog root share `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (the `--worklog-dir` override, WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX), so the log-based marker covers same-root multi-pane setups. The log is bounded (`DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 100`); protection windows beyond the roll are out of scope for this item (noted as a risk).
- The existing pre-dispatch claim (`wl update <id> --status in_progress`) and `wl next`'s default exclusion of in-progress items remain unchanged — per the operator's scoping decision this item does **not** rework the claim path (option A, not C).

## Existing state

- `dispatchDowntimeWork` already claims the item (`claimItem` → `wl update <id> --status in_progress --assignee Map`) before the pane spawns, and `wl next` excludes `in_progress` items by default (`filterCandidates`, `includeInProgress=false`). These protect against the same-instant cross-pane race but not against the observed 9-hour re-selection.
- `getNextAuditCandidate` (packages/herdr/src/index.ts) runs `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --json` and `selectAuditCandidate` picks the first item without a fresh audit (`isAuditFresh`), modified within `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_RECENCY_WINDOW_MS` (7 days), sorted by `sortIndex`. There is no exclusion of previously dispatched items.
- Dispatches are already logged durably per worklog root: `appendDowntimeLogEntry` (packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts) writes JSONL entries (`itemId`, `kind`, `dispatchedAt`, `cwd`, `title`) to `<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`; a per-item comment ("Auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker…") is added via `wl comment add` and is the durable cross-machine trail.
- Evidence: `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` in `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` at 01:51:29Z and 10:59:50Z (2026-08-09); item currently `in-progress`/`in_review` with `auditResult: None`.

## Desired change

1. **Add a dispatched-marker exclusion to the audit tier.** In `selectAuditCandidate` (or its caller `getNextAuditCandidate`), exclude candidates whose `itemId` has a downtime-dispatch marker and no fresh audit since. Preferred marker source: the shared rolling dispatch log `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (same worklog root; already written on every dispatch; `dispatchedAt` available for the "since" comparison). The per-item `herdr-downtime` worklog comment is the documented durable cross-machine trail and is the fallback/alternative if a field or comment-based marker is preferred during implementation. The exclusion must compose with `isAuditFresh` (fresh audit → item already excluded by existing logic).
2. **Parse the marker fail-safely.** Missing/unreadable log → empty; malformed lines skipped; no throw, no dispatch-blocking side effects.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Bounded log roll (`DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES = 100`):** if an item sits unaudited while the log rolls past 100 dispatches, the marker is lost and the item could be re-selected. Acceptable for the observed recurrence window (hours); documenting the bound and, if cheap, preferring the durable per-item comment marker (or a field/comment-based marker) mitigates. Out of scope to extend the log bound unless trivially safe.
- **Cross-host duplicates:** the log is per-worklog-root on a single host; two hosts sharing a worklog root over the network could still double-dispatch. The observed duplicate is same-host; cross-host protection (via the synced per-item comment) is a noted extension, not required by this item.
- **Assumption — the exclusion is audit-tier-only.** Plan/intake tiers self-guard via stage transitions; no change to their selection.
- **Scope-creep guard:** claim hardening (verified/atomic claim) and audit-lifecycle changes were explicitly out of scope (operator chose option A). If implementation surfaces a need for them, capture as a new work item rather than expanding this one.
- **Fail-safe lookup:** treating an unreadable/missing log as empty means a corrupted log cannot silently disable the audit tier; the trade-off (a corrupted log also cannot exclude anything) is acceptable.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `selectAuditCandidate` gains the dispatched-marker exclusion; doc comment updates for the audit-tier selection contract.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getNextAuditCandidate` reads the dispatch log (or passes it in) and applies the exclusion; wiring stays fail-closed.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — possibly a read helper for the bounded log (e.g., `readDowntimeLogEntries`); currently only `appendDowntimeLogEntry` exists.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` / `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts` — regression tests: duplicate-scenario exclusion, fail-safe lookup, composition with `isAuditFresh`, single-dispatch end-to-end.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts` — fail-safe `readDowntimeLogEntries` tests (missing/unreadable log → empty; malformed JSONL lines skipped).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — downtime worker docs: audit-tier selection now excludes previously dispatched items.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSGTLSUT002NF29` — the item observed duplicated (dispatched twice for audit, 2026-08-09). Evidence source for this bug.
- `WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG` — audit-tier dispatch (parent of the tier logic that re-selects items).
- `WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8` — dispatch audit logging (the `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` the marker will parse).
- `WL-0MSI9FDPI005Z0BV` — audit-tier downtime dispatch tests (extend with the re-dispatch regression).
- `WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX` — per-worklog-dir candidate selection (why the shared log is per worklog root).
- `WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE` — unify audit-freshness at-or-near logic across icon display and downtime dispatcher (open; related freshness logic).
- `WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7` — RCA of zero-dispatch night; documents the multi-pane poller environment where duplicates can occur.
- `WL-0MSG7ZTC000163FL` — Downtime worker test suite (test-first); the suite this fix extends with the re-dispatch regression.

### Related work (automated report)

See the automated find_related report in the item's edit history; high-signal additions beyond the curated list above: `WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP` (timer consolidation) and `WL-0MSJIPHD0001L1J9` (dispatch-task wedge robustness).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "The observed duplicate is audit-tier-only: a dispatched audit run reverts the item to `completed`/`in_review` without a fresh audit, so it becomes selectable again. Hardening the claim (verified + never-select-in-progress) prevents the cross-pane race but **not** this re-selection. How should the guard prevent re-dispatch of an item the downtime worker has already dispatched for audit? (A) Durable dispatched-marker exclusion — audit tier skips items already dispatched by the downtime worker (e.g., parsed from the shared `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, or a per-item marker), unless a fresh audit exists since. Stays entirely in the dispatcher. (B) Lifecycle change — dispatched audit runs keep the item `in_progress` until a valid audit is recorded (touches the audit skill/AGENTS.md workflow, not just the dispatcher). (C) Both A + verified claim hardening." — Answer (user): **"A"** — durable dispatched-marker exclusion, dispatcher-scoped, no claim-path rework, no lifecycle change. Source: interactive reply (intake session).
- Note: The user's original suggestions (mark in_progress on dispatch; never select in_progress) were investigated — both already exist in the code (`claimItem` before pane spawn; `wl next` excludes in-progress by default) but do not prevent the audit-tier re-selection; the dispatched-marker exclusion (option A) closes that gap.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-08-09T13:29:40Z — `/skill:plan` (session 019fe6b1-e8a7-705f-9cc5-4e9673957c2c): created child features **1. Regression tests for audit-tier re-dispatch exclusion** (test-first) and **2. Dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection**; dependency edge F2←F1; approval gate passed (risk Medium, operator approved); six automated review stages run — Stage 2 (completeness) added `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts` to Key Files. Effort/risk estimate retained from intake (Small / Medium — scope unchanged).

# Dispatched-marker exclusion in audit-tier selection

**Summary:** Add a fail-safe read helper for the rolling dispatch log and exclude items the downtime worker has already dispatched for `/skill:audit` from audit-tier candidate selection (parent WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY, option A — dispatcher-scoped, no claim-path rework). Closes the re-selection loop where a dispatched audit run reverts the item to `completed`/`in_review` without a fresh audit.

- [ ] `readDowntimeLogEntries(cwd)` returns `[]` on a missing or unreadable dispatch log and skips malformed JSONL lines without throwing (fail-safe — dispatch is never blocked by a log failure).
- [ ] `selectAuditCandidate` excludes candidates whose `itemId` has an audit-kind dispatch marker; composes with `isAuditFresh` (fresh audit → not a candidate, unchanged).
- [ ] `getNextAuditCandidate` loads the marker set from `<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (filtered to `kind === 'audit'`) and applies the exclusion; plan/intake tier selection is unchanged.

# Feature Request: --fields field-selection for wl list / wl search

## Problem statement

wl list and wl search return full work-item records (or compact snippets for search), with no way to request only the fields a caller needs. Full-record dumps are the root cause of token waste documented in SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents): bare wl list --json = 5.3 MB / 1,861 records; wl list --status completed = 4.9 MB; scripts (ship gates, triage, code-review) download tens-to-hundreds of KB of fields they never read (e.g. full descriptions) when they only need id, title, status, stage, priority.

## User stories

- As a release-gate script, I want wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title,status,stage,needsProducerReview --json so I stop downloading 4.9 MB of descriptions I discard.
- As an agent running /skill:audit, I want a compact project-status query (fields id,title,status,stage,priority) so the worklog overview stays in the low-KB range.
- As a triage helper, I want wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure --fields id,title,description --json so my match heuristics get exactly the fields they need.

## Expected behaviour

- New option on wl list and wl search: --fields comma-separated (e.g. id,title,status,stage,priority).
- Output objects contain ONLY the requested fields (plus id always, for usability); unknown field names are rejected with a clear error listing valid fields.
- wl list and wl search share the same field vocabulary: id, title, description, status, stage, priority, issueType, assignee, tags, createdAt, updatedAt, parentId, needsProducerReview, sortIndex.
- --json output shape unchanged (same keys; omitted fields absent). Human output uses the same projection for concise display.
- -f as shorthand is acceptable; must not clash with existing flags (-F/--format already taken).

## Acceptance criteria

1. wl list --fields id,title --json returns objects with only id/title; verified for filters and bare queries.
2. wl search term --fields id,title,status --json returns compact objects with only those fields.
3. Invalid field names produce a non-zero exit and a clear error listing valid fields.
4. Output size reduction verified: wl list --stage in_review --fields id,title --json is smaller than the full-record equivalent (target: >=90% reduction for the completed-status case cited above).
5. Existing output without --fields is unchanged (backward compatible); full test suite passes.

## Plan

### Child Work Items (dependency-ordered)

1. **WL-0MT5L3BGA001MKOP** - Create pickFields() projection helper module
2. **WL-0MT5L4MGL000Z43Y** - Write unit tests for pickFields projection helper (depends on 1)
3. **WL-0MT5L55AQ002WTGQ** - Add --fields option to wl list (depends on 1, 2)
4. **WL-0MT5L6G88006N4WD** - Add --fields option to wl search (depends on 1, 2)
5. **WL-0MT5L6TLQ004NDLK** - Integration test: end-to-end --fields flag verification (depends on 3, 4)

### Implementation Approach

1. Create packages/shared/src/fields.ts with pickFields(item, fields?) helper
2. Add fields?: string to ListOptions and SearchOptions in cli-types.ts
3. Apply pickFields projection in list.ts before JSON output
4. Apply pickFields projection in search.ts before JSON output
5. Write unit tests and integration tests

### Review Stages Summary

1. Requirements & AC alignment: All 5 ACs map to user stories and expected behaviour. No gaps or contradictions.
2. Completeness: Description has all required sections. Key files are valid.
3. Sequencing & dependencies: Test items before implementation items. Dependencies properly set.
4. Scope sizing: Small effort, Low risk - appropriate for scope.
5. Acceptance & testability: All ACs are testable with clear pass/fail criteria.
6. Polish & handoff: Plan is copy-pasteable and actionable.

## Plan Changelog

- 2026-08-23T09:09Z - Plan created with 5 child work items. Pre-check: Small effort, Low risk. All review stages passed.

## Appendix

- Q: Should --fields support nested field access (e.g. auditResult.readyToClose)? Answer (plan agent): No. The work item scope is flat field selection only. Nested access can be added later if needed. Final: not in scope.
- Q: Should -f shorthand be supported? Answer (plan agent): Yes, but -f is not taken in either list or search. Final: -f can be added as shorthand.

# Feature Request / Bug: FTS index freshness + silent query-error swallowing

## Problem statement

`wl search` help advertises "Full-text search over work items (title, description, comments, tags)" — and comment indexing is implemented and *works after a manual rebuild* (verified: column-scoped `comments:"Closed with reason"` MATCH returns rows; 1,567/2,462 indexed rows contain comment text; `wl search '"v0.1.11"'` returns comment matches). Two defects make comment search unreliable in practice:

1. **The FTS index is never updated incrementally.** `upsertFtsEntry(item)` (dist/persistent-store.js:963) is defined but has **zero call sites** — it is dead code. `saveWorkItem` / `saveComment` do not touch `worklog_fts`. The index only refreshes via the manual `wl search --rebuild-index` command. Any work item or comment created/edited since the last rebuild is invisible to search — silently stale results (recent items/comments missing, duplicates not detected by triage heuristics).

2. **Malformed FTS5 queries fail silently.** An unquoted punctuated query such as `wl search v0.1.11` produces an FTS5 syntax error (`fts5: syntax error near "."`) that the catch block (persistent-store.js ~1157) swallows, returning `[]` with no warning. Users cannot distinguish "no matches" from "invalid query". Version strings, file paths, and ids (all common search targets in this tool) are exactly the strings that trip this.

## User stories

- As an agent deduplicating test-failure work items, I want recently added comments and items to appear in `wl search` without requiring a manual `--rebuild-index`, so I don't create duplicates.
- As a user searching for `v0.1.11` or a file path, I want either correct matches or an explicit "invalid query" error, not a silent empty result.

## Expected behaviour

- Creating/updating a work item or adding/deleting a comment keeps the FTS index current (call `upsertFtsEntry` from the save paths; call `deleteFtsEntry` from item/comment delete paths).
- FTS5 query syntax errors are surfaced to the user (non-zero exit + clear message), not swallowed; only genuinely zero-match queries return empty results.
- Consider quoting/escaping hygiene: document (and optionally auto-quote) punctuated terms; an option like `--rebuild-index` remains as the backstop for bulk migrations.
- Optional: automatic index rebuild (or per-item reindex) when the index is detected empty/stale (e.g. hash-based staleness already used for embeddings).

## Suggested implementation approach

1. Wire `upsertFtsEntry` into `saveWorkItem` (dist/persistent-store.js:299) and into `saveComment`/comment-delete paths (comments currently don't trigger any FTS update at all).
2. Change `searchFts`'s catch block to rethrow/flag syntax errors (or validate the query with a dry MATCH first) so the command layer can report `error: invalid query syntax` with the offending term.
3. Add unit tests: new item searchable immediately after save; new comment searchable immediately after add; punctuated query error surfaces; delete removes from index.

## Acceptance criteria

1. After `wl create` + `wl comment add`, both the title and the comment text are found by `wl search` WITHOUT running `--rebuild-index`.
2. `wl search v0.1.11` (unquoted punctuated term) exits non-zero with a clear "invalid query — quote phrases" message instead of silently returning 0.
3. Deleting an item/comment removes it from subsequent search results.
4. `wl search --rebuild-index` still works as the manual backstop; full test suite passes.

## Related work

- related-to: SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ (SorraAgents) — its analysis assumed comments were not searchable; this request resolves that gap and would enable comment-based remediation queries (e.g. `shipped in v1.0.0` close-reason sweep).
- related-to: WL-0MSLW8GHQ0092PJK — `--fields` projection for list/search; both improve wl CLI efficiency.
