data.description:
# Maintenance routines skill: create/maintain daily scheduled test, standup, refactor sessions at high priority

## Headline

A new ContextHub skill (`/skill:maintenance-routines`) that creates and maintains the required daily scheduled maintenance sessions (test 07:00, standup 08:00, refactor 09:00) in each project's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatching all of them at **high request priority** so they are processed even in peak periods — backed by a herdr enhancement that threads a per-entry `priority` (default `high`) into the `X-Priority` request header.

## Problem statement

Every project should run regular automated maintenance routines (test suite, standup report, refactor pass). The herdr plugin already has the mechanism (`scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatched on idle by the downtime worker), but there is no maintained, canonical set: the current template/live config only carries `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (06:05, no priority), and **no** `/skill:test` routine. Worse, dispatched scheduled prompts have no work item, so they receive the downtime request-priority default `medium` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium`) — they can be starved behind peak-period contention. The operator wants the three routines scheduled daily (07:00/08:00/09:00) and dispatched at **high** priority.

## Users

- **Project operator** — wants the three routines to reliably exist in each project's schedule and to be processed even in peak periods.
- **Automated maintenance sessions** (`/skill:test`, `/skill:standup`, `/skill:refactor`) — must carry `X-Priority: high` on every provider request so `llama-proxy` serves them ahead of the contention queue.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I run `/skill:maintenance-routines` on a project and it ensures `/skill:test` (daily 07:00), `/skill:standup` (daily 08:00) and `/skill:refactor` (daily 09:00) are present and correctly configured in `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, without touching my last-run timestamps or any custom entries.
- As an operator, I know every scheduled maintenance session is dispatched with `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY=high` (→ `X-Priority: high`), so the daily test/standup/refactor runs are served even during peak periods.
- As an operator, when I provision a new project with `wl init`, it comes pre-loaded with the same three routines (daily, timed, high priority).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Skill exists and reconciles the schedule.** `skill/maintenance-routines/` ships a `SKILL.md`, a reconciler script and unit tests. Invoking it (or the script directly) reconciles the project-local `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (under the resolved worklog dir) so these required routines are present and exact:
   - `/skill:test` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "07:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:standup` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "08:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:refactor` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "09:00"`, `priority: "high"`
2. **Reconcile is non-destructive and idempotent.** Entries are created if absent; drifted fields (interval/time/priority) are corrected; `lastTriggeredAt` and all other user-defined entries are preserved verbatim; a second run makes no further changes; missing or malformed config files are handled fail-closed with a clear report; `--dry-run` shows the planned diff without writing.
3. **Herdr honours a per-entry `priority` field.** `ScheduledPrompt` gains an optional `priority` (`low|medium|high|critical`) validated in `parseScheduledPrompt` (invalid value → entry skipped with a warning, fail-closed); **absent → defaults to `high`** for scheduled prompts. The scheduled-prompt dispatch passes it through `spawnAgentPane({ priority })` → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (so `high` → `X-Priority: high` on every request). Unit tests cover parse defaults/validation and the dispatch threading.
4. **Template provisions the required set.** `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the `wl init` base set) is updated to the three required routines with daily `intervalDays`, `time` and `priority: high`, so new projects are provisioned with the routines (create-if-absent semantics unchanged — existing configs are never clobbered).
5. **Documentation criterion.** `packages/herdr/README.md` (Scheduled prompts section), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (Request priority section) and `CONFIG.md` (Scheduled-prompts config section) document the new `priority` field, the default-`high` behaviour, and the three routines; the maintenance-routines skill is referenced from the relevant skill docs listing.
6. **Testing criterion.** Skill tests (`pytest` under `skill/maintenance-routines/tests/`) cover reconcile/idempotence/preservation/dry-run; herdr unit tests (`vitest`) cover the new parse/validation and dispatch priority; full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No changes to the interactive dispatch path or to the other downtime tiers' mapping tables** (`request-priority.ts` stays fixed); only the scheduled-prompt entry schema, its dispatch call, and the skill/template change.
- The requested **default is `high`** for scheduled prompts (operator decision Q1): an entry that wants lower priority must set the field explicitly (`low`/`medium`). This is a deliberate change from the current downtime default (`medium`) for scheduled prompts only.
- No code-behaviour changes to `wl init` — only the **contents** of `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the provisioning path and create-if-absent semantics stay as-is).
- The skill must be safe to run from any project root (`wl`-independent — it reads/writes only `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, atomic tmp+rename, matching herdr's `saveScheduledPrompts` pattern).

## Existing state

- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (and the live `/.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`) currently carry only `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (daily `time: "06:05"`); no `/skill:test`; no priority field anywhere.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — schema (`id|prompt|intervalDays|lastTriggeredAt|time?`), fail-closed parse, due-check, atomic persist; **no priority support**.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchScheduledPrompt` calls `spawnAgentPane(prompt.prompt, { model, cwd, paneName, anchorId })` with **no priority** → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions({ priority: undefined })` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium` (docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md, "Scheduled prompts have no work item and get the downtime default (medium)").
- `src/commands/init.ts` — `ensureScheduledPromptsInstalled` copies the template create-if-absent; unchanged in behaviour.
- Skills precedent: `skill/heartbeat/` and `skill/pane-triage/` (SKILL.md + scripts + tests, tracked in ContextHub, deployed to `~/.pi/agent/skills/<name>`); shared helpers in `skill/shared/`.

## Desired change

1. **New skill** `skill/maintenance-routines/`: `SKILL.md` (spec: required-routines table, invocation, admission of a bootstrap `/skill:maintenance-routines` schedule), `scripts/maintenance_routines.py` (reconcile + `--dry-run`; atomic writes; preserves `lastTriggeredAt` and foreign entries), `tests/` (unit tests).
2. **Herdr priority support**: extend `ScheduledPrompt` + `parseScheduledPrompt` with optional `priority` (default `high`); thread it from `dispatchScheduledPrompt` → `spawnAgentPane({ priority })` → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`. `mapDowntimeRequestPriority` already maps `high`→`high`.
3. **Template**: update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` to the three routines (daily, timed, `priority: "high"`).
4. **Docs**: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CONFIG.md`; skill listed alongside heartbeat/pane-triage where appropriate.
5. **Tests**: pytest for the skill reconciler; vitest for parse/validation + dispatch threading in herdr.

## Key Files

- `skill/maintenance-routines/SKILL.md` — new skill spec (required-routines table, usage, dry-run).
- `skill/maintenance-routines/scripts/maintenance_routines.py` — new reconciler CLI (`--dry-run`, atomic write, preserves state).
- `skill/maintenance-routines/tests/test_maintenance_routines.py` — new unit tests (reconcile, idempotence, preservation, malformed config, dry-run).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — add optional `priority` (`low|medium|high|critical`, default `high`), validation in `parseScheduledPrompt`.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.test.ts` — new parse/default/validation cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchScheduledPrompt` passes `prompt.priority` to `spawnAgentPane`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (or the scheduled-prompts tier test) — dispatch threads `priority: 'high'` into the spawn opts/env.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` — updated to the three required routines.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CONFIG.md` — document the new field/default and the routines.
- `tests/skill/maintenance-routines/` — integration-style tests for the skill (repo test-suite convention, cf. `tests/skill/heartbeat/`).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX** (completed) — herdr downtime dispatcher: scheduled prompts (best-effort frequency) config — the mechanism the skill maintains.
- **WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH / WL-0MVF3Q3VL000UNCN** (completed) — request priority (`X-Priority`) mapping tables and `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` env threading — the priority plumbing we reuse.
- **WL-0MTF5UAJ4000LLZ9** (completed) — removal of scheduled-prompts console output (no-op here).
- **WL-0MUKYERLZ006ELL5** (completed) — non-terminal cooldown for dispatched panes (context for scheduled dispatch behaviour).
- **WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B** (completed) — periodic request scheduling to the pi worklog plugin; the scheduled-prompts feature parent.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B** – Add periodic request scheduling to pi worklog plugin (completed)
- **WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR** – Scheduled prompts: add time-of-day dispatch (time window) to scheduled-prompts tier (completed)
- **WL-0MKRPG64S04PL1A6** – wl doctor (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: convey, create, creates, currently, daily (+26 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: create, creates, daily, default, dispatched (+25 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: convey, create, creates, currently, default (+23 more)
- Skill-authoring precedents: `skill/heartbeat/`, `skill/pane-triage/` (SKILL.md + scripts + tests, deployed to `~/.pi/agent/skills`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — default-`high` changes politeness of ALL scheduled prompts** (including custom future entries). Accepted by operator (Q1: "default high"); any entry can opt down via an explicit `low`/`medium` field. Mitigation: document prominently.
- **Risk — parse strictness.** An invalid `priority` value rejects the whole entry (consistent with existing `time` handling) — a config typo could silently disable a routine. Mitigation: the skill always writes a valid value; tests cover the failure path.
- **Risk — skill/template drift.** If `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` is later edited, the skill's required table may diverge. Mitigation: keep the required-routines table in one place (the skill), and the template mirrors it (as Q3).
- **Assumption — the skill runs per project root.** Invoked via a pi session (herdr pane or manual) with `cwd` at the project root; it reads/writes only `<cwd>/.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (worklog-dir safe).
- **Assumption — operators may bootstrap the skill itself as a scheduled prompt** (e.g. daily `/skill:maintenance-routines`) to keep the schedule self-healing; not required for this item.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no changes to interactive dispatch, `request-priority.ts` tables, other downtime tiers, or `wl init` code; any opportunity discovered during implementation is recorded as a new linked work item, not added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: How should scheduled routines get high priority?**
  - Options: (a) per-entry `priority` field in `scheduled-prompts.json`, threaded through herdr dispatch → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`; (b) herdr always dispatches all scheduled prompts at `high`; (c) config-level default priority.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): "1. A (default high)"** — per-entry field; **absent → default `high`**.
  - Reasoning recorded: matches "all those work items should be sent high priority so they get processed even in peak periods"; keeps intent in the config; future entries can opt down explicitly.
- **Q2: How strictly should the skill maintain the required set?**
  - Options: (a) ensure the three required routines exist & match spec (create-if-absent, fix drifted fields), keep other user entries; (b) strict whitelist (remove anything else); (c) create-if-absent only (never fix drift).
  - **Answer (producer): "2. A"** — non-destructive reconcile, preserve custom entries.
- **Q3: Should new projects get the routines by default?**
  - Options: (a) also update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the `wl init` base set); (b) skill-only.
  - **Answer (producer): "3. A"** — template updated so every new project provisions the three routines at 07:00/08:00/09:00 high (`wl init` code path unchanged).

## Failure Signature

- Test file: `tests/cli/completion.test.ts`
- Failing cases (2 — one per shell):
  - `wl completion bash > contains all known subcommands`
  - `wl completion zsh > contains all known subcommands`
- Failure: `AssertionError: expected completion script to contain "worklist"` — the generated script's command list omits `worklist` (`audit … unlock update completion`, no `worklist`).
- Failing commit: surfaced on `dev` after `c8d8197f` (WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF, 2026-10-21 19:28).
- CI job: (not available)

## Root Cause (verified during planning)

**The source is correct; the failure is a stale-build artefact.** Two facts
combine:

1. **`tests/cli/completion.test.ts` spawns the *built* CLI and bypasses the
   build-freshness guard.** It hard-codes its entry point:

   ```ts
   const CLI_PATH = resolve(__dirname, '../../dist/cli.js');
   ```

   `dist/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:86`) and `npm test` does not rebuild it,
   so this file asserts against whatever build happens to be on disk — not
   against `src/`.

2. **The checked-out `dist/` predated the `worklist` command.** Observed
   state: `dist/cli.js` mtime `2026-10-21 15:52:42`; commits
   `c8d8197f` (19:28:20, adds `src/commands/worklist.ts` +
   `worklist` in `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES`) and `e1cedba5` (20:12:33) landed
   afterwards. `grep -c worklist dist/cli.js` → `0`; `dist/commands/worklist.js`
   did not exist.

**Verification performed (reproduce → rebuild → pass):**

```bash
node dist/cli.js completion bash | grep -c worklist   # 0  (stale build)
npm run build
node dist/cli.js completion bash | grep -c worklist   # 2  (command + id-arg list)
node dist/cli.js completion zsh  | grep -c worklist   # 1
```

`worklist` is the **only** required command missing from the stale script
(`init status create list show update delete export import next in-progress
sync github comment close recent plugins migrate dep re-sort doctor search
unlock audit completion` all appear), which is exactly why the single
assertion that tripped names `worklist`.

**Why this is not simply "rebuild and move on":** a rebuild fixes this
checkout but commits nothing (`dist/` is gitignored), so the same false
failure returns for any checkout whose build lags `src/`. The repo already
solved this class of problem twice:

- WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 converted every `dist/cli.js`-spawning test to the
  pre-compiled bundle helper `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts` ("as a side effect now
  run against current `src/` instead of whatever build happened to be on
  disk") and added the regression guard `tests/unit/no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts`
  — see `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`
  § "Change (test code + test config only)". **`completion.test.ts` was missed
  by that sweep.**
- WL-0MVH44JRR000A23U (same failure class, `entry-point-split.test.ts`) fixed
  `isDistFresh()` so `resolveStartupTarget('auto', …)` never selects a stale
  build.

So the durable fix is to finish the missed sweep for this file and make the
regression guard cover the *hard-coded `dist/` spawn* idiom, not only the
`tsx` idiom.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. From a checkout whose `dist/cli.js` predates the `worklist` command
   (`stat -c '%y' dist/cli.js` older than `git log -1 -- src/commands/worklist.ts`):
   - `npx vitest run tests/cli/completion.test.ts -t 'contains all known subcommands'`
2. Observe `expected completion script to contain "worklist"` for both the
   bash and zsh cases.
3. `npm run build` and re-run — both pass. (Confirmed during planning.)

## Desired Change

Keep it to test code, one new regression guard, and docs. No production code
change: `src/commands/completion.ts` already emits `worklist` correctly once
built from `HEAD`.

1. **Fix `tests/cli/completion.test.ts`** — resolve its CLI under test through
   the established, always-in-sync helper instead of `dist/cli.js`:
   `runCliProcess(['completion', 'bash'])` from `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts`
   (esbuild bundle of `src/cli.ts`, built once per test process, tsx fallback
   when esbuild is unavailable). Keep the existing assertions and the
   `--json`/unknown-shell/usage cases intact; only the spawn path changes.
2. **Extend the regression guard** — add `tests/unit/no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts`
   (modelled on `tests/unit/no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts`): scan `tests/**/*.ts`
   for the `dist/cli.js` spawn idiom and fail for any file outside a
   documented allowlist, with a message pointing at
   `runCliProcess()`/`cliInvocation()`.
   - Allowlist rationale (each entry needs a one-line reason in the test):
     `tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts` and
     `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts` intentionally exercise the built
     entry (both go through the freshness-aware `resolveStartupTarget` /
     explicit-dist contract), `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts`
     uses temp fixtures, `tests/unit/no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts` is the scanner
     itself, and `tests/cli/smoke.test.ts` asserts that the *built* artefact
     loads — that is its purpose.
3. **Migrate the remaining hard-coded spawn** —
   `tests/cli/doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts` (`cliPath =
   path.join(projectRoot, 'dist', 'cli.js')`) should use `cliInvocation()`.
   If it proves load-bearing in a surprising way, allowlist it with a reason
   rather than blocking the guard.
4. **Docs** — update `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (§ the cli-bundle sweep)
   to record that `completion.test.ts` (+ `doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts`)
   now use the bundle, that `no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts` is the second guard,
   and to restate the standing rule: **tests must not hard-code `dist/cli.js`;
   `npm run build` is required before a bare checkout's suite, and the guard
   keeps that from silently producing false failures.**

## Implementation Notes (for implement phase)

- **Red-first evidence cannot come from the ambient checkout.** `implement.py`
  runs `npm run build` before tests, so in a worktree both shells already pass.
  Drive the guard test red by fixture: create a temp `tests/`-like tree (or
  pass a root parameter) containing a file that spawns `dist/cli.js` and assert
  the scanner reports it — mirror `startup-target-freshness.test.ts` (temp dirs
  + controlled content) rather than mutating real mtimes.
- **Alternative considered and rejected:** switch to
  `resolveStartupTarget('auto', repoRoot)` + `buildStartupInvocation(...)`.
  Correct, but slower than the bundle and leaves this file on the tsx fallback
  path when `dist/` is stale; the bundle is the repo's stated convention for
  "a real subprocess is needed".
- Completion output includes plugin-provided commands (e.g. `stats`) — plugin
  loading is independent of the entry point, so the bundle produces the same
  command list as `dist/cli.js`.
- Do **not** touch `src/commands/completion.ts`, `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` or
  `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts` — all three are already correct.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `npx vitest run tests/cli/completion.test.ts` passes against the latest
  `dev` **both with a fresh `dist/` and with a deliberately stale/absent
  `dist/`** (the file no longer depends on ambient build state).
- [ ] `tests/cli/completion.test.ts` no longer hard-codes `dist/cli.js`; it
  spawns the CLI through `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts`
  (`runCliProcess`) and keeps every existing assertion (bash script shape,
  known subcommands, global options, dynamic work-item ID completion,
  completion-of-completion, unknown-shell error, `--json` payload) intact.
- [ ] A new guard test `tests/unit/no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts` fails when any
  test file outside a documented allowlist spawns a hard-coded `dist/cli.js`,
  and its failure message names the offending file and the recommended helper
  (red-first: proven against a fixture input, not only against the current
  tree).
- [ ] `tests/cli/doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts` either uses
  `cliInvocation()` or is allowlisted with a written reason.
- [ ] The two originally failing cases (`wl completion bash|zsh > contains all
  known subcommands`) pass, with `worklist` present in both generated scripts.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes
  (`docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`: cli-bundle sweep completeness, the new
  stale-dist guard, and the standing "tests must not hard-code `dist/`" rule).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Key Files

- `tests/cli/completion.test.ts` — spawn the CLI via `runCliProcess()`; drop `CLI_PATH`.
- `tests/unit/no-stale-dist-spawn.test.ts` — new repo-wide guard (modelled on `no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts`).
- `tests/cli/doctor-foreign-items-push.test.ts` — remaining hard-coded `dist/cli.js` spawn; migrate or allowlist.
- `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts` — reused (`runCliProcess`/`cliInvocation`); no change expected.
- `tests/unit/no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts` — the guard pattern to mirror (read-only reference).
- `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts` — fixture-with-temp-dirs pattern for the guard's red-first evidence (read-only reference).
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — documentation update (sweep completeness + guard + standing rule).
- `src/commands/completion.ts` — verified correct; **no change expected**.

## Related work

- `WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF` — added the `worklist` command and the
  `worklist` entry in `KNOWN_COMMANDS` (commit `c8d8197f`); its suite run had a
  fresh build, which is why the gate was green and this checkout's stale
  `dist/` was not.
- `WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8` — the cli-bundle sweep + `no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts`
  guard that this item completes.
- `WL-0MVH44JRR000A23U` — same failure class (`entry-point-split.test.ts`,
  stale `dist/`), fixed via `isDistFresh()`; establishes the
  "stale build is not a source defect; make tests independent of ambient
  build state" ruling.
- `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` — post-push verification item whose full-suite run in
  the advancing `dev` checkout first surfaced these two failures.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Assumption** — `runCliProcess()` reproduces `dist/cli.js`'s completion
  output exactly (same entry file, same command graph; only pre-compiled).
  Verified by the converted tests' assertions, which are unchanged.
- **Risk — esbuild unavailable → tsx fallback** makes the completion suite
  slower (~12 spawns), never wrong (`cli-bundle.ts` fails soft by design).
- **Risk — guard false positives** on files that legitimately test the build
  (three known sites). Mitigated by the documented allowlist above; new
  offenders get the migration message rather than a silent pass.
- **Assumption** — a production code change is *not* required. If the
  implement phase finds `completion.ts` genuinely omitting a registered command
  from `HEAD`'s build, that is a **new** defect: file it as a separate work
  item (`discovered-from` this one) instead of widening this scope.

## Plan notes

- The template ACs are preserved in intent and sharpened: AC1 keeps "the test
  passes on latest `dev`" but additionally requires independence from ambient
  build state (otherwise a rebuild — which commits nothing, `dist/` being
  gitignored — would satisfy it and the item would have no deliverable).
  AC2 keeps the docs requirement and names the exact file. AC3 keeps "full
  suite passes".
- The recurrence guard is the deliverable that makes this a real work item;
  it follows two completed precedents (`WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8`,
  `WL-0MVH44JRR000A23U`) rather than inventing a new mechanism.
- No children were created: effort Extra Small / risk Low, the change is one
  test file + one guard test + one doc, and it is a single vertical slice.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The plan pre-check returned `decision: "skip"` (effort **Extra Small**, risk
**Low**), and the root cause was established from repository evidence, so no
interview questions were required. Evidence reviewed:

- `tests/cli/completion.test.ts` (hard-coded `CLI_PATH = dist/cli.js`,
  `KNOWN_COMMANDS` incl. `worklist`).
- `src/commands/completion.ts` (introspects `program.commands`),
  `src/command-registry.ts` (`worklist` in `BUILT_IN_COMMAND_NAMES` /
  `COMMAND_LOADERS`; `FULL_REGISTRATION_COMMANDS = {completion}`).
- Live reproduction: stale `dist/cli.js` (mtime 15:52:42) → no `worklist`;
  after `npm run build` → `worklist` present in bash and zsh scripts.
- `git log --stat c8d8197f` (adds `src/commands/worklist.ts` and the
  `completion.test.ts` `+1 line` KNOWN_COMMANDS change), commit times vs
  `dist/cli.js` mtime.
- `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` `isDistFresh` / `resolveStartupTarget` (the
  existing freshness guard this file bypasses).
- `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts`, `tests/unit/no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts`,
  `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (the established convention + guard
  pattern), `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts` (fixture pattern).
- Prior items `WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8`, `WL-0MVH44JRR000A23U`,
  `WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF` (their comments record the same failure class).
- Duplicate check: `wl search "completion worklist"` / `wl search "stale dist"`
  / `wl search "test stale build"` — no open item covers this gap;
  `WL-0MVH44JRR000A23U` is completed and scoped to `entry-point-split.test.ts`.

**OPEN QUESTION (none blocking; recorded for the producer's awareness):** the
plan assumes the fix stays test-only. If the producer wants the *whole* suite
to stop depending on ambient build state (i.e. make `npm test` build `dist/`
first, or make CI rebuild before the run), that is a broader policy change and
should be a separate work item — it is deliberately **not** in this scope.

# Herdr downtime dispatch: claim local capacity via proxy reservation (never send-then-hope)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher polls `/llama/local/status` and launches panes into what it believes is free capacity. Two defects remain even after `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` (prefill-gate pacing) ships:

1. **Poll-and-send is racy.** With the prefill gate serialised (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`), new starts are a single ticket. Two herdr instances polling in the same 10 s tick can both be admitted and launch; the second queues behind the first's prefill and, on the current proxy, times out and goes remote (measured on the proxy side: queue depth reached 7 in-window while `available_slots` still reported 2 with the gate saturated; 261 requests fell back after queueing, 215 after the full 120 s). An idle window can be *observed* by N instances but only *owned* by one.
2. **The sent-work model is wrong for mid-session pressure.** Even with correct pane pacing, pane turns are continuous (29 sessions, median 30 requests/session on 2026-10-21); those turns cannot be gated by idle windows at all. The dispatcher (and the agents it spawns) must be able to claim capacity *per request* and defer when refused.

The proxy is adding an atomic reservation handshake — `POST /llama/local/reserve` returning a gate ticket, or a `429 {reason, retry_after_s}` refusal — plus `X-Local-Preference: local-only` and `X-Local-Route`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason` response headers (llm-manager `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL`). This item consumes that handshake so the dispatcher never launches work it cannot start.

## Goal / users

- As the downtime dispatcher, I want to launch exactly **one pane per idle window** (operator requirement, asserted in the comment on `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`): I ask the proxy for a ticket, launch only with a ticket, and defer with `retry_after` when refused — never poll-then-hope.
- As an agent session spawned by herdr, I want per-turn capacity claims so my turns either get a ticket (local) or an immediate, honest refusal to fall back (remote) — never a silent 120 s proxy-side wait.

## Desired change

1. **Reservation client:** on each dispatch decision, call `POST /llama/local/reserve` (reusing the existing single-flight status poll cadence; no new polling) with the pane's expected token size, priority and cache state.
   - Ticket granted → launch with `X-Local-Reservation` on the first request; treat the ticket as the pane's entry to the gate.
   - Refused (`429`) → defer with `retry_after`, record decision reason (`reserved-fallback` / `prefill-gate` / `queue-full`…).
   - Endpoint absent / failure → fail-open fall back to the `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` polling behaviour (never a hard failure against an older proxy).
2. **One-per-idle-window assertion:** after a successful launch, no second pane is launched until a fresh status tick shows `local_prefills_in_flight < local_max_concurrent_prefills` **and** the reservation was granted for that specific launch. Test the two-instances-same-tick race.
3. **Per-turn claims for agent sessions:** the herdr agent runner passes `X-Local-Preference: local-only` for work the operator marks local-first and `remote-ok` for background work; turns then receive the proxy's honest refusal instead of a silent fallback, and the runner records `X-Local-Route`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason` from responses into the decision log.
4. **Decision-log evidence:** each dispatch/defer records ticket state, `admit`, `projected_wait_s`, `retry_after_s`, and the response route headers.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — reserve client:** when the proxy serves the reserve endpoint (fixture), a dispatch first receives a ticket and only then launches with the reservation header; a refused ticket defers with `retry_after` and is recorded (`downtime-worker.mock.test.ts`-style mocked fetch, following the existing fixture pattern).
- **AC2 — failure mode backcompat:** endpoint absent/500/timeout → exactly today's polling behaviour, no crash, no stuck pane (tests for each).
- **AC3 — one-per-idle-window:** two instances observing the same idle window produce at most one launch; the second defers with the refusal evidence (test modelling the same-tick race).
- **AC4 — per-turn preference:** the runner sends `X-Local-Preference` per configured policy, parses `X-Local-Route`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason`, and records both in the decision log (tests).
- **AC5 — docs:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes — `packages/herdr/README.md` and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` document the reservation handshake, the one-per-idle-window rule, and the preference policy knob (with matching code comments).
- **AC6 — suite:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (run via the test skill).

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing single-flight status poll; the reservation call may piggyback on the same request cadence (no new polling loops).
- Fail-open: an older proxy is fully supported — absent fields/endpoint never block dispatch.
- Pacing only reduces concurrency; never raise the free-slot budget, never bypass fail-closed per-slot handling (`WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW`).
- Keep it surgical: this item extends `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX`'s pacing with the atomic claim; it does not rewrite the dispatcher.

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — reserve call, ticket header, deferral on refusal.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.parse.test.ts` / `.idle.test.ts` / `.test.ts` / `.fixtures.ts` — reserve + race tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/` agent-runner request path — `X-Local-Preference`, route-header parsing, decision log.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

## Related work

- **Depends on:** llm-manager `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` (proxy reservation endpoint + headers); adopts the contract it ACs.
- **Extends:** `WL-0MVHSZRZQ00482QX` (prefill-gate pacing — poll-based); its comment asserts the one-per-idle-window requirement.
- **Siblings:** `WL-0MVHSZQVX0000T6P` (per-slot capacity, completed/in_review), `WL-0MVHSZR9C0012NQY` (idle-age signal), `WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW` (fail-closed per-slot availability).
- **Proxy-side quad:** `LP-0MVICD2YW004DJPV` (occupancy-aware guard, prerequisite), `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` (reservation, this item's dependency), `LP-0MVIKPRMD000Y97R` (queue sweep after reservations).

## Risks

- **Reservation latency:** an extra round trip per dispatch. Mitigation: piggyback on the status poll cadence and measure; the ticket TTL covers the launch.
- **Over-deferral:** a pessimistic proxy refusal could starve panes. Mitigation: refusals only on calibrated verdicts (proxy fail-open) and the client-side fail-open path.
- **Contract drift:** the proxy contract is new; version the request (additive fields) and keep the fail-open parsing strict-but-tolerant.

## Goal

As an operator running `/skill:machine-hygiene`, I want the CPU / memory / I/O stall pressure metrics to report real values, so the diagnosis is based on the kernel's own pressure-stall signal instead of silently losing three of its twelve metrics.

## Problem

`scripts/metrics.py::_read_proc_pressure()` always returns `None` on Linux, so `cpu_pressure`, `memory_pressure` and `io_pressure` are permanently rendered as:

```
| cpu_pressure    | n/a | 🟡 | P1 | warning |
```

with the description "unavailable (non-Linux or kernel missing pressure stall info)", even though PSI is present and readable.

## Evidence (verified 2026-10-21, 16-core Ubuntu host)

```
$ cat /proc/pressure/cpu
some avg10=11.58 avg60=7.68 avg300=11.33 total=71756189671
full avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=0

$ cat /proc/pressure/memory
some avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=54872967

$ cat /proc/pressure/io
some avg10=0.00 avg60=0.00 avg300=0.00 total=242601913
```

So genuine CPU `some` pressure was ~11.6 percent (moderate contention, consistent with load 11.92 on 16 cores) and would have been visible. Instead the run reported all three as n/a.

## Root cause

```python
for line in lines:
    if line.startswith("avg"):            # <-- never true
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 4:
            return float(parts[1])
return None
```

PSI lines are prefixed `some ` or `full `, never `avg`. The tokens are `avg10=<v>`, `avg60=<v>`, `avg300=<v>` — not space-separated bare numbers — so even a corrected prefix match would index the wrong field and would need `split("=")`.

## Suggested fix

```python
def _read_proc_pressure(key: str, which: str = "some") -> float | None:
    """Return avg10 stall percentage for /proc/pressure/<key>."""
    lines = _read_file_lines(f"/proc/pressure/{key}")
    if lines is None:
        return None
    for line in lines:
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) >= 2 and parts[0] == which:
            for token in parts[1:]:
                if token.startswith("avg10="):
                    try:
                        return float(token.split("=", 1)[1])
                    except ValueError:
                        return None
    return None
```

Semantics to decide explicitly:

- `/proc/pressure/cpu` exposes only a `some` line. `/proc/pressure/memory` and `/proc/pressure/io` expose both `some` and `full`.
- Recommended: use `some` for `cpu_pressure` (any task stalled on CPU) and `full` for `memory_pressure` / `io_pressure` (all tasks stalled — the severe, actionable signal). Whatever is chosen must be documented in `SKILL.md` and in the metric `description`.
- The classification config key for `memory_pressure` is currently wired to the `memory_usage` thresholds (`pressure_specs` tuple `("memory", "memory_pressure", "memory_usage", ...)`). Once PSI parses, decide whether memory *pressure* stall percent should share the 80/95 *usage* thresholds or get its own `memory_pressure` block in `config.yaml` / `config.py::_DEFAULTS`. Note `config.yaml` has no `memory_pressure` section despite the SKILL.md metric table listing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `_read_proc_pressure` parses real `/proc/pressure/*` content and returns the `avg10` stall percentage for the selected `some`/`full` line; a unit test feeds verbatim `/proc/pressure` sample content for cpu (some only) and memory/io (some + full) and asserts the expected values.
- AC2: A unit test covers the failure modes: file missing -> `None`; file present but unparsable -> `None`; requested `full` line absent -> documented fallback behaviour.
- AC3: `scripts/evaluate.py` on a Linux host with PSI enabled renders numeric `cpu_pressure` / `memory_pressure` / `io_pressure` values (no `n/a`), verified by an actual run pasted into a comment on this item.
- AC4: The `some` vs `full` choice per metric is documented in `SKILL.md` and reflected in each metric's `description`.
- AC5: The threshold wiring for `memory_pressure` is either explicitly mapped to `memory_usage` (with a code comment and SKILL.md note justifying it) or given its own `memory_pressure` config block in `config.yaml` and `config.py::_DEFAULTS`.
- AC6: Degradation on non-Linux / PSI-less kernels still yields `None` and the existing "unavailable" message — unchanged, no crash.
- AC7: Changed-scope tests pass and the full suite stays green.

## Key files

- `scripts/metrics.py` — `_read_proc_pressure()` (~line 105), `pressure_specs` loop (~line 352)
- `scripts/config.py` — `_DEFAULTS` (add `memory_pressure` block if AC5 chooses that route)
- `config.yaml` — thresholds / documentation
- `SKILL.md` — metric table and `some`/`full` semantics
- `tests/` — new PSI parser unit tests

## Notes

- The skill currently lives only at `~/.pi/agent/skills/machine-hygiene/` (not tracked in this repo). Fixing it here means either promoting the skill into `skill/machine-hygiene/` alongside `skill/pane-triage/` (this repo's canonical home for global agent-framework skills) or patching the global copy by hand. Worth deciding as part of this item.
- Found alongside two already-filed machine-hygiene defects: WL-0MVI8YM07002Z9VY (threshold miscalibration) and WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ (duplicate proposed actions). All three were surfaced by the same run; this one is the loss-of-signal defect.

# Intake Brief — Herdr extension unresponsive on larger worklog databases (WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W)

## Problem statement

The Herdr Work Items pane freezes or visibly lags when it refreshes, is slow to
initially appear, and is slow to reflect some changes after agent writes —
problems that scale with the size of the worklog database. On a ~100 MB /
2,600-item worklog the pane's refresh path still spawns slow, memory-hungry
`wl` CLI processes (`wl worklist` ≈ 1 s / 1.2 MB JSON cold; `wl list` subsets
0.5–0.9 s each peaking ~130–145 MB; per-expand `wl dep list` ≈ 0.4 s) and the
auto-sync may spawn a ~36 s `wl sync` every 60 s. Recent fixes (event-driven
refresh, consolidated `wl worklist`, hydrator timeouts) improved the picture but
the extension remains sluggish — "improved but still not good enough".

## Users (example user stories)

- **Agent operators running the Herdr Work Items pane** — the primary user.
  - *As an operator, when the pane auto-refreshes, I want the UI to stay
    responsive (no multi-second freezes, keystrokes accepted promptly) so my
    monitoring flow is uninterrupted.*
  - *As an operator on a large worklog, when an agent writes to a work item, I
    want the pane to reflect the change within a couple of seconds so I can
    trust the list is current.*
  - *As an operator, I want the pane to open promptly and not feel like the
    extension is a drag on my machine even at 100 MB+ worklog scale.*

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Pane stays responsive during refresh:** a default-view refresh does not block the TUI event loop for more than ~200 ms of perceived lag in aggregate (verified with an automated test harness or measured timing on a large fixture DB) — keystrokes/commands process promptly while a refresh is in flight.
- **Single-figure refresh cost on large DBs:** a default-view refresh end-to-end (event → data load → render) is bounded to ≤ ~1.5 s wall-clock p95 on a DB of ~2,600 items / ~100 MB, including per-expand child fetches; the consolidated `wl worklist` single-read path stays the norm — no regression to multi-spawn refreshes.
- **Auto-sync cannot stall the pane:** while a long `wl sync` (measured ~36 s on the 100 MB DB) is in flight in the background, the pane remains responsive — no lock wait, no event-loop stall, at most a brief non-blocking status notice.
- **Change reflection latency:** after a `wl` write, the pane reflects the change within ~2 s p95 via the event-driven watch path at large-DB scale.
- **Reduced memory footprint:** a refresh's spawned `wl` processes peak at no more than a documented per-spawn budget below the ~130–145 MB/spawn observed baseline, OR concurrent spawns are bounded so aggregate RSS for a single pane stays under a documented ceiling (e.g. ≤ ~300 MB).
- **No regressions:** the full Herdr plugin + TUI test suites pass; the zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee and event-driven watch semantics are preserved.
## Constraints

- Must preserve the existing event-driven refresh, in-process SQLite read
  scopes, consolidated `wl worklist` single-read default view, and
  zero-spawn-when-idle guarantees (documented in
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`).
- Must not change the hydrator's core behaviour or the scheduler's sequential
  dispatch model without a separate work item.
- Fixes must target "large worklog" scale (100 MB+/2,600+ items) without
  regressing small worklogs.
- No new heavy dependencies; prefer reuse of the existing in-process SQLite
  read path (`@worklog/shared` `WorklogDatabase`) over new spawns.

## Existing state (measured)

- `.worklog/worklog.db` ≈ 109 MB, ~2,631 items, read cache 81 MB / ~709 entries
  (this repo).
- `wl worklist --json`: ≈ 1.0 s cold, ~1.2 MB payload.
- `wl list` (each of the four subsets): 0.5–0.9 s, peak ~130–145 MB RSS.
- `wl next`: ≈ 0.6 s. `wl dep list`: ≈ 0.4 s per call.
- `wl sync`: ≈ 36 s on this DB; auto-sync spawns fire-and-forget every 60 s
  (single-flight + heartbeat skip across panes).
- Herdr pane refresh: 30 s auto tick + event-driven (≤ ~150 ms debounce),
  single consolidated `wl worklist` read for the default view; in-process
  SQLite reads for actionable counts / child fetches within a refresh scope.
- Previous unresponsiveness work completed: WL-0MMNZWOZ60M8JY6E (TUI
  unresponsive, critical), WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P (hydrate timeouts), WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN (snappy event-driven refresh), WL-0MQFRY8TM006DIJ6 (wl next perf), WL-0MQOIBGIR006CWLR (background task runtime), WL-0MSGAEPOJ002824S / WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG (memoization + in-process reads), WL-0MVI0IT4S0070G78 (consolidated worklist read).

## Desired change

Investigate the remaining large-DB cost drivers in the Herdr refresh path and
shave them down to the acceptance criteria above. Known candidates (to confirm
during implementation):

1. **Auto-sync `wl sync` cost (~36 s):** profile why `wl sync` is so slow on a
   100 MB DB (git operations, JSONL export, DB compaction?) and either bound it
   or restructure so the pane never waits on / competes with it.
2. **`wl list`/`wl worklist` RSS (~130–145 MB/spawn):** confirm where the
   memory goes (full JSON materialisation? enrichments?) and consider streaming
   or trimming payloads; cap concurrent spawns.
3. **Per-expand `wl dep list` / `wl list --parent` spawns:** replace with
   in-process SQLite reads (via the existing refresh scope) so expanding nodes
   doesn't spawn more slow processes.
4. **Event-loop blocking:** ensure every remaining spawn is off the TUI event
   loop and each refresh's in-process SQLite work stays within the one-open
   refresh scope (no per-helper DB opens).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — consolidated worklist read, in-process
  read scope, CLI exec/timeouts, spawn cap.
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — background `wl sync` spawn/heartbeat.
- `src/sync.ts` / `src/commands/sync.ts` — `wl sync` pipeline (JSONL export,
  git push) — the main suspected ~36 s cost.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — refresh orchestration, guarded refresh,
  child-fetch on expand.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — the consolidated read command (payload size).
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — list/query paths used by these reads.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — per-item `wl dep list` calls (bounded by
  hydrator timeout work but still per-item spawns).

## Related work

- **WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P** — Hydrate task timeouts cause HERDR UI to become
  unresponsive (completed, high) — parent context for UI responsiveness.
- **WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN** — Make Herdr UI refresh snappy after agent work-item
  updates (completed, high) — event-driven refresh; AC 4 re-verification.
- **WL-0MNAGHQ33005BVY6** — TUI slow-down investigation (completed).
- **WL-0MMNZWOZ60M8JY6E** — TUI unresponsive to keyboard input (completed,
  critical).
- **WL-0MQFRY8TM006DIJ6** — Investigate wl next performance bottlenecks
  (completed, high).
- **WL-0MSNIX4V60012266** — Compress herdr plugin meta-data (completed) —
  vertical space, not to be confused with data-size perf.
- **WL-0MQOIBGIR006CWLR** — Background Task Runtime for non-blocking ops
  (completed, high).
- **WL-0MT1KJNGA006EEHU** — Memory pressure monitoring (completed, high).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the ~36 s `wl sync` is dominated by git push/network or JSONL
  export; fixing it may belong to a separate `wl sync` perf item (scope-creep
  guard: record a linked child, don't absorb).
- **Risk:** memory-per-spawn may be inherent to the current `better-sqlite3` +
  full-JSON payload; trimming payloads could change the fetcher contract —
  needs care to preserve the documented `wl worklist` payload stability.
- **Risk:** in-process SQLite reads on a 100 MB DB can themselves be slow
  (open + FTS DDL ~46–70 ms); the one-open-per-refresh scope must be kept.
- **Assumption:** the operator's "large DB" ≈ 100–200 MB / 2,600+ items
  (ContextHub's own scale) per Q2 answer; ACs are framed at that scale.
- **Assumption:** perceived responsiveness is driven by (a) refresh blocking
  and (b) write→reflect latency, per Q1/Q3 answers.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What does 'unresponsive' mean in practice?" — Answer (operator):
  "(a) The Work Items pane freezes/lags visibly when it refreshes — UI stutters
  or misses keystrokes for seconds", plus freeform "slow to reflect some
  changes" (b). Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Approximately how large is the worklog database where you see this?" —
  Answer (operator): "(a) Similar to ContextHub's own (≈2–3k items, 100 MB+
  worklog.db)". Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Is this a new recurrence after the recent fixes…?" — Answer (operator):
  "Improved but still not good enough" (b). Source: interactive reply.
- Research: measured on this repo's own `.worklog` (109 MB db, 2,631 items);
  timings listed under "Existing state". Prior-work links in "Related work".

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MN53B6B1071X95T** – Epic: Fix TUI Freezing Issues (completed)
- **WL-0MUEK7H39008VVUF** – Ship guard always reports 'Cannot verify pane state': wl list --json (8.5 MB) exceeds the 8 MB maxBuffer (completed)
- **WL-0MPGV61D0006SE7K** – TUI list adapter drops items because wl list JSON is wrapped (completed)

### Repository file matches

# F1 — Large-DB refresh budget harness and baseline

## Background

Parent WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W needs measurable, repeatable evidence for its ACs
(refresh ≤ ~1.5 s p95, event-loop blocking ≤ ~200 ms, spawn/RSS budgets,
write→reflect ≤ 2 s) at ~2,600-item / ~100 MB scale. Today large-DB numbers are
only reported ad hoc (intake "Existing state"); there is no checked-in harness,
so regressions are not caught and the fix items cannot prove their targets.
This item builds the verification foundation first (test-first), reusing the
ratchet/baseline pattern proven in WL-0MVFRRAXD001E7AN (startup import-budget
harness).

## Target outcome

A checked-in, reproducible large-DB performance harness that records the
pre-change baseline, asserts the parent's AC budgets, and gates the
implementation items (F3–F6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture generator deterministically builds a large worklog DB (~2,600
  items, nested parent/child + dependency edges, ~100 MB on disk) in a temp
  `.worklog` without touching the repo's real worklog; generation is fast
  enough for a default-suite test run (< ~20 s) while a "full-scale" variant
  is runnable on demand via a documented command.
- The harness measures, for a default-view refresh: end-to-end wall time (p95
  over ≥ 5 samples), aggregate TUI event-loop blocking time, spawned `wl`
  process count per refresh, peak RSS per spawn and aggregate for a single
  pane, and write→reflect latency via the event-driven watch path.
- A baseline budget file (e.g. `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-budget.json`)
  records pre-change numbers for each metric, the parent AC targets, and the
  measurement commands so numbers can be re-quoted in work-item comments.
- A fast ratchet/regression test in the default suite fails when a metric
  exceeds its budget plus documented headroom; timing is CPU-time based
  (`process.resourceUsage`) so a loaded shared host does not cause false
  failures (same approach as WL-0MVFRRAXD001E7AN).
- Spawn-count assertions include the zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee and the
  single consolidated `wl worklist` read for the default view — preserving the
  documented no-regression invariants (parent AC 6).
- Documentation: a `docs/dev/` note describes how to run the harness at full
  scale and re-baseline; the reference-host report is quoted in the
  completion comment.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `packages/herdr/test/perf/` with the fixture generator and harness, wired
  to the existing test runner and excluded from editor/agent ignore rules.
- Implement metric collectors (wall/CPU time, spawn accounting via the
  fetcher's injectable exec seam, RSS via `process.resourceUsage` + per-spawn
  `maxBuffer`/`ps` where available).
- Write the budget JSON, ratchet assertion, and docs; run the harness to
  capture the baseline quoted in the completion comment.
- Wire full-scale runs into a documented npm script (`test:perf:large`).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — fixture generator + metric collectors.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-budget.json` — baseline budgets and AC targets.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — reuse the injectable exec seam (`setExecFileAsync`) and refresh-scope helpers for spawn/RSS accounting.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — how to run/re-baseline (append).

## Deliverables

- Fixture generator + harness + ratchet test (green at baseline), budget JSON
  with measured pre-change numbers, docs, and a completion comment quoting the
  reference-host baseline.

## Dependencies

- None beyond parent WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W.

# F2 — Profile remaining Herdr refresh cost drivers

## Background

The intake brief lists known large-DB cost candidates but none are yet
profiled rigorously: `wl sync` ≈ 36 s (git push/network vs JSONL export vs DB
compaction?), `wl list`/`wl worklist` spawn RSS ~130–145 MB, per-expand
`wl dep list` / single-parent `wl list --parent` spawns, and the in-process
SQLite open cost (~46–70 ms FTS DDL). Parent AC 1–6 need per-driver numbers and
a decision on what is in scope vs. a separate `wl sync` perf item (intake
scope-creep guard: "record a linked child, don't absorb"). Uses the F1 harness.

## Target outcome

A ranked, evidence-backed cost table for one full refresh (event → data load →
render) plus a `wl sync` breakdown, with a decision per driver: in-scope fix
(feeds F3–F6) or separate work item (created with a blocker edge).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A measured cost table (wall time and CPU time, using the F1 harness at full
  scale) attributing refresh cost across: `wl worklist` payload build + JSON
  parse, in-process SQLite open (DDL/FTS) + queries, per-expand child/dep
  reads, hydrator per-item `wl dep list` spawns, and render. Each row states
  measured value, cost driver, and recommended action (fix-in-scope / separate
  item / no-op).
- A `wl sync` profile on a ≥ 100 MB DB breaking the ~36 s into: git fetch/push
  (network), JSONL export, DB compaction/wal checkpoint, and CLI overhead.
  Conclusion explicitly marks whether a `wl sync` perf fix is required and
  whether it is in-scope here or a new work item per the intake guardrail. If a
  separate item is warranted, it is created with a blocking dependency recorded
  on this item — this item itself does NOT absorb a `wl sync` fix.
- Confirmed memory breakdown for a `wl worklist` / `wl list` spawn (~130–145 MB
  peak): full JSON materialisation vs enrichments vs SQLite read cache. States
  whether the payload can be trimmed without changing the documented `wl
  worklist` payload contract (feeding F5's decision).
- The report is recorded as a comment on this item with exact re-runnable
  commands, timestamps, and the reference-host path.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add/reuse the F1 harness for full-scale sampling of each refresh stage
  (probe points via existing spawn accounting and scope helpers).
- Profile `wl sync` with `time -v` / `--loglevel`, git dry-run and
  `git count-objects`/pack inspection, and DB pragma checks (`page_count`,
  `journal_mode`, wal size).
- Triage `wl list`/worklist RSS with `node --cpu-prof`/`--heapsnapshot` or
  `--trace-gc` on the CLI entry; attribute to payload vs enrichment.
- Write the report comment and, if warranted, `wl create` the separate `wl
  sync` perf child with `wl dep add <sync-item> <this-item>`.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — full-scale sampling driver.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — spawn accounting / probe points.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` and `src/sync.ts` — `wl sync` pipeline to profile.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — payload build to profile/mem-diagnose.

## Deliverables

- Ranked cost table + sync breakdown comment, decision record, and (if
  required) a separate linked `wl sync` perf work item.

## Dependencies

- F1 (harness and baseline).

# F3 — Auto-sync isolation: pane never stalls on `wl sync`

## Background

Auto-sync spawns `wl sync` (≈ 36 s on a ~100 MB DB) fire-and-forget every 60 s.
Parent AC 3 requires that while a long sync is in flight the pane stays
responsive: no lock wait, no event-loop stall, no "hanging" indication beyond a
brief non-blocking status notice. The current single-flight + heartbeat +
`--if-idle` guards (auto-sync.ts) bound spawns but do not yet guarantee the
pane never competes with or waits on a long-running sync (IO contention with
refresh reads, process-group/PID effects, no UI notice). F2 profiles where the
~36 s goes and whether a `wl sync` fix is a separate item (scope guard).

## Target outcome

A refresh completes within budget while a long `wl sync` is in flight in the
background, with a non-blocking status notice shown; the pane never waits on
the sync lock or its process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a simulated/hooked long ~36 s `wl sync` in flight (F1 harness), a
  concurrent default-view refresh completes within the parent AC 2 budget and
  blocks the TUI event loop ≤ 200 ms aggregate (parent AC 1); asserted by an
  automated test in the default suite.
- The auto-sync spawn is verified off the TUI event loop and the pane shows a
  non-blocking status notice ("syncing…") that never blocks input; no "hanging"
  UI state beyond the notice (parent AC 3).
- No lock contention: an in-flight sync does not hold/reset the same SQLite
  handle or filesystem lock the pane's in-process refresh scope uses; a refresh
  never waits for a sync to finish (asserted with in-flight instrumentation:
  e.g. start time monotonic, no wait gap equal to remaining sync time).
- Existing guarantees preserved: single-flight, cross-pane heartbeat skip,
  `--if-idle`, 60 s interval, no concurrent sync spawns (parent AC 6); the F1
  zero-spawn-when-idle assertion still passes.
- If F2 concludes a `wl sync` perf fix is a separate work item, this item stays
  limited to pane-side isolation and references that item — no scope creep.

## Minimal Implementation

- Route auto-sync through the same background-task runtime used elsewhere
  (`packages/herdr/src` background helpers) with explicit event-loop decoupling
  and a tiny status model the pane renders without blocking.
- Add in-flight instrumentation (process start + PID + elapsed) so a refresh
  can verify non-interference; extend F1 harness with a "sync in flight"
  scenario.
- Add the non-blocking status notice and back it with the automated
  responsiveness test above.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — spawn path, single-flight, heartbeat.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — refresh orchestration + status rendering.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — in-flight sync scenario.

## Deliverables

- Off-loop auto-sync with status notice, in-flight instrumentation, an
  automated responsiveness-under-sync test, and updated
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` notes.

## Dependencies

- F2 profile results (plus F1 harness).

# F4 — In-process dependency and child reads on expand

## Background

Expanding a node still triggers per-item `wl dep list` (hydrator, ≈ 0.4 s each)
and single-parent `wl list --parent` spawns (`fetchChildrenForItem`); each
spawn costs 0.5–0.9 s and ~130–145 MB RSS. The batching in-process path already
exists for multi-parent fetches (`fetchChildrenForItems` via the refresh
scope) but the single-parent and per-hydrator-item paths still spawn. Parent
AC 2 bounds refresh end-to-end to ≤ ~1.5 s including per-expand child fetches,
and AC 5 bounds aggregate spawn RSS.

## Target outcome

Expanding a node (or hydrating its deps) performs zero `wl` spawns on the
large-DB path: all child/dependency reads are served in-process through the
one refresh-scoped SQLite connection, with the existing fail-open CLI fallback
unchanged for correctness edge cases.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Expanding a parent performs no `wl list --parent` / `wl dep list` spawn (F1
  spawn-count assertion) when the in-process path is available; child and
  dependency rows match the CLI's ordering, fields, depth and enrichment
  semantics on a ~2,600-item fixture.
- Hydrator dependency lookups use the in-process/refresh-scope read (or a
  bounded batched lookup) instead of one `wl dep list` spawn per item; the
  hydrator timeout behaviour from WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P is preserved.
- Fail-open preserved: when no worklog dir / SQLite file / `@worklog/shared` is
  available, or a stored audit fingerprint requires CLI enrichment, behaviour
  falls back to spawns exactly as today (existing `fetcher-inprocess` and
  `worklist-expand-refresh` tests still green).
- The one-open-per-refresh scope is kept — no new per-helper DB opens are
  introduced (parent AC constraints).
- Existing Herdr + TUI suites pass with zero-spawn-when-idle preserved (parent
  AC 6).

## Minimal Implementation

- Route `fetchChildrenForItem` through the shared batch/in-process reader when
  a scope is available; keep its signature and fail-open.
- Convert per-item hydrator `wl dep list` calls to a batched in-process dep
  read within the refresh scope (grouping visible items into one pass), with
  fail-open for the fingerprint/enrichment cases.
- Extend F1 harness assertions (expanded-node spawn counts) and the
  `fetchChildrenForItem/ForItems` in-process tests.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — single-parent fetch + batch reader + scope.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — per-item `wl dep list` calls.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — expand orchestration.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-inprocess.test.ts`, `worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts` — extend.

## Deliverables

- Spawn-free expand + hydrator dep reads on the in-process path, updated
  fail-open tests, F1 harness assertions green, and a completion comment with
  large-DB timing/spawn deltas vs baseline.

## Dependencies

- F2 profile results (confirms dep/child reads as a cost driver) and F1
  harness baselines.

# F5 — Bound `wl` spawn memory and concurrency for a single pane

## Background

Each surviving `wl worklist`/`wl list` spawn peaks at ~130–145 MB RSS on a
~100 MB DB (intake measurements). Parent AC 5 is satisfied either by reducing
per-spawn memory below a documented budget or by bounding concurrent spawns so
aggregate RSS for a single pane stays under a documented ceiling (e.g.
≤ ~300 MB). F2 determines where the memory goes and whether the `wl worklist`
payload can be trimmed without breaking its documented contract.

## Target outcome

A documented, enforced per-pane RSS/spawn budget that guarantees parent AC 5
at large-DB scale, without regressing small-DB behaviour or the consolidated
single-read default view.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-spawn or aggregate budget confirmed: measured peak aggregate RSS for a
  single pane during a full refresh (F1 harness, full scale) is at or below a
  documented ceiling (target ≤ ~300 MB as in parent AC 5), OR per-spawn peak is
  reduced below the ~130–145 MB observed baseline and the reduced number is
  documented as the new budget.
- Based on F2's evidence, either: (a) a payload trim on `wl worklist` (drop
  unused fields/streaming) with the documented payload contract preserved or
  explicitly revised and tested, or (b) a documented spawn cap (e.g. N
  concurrent `wl` spawns, queueing/deferred reads) whose aggregate RSS is
  asserted by an automated test — without waiting under the event loop.
- The budget and its enforcement are documented in
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` (parent AC 5 "documented budget").
- No regression to small worklogs and no change to the consolidated
  single-read default-view norm; zero-spawn-when-idle preserved (parent AC 6).
- All remaining `wl` spawns execute off the TUI event loop, and deferred/
  queued reads never block input: the F1 harness event-loop aggregation stays
  within the parent AC 1 ≤ ~200 ms bound with a spawn-heavy fixture (intake
  candidate 4).
- No new heavy dependencies (parent constraints) — prefer reuse of the
  in-process SQLite read path over new spawns.

## Minimal Implementation

- Apply the F2-validated memory fix (payload trim with contract test, or
  streaming) and/or add a concurrency semaphore around `wl` spawns in the
  fetch path with queued fallback reads.
- Add F1 harness assertions for aggregate RSS, spawn count, and event-loop
  blocking at full scale.
- Ensure every remaining spawn is dispatched off the TUI event loop (existing
  background-task runtime) with a bounded queue; assert no input-lock via the
  harness.
- Update docs; record before/after numbers in the completion comment.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — spawn path, exec seam, spawn cap.
- `src/commands/worklist.ts` — payload build (if trim chosen).
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — RSS/spawn assertions.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — budget documentation.

## Deliverables

- Enforced spawn/RSS budget with automated assertion, validated memory fix
  (trim or cap) per F2 evidence, docs, and measured before/after numbers.

## Dependencies

- F2 (memory breakdown + payload-contract decision), F1 harness.

# F6 — Single, cheap in-process SQLite open per refresh

## Background

In-process SQLite reads on a ~100 MB DB carry a non-trivial open cost (open +
pragmas + FTS DDL ~46–70 ms measured in earlier work; the one-open-per-refresh
scope from WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B exists to amortise it). Surviving per-helper
opens, read-only open DDL, and connection reuse across ticks are the remaining
levers. Parent AC 2 (≤ ~1.5 s default-view refresh p95) and AC 1 (no event-loop
stall) constrain this cost; F2 quantifies its share.

## Target outcome

A default-view refresh performs at most one cheap in-process SQLite open
(shared across all refresh helpers, read-only, minimal/no DDL when already
initialised), and the open cost is small enough that it never threatens the
refresh budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An automated test (F1 harness, full scale) asserts a default-view refresh
  performs at most one in-process DB open per refresh and that helper reads
  reuse that single connection (no per-helper open).
- The read-only open path is measured and documented: open+pragmas cost is
  recorded after the change (target: eliminate the ~46–70 ms FTS-DDL hit on
  already-initialised stores, e.g. by skipping DDL when schema/version already
  present), with numbers below the refresh budget headroom.
- Open is verified off the TUI event loop / within the existing refresh scope
  (parent AC 1); any background warm-up does not overlap a visible refresh in a
  blocking way.
- Fail-open preserved: a read-only open failure degrades to the existing `wl`
  spawn fallback; no change to the hydrator's core behaviour or scheduler
  (parent constraints).
- Existing Herdr + TUI suites pass; zero-spawn-when-idle preserved (parent
  AC 6).

## Minimal Implementation

- Refactor the refresh-scope open to: one shared connection per refresh across
  all helpers, read-only pragma set, and schema/DDL only when required
  (version check); verify `@worklog/shared` `WorklogDatabase` surface honours
  a read-only/no-DDL mode or the skip is done at the caller.
- Add harness timing for the open step; update docs budgeting the open cost.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — refresh scope + `InProcessRefreshScope` open.
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `WorklogDatabase` open/DDL path.
- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — open-cost timing.

## Deliverables

- One-cheap-open-per-refresh with automated single-open + timing assertions,
  fail-open tests green, and documented open-cost numbers.

## Dependencies

- F2 (quantifies open cost share), F1 harness.

# F7 — Large-DB responsiveness verification at scale

## Background

The parent's ACs are acceptance criteria for the whole pane behaviour at scale.
F1–F6 each deliver targeted fixes and tests; this item is the end-to-end
verification slice that confirms every parent AC holds together on a
~2,600-item / ~100 MB fixture after all changes, including the AC 4
write→reflect re-verification (extending WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN to large-DB
scale) and AC 6's full-suite no-regression gate.

## Target outcome

One reproducible end-to-end evidence run (documented commands + test suite)
that every parent acceptance criterion 1–6 is met at large-DB scale.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Pane stays responsive during refresh:** a default-view refresh does not block the TUI event loop for more than ~200 ms of perceived lag in aggregate (verified with an automated test harness or measured timing on a large fixture DB) — keystrokes/commands process promptly while a refresh is in flight. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Single-figure refresh cost on large DBs:** a default-view refresh end-to-end (event → data load → render) is bounded to ≤ ~1.5 s wall-clock p95 on a DB of ~2,600 items / ~100 MB, including per-expand child fetches; the consolidated `wl worklist` single-read path stays the norm — no regression to multi-spawn refreshes. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Auto-sync cannot stall the pane:** while a long `wl sync` (measured ~36 s on the 100 MB DB) is in flight in the background, the pane remains responsive — no lock wait, no event-loop stall, at most a brief non-blocking status notice. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Change reflection latency:** after a `wl` write, the pane reflects the change within ~2 s p95 via the event-driven watch path at large-DB scale. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **Reduced memory footprint:** a refresh's spawned `wl` processes peak at no more than a documented per-spawn budget below the ~130–145 MB/spawn observed baseline, OR concurrent spawns are bounded so aggregate RSS for a single pane stays under a documented ceiling (e.g. ≤ ~300 MB). (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)
- **No regressions:** the full Herdr plugin + TUI test suites pass; the zero-spawn-when-idle guarantee and event-driven watch semantics are preserved. (evidence: full-scale F1 harness report)

- All measured numbers are quoted in the completion comment against the F1 baseline; if any criterion is not met, the blocking fix item is referenced with its data rather than accepted silently.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the F1 harness with an end-to-end "all ACs" report mode aggregating
  every metric into one JSON report plus a human summary.
- Drive the event-driven write→reflect measurement at full scale (reusing the
  watch path from WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN) and assert AC 4 at large-DB scale.
- Run the full suite + full-scale harness, record the report comment, and mark
  this item (and via parent workflow, the parent) ready once green.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/test/perf/large-db-harness.ts` — end-to-end AC report mode.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — metrics under test (spawn/refresh path).
- `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` — in-flight sync scenario under test.
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — final numbers.

## Deliverables

- End-to-end AC evidence report (comment + checked-in harness mode), full-suite
  green, and the parent ready for review.

## Dependencies

- F3, F4, F5, F6 (all targeted fixes landed).
