# One-per-idle-window reservation race guard

## Summary

Assert and enforce the operator requirement that an idle window produces
**at most one** launch: after a ticket-backed launch no further pane starts
until a fresh status tick shows `local_prefills_in_flight <
local_max_concurrent_prefills` **and** a new reservation is granted for that
specific launch. Pin the same-tick two-instance race with a test.

## Covers parent ACs

- Parent **AC3** (one-per-idle-window) — the whole slice.

## Target outcome

Two herdr instances observing the same idle window cannot both launch; the
loser defers with the proxy's own refusal evidence instead of queueing a
doomed pane that later falls back to remote.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **C3-AC1 — one-per-idle-window (parent AC3).** two instances observing the same idle window produce at most one launch; the second defers with the refusal evidence (test modelling the same-tick race).
   The test runs two `createDowntimeWorker` instances against one mock proxy in
   the same tick and asserts exactly one pane is spawned, the second dispatch
   refused by the reservation call.
- **C3-AC2 — post-launch suppression (parent AC3).** After a successful
   launch, no second pane launches on later ticks while
   `local_prefills_in_flight >= local_max_concurrent_prefills`; only a fresh
   status tick with headroom **and** a ticket granted for that specific launch
   permits another spawn.
- **C3-AC3 — losing-instance evidence (parent AC4, dispatch evidence).** The
   losing instance's decision entry records the refusal reason,
   `retry_after_s` and `admit: false`, with a header token distinguishable
   from `prefill-cap`/`prefill-gate` so an operator can tell a lost race from
   a paced stop.
- **C3-AC4 — coordination-path parity.** The same one-per-idle-window rule
   holds on the coordination-leader dispatch path
   (`dispatchFromCoordination`) — no second launch in the same idle window
   there either (test).
- **C3-AC5 — no regression.** The guard never admits a dispatch the per-slot /
   saturated / prefill gates would refuse and never changes single-instance
   behaviour when the proxy grants normally (existing `downtime-worker.*`
   suites stay green).
- **C3-AC6 — docs (parent AC5 partial).** `packages/herdr/README.md` and
   `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` document the one-per-idle-window rule
   and how it composes with the existing coordination leader.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** C2 (reserve client + dispatch gate).
- **Blocks:** C5 (docs/suite gate).

## Constraints

- The proxy is the arbiter (atomic reservation grant); herdr does **not** add
  a second distributed lock — it only refuses to launch without its own
  granted ticket.
- Never raise the concurrency budget; never bypass the fail-closed per-slot
  handling (`WL-0MUXVPXAZ005RESW`).
- Reuse the C2 reserve client; no duplicate reservation code path.

## Risky assumptions

- The proxy grants at most one ticket per idle window across instances
  (stated contract). If it instead grants N tickets for N slots, the guard
  still holds for the serialised default (`cap = 1`); the `cap > 1` case
  intentionally permits `cap` concurrent launches, matching prefill headroom.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — launch/refusal guard state on the
  tick and on `dispatchFromCoordination`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` /
  `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` / new race test file — race and
  suppression tests (file chosen at implementation time).
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

## Deliverables

- In-flight launch guard, same-tick race test, coordination-path parity test,
  refusal-evidence decision entries, doc sections.
data.title: One-per-idle-window reservation race guard

# Per-turn local preference and route logging

## Summary

Give agent panes a per-turn capacity claim: a pi extension injects
`X-Local-Preference` (`local-only` for work the operator marks local-first,
`remote-ok` for background work) on the Local Proxy provider path and records
`X-Local-Route` / `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` response headers into a route log,
so a refusal is immediate and honest instead of a silent 120 s proxy-side
wait. The herdr runner sets the preference per spawn from a policy knob.

## Covers parent ACs

- Parent **AC4** (per-turn preference) — the whole slice (the dispatch-side
  decision evidence is delivered by C2-AC4).

## Target outcome

An agent turn either gets a local route or receives an immediate, recorded
fallback decision; the operator can read per-session route evidence next to
the dispatch decision log.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **C4-AC1 — per-turn preference (parent AC4).** the runner sends `X-Local-Preference` per configured policy, parses `X-Local-Route`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason`, and records both in the decision log (tests).
   Concretely: the herdr agent runner (`packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` /
   `run-pi-agent.sh`) sets the preference for each spawn from a policy knob
   (proposed `HERDR_LOCAL_PREFERENCE` env / herdr setting
   `downtimeLocalPreference`, default `local-only` for downtime panes and
   `remote-ok` for background/scheduled work); the extension sends that value
   on every proxied request and writes one JSONL route line per turn to the
   bounded route log; pure-module and runner-script tests assert both values
   and the unset (no header) case.
- **C4-AC2 — route log detail.** Each route line carries session id,
   timestamp, route, fallback reason and model, appended to a bounded log
   (proposed `.worklog/local-route.log`, rolling convention like
   `downtime-dispatches.log`, capped at 2000 entries). Absent or malformed
   headers write no entry and never throw.
- **C4-AC3 — fail-open backcompat.** With no knob set, no headers from an
   older proxy, or the extension absent, requests are byte-identical to
   today's (no header, no log, no behaviour change); a capture failure never
   breaks a turn (tests).
- **C4-AC4 — dispatch correlation.** Route-log entries carry the pi session
   id and the reservation ticket (when one was forwarded), so a dispatcher
   decision can be correlated with the turns it produced (test + doc).
- **C4-AC5 — docs (parent AC5 partial).** `packages/herdr/README.md` and
   `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` document the preference policy knob and
   the route log, with matching code comments.

## Dependencies

- **None** inside this item — independent of C1–C3 (separate pi extension +
  runner path) and can run in parallel; it only shares the contract header
  names pinned in C1.
- **Blocks:** C5 (docs/suite gate).

## Constraints

- The pi extension is the only place that can see the response headers (pi
  owns the request path); reuse the established extension pattern
  (`~/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-sse-signals` wraps the Local Proxy provider's
  `streamSimple` with a capturing fetch) and the repo installer
  (`scripts/install-pi-extension.sh`).
- Fail-open only: a missing preference knob or a broken extension must never
  block or alter a turn.
- No new polling loop; route logging is per response.
- No secrets/PII in the route log.

## Risky assumptions

- Pi's provider override can inject a request header and read response
  headers (precedent: `proxy-sse-signals` reads the body stream via a
  capturing fetch; the same wrapper exposes `Response.headers`).
- The route log location is acceptable as a per-root `.worklog/` artifact
  (same convention as the existing downtime logs); confirm at implementation
  if the producer prefers `~/.pi/agent/logs/`.

**OPEN QUESTION (producer):** is `local-only` the right default for downtime
panes (fail fast to remote) vs a wait-for-local default? Default proposed from
the parent's "work the operator marks local-first" wording; the knob makes it
configurable either way.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/index.ts` (new provider wrapper)
  and `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.ts` (new pure
  module, unit-testable without pi) — precedent
  `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/`.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `shared/run-pi-agent.sh`,
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (env/knob plumbing),
  `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` (knob default + clamp).
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

## Deliverables

- Local-preference pi extension + tests, runner/knob plumbing, bounded route
  log writer, doc sections.

# Worktree `@worklog/shared` resolves to the main checkout's stale `dist`

## Background

Discovered while implementing WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO (persist write-detection
tests): the new `tests/unit` tests exercise `WorklogDatabase.import()`
changes made in `packages/shared/src/database.ts`, but they failed with
"spy never called" symptoms until the **main checkout's**
`packages/shared/dist` was replaced with the worktree's build output.

Root cause chain:

1. `implement.py start` symlinks `<worktree>/node_modules -> <main-checkout>/node_modules`.
2. `<main-checkout>/node_modules/@worklog/shared` is itself a relative
   symlink `../../packages/shared`, i.e. the **main checkout's** shared
   package.
3. `packages/shared/package.json` `main`/`exports` point at
   `./dist/database.js` (gitignored build output).
4. `npm run build` inside the worktree rebuilds the **worktree's**
   `packages/shared/dist`, which nothing in the worktree resolves to —
   only `packages/shared/src/*.test.ts` (relative imports) see the change.

Effect: for any item that changes `packages/shared/src/**`, the default
gate (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) and the CLI (`src/**`) run against
whatever `packages/shared/dist` the main checkout last built. Correct new
code fails the gate (as seen here), and — worse — an agent can "fix" the
tests by weakening them, or a genuinely broken shared change can pass
because the gate exercised the stale build.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Running the sanctioned gate (`python3 <test skill>/scripts/run_tests.py --type full --scope full`) from a fresh worktree that changes `packages/shared/src/**` exercises the worktree's shared code, not the main checkout's `dist` — proven by a test-only change in the worktree that the gate observes.
- No writes through the `node_modules` symlink into the main checkout's `node_modules` (documented constraint), and the main checkout stays git-clean apart from gitignored build artifacts.
- `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md` (or a new `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` note) documents the resolution order and the supported way to make shared changes visible in a worktree.
- `implement.py finish`/`start` (or the test skill) either handles the shared-dist refresh automatically or emits an actionable warning naming the stale dist path.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/package.json` — `main`/`exports` → `./dist/database.js`.
- `node_modules/@worklog/shared` — relative symlink to `../../packages/shared`.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/scripts/link-shared.mjs` — existing link tooling.
- `.pi/skills_extensions/implement/` / implement skill scripts — where a refresh hook or warning would live.

## Provenance

- discovered-from: WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO

## Notes

Workaround used by WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO: build the shared package in the
worktree (`npm run build:shared`) then `rsync -a --delete
packages/shared/dist/ <main-checkout>/packages/shared/dist/` before running
the gate. `dist/` is gitignored so the main checkout stays clean.

## Summary

Add a `wl doctor prefix` subcommand that changes the configured project prefix in `.worklog/config.yaml` and renumbers every existing work item to the new prefix, preserving each item's suffix (e.g. `OSL-0MVK31VYQ007CN37` → `CC-0MVK31VYQ007CN37`). The flow must ask for confirmation before it changes anything, default to a read-only preview, and emit a machine-readable rename map.

## Motivation

Requested from the ContentCreator project (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContentCreator`), whose configured prefix is `OSL` while the project is now branded `CC`. 1207 work items carry the `OSL-` prefix, and `wl doctor foreign-items` correctly classifies any item whose prefix differs from `.worklog/config.yaml` as foreign — so editing the prefix by hand would make the whole backlog look foreign and break cross-project lookups.

## Scope (proposed)

- `wl doctor prefix` — read-only preview: current prefix, counts of items/comments/dependency edges/audit records, and sample renames.
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX>` — declare the target prefix (validated: non-empty, no `-`, ASCII alphanumeric).
- `wl doctor prefix --to <PREFIX> --confirm` — apply: rewrite the config prefix, then rewrite every ID-bearing record (`workitems.id`, parent references, dependency edges, comments' `workItemId`, audit results, waivers, and any other ID column), and write a rename map (`osl→cc` pairs) to `.worklog/prefix-rename-<timestamp>.json`.
- Confirmation gate: interactive run without `--confirm` prompts and requires an explicit `y`; a non-TTY run without `--confirm` aborts with no writes and a non-zero exit.
- Idempotent: re-running after a successful rename reports a no-op.
- `--json` output for scripting.
- Docs: `DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md` and `CLI.md`.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- [ ] `wl doctor prefix` (preview) reports counts and sample renames and changes nothing; covered by unit and temp-store integration tests.
- [ ] `--confirm` rewrites every ID-bearing record (items, parents, dependency edges, comments, audit results, waivers) and writes the rename map.
- [ ] Confirmation gate: non-interactive without `--confirm` aborts with a non-zero exit and zero writes; interactive requires explicit `y`.
- [ ] Re-running after a successful rename is a no-op, and a mid-run failure leaves the store recoverable (transactional or a documented rollback).
- [ ] `wl doctor foreign-items` reports zero foreign items after a confirmed rename.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated (CLI.md, DOCTOR_AND_MIGRATIONS.md, code comments).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Out of scope

Rewriting ID references held outside the worklog store — code comments, docs, test fixtures, git commit messages, branch and worktree names. The requesting project owns that sweep and will use the rename map.

## Related

- Requested by work in the ContentCreator project (`discovered-from` recorded there).

## Summary

`.worklog/config.defaults.yaml` in this repo has no `syncAllowedAuthors` list, so `wl sync` runs the author-identity gate in strict mode: it refuses to merge any incoming commit on `refs/worklog/data` whose author email differs from the store's `git config user.email`. The shared ref carries 3,687 commits authored by `pi@local` while this checkout's `user.email` is `sorra@thewizardscode.com`, so agent-initiated `wl sync` runs here were refused and needed `--allow-foreign-author`.

## Fix (as shipped)

Declare a narrow allow-list in `.worklog/config.yaml` — **not** in `.worklog/config.defaults.yaml`: that file is this repository's project *template* (`projectName: TestProject`, `prefix: TEST`), so identities listed there would leak into every project created from it.

```yaml
syncAllowedAuthors:
  - 250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com
  - pi@local
```

Never use `null`/`true` (allow-all); empty-author commits must stay refused.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The effective `syncAllowedAuthors` (defaults merged with `.worklog/config.yaml`) lists both identities, and `config.yaml` never shadows a defaults entry with a narrower list.
- [x] `wl sync` and `wl sync --dry-run` succeed in this checkout without `--allow-foreign-author`.
- [x] A guard test drives the real config merge and the real gate: listed authors accepted, unknown author refused, empty author refused even with the allow-all override (`tests/config-sync-allowed-authors.test.ts`).
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes — blocked by `tests/unit/persist-write-detection.test.ts`, already red on `dev` before this change (9 failures, introduced by commit `0d8324df`); triaged as `WL-0MVM9E3SV003III0`.

## Observed

Found while filing WL-0MVM8V79C003XH2J (prefix rename request) on 2026-10-24; the first sync was completed with `--allow-foreign-author` as a one-off, then `git pull` was run and `wl sync` re-tested.

# Split worklist TUI loop into context and handlers

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B. **Phase:** 6 of 7 (the hard part).

## Target outcome

`runWorklistTui` (currently lines 5581–7899, ~2,319 lines of nested closures over
one mutable context) becomes a thin orchestrator over named handler modules,
with a **single interface-typed context object owned by one module** and passed
explicitly to handler functions — no state duplication and no class-based
controller rewrite (parent constraint).

## Scope (measured closure groups inside `runWorklistTui`)

| New module | Contents | Est. size |
|---|---|---|
| `worklist.tui-context.ts` | The context interface + factory: `opts`, `termSize`, `items`, `state`, `renderer`, `inputActive`, view flags (`formState`, `preFormMode`, `preHelpMode`, `helpScrollOffset`, `shipItDialog`, `podcastNotice`, `blockedNotice`), freeze/sprint flags, dispose hooks. Single owner of the mutable context (AC5) | ~250 |
| `worklist.tui-handlers.ts` | Pane gate, agent tracker, live event subscriptions, pane-marker apply/refresh/batching, metadata blocker resolution + cache (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8), freeze-state refresh, review-queue sprint state | ~560 |
| `worklist.tui-refresh.ts` | Non-blocking sync status notice (F3 — WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N), `cleanup`, `closeEventSubscriber`, `doRefresh` (single-flight + pending), `doSync`, `openShipItDialog` / `openShipItDialogGuarded` | ~480 |
| `worklist.tui-input.ts` | `dispatchMouse`, `handleKeyInput`, streaming stdin decode (`onData` + `KeypressDecoder`), `readKeyFile`/`writeKeyFile`, `buildHelpEntries`/`buildHelpIconLegend` | ~800 |
| `worklist.tui-render.ts` | `render`, `onResize`, `TaskScheduler` wiring, hydrator runner, resume poll, db-change watch, and the `runWorklistTui` orchestrator that constructs the context and registers handlers | ~570 |

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `runWorklistTui` is retained at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical
   signature and return type (`Promise<WorkItem | undefined>`), implemented as a
   thin orchestrator (context construction + handler registration + teardown);
   no module and no single exported function carries the former 2,319-line body
   (AC1).
2. Every new module ≤1,000 lines with a responsibility doc comment; the TUI-local
   sub-banners (metadata-panel dependency blockers — WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8,
   review-queue depth indicator, event-driven window status — WL-0MSHB7DHO004RHBJ,
   non-blocking sync status notice — WL-0MVJV2O7H003HY9N, mouse event dispatch —
   WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ AC2–AC6, streaming stdin decode — WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH,
   consolidated scheduler loop — WL-0MSG4NMF0000YBRP, hydrator —
   WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI) and their inline work-item ids move verbatim (AC6).
3. **Single context, explicit passing.** The context type is declared once in
   `worklist.tui-context.ts`; handler modules receive it as a parameter and
   never re-declare a mutable field it already owns. `WorkItemListState`
   remains a single instance created by the orchestrator (AC5); the split guard's
   single-owner gate stays green.
4. Lifecycle ordering is preserved exactly: event-subscription setup, pane gate,
   refresh single-flight/pending, scheduler ticks, hydrator, resume poll and
   teardown order are unchanged — verified by the unmodified
   `worklist-integration.test.ts`, `worklist-active-pane-marker.test.ts`,
   `worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts`, `worklist-consolidated-refresh.test.ts`,
   `worklist-watch.test.ts`, `worklist-inflight.test.ts`,
   `worklist-sync-notice.test.ts` and `worklist.test.ts` TUI blocks (AC3).
5. Split guard, `tsc --noEmit`/build and the full `packages/herdr` suite pass;
   no new cycle; no runtime barrel import (AC4, AC9).
6. Docs updated: `packages/herdr/README.md` (module-layout block, `onPaneFocused`
   and `isInputActive` references at ~1619 and ~1781, and the ~1829 "task
   registration in `worklist.ts`" note), `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`,
   `docs/dev/herdr-events-subscribe-reliability.md`,
   `docs/dev/herdr-hydrator.md`, `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md`,
   `docs/dev/wl-process-spawning-investigation.md` — all path references resolve
   to the new modules.
7. **State ownership is explicit and singular.** The mutable
   `WorkItemListState` (848-line section) and the TUI-local mutable context
   currently closed over by `runWorklistTui` each live in exactly one module;
   extraction must not duplicate mutable state or fork the source of truth.
   → Owned by this slice: `WorkItemListState` and the extracted TUI context each live in exactly one module and no mutable state is duplicated.

## Minimal implementation

1. Introduce `worklist.tui-context.ts` with the context interface and factory;
   move the `opts`/state/flag declarations into it **without** changing any
   initial value or ordering.
2. Extract `worklist.tui-handlers.ts` (subscriptions, pane markers, blockers,
   freeze/sprint state) as functions taking the context.
3. Extract `worklist.tui-refresh.ts` (`doRefresh`/`doSync`/ship-it dialog/notice/
   cleanup) as functions taking the context.
4. Extract `worklist.tui-input.ts` (`handleKeyInput`/`dispatchMouse`/`onData`/
   key-file IO/help entries) as functions taking the context.
5. Extract `worklist.tui-render.ts` (render/resize/scheduler/hydrator/resume
   poll/db-change watch) and reduce `runWorklistTui` to orchestration.
   Land steps 1–5 as **separate commits**, each with the full suite green, so a
   behavioural regression is attributable to one closure group.
6. Run guard + build + suite; update docs.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-context.ts` — new (single context owner).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-handlers.ts` — new.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.tui-refresh.ts` — new.

Discovered during plan review of WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ (discovered-from:WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ).

Producer finding from the machine-hygiene session (2025-10-21): propose_remediations() in skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py emits a renice action for every large RSS contributor under memory/swap pressure without inspecting the target's current nice value. In the observed run every proposed target was already at nice 19 or 0, and the targets included two live test suites (AI_Hell vitest, tce-the-rising browser suite) - the action would have slowed active work.

Suggested fix (from producer): skip renice when min(nice) over the target pids is already >= the proposed nice value, and surface the current nice value in the action's reason/target so the operator can see why an action is proposed or suppressed.

Note: this is deliberately separate from the duplication fix in WL-0MVI8YJ1H007HUEZ (dedupe + single render); this item is the semantic safety change and needs process-nice collection support.

Scope: scanning niceness (/proc/<pid>/stat field 19) for target pids, suppressing no-op renicces, and tests for both suppressed and emitted cases. Related: skill/machine-hygiene/scripts/pressure_analysis.py (propose_remediations), metrics collection if nice must be collected centrally.

Goal: a local-only pane whose prompt exceeds the local provider's context ceiling should degrade predictably instead of stalling or failing, and the reason should be visible to the operator.

Observed problem: the local provider rejects a local-only request when the projected prompt exceeds ~38k tokens warm, or ~25k on a cold prefix. Because the pane is labelled local-only the proxy refuses the local route, and the work is not processed on the local slot. Evidence in this deployment's route logs (.worklog/local-route.log, 697 turns across 5 roots): 49 turns route remote with fallbackReason resident_prefix_insufficient and 44 with large_context_bypass; 72 turns actually served local. The thresholds and the exact refusal behaviour (hard error vs silent fallback) live in the external llama-proxy (LP project), not in this repo - confirm before designing the fix.

Open design questions to settle in plan:
- Is the correct behaviour a fallback to remote for over-threshold requests, an explicit hard error surfaced to the operator, or pre-dispatch routing (choose remote-ok when the projected context exceeds the ceiling)?
- Where is the projected context size knowable? The pi extension sees the outgoing request (before_provider_headers), the dispatcher does not.
- Interaction with WL-0MVNUIW77000VYAX (low priority -> local-only): over-threshold low-priority work must not become unprocessable.

ACs:
- [ ] Reproduce the failure deterministically (unit test or scripted proxy stub) for a prompt above 38k warm and above 25k cold, recording the observed proxy response headers.
- [ ] Document the confirmed thresholds and the refusal semantics (hard error vs fallback) in docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md.
- [ ] A local-only request over the ceiling produces a deterministic, observable outcome - no silent stall - with the reason recorded in .worklog/local-route.log.
- [ ] The chosen mitigation (fallback, hard error, or pre-dispatch routing) is covered by tests on both sides of each threshold.
- [ ] Operators can see over-threshold refusals without reading raw JSONL (documented query/ or herdr view).
- [ ] Full test suite green.

# tree_coverage AC extraction silently ignores numbered acceptance-criteria lists

discovered-from:WL-0MVGB23MM004X501

## Problem

`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (`extract_acceptance_criteria`) only collects
markdown bullets that start with `- ` or `+ ` inside the `## Acceptance Criteria`
section. Work items whose ACs are a **numbered** list (`1. …`, `2. …`) yield an
empty AC set, so `run_coverage_review` reports `fully_covered: true` /
`recommendation: proceed` with **zero parent ACs** — the AC coverage gate passes
vacuously instead of verifying that children cover the parent.

Observed during planning of WL-0MVGB23MM004X501: `apply_coverage_review` returned
`action: proceed` with `parent_acs: 0` against a description containing nine
numbered ACs. Contributors have worked around it by manually normalising AC lists
to `- ` bullets (e.g. WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS, WL-0MV02VA29009WBEN) or by documenting
the limitation (WL-0MUVSQ4EO00092E7), which means the failure mode is invisible
unless an operator notices a 0-AC result.

## Desired outcome

1. `extract_acceptance_criteria` also parses numbered list items (`1. `, `1) `)
   inside the AC section, keeping continuation lines and inline code intact.
2. A parent section that has a `## Acceptance Criteria` heading but yields zero
   parsed ACs is reported as a **conflict/stop condition** (or an explicit
   warning in the review result) rather than silently `proceed`, so a silent
   vacuous pass is impossible.
3. Existing bullet-form ACs and all currently passing coverage reviews are
   unaffected (regression tests over both formats).
4. Documentation in the plan/intake skills notes the supported AC formats.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Numbered AC lists (`1. …`) and bullet lists (`- …`) are both extracted by
  `extract_acceptance_criteria`, with matching output for equivalent content.
- A numbered AC list in a work item description produces a non-zero
  `parent_acs` count from `run_coverage_review`.
- An `## Acceptance Criteria` section that parses to zero ACs no longer returns
  `recommendation: proceed` silently — it is surfaced as a conflict or explicit
  warning in the review result.
- Unit tests cover: numbered list, bullet list, mixed list, empty AC section, and
  the zero-AC stop/warn behaviour.
- Plan and intake skill docs state which AC formats the tooling recognises.

## Notes

- Workaround for items already affected: normalise the AC list to `- ` bullets
  (wording unchanged) so coverage can be computed.
data.title: tree_coverage AC extraction ignores numbered acceptance-criteria lists

`.pi/test-config.json` pins `suiteCommands` to `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` and `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`. `run_tests.py changed_scope_commands()` returns `None` when custom suite commands are declared, so the implement finish gate and the pre-push full-scope hook only execute those two directories.

Colocated extension suites (`packages/tui/extensions/**/*.test.ts` — e.g. `Worklog/session-health.test.ts`, `Worklog/lib/worklog-dir.test.ts`) therefore never run in the local gate; they only run in CI (`.github/workflows/cli-tests.yml` → `npm test`). The gap is pre-existing (not introduced by WL-0MVGB23MM004X501), but it means extension-only regressions cannot be caught locally.

## Scope

- Decide whether to add a third suite command for `packages/tui/extensions` (and/or `packages/herdr`, which already has a group), weighing runtime cost.
- If added, verify `run_tests.py --scope full --summary` still records a single full-suite cache entry that audits accept.

- discovered-from:WL-0MVGB23MM004X501
data.title: Extend test-config suiteCommands to cover packages/tui extension tests

# Canonical full suite excludes `packages/` tests (tui 22 + shared 12 files)

*Discovered from WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR (canonical suite root-level `tests/` coverage).* That item closed the `tests/` gap by replacing the two narrow `suiteCommands` with the umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`. It deliberately kept its scope to `tests/`, so the `packages/` gap remains.

## Problem Statement

`.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` (the single source of full-suite evidence for `/skill:test --type full`, the ship release gate and audit F3) resolves only to `tests/`. Tracked test files by location:

| Location | Test files | In canonical suite? |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/` | 277 | Yes (since WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR) |
| `packages/herdr` | 129 | No — producer decision (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8); opt-in `--type herdr` / `--group herdr` |
| `packages/tui` | 22 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| `packages/shared` | 12 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| **Repository total** | **440** | **277** |

`packages/tui/**/*.test.ts` (22 files, incl. `packages/tui/extensions/local-preference/local-preference.test.ts`) and `packages/shared/**/*.test.ts` (12 files) run under a bare `npx vitest` / CI but are referenced by neither `suiteCommands` nor any `groups.*` entry, so no gate can execute or cache-evidence them.

## Goal

Every `packages/` test file is either executed by the canonical full suite (or a cache-recorded group that gates the corresponding paths), or has an explicit documented exclusion with a rationale — the same standard WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR applied to `tests/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.pi/test-config.json` covers `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` tests (in `suiteCommands`, or as named `groups` entries wired to their paths so `implement.py finish` selects them), or each exclusion is documented with a rationale in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`.
- A full `/skill:test` run (`python3 <test-skill>/scripts/run_tests.py --type full --json`) reports the newly covered files as executed, with the executed-file count recorded in the work item.
- Any failures surfaced by the change are triaged into `test-failure` work items.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (the "Test gates" section is shared, not duplicated) carries the updated coverage table (files executed / excluded / why) and the measured runtime.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Evidence-path constraint:** full-suite evidence for the audit resolves `--type full` from `suiteCommands` only; a new `groups.*` entry alone does not satisfy a "full suite passes" AC (see `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` → "Cache evidence scope").
- **Vitest filters are substring matches** on the repository-relative path, so `packages/shared` / `packages/tui` can be selected by positional filters (`-- tests` umbrella does not cover them; `-- packages` would also pull in `packages/herdr`, which is excluded by producer decision).
- **Do not re-litigate the herdr decision** (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8, closed won't-fix; `groups.herdr` added by WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN).
- Measure runtime before/after with the test-skill runner (`run_tests.py`), not ad-hoc `npx vitest`.
- Beware the `run_tests.py --suite node` trap: that suite name resolves through the legacy convention path (`tests/{unit,node,cli}`) and ignores `suiteCommands`; use the default `--suite all` for canonical runs.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/test-config.json` — `suiteCommands` / `groups` coverage for `packages/shared`, `packages/tui`
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — extend the shared "Test gates" section + coverage table
- `vitest.config.ts` — only if a dedicated config is needed to isolate `packages/` (keep `pool`/`isolate`/`singleFork` and the worktree exclusions)

## Related Work

- **WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR** — closed the `tests/` coverage gap (umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`); records the OPEN QUESTION that became this item
- **WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8** — herdr package suite excluded by producer decision (won't-fix)
- **WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN** — added `groups.herdr` to `.pi/test-config.json`
- **WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1** — source of the additional-gap evidence for `packages/tui/extensions/**`
data.title: Canonical full suite excludes packages/ tests (tui 22 + shared 12 files)

## Goal

Four test files import `WorkItem` from `packages/herdr/src/worklist.js`:

- `tests/unit/form-dialog-open-pane.test.ts`
- `tests/unit/chord-quick-create-open-pane.test.ts`
- `tests/herdr/stage-vocabulary.test.ts`
- `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts`

`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` only imports `type WorkItem` from `./fetcher.js` — it never re-exports it. Vitest does not typecheck and the herdr tsconfig excludes `*.test.ts`, so the gap has never failed a gate, but an IDE/tsc typecheck of those suites reports the missing export.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` re-exports `WorkItem` (type-only re-export) OR the four test files import it from `./fetcher.js` directly — whichever the worklist barrel epic's AC2 (re-export only symbols consumers use) prefers.
2. `npx tsc --noEmit` over the affected test files reports no missing-export error.
3. `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts` continues to pass; once `WorkItem` is exported, remove it from `KNOWN_MISSING_CONSUMER_EXPORTS` in `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/worklist-family.ts` (shrink-only) and regenerate `worklist.split-baseline.json`.

## Context

The worklist split guard (WL-0MVND6BL30066V6B) records this pre-existing gap as `unexportedConsumerSymbols: ["WorkItem"]` rather than widening the barrel during a move-only (read-only) guard child.

data.description:
## Problem

The test-run cache (`run_tests.py` + `test_cache.py`) can serve a **stale** result, and can also report **missing** for an entry that was just written. Both were observed in one session (WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A). Root cause undiagnosed — the symptoms below contradict `compute_git_state`'s documented content-sensitive fingerprint, so the fingerprint itself may be captured at the wrong moment.

Discovered during WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A (discovered-from).

## Symptom 1 — a stale GREEN was returned for a changed tree

While validating RED witnesses for the peer-offer cooldown work:

1. Production fix applied (5 dirty files) → `run_tests.py --scope changed --group herdr --json` → `Test Files 130 passed`.
2. Production changes reverted (`git checkout -- <3 prod files>`; 2 dirty test files) → the same command → **130 passed / 4007 tests**, i.e. the RED witnesses "passed" without the fix.
3. The same command again, after adding `console.log` diagnostics to those same two test files, **reused the same cache directory** (`metadata.json` `completed_at` unchanged) — a cache hit, despite the file contents having changed.
4. `--no-cache` produced the expected **4 failures**, confirming the RED witnesses were valid.

## Symptom 2 — `--summary` reports `missing` for an entry just stored

Immediately after `run_tests.py --scope full --json` finished green at HEAD (`Test Files 280 passed | 1 skipped`, `Tests 4102 passed | 5 skipped`, cache dir `ada07d39…` with `scope: full`, `test_type: full`, `exit_code: 0`), `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` (with and without `--scope full`) reported `{"scopes":{"all":"missing"}}`. The checkout was clean at the same HEAD; `compute_git_state()` returned `2838fdc3…` while the stored entry held `6155836a…` — so the entry was keyed on a *transient* dirty state that existed during the run (plugin/`wl`/`dist`/test-created files) and can never be queried again afterwards.

## Impact

- A RED/GREEN verification can be silently wrong — exactly the evidence an audit consumes.
- `implement.py finish`'s changed-scope gate can pass on a stale cached run.
- The audit's `query_cached()` fast path misses for the same reason, forcing an unnecessary full-suite re-execution (F3).
- Agents are likely to trust the green summary and never use `--no-cache`.

## Proposed direction (for intake)

- Make the fingerprint stable for the *state an operator/agent can reproduce*: exclude ignored/transient paths (`.worklog/`, `dist/`, test scratch dirs) from the dirty-path content hash, or snapshot the state before the run rather than after.
- Re-check the content-hash path for `--scope changed` runs (symptom 1) — the file list may be reused where the content hash is not.
- Surface `cached: true` prominently in human-readable output so a re-used result is never mistaken for a fresh one.
- Document/automate: verification runs that must prove RED/GREEN should use `--no-cache`.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)

- Editing only the contents of an already-modified file invalidates the cache entry for that scope/group.
- A run's entry is queryable by `--summary` immediately afterwards from a clean checkout at the same HEAD.
- A cached result is visibly marked as cached in non-JSON output.
- Regression tests: (a) two runs with a content-only change between them do not share a cache entry; (b) `--summary` finds the entry written by the preceding `--scope full` run.
data.title: Test-run cache returns stale results when only the contents of already-modified files change

**Discovered-from:** WL-0MVP9RW4Z006VLW1 (sync split, child 5 of 6).

## Problem

`tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` ("push command uses --no-verify to avoid recursive pre-push hook") reads production source and greps for the literal push command line. That is anti-pattern #1 in the shared Test Writing Guidelines (grep source instead of asserting behaviour): it couples the test to a file path and a literal command string, so any legitimate move (as in the sync split) or message reformat breaks it, while a real regression in push behaviour would not necessarily be caught.

Child 5 re-pointed the grep from `src/sync.ts` to `src/sync/push.ts` (assertions unchanged) to keep the gate green — a stop-gap, not a fix.

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the test to prove the observable behaviour — that pushes performed by the sync push paths bypass the pre-push hook — without grepping source text.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The test drives `gitPushDataFileToBranch` through the existing git mock (which already traces invocations) and asserts the recorded push invocation contains `--no-verify` (and, for the rewrite path, `--force --no-verify`).
2. No `readFileSync` of production source remains in the test for this behaviour.
3. The test fails if `--no-verify` is removed from either push command (negative proof), and passes on the current tree.
4. Only `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` (plus mock assertions if required) changes; no production behaviour change; `/skill:test` (changed scope) is green.

## Notes

- Related: WL-0MVP9RW4Z006VLW1 re-pointed the assertion; this item removes the anti-pattern.
data.title: Replace the source-grep push assertion in tests/sync-worktree.test.ts with a behavioural test

data.description:
Fix stale packages/herdr/package-lock.json drift that fails the test-skill live-repo guard

Discovered during WL-0MVOBP6K0007574C (extract dependency and comment modules).

## Problem

`packages/herdr/package.json` declares a root `bin` entry
(`worklog-pane-close` -> `dist/pane-close-cli.js`) and a `postinstall` script,
but the committed `packages/herdr/package-lock.json` (last touched
2026-08-11, WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4) predates both. Any `npm ci`/`npm install` in
that package rewrites the lockfile with `hasInstallScript: true` and the root
`bin` block.

`tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` executes `scripts/install-herdr.sh`
(cwd = repo root), which runs `npm ci` inside `packages/herdr`. The rewritten
lockfile is therefore a mutation of a guarded checkout made during a test run,
so the test skill's live-repo guard fails the run:

```
live-repo mutation detected: the test suite changed a guarded checkout for <repo>.
  added path [ M] packages/herdr/package-lock.json
```

Every test in the suite passes (281 files / 4,113 tests, exit 0) — only the run
verdict is failed. Consequences:

- The per-repo test cache can never hold a green full-suite entry for HEAD, so
  the audit skill cannot auto-verify execution-dependent ACs (F3 re-executes and
  fails the same way).
- Each full-suite run leaves the main checkout dirty.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `packages/herdr/package-lock.json` is regenerated (`npm install` in
   `packages/herdr`) and committed so it matches `package.json`'s `bin` and
   `postinstall`.
2. A full-suite run (`run_tests.py --scope full`) at that commit reports
   `success: true` with no `live_repo_mutation` field, and leaves
   `git status` clean.
3. `npm run build` and `npm ci` in `packages/herdr` produce no further lockfile
   diff.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/package-lock.json`
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — read-only
- `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` — read-only (reproduction)

## Constraint

Lockfile-only change; do not alter `package.json` or the install script.
data.title: Fix stale packages/herdr/package-lock.json drift that fails the test-skill live-repo guard

discovered-from:WL-0MVR8EXR6009F05V

## Goal

**As** an operator running several worklog roots on one machine, **I want** the downtime leader to know about a root even when no herdr instance happens to be running in it, **so that** a root with dispatchable work is never invisible to the dispatcher.

## Problem

The dispatcher's candidate universe is derived from **live instances**, not registered roots:

- `computeMostImportantItem` runs per instance and is called by `runCoordinationCheckIn`; only a running herdr instance in a root writes a coordination entry (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.coordination.ts:145`, `downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:928+`).
- The leader's only cross-root reach is the offer list plus one own-backlog fallback hard-scoped to `opts.cwd` (`downtime-worker.coordination-leader.ts:801-880`, AC2 of WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24).

Measured 2026-10-27T21:55Z: `ContextHub` has **9 of 30** window items dispatchable (`WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ`, `WL-0MNM7EVJG0097Y44`, `WL-0MVPUCVXL0099TND`, six refactor items, …), and **zero** coordination entries, because no herdr instance is running in that root. Its per-worklog `downtime-coordination.json` is `{"version":1,"entries":[]}`. The machine-wide file holds only `tce-the-rising` entries.

Leadership rotation cannot fix this: the empty-leader hand-off (`WL-0MVP7QHUB003ZA2A`) hands off to *a peer*, and there is no peer in that root to hand off to.

## Why this is separate from `WL-0MVR8EXR6009F05V`

It is a different problem class — **root discovery**, not dispatcher gating. Fixing the audit-tier budget or adding attribution would not make a root with no open pane reachable. Conversely, a root sweep would not have fixed `AI_Hell` (all items held) or `tce-the-rising` (audit tier unreachable).

## Options (to evaluate at intake)

- **O1 — Registered roots.** An explicit config list (e.g. `downtimeWorklogRoots`), or discovery by scanning a parent directory for `.worklog/worklog.db`. The leader sweeps registered roots round-robin via `getHerdrListHead(root, window)` and applies the same sequential filter chain. Note `downtime-round-robin-by-root.ts` still exists with a cursor (the retired-by-WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 helpers), so the cursor machinery is partly present.
- **O2 — Per-root offers from a single instance.** One instance offers on behalf of a set of roots. Cheaper than O1 but reintroduces "who offers which root" ownership questions.
- **O3 — Hardware/heartbeat registry.** Instances publish liveness per root so the leader can distinguish "no instance" from "instance offered nothing". Overlaps with the stale-entry problem (see below).

## Related observation

Coordination entries never expire: `pruneStaleEntries` is a deliberate no-op (`packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts:366`, WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P), and `hasPeerOffer` (`coordination.ts:350`) only checks `instanceId !== self && workItemId.length > 0`. During the 2026-10-27 investigation the dead instance `b4365ff1` (lastUpdated `2026-10-27T14:30:20Z`, 7+ hours stale) still counted as a live peer. The predicate is documented as "conservative… never a starvation", which was sound when entries expired; with expiry retired it no longer is. Any solution here should also decide whether a stale entry should make the leader *more* willing to sweep.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A root with dispatchable work but **no running herdr instance** is reachable by the leader, and work from it is dispatched. Verified live on `ContextHub` (currently 9 dispatchable, 0 offers).
- AC2: `AI_Hell`-style gated roots are still not dispatched — a sweep must not bypass any existing safety gate (`assignee` hold, producer-review, code-freeze, freshness, caps, slot minimums, in-flight, review-queue). Gates remain sequential filters.
- AC3: The canonical ranking contract is preserved: a sweep is a bounded **window** over registered roots using the same `getHerdrListHead` path, never a second ranking.
- AC4: Fairness: no single root can monopolise the leader (a bounded per-root share or round-robin cursor), demonstrated by a multi-root test with two roots each holding dispatchable work.
- AC5: Fail-open: an unreadable/missing root in the registry is skipped without a strike, and never crashes the tick.
- AC6: Fail-safe: an empty or unresolvable registry leaves today's behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged.
- AC7: The stale-coordination-entry question above is explicitly resolved (either entries gain a heartbeat, or `hasPeerOffer` is made liveness-aware) with the decision recorded on this item.
- AC8: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents the root-discovery model and how it composes with the offer list.

## Constraints

- Must not reinstate the unconditional non-critical window widening superseded by WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9.
- Must not require a running pane per root (that is the bug being fixed).
- Config schema additions need clamping/validation consistent with `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`.
data.title: Downtime leader cannot see a worklog root with no running herdr instance

data.description:
## Goal

**As** a producer or agent scanning the herdr worklist, **I want** each work item to show who holds it — an `Assignee` metadata row plus an `[assignee]` prefix on the item's title — **so that** I can tell a producer hold (`Map`) or an active agent claim apart from an unheld item at a glance, without opening the item or running `wl show`.

## Background

`assignee` is the claim/scheduling-hold field (see `AGENTS.md`: the producer sentinel is `wl update <id> --assignee Map`, released with `--assignee ""`; claim tiers write the agent name). It is already present end-to-end in the data layer — `wl show` / `wl list --json` return it and `normalizeItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) parses it into `WorkItem.assignee` — but the herdr TUI never displays it. The `wl show` CLI already renders an `Assignee` row, so the CLI is out of scope.

Related work (not duplicates): WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR surfaces the *aggregate* "entire dispatch window held" banner (header count + warning banner), and WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0 restored the per-item `Reviewed` metadata row + list icon — the closest precedent for this shape of change (shared `buildMetaRows` row, list/preview/detail parity, `noIcons` mode, README docs).

## Surfaces

- **Preview** — the selection-list metadata panel (`buildMetadataPanelLines` → `buildMetaRows`) and the hover tooltip.
- **Detail view** — the full item view (`formatDetailContent`: header title + shared metadata table).
- **List rows** — `formatItemLine` (selection list, browse feed and log-derived dispatch rows all render through it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `buildMetaRows` returns an `Assignee` row carrying the item's raw assignee value whenever `assignee` is a non-empty, non-whitespace string, positioned immediately after the `Effort` row so `pairMetaRows` compound pairing (Status+Stage, Priority+Type, Created+Updated, Audit+AuditedAt) can never absorb or reorder it; the row is omitted entirely when `assignee` is undefined, null, empty or whitespace-only.
- AC2: One shared helper (`formatTitleWithAssignee` in `worklist.format.ts`) returns `[<assignee>] <title>` for an assigned item and the byte-identical title for an unassigned one, and every title-rendering surface uses it: selection-list rows (`formatItemLine`), the preview metadata `Title` row, the detail-view header, and the hover-tooltip title line.
- AC3: Unassigned parity — for an item with no assignee every surface renders exactly as today: no `[] ` prefix, no leading space, no empty `Assignee` row, and the existing herdr suites pass unchanged.
- AC4: Rendering invariants hold — list rows still truncate within `maxCols` (display-width aware), the `[assignee] ` prefix inherits the title's priority colour, `noIcons` mode is unaffected, and `metadataPanelContentHeight` counts the extra row so the panel's `m`/`M` scroll clamp can still reach it.
- AC5: Visibility of a real hold — an item with `assignee: "Map"` renders `[Map]` before its title in the list row, the preview `Title` row and the detail header, and `Assignee  Map` in the preview panel and detail metadata table.
- AC6: `packages/herdr/README.md` documents the new `Assignee` row and the `[assignee]` title prefix in its metadata-panel, detail-view and hover-tooltip sections.
- AC7: Test-first — every AC above is covered by a failing test in the herdr vitest suite before the implementation lands, and the full gate is run through `/skill:test`.

## Minimal implementation

1. **Test (red first).** Extend the existing herdr suites (`worklist.test.ts`, `worklist-icon-truncation.test.ts`, `worklist-child-coverage.test.ts`) with: assigned/unassigned `buildMetaRows` + `pairMetaRows` cases, `formatTitleWithAssignee` unit cases, assigned/unassigned `formatItemLine`, `formatDetailContent` header, `formatTooltipLines`, and `metadataPanelContentHeight` accounting.
2. **Helper.** Add `formatTitleWithAssignee(item)` (or `(title, assignee)`) to `worklist.format.ts` — the leaf formatting module — so `worklist.ts` (the not-yet-split monolith under the ≤1000-line shrink-only allowlist) does not grow logic.
3. **Metadata row.** Add the `Assignee` row to `buildMetaRows` after `Effort`, and route the `Title` row through the helper — this covers the preview panel and the detail table in one change.
4. **Title surfaces.** Use the helper in `formatItemLine` (inside the priority-coloured segment) and `formatTooltipLines`, and in the `formatDetailContent` header.
5. **Docs.** Update the README's Metadata panel / detail view / hover tooltip bullets and the `Metadata panel` reference section.

## Plan

Single vertical slice (code + tests + docs); effort Extra Small and risk Low, so no phasing and no prototype is warranted. Between-phase guidance is not applicable — the change is one slice through the shared formatter, its four render call sites, tests and docs.

## Out of scope

- herdr **pane titles** (`pane-title.ts`): load-bearing for active-pane detection via work-item ID matching and width-bounded; adding an assignee prefix would risk truncating the ID.
- The `wl show` / `wl list` CLI output — it already renders `Assignee`.
- `Blocked By` rows: they display *other* items' titles and carry no assignee data.
- Dispatch, claim, sorting and filtering behaviour: this is display-only.

## Assumptions

- A1: "preview and detail views" means the herdr selection-list metadata panel and the full detail view; "the title for the item" means every surface that renders the item's title (list row, preview `Title` row, detail header, hover tooltip).
- A2: the `Assignee` value renders as plain text (no icon — `@worklog/shared/icons` has no assignee icon), and the `[assignee]` prefix inherits the row/title priority colour.
- A3: a whitespace-only assignee is treated as unassigned.
- A4: the change is display-only — no dispatch, claim, sort or filter behaviour changes.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.format.ts` — new `formatTitleWithAssignee` helper (leaf formatting module)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.meta.ts` — `Assignee` row + `Title` row prefix (preview panel and detail table)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.detail.ts` — detail-view header title prefix
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `formatItemLine` and `formatTooltipLines` use the helper
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-icon-truncation.test.ts` — width/ANSI and parity tests
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — metadata row, list row, detail and tooltip tests
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — surface documentation

## Appendix: planning decisions and assumptions

No clarifying question was raised: this item was dispatched with effort **Extra Small** and risk **Low** (below the planning threshold), so the plan-skill skip path performed an automated review of the existing content instead of decomposing it, and the item text plus the repository analysis below resolved every point the plan needs. Decisions recorded in lieu of questions:

- D1: Surface selection — "preview" and "detail views" were mapped to the herdr metadata panel and `formatDetailContent`, and "the title for the item" to all four title-bearing render call sites. Evidence: `worklist.meta.ts` (`buildMetaRows`), `worklist.detail.ts` (`formatDetailContent`), `worklist.ts` (`formatItemLine`, `formatTooltipLines`). Recorded as assumption A1; callable out at review.
- D2: Data availability — no fetcher or schema change is required because `normalizeItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) already maps `assignee` from both `wl show` and `wl list --json`. Evidence: live `wl list "Show assignee" --json` returns `"assignee": "plan"` for this item.
- D3: Duplicate check — `wl search` over "assignee", "assignee display" and "show assignee" surfaced no item covering per-item assignee display. Nearest neighbours: WL-0MVR8FN1D002SCIR (aggregate hold banner) and WL-0MVAMS4RO000H3B0 (restore `Reviewed` row/icon). No overlap covering these ACs, so nothing was closed or rewritten.

# `wl update --status blocked` silently reverts to `open` and still reports success

Discovered while parking `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (tce-main-street) on an assignee hold on 2026-10-29.

## Problem

On a specific item, `wl update <id> --status blocked` succeeds, prints `Status ⛔ Blocked`, returns `"status": "blocked"` in `--json`, and then the **stored** record is `open` — with an `updatedAt` 20–30 ms *after* the write that the command reported.

Reproduction (tce-main-street worklog, item `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`):

```
$ wl update MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4 --status blocked --json | jq -r .workItem.status
blocked
$ sleep 2; wl show MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4 --json | jq -r '.workItem.status + " " + .workItem.updatedAt'
open 2026-10-29T17:55:59.257Z      # the update's own record said 17:55:59.234Z
```

- Reproduced **4×**, including with `--if-status open`, and via the SQLite store directly (`workitems.status = 'open'`, `updatedAt` = the later timestamp).
- **Not** a sync artefact: `.worklog/last-sync-time` was `17:24:20Z`, well before the writes, and no other `wl` process touched the item (`downtime-*.log`, `local-route.log` checked).
- The revert is specific to **`status`**: `--assignee Map` and `--do-not-delegate true` writes on the same item persist.
- The **create** path persists blocked: sibling items `MS-0MVTEVKOD002OKSO` and `MS-0MVTEVL4Z009LUUR` (created with `--status blocked` by the plan) stay blocked.

Distinguishing feature of the affected item: it has **only an inbound** dependency edge (`MS-0MVTEVLL000948T1` depends on it) and no outbound edges; its blocking reason is recorded in prose.

## Impact

An explicit status write that silently does not stick is a data-integrity hazard: a caller that blocks an item to stop `wl next` / auto-dispatch from starting it gets `success: true` and a rendered `Blocked` state, but the item stays schedulable. Here it would have allowed a verification child to be started against a prerequisite that has not landed — the exact failure the parent item's Q3 decision is about.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A deterministic reproduction exists as a test: create an item, give it an inbound edge only, `wl update --status blocked`, assert the **persisted** status is `blocked` (this currently fails).
- [ ] Root cause named on this item: which write path produces the second record and why it wins (candidates: a post-update re-sort writing from a pre-change snapshot; a derived-status reconciliation that maps blocked-without-outbound-edges to open; a second store/export mirror).
- [ ] Fixed so an explicit `--status blocked` either persists or **fails loudly** with the reason — never `success: true` with a silently different stored value.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the matrix: blocked with no edges; blocked with inbound edges only; blocked with outbound non-terminal edges; blocked with outbound terminal edges; and `--if-status` CAS interaction.
- [ ] The test names are cited on this item as evidence.
- [ ] Full node/pytest suites green for the change.

## Key Files

- `src/commands/update.ts` — status handling, re-sort after update.
- `src/commands/dep.ts` (line ~61 sets `status: 'blocked'` when an edge is added — the semantics the update path should agree with).
- `src/status-stage-rules.ts`, `src/commands/status-stage-validation.ts` — status/stage compatibility.
- `packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts` (`reconcileDependentStatus`) — the second write that reverts the status.
- `packages/shared/src/database/sort.ts` (`reSort`) — ruled out: writes only `sortIndex`.
- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — SQLite writer used by the store (`worklog.db`); no second mirror.

## Evidence trail

- Origin: `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6` (tce-main-street), comment `MS-C0MVTUG5U90041PQ1` and its follow-up.
- Workaround applied there so the hold is machine-enforced: `--assignee Map` + `do-not-delegate` tag on the affected child.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-30 (re-run): re-planned an item still at `intake_complete` although its decomposition and root-cause analysis were recorded on 2026-10-29. Verified the root cause against the current tree — `db.update` still calls `hooks.reconcileDependentStatus(id)` after a status/stage change (`packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts`, `updateWorkItem`), that reconciliation still maps `blocked`-with-no-active-blockers to `open` (`packages/shared/src/database/dependencies.ts`), and `db.update` still returns the pre-reconcile snapshot; `src/commands/update.ts:565` still performs the redundant post-update self-reconcile. Confirmed all cited Key Files exist, except the to-be-created `tests/regression-explicit-blocked-status.test.ts`. Tightened this item's Key Files to real paths (the `src/storage*/` / "worklog.db writer" bullets did not exist). Re-ran the six automated review stages and the AC coverage review (100% coverage by the four children); advanced the stage to `plan_complete`. No children were added, rewritten, or closed.

# Fail loudly when a persisted status diverges from an explicit request

Parent: WL-0MVTUKSJZ003WK82 (AC3 — "persists or fails loudly"). Depends on the
fix task.

Defence in depth: even after the reconcile fix, an explicit `--status` write
must never report `success: true` while the stored value differs. The CLI
re-reads the persisted record after the write and fails non-zero with a
diagnostic when it does not match the explicit request.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl update <id> --status <s> --json` compares the persisted status with the requested value and exits non-zero, with a distinct error code (e.g. `status-not-persisted`) naming both values, when they differ.
- [ ] No update path can report `success: true` for an explicit `--status` request whose persisted status differs.
- [ ] A test exercises the guard through a controllable/stubbed seam and asserts the non-zero exit and error, never `success: true`.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add the post-write comparison per id in `src/commands/update.ts`, after the update returns, using the persisted record the fix task now returns.
- Emit the distinct error via the existing `output.error`/JSON failure envelope.
- Test with an injected runner/store seam (or a targeted test double) that forces a divergent persisted value.

**Key Files:**
- `src/commands/update.ts`
- `src/cli-output.ts`
- `packages/shared/src/database/work-items.ts`

# Refactor guard: worklist split invariants

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B — decompose `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `worklist.ts` split, I want one automated gate that
fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so that every
extraction child can land safely without touching any existing test file and
without a reviewer having to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5 require: every production module ≤1,000 lines, an
unchanged public surface at `./worklist.js`, unmodified test files, no new
circular imports, and a single `WorkItemListState` declaration. Nothing in the
repo enforces these for `worklist.ts` today. The `downtime-worker` series
already built exactly this machinery for its own split
(`packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` + `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`);
this child reuses it rather than duplicating it.

Facts captured at plan time (2026-10-30, `dev`, `worklist.ts` = 7,899 lines):

- **36 consumer files** import from `./worklist.js`/`./worklist`: 2 production
  (`index.ts` → `getTermSize`, `runWorklistTui`; `fetcher.ts` → `STAGES`,
  `Stage`) and 34 test files, of which **24** are `worklist*.test.ts` suites.
- **66 distinct symbols** are imported across those consumers; the other 23 of
  the 89 current exports are unused outside the module and become internal
  (parent AC2).
- `WorkItemListState` is declared **once** (`worklist.ts:490`) — the single
  owner AC5 protects.
- `runWorklistTui` is declared once (`worklist.ts:5581`, `export async function`)
  and must stay at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical signature
  (child WL-0MVND6MQS000L01W).
- The live static import graph already contains one large component that
  includes `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
  (`CYCLE_BASELINE` in `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`). It is
  pre-existing and out of scope; what the gate forbids is a **new** cycle member
  or a new **runtime** cycle (parent AC4).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New **additive** test file `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts`
   (vitest) exists and passes on the current tree **before any production code
   moves**; no existing test file is modified (parent AC3).
2. Committed baseline `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` records
   the 66 consumer-imported symbol names plus provenance (generation command,
   source commit, timestamp, scanned globs).
3. **Public-surface gate:** every baseline symbol is still exported by
   `./worklist.js` (value or type), and every symbol the live consumers import
   from the barrel is exported by it — so a lost or trimmed re-export fails the
   suite (parent AC2).
4. **Single state-owner gate:** exactly one production
   `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module declares `WorkItemListState`
   (parent AC5), mirroring the `dispatchInFlightCount` gate.
5. **Barrel/cycle gate:** no production `worklist.*.ts` module contains a
   runtime (value) import of `./worklist.js` (nor of `./index.js`); the static
   import graph of `worklist*.ts` modules contains no cycle outside the recorded
   baseline allowlist (parent AC4).
6. **Size gate:** every production `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module is
   ≤1,000 lines, excluding an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains
   only `'worklist.ts'`; a further assertion proves the allowlist only ever
   shrinks (it must remain a subset of the plan-time list). The final barrel
   child empties it (parent AC1).
7. Each gate is proven to fail on a deliberately broken input (a synthetic
   >1,000-line module, a dropped export, a runtime barrel import, a duplicated
   `WorkItemListState`, a new cycle) — the failure modes are unit-tested, not
   assumed.
8. **Reuse, do not fork, the scanner:** extend
   `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` minimally so the barrel path, the
   module-family matcher and the single-owner declaration name are injectable
   (each defaulting to today's `downtime-worker` behaviour). The existing
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` and
   `downtime-worker.split-baseline.json` must stay **byte-identical and green** —
   duplicating the 28k-line scanner is not acceptable.
9. `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes, including the new guard suite and the
   untouched `downtime-worker` guard.
10. A comment on this item records the baseline generation command and the
    gate-to-parent-AC mapping.

## Minimal implementation

1. Parametrise `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`: accept a
   `barrel`/`family`/`declarationName` target (defaults unchanged) in
   `isSplitFamilyFile`, `splitFamilyModules`, `findBarrelValueImports`,
   `findSplitFamilyCycles` and `findDispatchInFlightDeclarations`; add a
   `--target worklist` branch to the `--write-baseline` CLI.
2. Generate the baseline: scan `src/**/*.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/*.ts` for
   `import … from './worklist.js'`, normalise `type ` prefixes, dedupe, sort →
   `worklist.split-baseline.json` with provenance fields (expect 66 symbols).
3. Write `worklist.split-guard.test.ts` with the five gates (exports,
   single-owner, cycle/barrel, size+allowlist, baseline provenance), each as a
   separately named `it()` so failures are legible.
4. Add the negative-case fixtures (temp files under `os.tmpdir()` or inline
   sources parsed by the same helpers) and assert each gate reports a failure.
5. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` from the guard's helper section so the final child
   (`WL-0MVND6OOL004SK9N`) can empty it in one line.
6. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope); record the guard output in a comment.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` — new
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` — minimal parametrisation (defaults preserved)
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — read-only (no edits in this child)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` — must stay unchanged and green

## Constraints

- Additive only: adding a test file and a parametrisation hook does not violate
  parent AC3 ("no test file is modified").
- No production `worklist*.ts` edits in this child — it lands first, alone.
- No new runtime dependencies (`typescript` is already used by `scan.ts`).

## Dependencies

None — first child; every extraction child is blocked by this one.

## Notes

- Test-writing guidance: `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.
- Precedent: `WL-0MVLIHWOY003IP5E` (downtime-worker split guard) — same shape,
  same AC numbering, already green on `dev`.

The slash command autocomplete feature has been successfully implemented for the OpenCode prompt in the TUI.

- **Location**: src/commands/tui.ts

- **Commands**: 28 predefined slash commands available for autocomplete
- **Behavior**:

  - Suggestions update as you type
  - Press Enter to accept suggestion and add trailing space
  - Normal text entry unaffected

- Display shows: ↳ /commit (in gray below input)
- Enter completes to: /commit [space]

Implemented SSE-based input handling for OpenCode server agents.

## Implementation details:
- Added Server-Sent Events (SSE) connection for real-time streaming
- Listen for input.request events from the server
- Display input prompts with appropriate UI labels (Yes/No, Password, etc.)
- Send input responses back via /session/{id}/input endpoint
- Handle permission requests from agents
- Show user input in cyan color in the output pane

## Event handling:
- message.part: Stream text, tool-use, and tool-result in real-time
- message.finish: Mark response as completed
- input.request: Show input field and wait for user response
- permission-request: Handle permission dialogs

## User experience:
- Input requests appear inline with agent output
- Clear visual indicators when input is needed
- Input field appears at bottom of pane with appropriate label
- User responses are displayed in the conversation flow
- Escape key cancels input mode

Commit: b93e636

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
Fixed textarea viewport/scrolling issue when using Ctrl+Enter

Problem: When pressing Ctrl+Enter to add a new line, the first line would disappear and only reappear when typing a character.

Root cause: The textarea was setting the new value before the dialog had expanded, causing rendering issues with the viewport.

Solution in commit cdf5991:
- Update layout and expand dialog BEFORE setting the new value
- Improved scroll calculation to properly keep cursor line visible
- Added viewport handling when box height changes
- Force internal cursor update to refresh the display

The textarea now properly displays all content when adding new lines.

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
FOUND THE ROOT CAUSE! Fixed textarea scroll issue in commit abe7e24

Problem: When pressing Ctrl+Enter to add lines, the first line would disappear.

Root Cause: The textarea has scrollable=true and maintains internal scroll state. When adding a newline:
1. The cursor moves to line 2
2. The dialog expands to fit 2 lines
3. But the textarea's scroll position wasn't being reset
4. If scroll was > 0, line 1 would be scrolled off the top

Solution: Explicitly set scroll to 0 whenever totalLines <= visibleLines. This ensures all content is visible from the top when it fits in the viewport.

The fix was simple - we were only setting scroll when content EXCEEDED the visible area, but never resetting it to 0 when content should be fully visible.

data.author: OpenCode
data.comment:
SUCCESS! Fixed the Ctrl+Enter textarea rendering issue in commit ae5b9e2

The root cause was finally identified:
1. Ctrl+Enter sends a 'linefeed' keypress event (not 'C-enter')
2. Blessed's textarea handles this internally and inserts the newline
3. Our .key(['C-enter']) handler never ran because blessed processed it first
4. We were resizing AFTER the newline was inserted, causing scroll issues

The solution:
- Intercept the 'linefeed' keypress event BEFORE blessed processes it
- Read the current line count
- Calculate the future line count (current + 1)
- Resize the dialog preemptively to the correct height
- Let blessed insert the newline naturally
- Scroll to bottom after insertion completes

Now when pressing Ctrl+Enter:
- The box expands smoothly
- All content remains visible
- The cursor stays visible on the new line
- No content scrolls off screen unexpectedly

This was a complex debugging journey that involved understanding blessed's internal event handling!

data.author: @OpenCode
data.comment:
Audit: Enumerated all event listener usages (\.on/\.once) under src/ and noted recommended cleanup actions. Summary:

- Files requiring explicit cleanup (transient UI widgets, child processes, SSE): src/tui/opencode-client.ts, src/commands/tui.ts, src/tui/components/modals.ts, src/tui/components/dialogs.ts, src/tui/components/opencode-pane.ts, src/tui/components/overlays.ts, src/tui/components/list.ts, src/tui/components/detail.ts, src/tui/components/help-menu.ts, src/tui/components/toast.ts, src/tui/update-dialog-navigation.ts, src/tui/update-dialog-submit.ts

- Files where handlers are expected to be long-lived or global (no action required unless future refactor): src/cli.ts (process SIG handlers), src/index.ts, src/sync.ts (child process usage should still be audited in context).

- Recommendations (per-file):
  * Remove/deregister listeners on destroy for transient blessed widgets (use removeAllListeners or remove specific handlers) — applicable to all files creating widgets: components/* and commands/tui.ts.
  * Child process handlers (stdout/stderr/error/close) should be registered once and removed in stop/cleanup; ensure proc.kill() is preceded by removing listeners and nulling refs.
  * SSE/HTTP request listeners must be removed/aborted on stream finish/error to avoid late payload processing (opencode-client.ts).
  * Add unit tests that create/destroy widgets and start/stop child processes repeatedly to assert listener counts do not grow and no duplicate handling occurs.

Full per-file line references and notes were recorded locally and are available on request. I will attach a detailed per-file list as the next comment if you want it posted to the work item.

Planning Complete. Decomposed into 6 child features:

1. Move mode state and descendant detection (WL-0MLQXVUI91SIY9KM) — foundational types and state helpers
2. Move mode keybinding and activation (WL-0MLQXW5MX1YKW5H1) — `m` key wiring, Esc cancellation
3. Move mode visual feedback (WL-0MLQXWHZD107999R) — source highlight, descendant dimming, footer context
4. Target selection and reparent execution (WL-0MLQXWUCY08EREBY) — confirm target, execute reparent, tree refresh + cursor follow
5. Unparent to root via self-select (WL-0MLQXX4RE1DB4HSB) — self-select clears parent, edge cases
6. Move mode documentation and help updates (WL-0MLQXXF1P00WQPOO) — TUI.md and help menu

Dependency chain: F1 -> F2 -> F3 -> F4 -> F5 -> F6

Design decisions confirmed during interview:
- Move mode works in filtered views; hidden items simply cannot be targets
- Post-move cursor follows the moved item (auto-expand parent, scroll to item)
- Footer shows source item title and ID for context
- Visual treatment uses both color (background/foreground) AND prefix markers
- No confirmation dialog; moves execute immediately
- Unit + integration tests required (mocked blessed)

No open questions remain.

All 220 tests pass including the new worktree tests.

Implementation satisfies all acceptance criteria:
✓ wl init in new worktree places .worklog in worktree directory, not main repo
✓ wl init in main repository still places .worklog in main repo
✓ wl init in subdirectory finds repo-root .worklog if it exists
✓ Each worktree maintains independent worklog state
✓ All existing tests pass
✓ Code handles both main repos and worktrees correctly

data.author: @AGENT
data.comment: Added failing regression test to reproduce single-machine overwrite: tests/sync.test.ts → 'local persistence race' → 'can overwrite a recent update if sync imports a stale snapshot'. The test now fails (expected status 'completed' but got 'open') when a stale snapshot is imported, matching observed behavior. Run: npm test -- --run tests/sync.test.ts

data.author: @AGENT
data.comment:
Plan to fix overwrite (single-machine, concurrent writers):

Root cause: multiple WorklogDatabase instances hold stale snapshots. Any write exports the instance snapshot to JSONL, so a stale instance can overwrite newer changes from another instance.

Recommended fix (Option 1): merge-on-export in WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl.
- Before writing JSONL, load current JSONL from disk and merge with in-memory snapshot using mergeWorkItems/mergeComments (newer updatedAt wins; non-default beats default).
- Write merged result back to JSONL.
Why it works: prevents stale writers from overwriting newer fields; each write reconciles with latest on-disk state.

Alternatives:
- Import-before-write guard based on JSONL mtime (simpler but still racey).
- File lock around JSONL writes (robust but more complexity).

Plan:
1) Implement merge-on-export in WorklogDatabase.exportToJsonl.
2) Update failing regression test in tests/sync.test.ts to pass.
3) Run npm test -- --run tests/sync.test.ts.

Expected outcome: stale snapshot imports no longer revert recent updates.

Changes: refresh from JSONL before update/delete to avoid stale snapshot overwrites; added regression test for multi-instance JSONL writes; tightened CLI delete/show test error handling.
