# Investigation: downtime dispatcher vs herdr selection list — divergence brief

## Summary (investigation only — no code changes)

Herdr's selection list and the downtime dispatcher disagree because they
start from **different input sets, staged through different pipelines,**
and grouped into different presentational shapes. `wl next`'s
`packages/shared/src/database.ts:computeScore`/`reSort` ranking
(AC3 determination, WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS) is the canonical "most
important" — the herdr list and the dispatcher both need to be aligned
to it (scope of WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2).

## Exact code paths compared

- Herdr list (what the producer browses with `prefix+l`):
  - `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems(count)`:
    - `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (auto `reSort` of the full score
      order via `getAllOrderedByScore(recencyPolicy)` + `assignSortIndexValues`)
      — `wl next` without `-n` returns the *single* top candidate;
      with `-n` it returns the score-ordered batch up to the hard cap
      (default 32, hard-capped on the CLI side regardless of `browseItemCount`).
    - Also fetches `fetchMandatorySubsets()`:
      - `wl list --priority critical --root-only`
      - `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`
      run in parallel and merged by ID (first wins).
    - Merged set fed through `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems(merged, browseItemCount)`
      — mandatory (critical ∪ completed/in_review, root-only, not `done`)
      always shown; `browseItemCount` caps ONLY the remaining "other"
      items, then `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`
      re-groups every displayed item.
  - `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` filters to
    `!parentId && stage !== done`, mandatory-always logic,
    "others" limited to `browseItemCount - mandatory.length`.
  - `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` calls
    `assignItemGroups` → `groupItemsByFilePaths` partitioning;
    rendered with collapsible group headings via `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.

- Downtime dispatcher (what runs when slots are idle):
  - `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork`
    dispatched tiers in fixed order: **audit** →
    **critical**(`getNextCriticalCandidate` / `computeMostImportantItem`) →
    **implement**(`getNextImplementCandidate`) →
    **plan**(`wl next --stage intake_complete`) →
    **intake**(`wl next --stage idea`), each with its own
    input source and post-filtering.
  - Legacy "scheduled-prompts" stage runs *before* any tier if a
    due prompt exists (`getDueScheduledPrompt`).
  - Shared ranking is `packages/shared/src/database.ts`:
    `filterCandidates` → `handleCriticalEscalation` →
    `findNextWorkItemFromItems` / `getNextWorkItem` →
    `getAllOrderedByScore` → `computeScore` → `reSort` →
    `selectBySortIndex` ordering (falling back to
    audit-not-ready boost + effective-priority + age when sortIndex equal).

## Live sample (2026-09-02, ContextHub root, `browseItemCount=20`)

Current database snapshot (`wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress`):
- 20-item result (top by `wl next -n 20` score, with grouping metadata):
  1. WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q critical plan_complete in_progress (Critical Group 1)
  2. WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N critical in_progress in_progress (Critical Group 2)
  3. WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V high plan_complete in_progress
  4. WL-0MSNI6TQ5003JY1Z high intake_complete open
  5. WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9 high plan_complete open
  6–8. other intake_complete open
  9–16. high idea (open + in_progress) + medium idea
  17–20. medium/in_progress idea + in_review candidates
  - mandatory sets merged: 2 critical root (non-done) + 1 completed/in_review root
  - all mandatory items already fell within the top-20 wl-next window at this
    snapshot so herdr's merged view and the raw `wl next -n 20` window
    agreed; at larger backlogs they diverge (cap 32 above).

Downtime dispatcher on same snapshot:
- Audit tier: 1 candidate (WL-0MTCP0ILG008YV84 completed/in_review)
- Implement tier: WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9 (open plan_complete, risk Medium ≤ Medium, effort Medium ≤ Medium)
- Plan/intake tiers: 0 open intake_complete; 0 open idea (all blocked by dep or status)
- Critical tier: 0 critical open root (none available)
- Result: dispatcher selects **WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9** (implement tier) as most-important,
  which appears in the herdr top-20 at position 5 today — agreement on this
  sample once filters are considered, but off-window candidates could land
  at rank 33+ of `wl next -n` while the herdr mandatory merge rescues them.

## Divergence gap map

| Dimension | Herdr list (`fetchNextItems`) | Downtime dispatcher (`dispatchDowntimeWork` / `computeMostImportantItem`) | Why they diverge |
|-----------|----------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------|
| **Input set / cap** | `wl next -n N` batch capped at 32; mandatory `wl list` merge bypasses the cap for critical+in_review | Stage-scoped `wl next --stage X` per tier (audit tier uses `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` directly) + `wl list` for audit | A high-scored item beyond rank 32 in the wl-next global order is invisible to herdr unless it is critical/in_review; the dispatcher never calls `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` and so never sees that global window at all |
| **Stage filter** | No stage filter — global ranking across all stages | Per-tier call forces stage (`--stage plan_complete`/`intake_complete`/`idea`; audit forces `completed/in_review`) | Dispatcher scopes candidates by stage before ranking; herdr shows global top by score |
| **Risk/effort filter** | None in herdr list (risk/effort not applied server-side to the global `wl next -n` call) | Implement tier applies `risk ≤ Medium, effort ≤ Medium` (server-side filters; items with unset/empty risk/effort excluded, AC2) | A high plan_complete item with High/Severe risk or Large effort can appear in herdr top-20 but be invisible in the implement tier |
| **Audit tier, marker, recency** | No audit recency; no dispatched-marker exclusion; no "no valid audit in 7d" gate; in_review items grouped last via `assignItemGroups` | Audit tier: `wl list` caps 7-day recency window, no-valid-audit check, durable `dispatched-marker` exclusion, active-audit single-flight, 2h stale window, code-freeze tri-state gate (`frozen`/`ambiguous` skips audit+implement) | Same in_review item can appear at group 8 in herdr but at the TOP of the dispatcher when its updatedAt is recent |
| **Blocked / in_review handling** | Shows `in_review` in-review group last; `done` excluded; `blocked` filtered only by deltas | Per-tier `--\-status open` guard (plan/intake) excludes completed; dep-blocked items excluded via `filterCandidates` unless overridden; `includeInProgress` toggles with claim; ``other`` vs "dispatchable" exclusion | A blocked or completed/in_review item can be visible in herdr (mandatory/In Review) but never dispatchable; opposite unlikely (dispatcher cannot surface a child independently — see below) |
| **sortIndex / reSort / recency-policy** | `wl next` auto calls `reSort(recencyPolicy)` (default `ignore`); herdr's `regroupWorkItems` sorts by group number then `compareGroupableItems` (critical→plan/intake→idea→other→in_review, then stage order then priority then id) — NOT by sortIndex | Legacy dispatcher path's per-tier `wl next --stage` also triggers auto-`reSort`; coordination leader recomputes via `computeMostImportantItem` after fresh `wl show` + `isAuditFresh`; `sortIndex` used as tie-break only in leader's `--no-re-sort` path | Herdr grouping changes presentation order even within a score band — herdr position ≠ canonical `wl next` rank; `--recency-policy=prefer/avoid` could further shift wl-next batch while herdr's group sort is recency-agnostic |
| **Grouping vs flat ordering** | `regroupWorkItems` assigns file-path partitioning (critical vs Group N) and collapsible headings (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94) | Dispatcher selects a *flat* single candidate (no group) — ranking comparison ignores file-path grouping | Divergence in "which work can safely he

# Investigation conclusion (producer already reviewed — Q1–Q3 resolved 2026-09-02)

## Producer determination (WL-C0MTK1HLCE0096ERS, 2026-09-02)

- **Q1 "most important" = wl next score order** (`packages/shared/src/database.ts:computeScore`/`reSort`) — authoritative, not dispatcher tier order.
- **Q2 Unify** — herdr list + downtime dispatcher share one ranking (wl next), not intentionally divergent.
- **Q3 Sample window LGTM** — default browseItemCount / ContextHub root / `wl next -n 20`.

Follow-up already filed: **WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2** (idea, medium) — *Unify herdr selection list and downtime dispatcher on wl next canonical ranking*.

## Reproducible sampling scripts

```bash
# wl next global score order (canonical; auto reSort with --recency-policy ignore)
wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress --json              # herdr fetcher base
wl next -n 500 --include-in-progress --json              # full 96-item order today

# Herdr mandatory subsets (merged by fetcher.ts)
wl list --priority critical --root-only --json
wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json

# Dispatcher per-tier selections (same snapshot)
wl next --stage plan_complete --json                     # implement tier base
wl next --stage plan_complete --risk Medium --effort Medium --json   # risk/effort caps
wl list --priority critical --status open --root-only --json         # critical tier
wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only --json      # audit tier

# Dispatcher audit logs + code-freeze marker
cat .worklog/downtime-dispatches.log | tail -20
cat .worklog/code-freeze.json   # tri-state gate: not-frozen / frozen / ambiguous

# Code-freeze / recency knobs
#   wl commands run reSort with --recency-policy (default ignore);
#   herdr grouping is recency-agnostic — record the flag used in samples.
```

`sortIndex` freshness: `wl next` CLI auto-calls `reSort(recencyPolicy)`; a stale
`sortIndex` (older `.worklog/worklog.db` row before the next CLI call) can make
two successive `-n` batches see different indexes — always record whether
`--no-re-sort` was used.

data.author: Audit
data.comment:
# Audit Report: WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 - FAILED

## Title
Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (supersedes wl next unification)

## Status
**FAILED — Incomplete Implementation**

## Acceptance Criteria Assessment

### AC1: Dispatcher consumes Herdr list head — ❌ FAILED
**Expected:** `dispatchDowntimeWork` derives its candidate from the Herdr selection list head (`fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`). No second ranking implementation.

**Actual:** `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:628` still contains the production no-op stub:
```typescript
getHerdrListHead: async (_cwd: string): Promise<...> => ({ ok: true, items: [] }),
```

The stub returns an empty items array. While `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:2149` does call `deps.getHerdrListHead(opts.cwd)`, the result is always empty, causing the dispatcher to fall through to the legacy tier chain.

**Evidence:**
- `index.ts` (current HEAD, same in commit 5594bbb2): line 628 returns `items: []`
- `downtime-worker.ts` line 2149-2150: `const head = await deps.getHerdrListHead(opts.cwd)` → always empty
- When `head.items.length === 0`, execution falls through to the legacy tier chain (lines 2168+)

### AC2: No duplicate ranking; gates are filters — ⚠️ PARTIALLY MET
**Expected:** Safety gates act as sequential filters on Herdr-ordered candidates. If no candidate passes, dispatcher reports "no candidate" — no fallback ranking.

**Actual:** When the Herdr list is empty (due to the stub), the dispatcher falls through to the legacy tier chain:
```
legacy tier chain: audit → implement → plan → idea (wl next --stage per tier)
```

This is a **second, competing ranking implementation** that re-ranks using a different order than the Herdr list. The code comments acknowledge this as "test-compat fallback" but it remains active in production.

**Evidence:**
- `downtime-worker.ts:2168-2200`: Fallthrough to legacy tier chain when `head.items.length === 0`
- Comments claim "Production `createDowntimeDeps` always returns a non-empty head" — this is false due to the stub

### AC3: Herdr list remains sole ranking path — ❌ FAILED
**Expected:** `fetchNextItems` / `selectWorkItems` / `regroupWorkItems` are the sole ranking path. No `wl next`/`database.ts` scoring change required.

**Actual:** The dispatcher still implements its own ranking via the legacy tier chain as a fallback. The Herdr list plumbing (`fetchNextItems` → `getHerdrListHead`) is not wired up in production.

### AC4: Contract documented — ✅ PASSED
**Expected:** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` state explicitly: dispatcher selects the first dispatchable item from the Herdr selection list.

**Actual:** Documentation correctly states the contract. The issue is the implementation gap between documented intent and live code.

### AC5: No regression; observable agreement proven — ❌ FAILED
**Expected:** `wl next -n` / Herdr list / downtime pick agree; a reproducible sampling script shows agreement.

**Actual:** No agreement is possible because `getHerdrListHead` returns empty. The dispatcher picks from `wl next --stage plan_complete` (legacy) while the Herdr list shows a completely different order.

**Observable divergence on AI_Hell:**
- Herdr UI shows: 2 `plan_complete` items (1 `in_progress`), 4 `in_review` items
- Downtime dispatch picks: `wl next --stage plan_complete` → `AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4` (already in dispatched-marker)
- These do not agree

## Root Cause

The implementation landed in commit 5594bbb2 only the **dispatcher-side plumbing** (`dispatchFromHerdrList` with filters-only logic, `downtime-worker.ts:2137`). The **consumer-side wiring** (`getHerdrListHead` calling `fetchNextItems`) was intentionally stubbed as "production no-op" pending a fix to `WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX` (browseItemCount/cap/mandatory-merge fix).

This created an **incomplete wire-up**: the dispatcher calls `getHerdrListHead` expecting a populated list, but receives an empty array, and silently falls through to the legacy ranking.

## Impact

1. **Herdr extension and downtime dispatcher diverge on ranking** — exactly what AC1 was meant to prevent
2. **Downtime dispatch is effectively paused** for worklogs where the Herdr list would have candidates — e.g., `AI_Hell` shows items in Herdr UI but dispatcher picks from legacy tier (already-exhausted backlog)
3. **The stub comment is misleading** — "Production no-op for now" is a lie; it's always-on in production

## Recommended Resolution

1. **Immediate:** Replace the stub with a real `fetchNextItems` call, OR explicitly disable the dispatcher until the wire-up is complete
2. **Short-term:** Complete `WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX` (browseItemCount/cap/mandatory-merge fix) to unblock the Herdr list plumbing
3. **Medium-term:** Remove the legacy tier chain fallback from `downtime-worker.ts` once all tests use Herdr-head stubs
4. **Documentation:** Update AC4 docs to note the stub dependency and planned removal of legacy chain

## Items Requiring Attention

- `WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX` — "counts in Herdr selection list are incorrect" (open, intake_complete) — blocks the Herdr list plumbing
- `downtime-worker.ts:2168+` — Legacy tier chain fallback (should be removed, not retained)
- `index.ts:628` — Stub comment ("production no-op") is incorrect

## Ready to Close: No

data.comment: RCA session 2026-09-13: The three-strike cascade is caused by items with stage='in_progress' (a retired stage value). When wl update --status in_progress is called for these items, the update command validates the item's current stage and throws 'Invalid stage in_progress' → CLI error → strike. Affected items: CG-0MT5XT7K3005IBBV, WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR. **Issue type decision guide** — full table in [docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md](../../docs/dev/intake-skill-reference.md). Summary:

- `bug` — currently **incorrect/broken**; the change corrects wrong behavior (not net-new capability).
- `feature` — **adds new capability** that did not exist before (not merely fixing broken).
- `chore` — **does not change code behavior** (config, CI, docs, deps, formatting).
- `task` — general-purpose (tests, refactoring, investigation, benchmarking).
- `epic` — **large scope** needing decomposition into subtasks.

**Decision procedure** — when uncertain, ask: (1) *broken/incorrect?* → `bug`; (2) *net-new behavior?* → `feature`; (3) *no code-behavior change (docs/CI/deps/formatting)?* → `chore`; (4) *general-purpose (tests/refactoring/investigation)?* → `task`; (5) *large enough for subtasks?* → `epic`.

**Priority classification guide** — use these rules to assign the correct `priority` (consulted only when the operator has not supplied an explicit priority value via `--priority` or similar flag):

| Priority  | Use when… | Do NOT use when… | Examples |
|-----------|-----------|-------------------|----------|
| `critical` | Security vulnerabilities, data loss, broken builds, or blocking the release pipeline | The issue is not blocking or does not involve data security/integrity | Patching a CVE, fixing CI pipeline failure, recovering from data corruption |
| `high`    | Major features, important bugs, or anything blocking other work | The work is not urgent or blocking | Shipping a major feature, fixing a significant user-facing bug |
| `medium`  | Default priority for standard features, enhancements, or non-blocking bugs | The issue is critical/high urgency or trivial | Regular feature development, minor bug fixes, improvements |
| `low`     | Polish, minor optimizations, nice-to-have improvements | The issue affects functionality or user experience | Cosmetic fixes, minor refactoring, documentation polish |

**Decision procedure** — when priority is not specified by the operator, ask:
1. *Does this involve security, data loss, or a broken build/release pipeline?* → `critical`
2. *Is this a major feature, important bug, or is it blocking other work?* → `high`
3. *Is this trivial polish or a nice-to-have with no functional impact?* → `low`
4. *Otherwise?* → `medium` (default for standard work)

Goal: confirm background sync/refresh stops while a text-input overlay is open and resumes after close.

- Worklist pane open with defaults (`autoSync=true` / `syncIntervalMs=60000`, `autoRefresh=true` / `refreshIntervalMs=30000`).

1. Sync suppressed while typing

2. Refresh/re-render suppressed while typing

   - Expected: no list re-render, no flicker/focus loss; the typed text is preserved character-for-character.
3. No dropped keystrokes across a scheduled tick

5. Regression guard (not typing)
   - With no overlay open, confirm the normal 30s refresh and 60s sync cadence continues, and the pause-when-hidden / heartbeat / DB-change gates still behave as before.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Audit remediation — root cause of remaining dropped keypresses found and fixed

Producer rejection: "We are still missing keystrokes when typing fast."

Root cause: the tick gate stops background sync/refresh while a form is open, but it cannot stop the PTY from COALESCING several keystrokes into a single stdin data event during fast typing. Both FormState.handleInput and ShipItDialogState.handleInput only accepted a single character (key.length === 1) and silently returned none for any multi-character chunk, discarding every character in it. Reproduced with a focused test: handleInput('hello') left the field empty.

Fix:
- New pure, dependency-free module packages/herdr/src/key-input.ts exports splitKeypresses(), a shared raw-stdin-chunk tokeniser. It keeps escape sequences intact as one token (CSI arrows / PageUp-Down / Ctrl+Enter / bracketed-paste markers, SS3, Alt-Meta) and returns every other code point as its own key, so no bytes are dropped.
- FormState.handleInput (form-dialog.ts) and ShipItDialogState.handleInput (ship-it-dialog.ts) now run each chunk through splitKeypresses() and apply every key in order, returning the first terminal result (submitted/cancelled/paste/cut). Single-key callers are unchanged.
- The typing gate (isInputActive + createGatedTick) remains; it addresses sync/refresh contention, while the tokeniser addresses the residual fast-typing loss.

Tests (all green):
- key-input.test.ts (15): tokeniser unit coverage incl. mixed chunks and incomplete CSI remainder.
- form-dialog.test.ts (+8): coalesced chunks append every char, printable-before-escape, submit on trailing Enter, Backspace/Tab inside a chunk, bracketed paste.
- ship-it-dialog.test.ts (+3): 'ship' in one chunk appends fully, 'ship' submits, Backspace in a chunk.
- worklist.test.ts (+2): fast-typing chunk simulation across a skipped tick for FormState and ShipItDialogState.

Full packages/herdr suite: 2968 tests pass. Root build (tsc) clean.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Completed work pushed to dev, see commit 42ad5f99.

Root cause (residual dropped keypresses after the earlier tick-gate + tokeniser fix):
1. Background refresh/sync was only gated at the two scheduler ticks. Other paths called doRefresh/doSync directly — tab-focus resume, the herdr event subscriber (pane_focused), the hidden->visible resume-poll fallback, the command-completion onRefresh hook — so a re-render could still contend with typing. The typing gate now lives INSIDE doRefresh/doSync (single inputActive() predicate), so every background path pauses; agent-status event re-renders are gated too. Skips are silent and not coalesced (next tick after close resumes within one interval).
2. Raw stdin was decoded per data event. A multi-byte UTF-8 code point or an escape sequence split across chunks lost bytes (U+FFFD), and a chunk ending in the bare ESC introducer was read as the Esc key and cancelled the open form. New KeypressDecoder (key-input.ts) buffers the incomplete tail via StringDecoder + the CSI tokeniser and completes it from the next chunk; a lone trailing ESC is still emitted immediately as Escape.

Tests: key-input.test.ts (+9: streaming splitter + decoder incl. UTF-8/mouse/bracketed-paste splits, no-byte-loss round-trip); worklist-inflight.test.ts (+4: auto-refresh/auto-sync paused while a form is open and resumed after close; split CSI arrow and split SGR mouse reassembled through the real stdin listener). Full packages/herdr/src suite: 3066 tests pass; tests/herdr: 517 pass; herdr tsc --noEmit clean; repo full-suite gate + pre-push hook green.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Design decision (AC1 + AC2):

**AC1 (audit-trail comment):** implemented in the CLI layer (`src/demotion-audit.ts`, `recordDemotionAuditTrail`) and invoked from both attach paths (`create.ts`, `update.ts`) right after a successful demotion. It writes a comment on the parent naming the attached child (id + title), the actor (`child.createdBy` or `system`), the from→to status/stage, and an ISO timestamp, with the child referenced.

Why the CLI layer rather than `packages/shared/src/database.ts`: worktrees symlink `node_modules`, so `@worklog/shared` resolves to the main checkout's built `dist` for both runtime and `tsc` type-checking. Changing the shared `demoteParentOnChildAdded` signature breaks the worktree build (TS2554), and shared-only changes are invisible to the worktree test suite. Placing the comment at the CLI layer keeps it fully verifiable. The CLI commands are the sole callers of `demoteParentOnChildAdded`, so every demotion is covered. The write is best-effort: it never undoes the demotion or aborts the attach.

**AC2 (queue surfaces vs churn):** Child 1 (WL-0MU2QKB98007BKYT) removed the `updatedAt` stamping from `batchUpdateSortIndices`, so re-sort no longer counts as activity. AC2 therefore reduces to verifying the `wl recent` surface, covered by `tests/cli/recent-churn-vs-semantic.test.ts` (re-sort leaves ordering and `updatedAt` untouched; a genuine title edit moves the item to the top).

Regression coverage: `tests/cli/create-update-demote-parent.test.ts` (comment on create + reparenting demotion; no comment for an exempt bot child).

data.comment:
Root cause (diagnosed, not a product regression): `isPaneVisible()` resolves the herdr binary as `process.env.HERDR_BIN_PATH ?? "herdr"` (visibility.ts). The test exec mock in `worklist-visibility.test.ts` only recognises `bin === "herdr"` (makeExecMock), but when the suite runs INSIDE a herdr pane the inherited `HERDR_BIN_PATH` (e.g. `/home/rgardler/.local/bin/herdr`) is used, so the mock falls through to its generic branch, `payload.result.tab.focused` is undefined, and `isPaneVisible()` fails open to `true` → the "hidden" refresh tick dispatches the fetcher. Because `afterEach` deletes `HERDR_BIN_PATH`, only the FIRST test in the file is affected — exactly the observed 1 failed / 16 passed. CI (no herdr env) is green, so this is a test-hermeticity defect, not a regression on dev.

Scope: make the test hermetic — clear inherited herdr env vars in `beforeEach` and make the exec mock match `herdr tab get` by ARGUMENTS rather than the exact binary name. No production-code change.

## Description

# Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2)

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork`) and the Herdr extension selection list (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` → `worklist.ts`) disagree on "most important item" because the dispatcher maintains its own tier ordering (`wl next --stage …` per tier + `wl list` audit query) instead of reusing the Herdr list. The project needs the dispatcher to consume the Herdr list head so the two selectors agree by construction. Supersedes prior "unify on `wl next`" scope per producer determination WL-C0MTKL9X34004YJS1 (2026-09-02).

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — needs a single trustworthy queue; the item dispatched during downtime was visible at the top of `prefix+l` and reflects declared prioritization intent.
- **Herdr user browsing `prefix+l`** — expects downtime work to track exactly what the visible list shows, so automated work does not appear arbitrary.
- **Maintainer of herdr / downtime-worker / wl next** — needs a single ranking contract; ranking logic lives only in the fetcher/smart-selection/grouping/database pipeline.

Example user stories:
- As a producer, I want the downtime dispatcher to pick the first item shown in the Herdr list, so automated work follows the priority I already see.
- As a herdr user, when downtime dispatches `/skill:implement WL-XYZ`, I want WL-XYZ to have been at the head of the Herdr list, so I understand why it was chosen.
- As a maintainer, I want the ranking contract documented as "dispatcher == Herdr list head" so future safety gates are evaluated as filters, not a competing ranking.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dispatcher consumes Herdr list head** — `dispatchDowntimeWork` (and any coordination-leader path) derives its candidate from the Herdr selection list head rather than a separate tier ordering / stage-scoped `wl next` / `wl list` audit query. No second ranking implementation remains on the dispatch path.
2. **No duplicate ranking; gates are filters** — tier ordering / `wl next --stage` per-tier calls / audit `wl list` ranking are no longer used to pick "most important". Any safety gates that must remain (code-freeze skip, dispatched-marker exclusion, active-audit single-flight, per-process single-flight / CAS claim) act as sequential filters on the Herdr-ordered candidates. If no Herdr-ordered candidate passes the filters, the dispatcher reports "no candidate" rather than falling back to a separate ranking.
3. **Herdr list remains sole ranking path** — `fetchNextItems` / `selectWorkItems` / `regroupWorkItems` stay the sole ranking path (mandatory-always for critical + `completed`/`in_review`, `browseItemCount` windowing of "other" items, grouping logic, `reSort`/`computeScore` as used by the fetcher). No `wl next`/`database.ts` scoring change is required to fix the divergence; if `fetchNextItems` delegates to `wl next` internally that internal detail is acceptable — the observable contract is "dispatcher == Herdr list head".
4. **Contract documented** — `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` (and `src/commands/next.ts` help if it references dispatcher selection) state explicitly: dispatcher selects the first dispatchable item from the Herdr selection list; any remaining safety override (e.g. code-freeze) is documented as a skip/filter on that sequence, not a ranking.
5. **No regression; observable agreement proven** — existing `wl next` / herdr fetcher/grouping / downtime-worker fixtures pass; a reproducible sampling script shows `wl next -n` / Herdr list / downtime pick agree (downtime picks the list head after filtering) on a fixture. Dispatched-marker / code-freeze / single-flight gating still respected as filters on the Herdr sequence.

## Constraints

- Zero npm deps for herdr; `smart-selection.ts`/`grouping.ts` duplicated per TUI stays in sync with `src/commands/*` if touched.
- `browseItemCount` clamping (1–50) and root-only / `done`-exclusion rules respected.
- Do not fork a second ranking; reuse the Herdr list pipeline.
- Investigation only touched the prior item (WL-0MTJZCXQK0045X5Q); this item carries the implementation.
- Backwards compat: existing dispatched-marker / code-freeze gating semantics preserved as filters.

## Existing state

- **Herdr list:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` runs `wl next -n N --include-in-progress` (auto `reSort` unless `--no-re-sort`), merges mandatory subsets via `fetchMandatorySubsets` (`wl list --priority critical --root-only` and `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only`), applies `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` (root-only, `stage != done`, mandatory always shown, `browseItemCount` limits only "other" items), and regroups with `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems` / `assignItemGroups` (Critical Group N / Group N / Idea / Other / In Review). Rendered via `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **Downtime dispatcher:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:dispatchDowntimeWork` — tier order audit → implement (`wl next --stage plan_complete` with risk/effort caps) → plan (`wl next --stage intake_complete`) → fallback idea (`wl next --stage idea`); audit tier uses `wl list --status completed --stage in_review --root-only` with 7-day recency / dispatched-marker / active-audit / code-freeze gates; pre-dispatch CAS claim, per-process single-flight, scheduled-prompts tier, round-robin cursor, cooldowns.

    # Audit Report: WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2 - FAILED

## Title
Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (supersedes wl next unification)

## Status
**FAILED — Incomplete Implementation**

## Acceptance Criteria Assessment

### AC1: Dispatcher consumes Herdr list head — ❌ FAILED
**Expected:** `dispatchDowntimeWork` derives its candidate from the Herdr selection list head (`fetcher.ts:fetchNextItems` → `smart-selection.ts:selectWorkItems` → `grouping.ts:regroupWorkItems`). No second ranking implementation.

**Actual:** `packages/herdr/src/index.ts:628` still contains the production no-op stub:
```typescript
getHerdrListHead: async (_cwd: string): Promise<...> => ({ ok: true, items: [] }),
```

The stub returns an empty items array. While `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:2149` does call `deps.getHerdrListHead(opts.cwd)`, the result is always empty, causing the dispatcher to fall through to the legacy tier chain.

**Evidence:**
- `index.ts` (current HEAD, same in commit 5594bbb2): line 628 returns `items: []`
- `downtime-worker.ts` line 2149-2150: `const head = await deps.getHerdrListHead(opts.cwd)` → always empty
- When `head.items.length === 0`, execution falls through to the legacy tier chain (lines 2168+)

### AC2: No duplicate ranking; gates are filters — ⚠️ PARTIALLY MET
**Expected:** Safety gates act as sequential filters on Herdr-ordered candidates. If no candidate passes, dispatcher reports "no candidate" — no fallback ranking.

**Actual:** When the Herdr list is empty (due to the stub), the dispatcher falls through to the legacy tier chain:
```
legacy tier chain: audit → implement → plan → idea (wl next --stage per tier)
```

This is a **second, competing ranking implementation** that re-ranks using a different order than the Herdr list. The code comments acknowledge this as "test-compat fallback" but it remains active in production.

**Evidence:**
- `downtime-worker.ts:2168-2200`: Fallthrough to legacy tier chain when `head.items.length === 0`
- Comments claim "Production `createDowntimeDeps` always returns a non-empty head" — this is false due to the stub

### AC3: Herdr list remains sole ranking path — ❌ FAILED
**Expected:** `fetchNextItems` / `selectWorkItems` / `regroupWorkItems` are the sole ranking path. No `wl next`/`database.ts` scoring change required.

**Actual:** The dispatcher still implements its own ranking via the legacy tier chain as a fallback. The Herdr list plumbing (`fetchNextItems` → `getHerdrListHead`) is not wired up in production.

### AC4: Contract documented — ✅ PASSED
**Expected:** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` and `packages/herdr/README.md` state explicitly: dispatcher selects the first dispatchable item from the Herdr selection list.

**Actual:** Documentation correctly states the contract. The issue is the implementation gap between documented intent and live code.

### AC5: No regression; observable agreement proven — ❌ FAILED
**Expected:** `wl next -n` / Herdr list / downtime pick agree; a reproducible sampling script shows agreement.

**Actual:** No agreement is possible because `getHerdrListHead` returns empty. The dispatcher picks from `wl next --stage plan_complete` (legacy) while the Herdr list shows a completely different order.

**Observable divergence on AI_Hell:**
- Herdr UI shows: 2 `plan_complete` items (1 `in_progress`), 4 `in_review` items
- Downtime dispatch picks: `wl next --stage plan_complete` → `AH-0MTG5MGPZ00986B4` (already in dispatched-marker)
- These do not agree

## Root Cause

The implementation landed in commit 5594bbb2 only the **dispatcher-side plumbing** (`dispatchFromHerdrList` with filters-only logic, `downtime-worker.ts:2137`). The **consumer-side wiring** (`getHerdrListHead` calling `fetchNextItems`) was intentionally stubbed as "production no-op" pending a fix to `WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX` (browseItemCount/cap/mandatory-merge fix).

This created an **incomplete wire-up**: the dispatcher calls `getHerdrListHead` expecting a populated list, but receives an empty array, and silently falls through to the legacy ranking.

1. **Herdr extension and downtime dispatcher diverge on ranking** — exactly what AC1 was meant to prevent
2. **Downtime dispatch is effectively paused** for worklogs where the Herdr list would have candidates — e.g., `AI_Hell` shows items in Herdr UI but dispatcher picks from legacy tier (already-exhausted backlog)

2. **Short-term:** Complete `WL-0MT26TE72002FLKX` (browseItemCount/cap/mandatory-merge fix) to unblock the Herdr list plumbing

4. **Documentation:** Update AC4 docs to note the stub dependency and planned removal of legacy chain

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Root cause identified and fixed

The intermittent 'error (?)' icon was NOT an unknown-stage fallback. The lines showing '�' are the U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER produced when the line-truncation loops in formatItemLine and truncateLine appended only the LOW surrogate of a supplementary-plane emoji (u+1F513, u+1F4CB, u+1F50D, ...). Writing that unpaired surrogate to stdout encodes it as EF BF BD, which terminals render as a white diamond/question-mark glyph. The bug is intermittent because it only fires when a row's line width exceeds the pane AND the truncation point lands inside an emoji (narrow pane / long title).

Fixed in packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts (both truncation loops now append the full character — both surrogate halves — and advance by two code units). Regression tests added in packages/herdr/src/worklist-icon-truncation.test.ts asserting no lone surrogates / no U+FFFD after UTF-8 round-tripping for formatItemLine, formatMetadataPanel and formatDetailContent across truncating widths, including the exact reported row (WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67 shape: status open + stage plan_complete + critical + long title).

Verification: full suite green at the committed state (85 files / 641 tests passed, 4 skipped; second suite 20 files / 415 passed; 0 failures). Commit 6af00da2 pushed to dev.

## Interview command — reliability fix (re-implementation)

**Root cause of the audit rejection ("does not reliably detect questions"):** the parser only understood the legacy numbered form (`1. **Q:** …` / `**A:** …`). Real work items almost universally use the intake/plan appendix format:

```
## Appendix: Clarifying questions
- Q: "…" — Answer (user): "…". Source: …
```

plus variants (`- **Q1**:`, `**Q**:` with no bullet, `- **Q1 (scope):**`, `- **Q2 — Scope:**`, inline answers on continuation lines, `**Answer** (user, interactive):`). None of these were detected.

**Fix:** tolerant question/answer detection covering all observed variants; answers are written back in place so `Source:` lines, attribution, quotes and bold markers are preserved losslessly. Interrupted sessions resume (answers persisted after each response); `needsProducerReview` is cleared only when every question is answered.

**Corpus validation** (224 clarifying-questions sections exported from SorraAgents):
- 186 sections with questions, 619 Q/A pairs, 53 outstanding
- 0 sections with question markers but zero parsed pairs (was 16 before the fix)
- `rebuildQAPairs(parseQAPairs(content)) === content` for all 224 sections (lossless)

**Tests:** `tests/cli/interview.test.ts` — 42 tests (parser variants, lossless rebuild, core loop, resume/interrupt, command registration).

**Assumption / dependency note:** the parser targets the formats actually produced today (documented in the intake skill's appendix). The separate SorraAgents item SA-0MUC9TKC8000AUMX (canonical interview contract) is about interview *conduct* and does not gate reliable detection of the current persisted format; if it later redefines the appendix format, the detector can be extended without loss.

data.author: pi
data.comment:
Implementation design notes (pre-finish):

1) AC1 leader-gating: the cheap idle switch is gated on the existing downtime leader (DowntimeWorker.isLeader) via a live isLeader() probe — no separate election. Non-leaders skip tick() entirely (no proxy fetch, no mode read, no POST). The fast switch fired from onOperatorCommand remains on all instances: the operator's active pane may not be the downtime leader, so gating fast on leadership would leave the proxy in cheap while the operator is actively working (contradicting AC4 'the proxy remains in fast mode while the active pane receives commands'). Only the cheap switch — the flip-flop source — is leader-gated, matching AC1's '(cheap POST)' wording. This is a deliberate, documented deviation from the brief's desired-change note #4 ('only leader fires fast POST').

2) AC2/AC6 shared activity: every instance writes mode-activity.json (atomic temp+rename, monotonic max) into getMachineCoordinationDir() ?? join(targetCwd, '.worklog') — the same directory as the downtime leader lease. The leader's idle evaluation uses max(local clock, shared timestamp), so the proxy stays fast while any pane has recent activity. Shared read failure falls back to the local clock (fail-closed, AC6).

3) AC3 threshold: the default was raised 15->30 min by WL-0MUDVBKH00009OGY (completed, manual review) during this item's lifetime, and that item scoped this one as 'unrelated to the threshold value'. This item's AC3 explicitly requires 3_600_000 (60 min), so the shipped default is now 60 min; existing installs keep their persisted override (no forced migration). Assumption recorded: AC3 is honoured as written (60 min) despite the intervening 30-min default. The 60s floor is unchanged.

4) AC5 leadership transitions: the probe is read live each tick, and the leader reads the shared activity file on every tick, so a handover is honoured on the next tick with no spurious switch.

Verification so far: herdr typecheck green; full herdr suite 2502 tests / 68 files green; root build green.

- Added `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX = 30` (`downtime-worker.ts`): the documented bound on additional items scanned.
- Added `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` — re-reads the SAME ranking path with `head length + DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX`, returns only the newly visible items (order-preserving set difference). Fail-open to `[]`.
- `getHerdrListHead(cwd, limit?)` dep now forwards an optional limit; `index.ts` passes it to `fetchNextItems(limit ?? 30)`.
- Both dispatch paths extended: `dispatchDowntimeWork` (direct) and `computeMostImportantItem` (coordination check-in offer). No second ranking; TUI worklist still renders exactly `browseItemCount`.
- Docs updated: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (new 'Extended dispatch window' section + no-candidate cooldown note) and `packages/herdr/README.md`.

## Tests

- New regression suite `dispatch-window extension — head-cap starvation` (11 tests) in `downtime-worker.test.ts`: reproduces the 30-item head / 22nd-other scenario, asserts the out-of-window item is found for both dispatch paths, asserts bound `head+30`, extension skipped when the head already yields a candidate, freeze still extends to reach plan/intake, fail-open on empty/failed extended lookup, and unit coverage for `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`.
- `index.test.ts`: wiring test asserting `getHerdrListHead` forwards `-n 30` by default and `-n 60` for an explicit limit.

While writing the regression test I found that `dispatchFromHerdrList` builds its `classifyItemForDispatch` input WITHOUT threading `needsProducerReview`, so the producer-review gate is not enforced on the live Herdr-head dispatch path (the offer path `computeMostImportantItem` does honour it). ## Status: implementation complete on dev; AC5 blocked on environment evidence

Commits: dde229a2 (per-slot gate + array local_owner_session_id parsing) and
23722a08 (reuse the perSlotMode predicate in the gate — same detection as
evaluateIdle, per the plan).

Re-applying state after a wl sync merge reverted status/stage and dropped the
earlier implementation comment (a concurrent/remote state overwrote them).

### What AC5 needs

AC5 = "in cheap mode, dispatches are observed in downtime-dispatches.log while a
previously dispatched agent is still working". Implementation is not the
blocker; the following environment facts/actions are:

1. **Confirm cheap-mode per-slot identity is served (KEY OPEN QUESTION).**
   The fix only engages when the status carries a usable per-slot array:
   perSlotMode requires Array.isArray(slots) AND 0 < requiredFreeSlots < total_slots.
   Live samples right now are single-slot (total_slots=1) and serve slots=[] with
   slots_stale=true, so the per-slot branch never fires. Proxy log analysis
   (20k-line tail) shows cheap mode is frequent (10,255 of 10,531 status_request
   records have total_slots=3; 1,260 have 3 slots, >=2 free, an array owner lease,
   and slots_stale=false), but the log does not include the per-slot body.
   If cheap-mode responses also serve slots=[] (or omit slots), perSlotMode is
   false and the stall persists — AC5 would fail and this needs a follow-up
   change (relax the count-based gate for the spare-capacity case).

2. **Force/extend a cheap-mode window.** The scheduler is
   [('01:00','cheap'),('10:00','fast')] in proxy-local (UTC+1) time. Options:
   wait for the 01:00 proxy-local window, or manually force cheap mode.

3. **Run the fixed worker.** The live downtime worker must be restarted on
   commit 23722a08 (currently it may be running an older build).

4. **A dispatched agent left 'working'** while >=1 other slot is free and unowned,
   and `runningPanes > 0` for the worker (i.e. the RCA condition).

5. **Acceptable evidence (proposal).** Either:
   (a) live: >=2 GET /llama/local/status samples in the window showing
       total_slots=3, available_slots>=2, an array local_owner_session_id, and a
       non-empty slots array; plus >=1 downtime-dispatches.log entry timestamped
       inside that window while a previously dispatched pane reports 'working'; or
   (b) replay: a captured cheap-mode payload fed through the real
       createDowntimeWorker + real fetchLocalStatus (stub HTTP) asserting a
       dispatch occurs with the lease held — machine-verifiable, no overnight wait.

AC1-AC4 are met by unit tests (594 tests pass in downtime-worker.test.ts).

### Questions for the producer

- Q1: Does the proxy serve a non-empty per-slot array (is_processing, and
  per-slot owner_session_id) in cheap mode? Please capture one raw
  /llama/local/status body from a cheap-mode window.
- Q2: May I force cheap mode, or should I wait for the 01:00 proxy-local window?
- Q3: May I restart the live downtime worker on 23722a08, and for how long may
  the observation run?
- Q4: Is the replay harness (5b) acceptable as AC5 evidence if live capture is
  impractical?

## Clarifying Questions (intake — Wire `wl interview` into the `r-i` chord)

I could not finalise the intake without producer input on scope. Context found during research:

- `r-i` is already present in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` as `!!wl interview <id>`, added by the **completed** item **WL-0MU95SGEB006HQAM** (commit `652ec575`).
- `dispatchChordCommand` does **not** explicitly recognise the `!!wl interview` family (`!!wl reviewed`, `!!wl (close|delete|update|search)`, and `&& wl audit-set` are recognised). Probe at intake time: `dispatchChordCommand('!!wl interview <id>')` → `false`; `executeResolvedCommand('!!wl interview <id>')` → `'callback'` with `onCommand('!!wl interview TEST-123', …)`. The chord therefore still opens a pane via the generic fallback, but `interview` is not in `isWlModifyingCommand`, so the list does not refresh immediately after answers are recorded / `needsProducerReview` clears.
- `CLI.md` documents `wl interview <id>`; `wl <id> interview` is not valid CLI syntax.

Questions:

1. This request appears largely satisfied by the completed WL-0MU95SGEB006HQAM. Should this item be **(a)** closed as a duplicate/superseded, or **(b)** kept to harden the wiring (explicit `dispatchChordCommand` recognition + modifying-command refresh + dispatch-path test)? **Recommended:** (b) only if the missed-refresh/dispatch-recognition gap matters; otherwise (a) close as duplicate — the chord already exists and dispatches.

2. Is the literal command ordering `wl <id> interview` intended as a new id-first CLI syntax, or is it loose phrasing for the existing `wl interview <id>`? **Recommended:** loose phrasing; `CLI.md` documents only the subcommand-first form (`wl interview <id>`).

3. Should the `r i` path be verified end-to-end in a herdr pane (confirming the pane supplies interactive stdin to the TTY-requiring `wl interview`), or is that out of scope? **Recommended:** include a lightweight verification and document any limitation, because `wl interview` requires a TTY.

The full draft brief (with these as OPEN QUESTION entries in the Appendix) has been written to the work-item description. I am stopping here and flagging the item for producer review.

data.comment:
## RCA — why the original fix didn't work (producer rejection NL)

Producer rejection (recovered from the herdr command log): *"This doesn't seem to work, I'm seeing the local retry mechanism overriding the recommended wait duration. Take a look in the logs to see if there is evidence of this happening. If there is then RCA and fix."*

### Evidence

Scanned all Pi session journals (`.pi/agent/sessions/`): **435** `503 startup_ramp` errors. Every single one has this exact assistant error message shape, with **no `retry_after` field**:

    503: {"type":"startup_ramp","code":"startup_ramp","message":"Server is starting up; retry shortly."}

Reconstructed retry gaps from session `herdr-1789911496-958088-22373` (AI_Hell, 2026-09-20): `+2.4s / +4.2s / +9.2s / +16.1s / +32.3s / +60.3s / +60.3s` — i.e. the local exponential schedule, ignoring the proxy's recommended wait.

### Root cause

1. The original fix parsed the retry hint from the assistant **error message** (`parseServerRetryDelayMs`). Real startup-ramp errors never contain `retry_after`; the hint is only on the **HTTP `Retry-After` header**.
2. Pi's `openai-completions` provider (the Local Proxy's API) throws on the non-2xx response *before* the `after_provider_response` extension event fires, and `formatProviderError` renders only `<status>: <body>` — the header value is dropped before the extension ever sees it.
3. Therefore `parseServerRetryDelayMs()` returned `undefined` for every real ramp error, and the loop fell back to plain exponential backoff — exactly the producer's observation.

### Fix

- New `createRetryHintCapturingFetch()` — a transparent `globalThis.fetch` wrapper installed at recovery registration. It records `Retry-After` / `Retry-After-Ms` from 429/5xx responses and clears the hint on 2xx. This is the only point where the header is observable for `openai-completions`; it sits inside `proxy-sse-signals`'s capturing fetch (which reads `globalThis.fetch` at call time).
- New `parseRetryAfterHeaders()` parses the captured header (delta-seconds, `retry-after-ms`, HTTP-date; `Headers` or plain record).
- `resolveRetryDelay()` now takes a `headerHintMs` argument that **takes precedence** over the error-message hint, and reports `hintSource` (`header` | `message`).
- The error-message parse is retained as a fallback (AC2) for providers that fold the hint into the text.
- `installFetchRetryHintCapture()` is called from `registerRecoveryModule()`; `triggerInvisibleContinue()` passes the captured hint into `resolveRetryDelay()`.

The retry loop remains the single retry layer (AC7): the fetch wrapper only observes, it does not retry.

### Scope note (deviation, still flagged for producer)

The brief's constraint says the change belongs in the Pi coding agent codebase. That source checkout is not available in this environment (no `/home/rgardler/projects/pi-coding-agent`; the installed pi is a root-owned bundle with no `src/`). The fix therefore lands in the Worklog recovery module — the layer that actually performs the observed `2/4/8/16/32/60` retries (it suppresses pi's built-in `_prepareRetry`).

data.author: pi-agent
data.comment:
## Post-implementation log verification (2026-09-25): clients still do NOT honour Retry-After

Investigated whether clients now respect the proxy's retry instruction. **They do not.** Evidence from proxy and client logs.

### Proxy IS emitting the hint
`/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log`, mode-switch drain gate (ui.py) returns 503 with both `Retry-After` header and top-level body `retry_after`:
- 2026-09-25 13:13:17.268 `Deferring chat request during mode-switch drain (retry_after=44s)`
- 2026-09-25 13:13:19.291 (retry_after=42s), 13:13:23.304 (38s), 13:13:31.327 (30s)

### Client is ignoring it
Client session `herdr-1790338396-3843403-13820` (09-25, after fix commit 5ccc2ae3) hit the drain. The folded assistant error is:
`503: {"type":"mode_switch_drain","code":"mode_switch_drain","message":"Mode switch in progress; retry shortly."}`
Retry gaps remain the old exponential pattern, independent of the 44/42/38s hints: **+2.0s, +4.0s, +8.0s (+16.0s)**.

Same pattern in post-fix sessions:
- 2026-09-22 09:07:11 — gaps +2.0 / +4.0 / +8.0
- 2026-09-23 15:44:38 — gaps +2.1 / +4.0 / +8.0
- 2026-09-25 13:13:17 — gaps +2.0 / +4.0 / +8.0

Across ALL client session journals, no assistant `errorMessage` ever contains `retry_after`/`Retry-After`.

### Root cause — the fix parses a surface the hint never reaches
1. Proxy body is `{"error":{...},"status":503,"retry_after":N}` plus `Retry-After` header.
2. `openai` SDK v6.40.0 (`src/core/error.ts` `APIError.generate`) does `const error = errorResponse?.['error'];` — it keeps only the inner `error` object and discards the top-level `retry_after`/`status` (header IS retained on `error.headers`).
3. pi-ai 0.87.x `normalizeProviderError`/`pickBodyText` stringifies only `error.error` into `errorMessage` → `503: {inner object}`; headers are not folded in.
4. The Worklog extension's `parseServerRetryDelayMs()` (AC1/AC2) parses `errorMessage`, which contains no hint → returns undefined → falls back to `calculateDelay()` exponential backoff, no jitter.
5. pi-ai's provider-level `retryProviderRequest` DOES read `error.headers.get('retry-after')`, but remains disabled (`maxRetries: 0`; `retry.provider.maxRetries` unset).

### Conclusion
AC1/AC2 are NOT met in practice (unit tests pass because they feed a synthetic error string containing the hint, which the real pipeline never produces). AC5 (jitter) is therefore also not exercised. This is consistent with the existing manual audit rejection (2026-09-23).

Remediation options (out of scope here, for a follow-up): (a) enable provider-level `retry.provider.maxRetries` so pi-ai honours the header directly, or (b) surface `Retry-After`/`retry_after` into `errorMessage` (or expose headers to the extension), or (c) have the proxy put the numeric hint inside the `error` object (e.g. `error.retry_after`) so it survives SDK folding.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## RCA — why the previous fix still did not work

Re-read the producer's rejection and the herdr-downtime RCA (`WL-C0MUG2D1JI00581HX`). The previous fix correctly added `Retry-After` header capture via a transparent `globalThis.fetch` wrapper, but left the delay decision as `floor = max(exponential, serverHintMs)`.

That `max()` is the defect behind *"the local retry mechanism overriding the recommended wait duration"*: once the local exponential outgrows the server hint, it silently overrides it. With the proxy's ramp hints of 5-18s, the effective schedule still becomes:

| attempt | local exponential | Retry-After | `max()` delay (jitter 0) |
|---------|-------------------|-------------|--------------------------|
| 1 | 2s | 7s | 7s |
| 2 | 4s | 7s | 7s |
| 3 | 8s | 7s | 8s |
| 4 | 16s | 7s | **16s** |
| 5 | 32s | 7s | **32s** |
| 6 | 60s | 7s | **60s** |

So the header is captured, but the local backoff still governs from attempt 4 onward — the client waits *longer* than the server asked, ignoring the hint.

### Fix

When a usable server hint is present it is now **authoritative**: `delay = min(hint * (1 + jitter), maxDelayMs)`. The local exponential backoff applies **only** when the hint is absent/malformed (AC3 unchanged). Upward-only jitter (AC5) and the configurable cap (AC1) are preserved.

### Verification

- The hint-derived delay no longer escalates with the attempt number.
- Missing/malformed hints still produce the original exponential schedule.
- Full-ramp survival (AC4) unchanged (the loop has no retry budget).

These were verified against `dev` during planning and they change the emphasis of the ACs:

1. **The critical-first scan filters on `status`, so "marker bypass" alone cannot duplicate.** The
   scan only accepts `open`/`blocked` items, and `dispatchClaimedTier` performs a CAS claim
   (`claimItem`) guarded on the expected `status`+`stage`. A duplicate therefore requires the item
   to be genuinely `open` at the expected stage at re-dispatch time. **H2/H5 (the item's status
   reverts to `open` while a dispatch pane is still live) is the necessary partner to H1**, and is
   precisely the scenario the critical escalation path was *built for* — the dispatcher docs
   already name it: *"a previous dispatch was rolled back / the implementing agent aborted and
   reset the item to `open` while the standing marker remained"*
   (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, "Critical escalation in the Herdr-head contract"). The
   escalation fix (WL-0MU6UL3XY001M3VT) traded starvation for this duplicate window.
2. **A second, distinct vector exists on the coordination path.** The same docs state the
   coordination leader *"validates offers at dispatch-time **without a marker check**"*
   (`computeMostImportantItem` / offer dispatch). Any fix scoped only to
   `dispatchFromHerdrList` leaves this path open. AC5 already anticipates this ("both the
   Herdr-head and coordination dispatch paths").
3. **A live-pane signal already exists but is not item-scoped.** `getRunningDowntimePanes`
   (`RunningPanesResult = {ok, count, paneIds?}`) plus `parseHerdrPaneListOutput` are already
   wired and already exclude terminal agent states; `buildDowntimePaneTitle` preserves the item id
   as a **suffix** (`Downtime triggered <kind> … - <ITEM-ID>`), so an item-scoped in-flight
   predicate is a small extension, not new infrastructure. The existing helper is explicitly
   documented as *not* a capacity limit (WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3) — the guard must be
   **item-scoped and gated on a non-terminal ("working") agent**, never a global pane count, or it
   reintroduces the stall it warns about.
4. **`appendRollingJsonl` is non-atomic on the write path** (`readFile` → push → trim →
   `writeFile` to the target path, `downtime-log.ts`). A concurrent reader can observe a truncated
   or empty file, which makes `dispatchedItemMarkers`/`dispatchedItemStages` momentarily lose the
   marker — confirming AC4's premise (H3) as a real *contributing* factor even though it cannot by
   itself explain a critical-tier duplicate.
5. **The pane/session id is not available at marker-write time.** `recordDispatch` runs **before**
   `spawnAgentPane` (fail-closed ordering: a marker write failure aborts the dispatch), and
   `DowntimeSpawnResult` is `{ok: true}` with no pane id; `send-to-pi.sh` is fire-and-forget. AC6
   therefore needs either an optional post-spawn **enrichment entry** (same `itemId`/`kind`, copying
   `dispatchedAt`+`stage` so marker semantics are preserved — the reader takes the **last** entry per
   item) or an extended spawn contract. The plan recommends the enrichment entry (fail-open: a
   failed lookup never blocks or un-marks a dispatch).
6. **The incident root log is not on this host.** `scan_duplicate_dispatches.py` over the five
   default roots finds **no `LP-*` entries at all** (the `LP-` project root/log is not present), so
   AC1 cannot rest on host log forensics alone. AC1 must be satisfied by **instrumentation +
   reproduction** (the AC's own sanctioned route: "via targeted instrumentation or reproduction"),
   with the 13:54:33Z evidence in this description as the anchor.

---

### Proposed features (7) — each a minimal end-to-end slice (code + tests + docs)

Test-first: the failing reproduction (F1) and the permanent regression suite (F2) land **before**
either implementation feature (F3/F4).

| # | Short title | ACs covered | Prio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | Reproduce and confirm re-dispatch mechanism | AC1 | high |
| F2 | Regression suite: one dispatch per in-flight critical item | AC5 | high |
| F3 | In-flight guard: Herdr-head and normal paths | AC2, AC3 | high |
| F4 | In-flight guard: coordination offer path | AC2 | high |
| F5 | Atomic rolling-log writes | AC4 | medium |
| F6 | Dispatcher log: selection path and pane id | AC6 | medium |
| F7 | Post-fix duplicate-dispatch verification | AC2 (evidence) | medium |

#### F1 — Reproduce and confirm re-dispatch mechanism (AC1)

- **Summary:** Establish, by reproduction and targeted instrumentation, exactly which selection
  path produced the second dispatch — before any fix is written.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - AC1.1 A characterisation test drives **two idle cycles** in one process against a critical
    implement/plan item that is observed `open` at its marker's stage while its dispatch pane is
    live, and asserts `1` dispatch. Today it must **fail** (2 dispatches) — the RED witness.
  - AC1.2 The verdict names the confirmed selection path (Herdr-head critical-first scan vs
    coordination offer dispatch) with a source line reference and cycle-by-cycle trace.
  - AC1.3 Each of H1–H4 is marked **confirmed / refuted / not reproducible**, with the evidence
    that discriminates it; H2+H1 is confirmed or refuted explicitly.
  - AC1.4 Residual uncertainty and any new hypothesis (e.g. H5 status revert) is recorded, with the
    workaround applied in F3/F4 stated for each open hypothesis.
- **Minimal implementation:** add a deterministic two-cycle harness around `dispatchDowntimeWork`
  using the existing injectable `getHerdrListHead` / `claimItem` / `spawnAgentPane` /
  `recordDispatch` / `getRunningDowntimePanes` seams; simulate the live pane via the pane-list
  fixture; record the selection reason per cycle (feeds F6).
- **Prototype/experiment:** the two-cycle reproduction itself — success threshold: the RED test
  observes 2 dispatches pre-fix and 1 post-fix.
- **Dependencies:** none.
- **Deliverables:** RCA verdict comment on this item; new test block in
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`.
- **Key Files:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

#### F2 — Regression suite: one dispatch per in-flight critical item (AC5)

- **Summary:** Promote F1's witness into the permanent, path-covering regression suite named by AC5.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - AC5.1 Two consecutive idle cycles over a Herdr head containing a critical `plan_complete`
    implement item **already claimed/in-flight at the same stage** produce **exactly one** dispatch
    on the Herdr-head path.
  - AC5.2 The same two-cycle assertion passes for the **coordination** path
    (`computeMostImportantItem` → offer → leader dispatch).
  - AC5.3 The suite is RED at F2 completion and GREEN after F3+F4 (recorded as the dependency
    evidence for those features).
  - AC5.4 Non-critical duplicates are covered by at least one case at the same stage with a stale
    marker (guards against a critical-only regression).
- **Minimal implementation:** extend the existing `downtime-worker.test.ts` critical-first describe
  block and `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` critical-offer describe block; assert on dispatch
  counts, not just the returned outcome, so a second cycle cannot pass unnoticed.
- **Dependencies:** F1.
- **Deliverables:** new tests in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` and
  `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`.
- **Key Files:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts`

#### F3 — In-flight guard: Herdr-head and normal paths (AC2, AC3)

- **Summary:** Replace the critical-first scan's **unconditional** marker bypass with a
  **stale-only** bypass gated on an item-scoped live-pane check.
- **Recommended mechanism (to be confirmed by F1):** escalate a critical candidate when **either**
  the marker is stale/absent **or** no *live working* dispatch pane exists for that item id; skip
  when a live working pane exists. Fail-closed on a failed/ambiguous pane query (skip, never
  duplicate) — the cycle retries and escalation still completes within a bounded number of cycles.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - AC2.1 With a live `working` downtime pane whose label suffix is the item id, **no** dispatch
    (or coordination offer) for that item is attempted — regardless of marker freshness, stage
    advancement, or `status` being `open`.
  - AC2.2 A failed or unparseable pane query is fail-closed: no dispatch for a candidate whose
    in-flight state cannot be proven.
  - AC2.3 Panes whose agent is absent, `done`, or `exited` do **not** block dispatch (no
    idle-pane deadlock).
  - AC2.4 The guard is item-scoped; it never uses a global running-pane count as a dispatch limit
    (WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3 invariant preserved).
  - AC3.1 A critical item with a fresh **or** stale marker and **no** live pane is still escalated
    within one idle cycle (all existing critical-first tests stay green).
  - AC3.2 Escalation remains bounded: it is deferred only while a live pane exists, never by a
    fixed TTL alone.
- **Minimal implementation:** add an item-scoped in-flight resolver (extend
  `RunningPanesResult` to expose pane records, or add a sibling dep returning
  `{paneId, itemId, kind, agentStatus}[]`) resolved **once per idle cycle** and threaded into
  `dispatchFromHerdrList`; consult it in the critical-first loop and in the normal loop's marker
  decision for critical candidates.
- **Dependencies:** F2.
- **Deliverables:** code + unit tests + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` update under
  "Critical-first tier & freeze split-by-skill".
- **Key Files:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts`,
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

#### F4 — In-flight guard: coordination offer path (AC2)

- **Summary:** Apply the same in-flight guard where the coordination leader validates and
  dispatches offers (documented as running **without a marker check**).
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - AC2.5 An offer for a critical item with a live working dispatch pane is **withheld or rejected**
    at dispatch time, and the rejection reason is recorded.
  - AC2.6 `computeMostImportantItem` no longer offers a critical item that is in-flight (pane-live),
    so a non-critical offerable item is chosen instead when one exists.
  - AC2.7 Cross-root offers use the **offer's own root** for the pane query (no leader-root
    cwd regression — the WL-0MTQ14W7L003II5A invariant).
- **Minimal implementation:** resolve the in-flight set for the offer's root in the offer
  computation and re-check at leader dispatch; reuse F3's resolver.
- **Dependencies:** F2 (F3 provides the resolver; a shared-helper extraction is acceptable and
  should be factored so F3/F4 do not duplicate logic).
- **Deliverables:** code + tests in `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` + docs update.
- **Key Files:** `packages/herdr/src/coordination.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`,
  `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

#### F5 — Atomic rolling-log writes (AC4)

- **Summary:** Make both rolling JSONL logs atomically replaced so a concurrent marker read can
  never observe an empty or partial file.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - AC4.1 `appendRollingJsonl` writes to a temporary sibling file and `rename`s it over the target;
    a test asserts the target path is never opened for direct writing and that no temp file is left
    behind on success or failure.
  - AC4.2 A concurrency test that hammers append + read in parallel observes **only** complete,
    parseable JSONL lines (never empty, never partial) — fails against the pre-fix writer.
  - AC4.3 Trimming to `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES` (100) and the throw-on-I/O-failure (fail-closed)
    contract are unchanged; the JSONL format stays human-readable.
  - AC4.4 Both `downtime-dispatches.log` and the coordination log use the atomic writer.
- **Minimal implementation:** temp file name including pid + random suffix, `writeFile` + `rename`
  (same directory to stay on one filesystem); keep `mkdir` recursive and the existing
  read/trim/append logic; clean up the temp file on error before rethrowing.
- **Dependencies:** none (independently shippable).
- **Deliverables:** code + tests + `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` "Rolling log trimming"
  update.
- **Key Files:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/coordination.test.ts`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

#### F6 — Dispatcher log: selection path and pane id (AC6)

- **Summary:** Extend the log schema with the selection path/reason and the resolved
  session/pane id so the next RCA is answerable from the log alone.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - AC6.1 Every successful dispatch entry records `selectionPath` (e.g. `critical-first` |
    `normal-scan` | `coordination-offer` | `scheduled-prompt`) and a machine-readable
    `selectionReason` (e.g. `marker-stale`, `marker-fresh-no-pane`, `non-critical`).
  - AC6.2 The pane/session id is recorded for successful dispatches via a post-spawn enrichment
    entry that **preserves** `itemId`, `kind`, `stage` and `dispatchedAt` so marker semantics
    (last-entry-wins, stale-release, fail-closed staleness) are unchanged — proven by a test that
    round-trips the enriched log through `dispatchedItemMarkers` / `markerStillExcludes`.
  - AC6.3 Enrichment is fail-open: if the pane id cannot be resolved, the dispatch still succeeds
    and the schema records an explicit `paneId: null`/absent marker rather than a guess.
  - AC6.4 Backward compatibility: legacy entries without the new fields parse and behave exactly as
    before (existing `downtime-log.test.ts` compatibility tests stay green).
  - AC6.5 `scan_duplicate_dispatches.py` reports the new fields for post-fix evidence.
- **Minimal implementation:** add the two fields to `DowntimeDispatchEvent`; thread the selection
  path/reason from the selection loops; append the enrichment entry after a successful spawn
  (best-effort, swallowed like the existing failure trace).
- **Dependencies:** F1 (the reason vocabulary is defined by the confirmed mechanism).
- **Deliverables:** code + tests + docs log-schema update.
- **Key Files:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts`,
  `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`

#### F7 — Post-fix duplicate-dispatch verification (AC2 evidence)

- **Summary:** Produce reproducible evidence that no new duplicate dispatch occurs after the fix
  window, and that a duplicate is impossible with a live pane.
- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - AC-V1 `scan_duplicate_dispatches.py --since <fix-deploy timestamp>` over the default roots

  - AC-V2 The full suite (`npm test`) passes with F1's RED witness and F2's suite GREEN.
  - AC-V3 The verification method, window, roots and commands are recorded on this item so the
    check is repeatable.
- **Minimal implementation:** run the scan before/after a bounded observation window; record the
  JSON report as an artifact on the item.
- **Dependencies:** F3, F4, F5, F6.
- **Deliverables:** verification comment + attached scan JSON.
- **Key Files:** `packages/herdr/scripts/scan_duplicate_dispatches.py`,

### RCA side-finding: `wl reviewed <id> true` releases the item to `open`

While flagging this item for producer review, `wl reviewed WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 true` returned
`needsProducerReview: true` but **also transitioned `status` from `in-progress` to `open`** while the
item's plan pane (`w2N:p1J`, session `herdr-1790031772-1558598-29245`) was still live. The item was
immediately re-claimed with `wl update WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 --status in_progress`, so the window was
seconds long.

This matters for this RCA: it is a second, **tool-level** contributor to the H1+H2 mechanism. A
critical item that is momentarily `open` at its marker's stage is precisely what the Herdr-head
critical-first scan re-selects (it bypasses the fresh marker), and if the CAS claim is issued in that
window it can succeed because the DB genuinely says `open`.

- **Recommendation (in scope for F1/F3):** the plan skill's documented pause-for-producer-input path
  (`wl reviewed <id> true`) must not implicitly release the claim on a downtime-dispatched run.
  Either use `StatusLifecycle.update_status(id, "open", needs_producer_review=True)` atomically, or
  ensure `wl reviewed` does not mutate `status`. Recorded here rather than filed as a separate item
  because it is part of the same duplicate-dispatch class; F1 should confirm it with the live-pane
  reproduction.
- **Evidence:** `wl reviewed WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 true --json` → `status: open`;
  `wl update … --status in_progress --json` → `status: in-progress`, `needsProducerReview: true`.

  2. pane query succeeded, no live pane → **escalate** (`no-live-pane`);

  This is neither blind fail-closed nor blind fail-open: escalation is never permanently starved, and a
  duplicate is never permitted while a pane is live. It is benign in practice because pane spawn itself
  requires herdr, so a persistent pane-query outage also prevents dispatch. **Adopted for WL-0MUBVKXQJ000L8EO.**
- **Q5 — pane id for AC6.** Producer: *"whatever you think is best."* → **adopted the post-spawn

- **Q6 — effort.** Producer: *"re-estimate"* → the `effort-and-risk` estimate is re-run as step 8.
- **Q7 — F3/F4 split.** Producer: *"separate"* → **kept separate** (both depend on the regression
  suite directly, so they can proceed in parallel sharing one resolver).

data.comment:
## RCA verdict — confirmed mechanism (F1 / AC1)

**Status: root cause CONFIRMED by reproduction + targeted instrumentation.** The 2026-09-21T13:54:33Z
re-dispatch of `LP-0MUAY9AMS002O2ZO` is reproduced deterministically in-process, and the live
incident recurred on this very item during this session (see "Live reproduction" below).

### Confirmed selection path

**Herdr-head critical-first scan** — `dispatchFromHerdrList` → `selectCriticalFirstCandidates`
(`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:1890`, filter at `:1896`), loop at `:1941`.

- The scan selects `priority === 'critical' && (status === 'open' || status === 'blocked')` (`:1896`).
- The loop **deliberately bypasses the dispatched-marker exclusion** for these candidates
  (`:1928`–`:1940` — "this loop bypasses the non-safety filters"). No marker check is applied.
- The only remaining serialisation is the CAS claim in `dispatchClaimedTier`
  (`:2106` `expected = TIER_EXPECTED[kind]`; `:2166` claim; `:2169` `if (!claim.ok)`).

The coordination offer path (`computeMostImportantItem` → `dispatchFromCoordination`) is a
**second, independent** vector and is covered separately by F4 (WL-0MUBVKYH5009CGBI); it was not
the vector for this reproduction (the head path fired first).

### Cycle-by-cycle trace (two idle cycles, one process)

| Cycle | Candidate observed | Selection | Marker state | CAS claim | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `CR-DUP`, `critical`, `open`, stage `plan_complete` | critical-first scan (marker bypass) | fresh implement marker at `plan_complete` | `{status:'open',stage:'plan_complete'}` **matches DB → succeeds** | pane spawned (#1) |
| 2 | `CR-DUP`, `critical`, `open`, stage `plan_complete` (status reverted / never advanced) | critical-first scan re-selects (marker bypass, `:1941`) | fresh marker still present | **succeeds again** (DB genuinely `open`) | **pane spawned (#2) — DUPLICATE** |

RED witness: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` →
`RCA: critical in-flight re-dispatch with a live pane (WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 / AC1.1)`.
Observed pre-fix: `OBSERVED_SPAWN_COUNT=2`, `secondDispatched=true`; asserted post-fix target is `1`.
The test is committed as `it.fails` so the suite stays green while the defect is open; F3 flips it to `it`.

### Hypothesis decision table (AC1.3)

| # | Hypothesis | Verdict | Discriminating evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H1 | Critical-first scan bypasses the marker exclusion | **CONFIRMED** | `:1937`–`:1940` bypass comment + loop; removing the bypass in the witness drops spawns from 2 → 1 |
| H2 | Stale item `status` in the dispatcher snapshot | **REFUTED as a separate cause** | `getHerdrListHead` is re-read every dispatch; the scan filter (`:1896`) only accepts `open`/`blocked`, so a stale `in_progress` snapshot cannot be selected at all |
| H3 | Non-atomic rolling-log rewrite (`appendRollingJsonl`) | **CONFIRMED as a real, contributing defect** (cannot alone cause a critical-tier duplicate) | `downtime-log.ts` `readFile → push → trim → writeFile` to the target path; a concurrent reader can momentarily see a truncated/empty file and lose the marker. Cannot explain this duplicate because the critical-first loop never consults the marker |
| H4 | Multiple leaders | **REFUTED** | single-leader model holds on this host; no second leader lease observed; the reproduction needs no second instance |
| H5 | Item `status` reverted to `open` while a dispatch pane is still live | **CONFIRMED — necessary partner of H1** | CAS (`:2166`) succeeds only when the DB genuinely says `open` at the expected stage. Reproduced by observing the item as `open` at `plan_complete` on cycle 2 with a live pane. **H1+H5 is the confirmed pair** |
| H2+H1 pair | — | **REFUTED** (H2 is not a cause); **H1+H5 CONFIRMED** | as above |

### CAS / bypass analysis (AC1.5)

The duplicate **required a real DB `status: open` at the expected stage** — the CAS is not the gap;
it faithfully claims an item the database reports as dispatchable. The gap is the **absence of any
in-flight guard**: the dispatcher has no item-scoped notion of "a pane for this item is already
working". Fixing the bypass alone would not be enough (H5 must also be gated), and gating only the
marker would not help the critical path (it ignores the marker). F3's item-scoped live-pane guard is
therefore **justified by evidence, not assumed**.

### Live reproduction during this session (strongest evidence)

While running `/skill:implement` on **this** parent (`WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4`), the first
`implement.py start` invocation hit the dirty-working-tree gate and executed its documented abort
path, which resets the item to `status: open` **while this pane was still live**:

- `wl show WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4 --json` immediately after → `status: open`, `stage: plan_complete`
  (the marker's stage), assignee retained.
- This is exactly the H5 precondition, caused by a **tool-level** path (not an agent abort).
- The item was re-claimed within seconds (`StatusLifecycle.update_status(..., 'in_progress')`) to
  close the duplicate window. No second pane spawned this time, but the window was live.

This corroborates the planning side-finding (`wl reviewed <id> true` also releases `status` to
`open`): **any** path that resets a critical item to `open` while its pane is live re-arms the
critical-first scan. F3's guard is the single fix that closes all of them.

### Residual uncertainty (AC1.4)

- **H3 (atomic log)** remains a real latent defect even though it is not this duplicate's cause;
  it is fixed independently by F5 (WL-0MUBVL1FI0071WN3). Residual risk: a lost marker can still
  cause a *non-critical* re-dispatch on the normal path (the marker is the only guard there until
  F3's guard lands).
- **`wl reviewed <id> true` / `implement.py start` abort resetting `status`** is a tool-level
  contributor. F3's in-flight guard makes it harmless (no duplicate while a pane is live); a
  separate hygiene fix to stop those paths releasing a live claim is **out of scope** here and
  recorded as residual risk, not fixed.
- **Cross-root scope:** the scan fix covers all roots that share the dispatcher; the coordination
  path (F4) is the remaining unguarded vector.

### Workaround applied by F3/F4

F3 replaces the unconditional bypass with a **stale-only bypass gated on an item-scoped live-pane
check** (live `working` pane → skip; pane query succeeded + none → escalate; pane query failed →
marker-TTL fallback). F4 applies the same guard to the coordination offer path. Together they close
the H1+H5 window on both dispatch paths.
