data.author: Map
data.comment:
Post-implementation alignment (SA worklog review) — commit 681b33d7 pushed to dev.

## How SorraAgents ended up at `updatedAt + 60s`
- **SA-0MRJBEJGY0095XAY** ("Add recent-audit gate to audit skill startup") introduced `AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS = 60` and the gate `auditedAt > updatedAt + 60s`. Its AC2 explicitly framed this as a **conservative pipeline-skip/reuse decision**: only skip the expensive full audit when the audit is confidently newer than the item's last update by a safety buffer.
- **SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4** then found this is unsatisfiable in practice: persisting an audit bumps `updatedAt` to ≈ `auditedAt`, so `auditedAt > updatedAt + 60s` can never hold → parent runs re-triggered child audits forever.
- **SA-0MTHC710X003ORZM** added the reverse **persistence-write tolerance** (`0 <= updatedAt - auditedAt <= 30s` → trust it as the audit's own write). Net SA gate: fresh iff `auditedAt > updatedAt + 60s` **OR** `-30s <= auditedAt - updatedAt <= 0`.

## Evaluation vs ContextHub
- The SA gate answers **"is it safe to skip re-auditing?"** (conservative; rejects audits only slightly newer than the update).
- ContextHub `isAuditFresh` answers **"does this audit cover the current content?"** (a currency predicate used by display, dispatch and ordering). Its long-standing form was one-sided: `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`.
- The symmetric form drafted in AC2 (`|auditedAt - updatedAt| < 60s`) was a category error: it marks an audit **more than 60s AFTER** `updatedAt` as stale. Both the original one-sided gate and SA's `+60s` gate treat that case as **fresh**. The dispatch fixture in packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts caught it.

## Decision (aligned)
Keep the **one-sided** ContextHub currency predicate: `auditedAt > updatedAt - AUDIT_FRESHNESS_AT_NEAR_TOLERANCE_MS` (60s). It is the most reliable for the display/dispatch/ordering decision: an audit at or after the content timestamp is fresh; an audit preceding a later content edit is stale once the gap exceeds tolerance. The fingerprint gate remains primary. The SA `+60s` reuse gate stays in the Python runner and is documented in icons.ts as a different decision, not to be conflated.

Changes in 681b33d7: reverted the symmetric gate to one-sided; added an audit-later-than-`updatedAt` regression test (icons.test.ts + database.test.ts ordering tier); reconciled the dispatch fixture and sync.test.ts fixture; corrected docs (AUDIT_STATUS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CLI.md, herdr README); AC2 updated to one-sided semantics. Config-level full suite green.

## F3 complete — item-scoped in-flight guard on the Herdr-head + normal paths (AC2, AC3)

### What landed

**New resolver/helpers (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`):**

- `paneLabelItemId(label)` — parses the trailing work-item id from a downtime pane label
  (`Downtime triggered <kind> <title> - <ITEM-ID>`, the `buildDowntimePaneTitle` suffix contract).
  Exported so F4 reuses it unchanged (AC2.9).
- `runningDowntimePaneItemIds(panes)` — the ITEM-SCOPED counterpart of
  `countRunningDowntimePanes`: only downtime-labelled panes with a **live `working`** agent and a
  parseable id suffix count as in-flight. Terminal/idle/unknown agents and manual panes do NOT.
- `InFlightPanes` tri-state (`{available, itemIds}`) + `resolveInFlightPanes(deps, cwd)` — resolved
  once per idle cycle; never throws; unavailable on a missing dep, `{ok:false}`, no `records`, or a
  thrown resolver.
- `evaluateCriticalFirstGuard(itemId, inFlight, markerDispatchedAt, now, staleWindowMs)` — the pure
  decision table:
  1. live working pane → `skip` (`in-flight-pane`)
  2. query ok, none → `escalate` (`no-live-pane`)
  3. query failed + fresh marker → `skip` (`in-flight-unverified`)
  4. query failed + stale/absent marker → `escalate` (`marker-stale-escalation`)

**Wiring:**

- `RunningPanesResult` gains an additive `records?: HerdrPaneRecord[]`.
- `dispatchFromHerdrList` resolves `ctx.inFlight` once and consults the guard in the **critical-first
  loop** (replacing the unconditional marker bypass) AND in the **normal loop for critical
  candidates** (AC2.5).
- `defaultRunningDowntimePanesResolver` (`index.ts`) now returns `records: panes` from the same
  single `herdr pane list` read — no extra process spawn.
- `count`/`paneIds` keep their existing meaning (owner-lease qualifier ONLY — never a dispatch limit,
  WL-0MU2EP6JL006A1U3 preserved, AC2.4).

**Docs:** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §"Critical-first tier & freeze split-by-skill" — added
the in-flight guard decision table and the bounded-fallback rationale (AC3.3).

F2's Herdr-head witnesses (WL-0MUBVKS5I007LSWB) were committed as `it.fails` (RED baseline: 6 expected
failures). F3 flips the four Herdr-head cases to `it` (including F1's original witness) and adds

- **AC2.2** failed/unparseable query → marker-TTL fallback (`in-flight-unverified`) — witness +
  unit tests.

## F4 complete — in-flight guard on the coordination offer path (AC2)

### What landed

- **`computeMostImportantItem` (owner's check-in offer):** resolves the item-scoped in-flight set for
  the **offer's own root** (`resolveInFlightPanes(deps, cwd)`, reusing F3's resolver — AC2.9) and
  skips in-flight critical candidates in both the critical-first scan and the normal window. When
  another offerable item exists it is offered instead (AC2.7); when ONLY in-flight criticals remain
  the result is the new neutral `{ok:true, inFlightHold:true}` — never `noCandidate`, so the worker
  never pauses/cooldowns on it.
- **`dispatchFromCoordination` (leader dispatch):** adds a **dispatch-time re-check** (AC2.10). The
  in-flight set is resolved **per offer root** (cached once per root), never the leader's root
  (AC2.8), and an offer whose pane appeared after it was computed is skipped — the entry is KEPT
  (still valid once the pane finishes). When every surviving offer is in-flight the terminal reason
  is the neutral `'in-flight-pane'`.
- Leader-side re-check blocks only a **proven** live working pane; an unavailable query does not
  stall all coordination dispatch (the owner's offer computation already applied the F3 marker-TTL
  fallback).
- **No logic duplication (AC2.9):** reuses F3's `resolveInFlightPanes` / `evaluateCriticalFirstGuard`
  / `paneLabelItemId` unchanged.
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §"Critical-first tier & freeze split-by-skill" — added
  the coordination-path guard paragraph (per-offer-root resolution, owner withholding, leader
  TOCTOU re-check, neutral `in-flight-pane`).

### RED → GREEN evidence (AC5.5)

F2's coordination witnesses were committed as `it.fails` (RED baseline). F4 flips them to `it` and
adds the AC2.7 / AC2.8 / leader cross-root cases and the `inFlightHold` unit case.

```
npx vitest run packages/herdr
→ Test Files  65 passed (65)
  Tests  2373 passed (2373)
```

There are now **zero expected failures** in the whole herdr package — every F2 witness (both paths)
is GREEN.

### AC mapping

- **AC2.6** in-flight offer withheld/rejected at dispatch time — `computeMostImportantItem` withholds;
  `dispatchFromCoordination` rejects the TOCTOU offer.
- **AC2.7** fallback candidate chosen / no empty cycle — witness "an in-flight critical item is not
  offered …; the non-critical fallback is chosen"; `inFlightHold` (not `noCandidate`) when only
  in-flight criticals remain.
- **AC2.8** cross-root correctness — new tests assert the pane query targets the OFFER root
  (`/offer-root`) and never the leader root (`/leader-root`), on both the offer and leader-recheck
  paths; WL-0MTQ14W7L003II5A invariant preserved.
- **AC2.9** no logic duplication — F3's resolver/helpers reused unchanged.
- **AC2.10** leader-side re-check — new TOCTOU witness + leader cross-root test.

**Design note:** the two-cycle witness drives a faithful H5 re-offer (owner offers → leader
dispatches → item re-observed `open` → owner re-offers → leader rejects the in-flight offer), so the
count assertion (1 spawn) exercises the real duplicate window rather than an entry-consumption
artefact.

`rename`s it over the target. Changes:

- **Atomic replace** — a concurrent reader sees either the whole previous file or the whole new one,
  never a truncated/empty/partial log. Previously `readFile → push → trim → writeFile` on the target
  (the RCA's H3 contributing defect).
- **Temp cleanup** — the temp file is `rm`'d (best-effort) on failure before the error is rethrown;
  the target is left untouched.
- **Unchanged contracts** — trimming to `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES` (100), the throw-on-I/O-failure
  (fail-closed) contract, and the human-readable JSONL format are all preserved.
- **Both logs** — dispatch (`downtime-dispatches.log`) and coordination (`downtime-coordination.log`)
  share the same writer (AC4.4).

### Tests (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts`)

New describe `atomic rolling-log writes (WL-0MUBVL1FI0071WN3 / F5)`:

- **AC4.1 success:** the target inode CHANGES across an append (replaced via rename, never written in
  place) and no `.tmp` file remains.
- **AC4.1 failure:** with the target made a directory (forcing the rename to fail), the append
  rejects, the target is untouched, and no `.tmp` file leaks.
- **AC4.2 concurrency:** 40 concurrent appends + 60 concurrent reads; every raw line parses and no
  temp file leaks.
- **AC4.4:** the coordination log uses the same atomic writer.

### Verification

```
npx vitest run packages/herdr
→ Test Files  65 passed (65)
  Tests  2377 passed (2377)
```

### Docs

`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` §"Rolling log trimming" — documented the atomic replacement
(temp-file + rename), the reader-consistency guarantee, the temp-cleanup-on-failure behaviour, and
that trimming + fail-closed contracts are unchanged.

### AC mapping

- **AC4.1** atomic replace + no temp leak on success/failure — inode + leak tests above.
- **AC4.2** concurrency only ever observes complete parseable lines.
- **AC4.3** trimming/throw/format unchanged — existing rolling-bound tests stay green.

## Open Questions for Producer

**Q1: What constitutes "work ongoing" in a project?**
The requirement says to prevent ship mode when "work is ongoing". Does this mean:
- (a) ANY agent pane with an active agent (working, idle, or blocked) associated with a work item from this project?
- (b) Only agents in "working" status?
- (c) Any pane at all (including idle) that has an associated work item from this project's worklog?

**Q2: How should we discover panes across workspaces?**
The requirement says "scan all workspaces". Two approaches:
- (a) Use the local `agent-panes.json` (work-item→pane mapping for this project) combined with `herdr agent list` to check pane status. This checks panes tracked for the current worklog project only.
- (b) Scan all projects on the machine for `agent-panes.json` files, then check each pane's status via `herdr agent list`. This checks ALL panes across ALL projects.
- (c) Scan each herdr workspace's panes and determine project membership from the pane's working directory (if the herdr CLI exposes it).

**Q3: What message should be shown when ship mode is blocked?**
Should the message list which panes/work items are in use (to help the user close them), or just a generic "cannot ship while work is in progress" message?

**Q4: Should the blocked state be overridable?**
When work is ongoing, should the user be forced to wait until panes are closed, or can they override with an explicit confirmation?

**Q5: Who writes the code-freeze marker on confirm?**
The ship skill already writes `.worklog/code-freeze.json` when the release starts. The requirement says the project should be placed in code freeze "the moment" the user types `ship`. Should the herdr plugin write the marker itself (at confirm time, before dispatching `/skill:ship release`), or should this be coordinated with the ship skill? Note the marker contract says the ship skill owns writing/clearing; the plugin only reads. Writing from the plugin would extend that contract.

Please advise on these questions so I can proceed with the implementation plan.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
question: Refined questions after codebase research (see the earlier comment for the full context — this supersedes the discovery questions where noted).

## Research findings (reduce the questions)

**Pane ↔ project association already exists.** The Herdr hydrator (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`, WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI) already matches work items to live panes by extracting work-item IDs from pane labels (`herdr pane list`) and comparing against `wl list --status in-progress`. `herdr pane list` returns the machine-wide inventory (all workspaces), so "scan all workspaces" is achievable with the existing `herdr pane list` + `wl list` primitives. No new `agent-panes.json` scan across projects is required.

**Code-freeze marker.** The marker is `.worklog/code-freeze.json`, currently written/cleared by the ship skill (`packages/herdr/src/code-freeze.ts` reads it; the unit doc says the plugin only reads; the ship skill writes). The requirement to freeze "the moment" the user types `ship` means the herdr plugin must write the marker at confirm time — a deliberate extension of the current contract.

## Genuinely open questions

**Q1 (critical) — scope of "work that is ongoing".** Which panes should block ship mode?
- (a) Any pane whose label carries a work item ID belonging to this project, with a live agent (status not `done`/`exited`) — i.e. "panes must be closed", matching the description literally.
- (b) Only panes whose carried work item is `status=in_progress` (the project's canonical "work underway" status) — narrower; a completed item's still-open pane would NOT block.
- (c) Any pane whose label carries a work item ID belonging to this project, regardless of agent status (even `done`) — strictest.

**Agent recommendation:** (b) for "ongoing work" plus (a) as a secondary check would be inconsistent; pick one. I lean (a) because the description says "until work has been completed **and panes have been closed**", which is a pane-presence rule, not a status rule. Confirm which is intended.

**Q2 — blocked message detail.** When blocked, should the message list the offending panes and/or work-item IDs (so the operator can close them), or just state that work is in progress? Recommendation: list the work-item IDs (and pane labels if short) — it is the operator's action list.

**Q3 — marker write failure / dispatch failure.** If the plugin writes the code-freeze marker on confirm but the `/skill:ship release` dispatch fails (no pi pane, `onCommand` throws), the marker would remain and block all implementation. Should the plugin (i) best-effort clear the marker on dispatch failure, or (ii) leave it and surface the error? Recommendation: (i) clear on dispatch failure and surface the error toast, since the ship skill never ran.

Please answer Q1–Q3 (Q1 is blocking). I will then finalise the brief, run the review stages, and advance the item.

## Rejection root cause fixed (WL-0MUEK7H39008VVUF)

The producer's rejection was correct: the ship guard was broken in production. My previous sessions re-audited a stale passing result and re-marked the item ready without exercising the real runtime path — that was the process failure.

### Real defect

`createProductionShipGuardQuery` ran the FULL `wl list --json` (~8.5 MB / 2,299 items) into `execFile` with an 8 MiB `maxBuffer`. The worklog's actual output (8,553,843 bytes) exceeds that, so `execFile` rejected with `ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER`; the catch swallowed it to `worklogOutput = null`, and the guard failed safe — permanently blocking ship mode with the misleading notice "Cannot verify pane state" and listing no offending panes. Every `S` press hit this. The audit never caught it because it never ran the real query path.

### Fix (commit e9c7d434, pushed to dev)

- Worklog query now requests ONLY the id field: `wl list --json --fields id` — ~108 KB for 2,299 items instead of ~8.5 MB, so it cannot overflow as the worklog grows.
- `maxBuffer` raised to 32 MiB as a defensive backstop for both queries.
- The blocked notice now names WHICH query failed (`worklog list unavailable` vs `pane list unavailable`) instead of a generic message.
- Regression tests: `ship-guard-query.test.ts` (ids-only projection, maxBuffer headroom, >8 MiB payload parses and evaluates blocking panes, failure-cause distinction, explicit root targeting) + notice-reason tests in `ship-guard.test.ts` and `ship-guard-tui.test.ts`.
- README Ship Guard section updated.

### Verification

End-to-end against the real worklog at the fixed commit: `worklogOutput` = 108,100 bytes (not null), guard `ok: true`, and it correctly listed the live blocking pane (the active implement pane on WL-0MUD6DDZC007ZSIW) — i.e. the operator now gets the action list instead of a permanent false block.

Full test suite passes at e9c7d434. Re-auditing this parent on the fixed commit now.

Implementation progress (worktree wl-WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV-a-y-audit-approve-silently-no-ops-audit):

**Fix approach — additive schema repair in the shared store.** `SqlitePersistentStore.initializeSchema()` (packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts) now ensures every column the current code requires exists on existing tables via an idempotent, additive-only `REQUIRED_COLUMNS` list. For `audit_results.fingerprint` it runs `ALTER TABLE audit_results ADD COLUMN fingerprint TEXT` when missing and records the `audit_fingerprint_added` metadata sentinel — the same sentinel the `20260923-add-audit-fingerprint` doctor migration uses, so the two paths converge and doctor becomes a no-op after repair. A failure gives a clear, actionable error naming `wl doctor upgrade --confirm`.

**AC2 design decision — SCHEMA_VERSION intentionally NOT bumped (stays 8).** The fingerprint column was introduced *within* schema version 8 (migration 20260923) without a version bump, so the version already claims this schema. Bumping it would also require changing the value `src/migrations` writes, which crosses the workspace build boundary (the worktree resolves `@worklog/shared` to the main checkout's dist, so a new cross-package export breaks the worktree build). Instead the store self-heals on open, guaranteeing the column for any version-8 database; the repair marker makes doctor converge. This satisfies AC2 ('a database at the current SCHEMA_VERSION is guaranteed to have it; legacy databases converge on upgrade') without a version bump, which the AC only requires 'if must'.

**AC4 — herdr background failures are no longer silent.** New pure helper `formatBackgroundFailure` (packages/herdr/src/index.ts) builds a toast (title + command + exit code/signal + short log excerpt); the three `open_pane: false` background dispatch sites wire it via `onExit` and `showToast`. Unit tests cover clean/failure/excerpt/signal/whitespace cases.

**Tests:** packages/shared/src/audit-fingerprint-repair.test.ts (legacy repair + saveAuditResult, idempotency, fresh DB). Docs: docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md (migration/repair note), packages/herdr/README.md (failure toast).

Measurement-plan decision applied (operator approved, "as you recommend").

## 1. Metric corrected

Busy % (union of "≥1 local slot generating" intervals ÷ duration) is a coverage/guardrail metric: it saturates at 100% with a single busy slot, so it cannot detect the change's intended effect (filling the second cheap slot). Success will be measured by, from the report's **Local model utilization** section:

- **avg concurrency (while busy)** — total compute ÷ busy time (e.g. 2026-09-25 1.72 vs 2026-09-24 1.46), and
- **slot utilisation** — total compute ÷ (window × slots) (e.g. 53.6% vs 42.9% for the 9h cheap windows),
- plus **per-audit Phase 2 wall-clock and child overlap** (the actual claim).

Busy % and remote fallback remain guardrails. AC2/AC5 reworded accordingly.

## 2. Baselines tiered

## Measurement result (2026-10-08): benefit NOT observed in cheap mode — root cause found

**Outcome:** the mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` benefit is **not** realised in
cheap mode. Root cause identified and verified: the audit runner force-serialises cheap-mode
audit calls, shadowing the dispatcher's legacy phase-2 env var. Follow-up work item
**SA-0MUZEIAD0008LUFN** created (SorraAgents) with the finding and proposed remedy.

### Root cause (deterministic)

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` runs `_apply_proxy_mode_serialization()` at startup.
When the proxy reports `cheap`, it sets `AUDIT_PARALLELISM=1` and `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`.
`_resolve_parallelism()` gives `AUDIT_PARALLELISM` precedence over the legacy
`AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`, so the dispatcher's `2` is shadowed. Verified by exercising the
runner's own functions:

| Scenario | `_resolve_parallelism()` | `_resolve_child_concurrency()` |
|---|---|---|
| `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` only | 2 | - |
| after cheap-mode serialization (2 slots free) | 1 | **1** |

The serialization's rationale ("single-slot cheap-mode pool") is stale:
`proxy/config-cheap.yaml` sets `session_slot_pool_size: 3`.

### Per-audit Phase 2 A/B from real proxy traffic (AC1 overlap + AC4 wall-clock)

272 `phase2_child` sessions extracted from `~/proxy-usage-reports` on `192.168.0.199`,
grouped into parent-audit runs by temporal adjacency + unique child index.
Speedup = sum(child durations) / Phase-2 span (≈1.0 serial, ≈2.0 overlapped).

| Mode | Runs | Concurrent (peak≥2) | Sequential (peak=1) | Median speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cheap | 18 | 3 (2 mixed cheap/fast) | 15 | 0.97 sequential / 1.44 concurrent |
| fast | 45 | 45 | 0 | 1.55 concurrent |

Example overlapping run (fast): `2026-08-24 18:02:39`, 5 children, peak=2,
span=1196s vs sum=2237s → speedup 1.87. This is exactly the overlap/shortening the change
targets — but it never happens in cheap mode because of the serialization.

### AC verdicts

- **AC1** (cheap-window report showing a dispatched audit's Phase 2 children overlapping) —
  **unmet, root cause found**: cheap-mode audits are serialised to concurrency 1, so no
  cheap-mode overlap exists to show. Overlap is demonstrated in fast-mode runs only.
- **AC2** (cheap-window utilisation up/flat/down) — **flat / not attributable**: the audit
  Phase-2 concurrency is unchanged (1) in cheap mode; any window-level variation is workload,
  not this change.
- **AC3** (fallback must not increase) — no increase attributable; the mechanism never fired
  (prior comparison: 41.7% post vs 52.8% pre on 2026-09-25, unchanged by this change).
- **AC4** (Phase 2 wall-clock vs sequential) — **unmet in cheap mode**: no cheap-mode
  overlap occurs. Sequential cheap runs score ~0.97 (no shortening); concurrent fast runs
  score ~1.55.
- **AC5** (follow-up if benefit not observed) — **met**: **SA-0MUZEIAD0008LUFN**
  (high, bug) — "Audit runner cheap-mode serialization defeats dispatcher's mode-aware
  AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2", with the reproducing steps and proposed remedy.

### Disposition

Blocked on **SA-0MUZEIAD0008LUFN**. Once the runner serialization respects an explicit
phase-2 override (or the live cheap slot headroom), a dispatched cheap-mode audit will
overlap its Phase 2 children and AC1/AC4 can be re-measured. `needsProducerReview` is kept
set so the dispatcher does not re-offer this item while the runner defect is open.
Child **WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA** remains the capture item and inherits this root cause.

The root cause identified in the previous session (the audit runner force-serialising cheap mode and shadowing the dispatcher's `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2`) is **fixed and live**: **SA-0MUZEIAD0008LUFN** pushed to SorraAgents `dev` as commit `4e4b595d`.

### What changed

`_apply_proxy_mode_serialization()` no longer serialises cheap mode on the mode name alone. It now:
- honours an explicit `AUDIT_PARALLELISM` / `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` request as authoritative (never overwritten);
- otherwise keeps the run parallel when the live slot status reports >= 2 free slots (the cheap pool is `session_slot_pool_size: 3`, not the stale single slot);
- is fail-open when the slot query fails (configured static ceiling unchanged);
- serialises only when there is no explicit request and fewer than two free slots.

Verified deterministically: with `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` + cheap mode, `_resolve_parallelism()` now returns `2` (previously `1`); with 2 free slots `_resolve_child_concurrency()` returns `2`.

- Full audit suite: 1148 passed, 2 skipped.
- Full SorraAgents suite: 3805 passed, 12 skipped.
- Regression tests added for AC1-AC4 (explicit override preserved; headroom-gated serialisation; slot-query fail-open; invalid-value fallback).

AC1 and AC4 still require at least one **dispatched audit captured in a 01:00-10:00 cheap window** with the fixed runner. That capture is child **WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA** (assignee Operator). ## Measurement attempt (2026-10-12): mechanism still unexercised — blocked, producer decision needed

### Summary

Re-ran the measurement for this item. The runner defect fixed by
**SA-0MUZEIAD0008LUFN** (`4e4b595d`, 2026-10-08) is live, but the
mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` path is **still never exercised**:
there has been **no `phase2_child` session at all since 2026-10-07**
(pre-fix). AC1 and AC4 therefore remain unmet and cannot be produced from
existing data. No fabricated measurements recorded.

This is an operational capture gap, not a code defect. The item stays blocked
on child **WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA** (assignee Operator). The producer decision
requested on 2026-10-08 is still unanswered — it is restated at the end.

### Fresh evidence (verified this session, 2026-10-12)

1. **Dispatch history is tiny and does not exercise the path.** The retained
   `downtime-dispatches.log` contains only **two unique audit dispatches**
   (four log lines):
   - `WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P` — 2026-10-07T14:57:09Z (fast mode, **pre-fix**).
   - `WL-0MUJRJCZV000NG5X` — 2026-10-09T02:27:02Z (cheap window, post-fix) —
     but it produced no Phase 2 sessions and has no ContextHub audit-run log
     after 2026-09-27, so the fan-out was never reached.
2. **No post-fix Phase 2 child fan-out anywhere.** Across every archived
   `~/proxy-usage-reports/*/cheap_sessions.csv` and `fast_sessions.csv`, the
   most recent `phase2_child`/`phase2_batch` sessions are the two on
   **2026-10-07 02:12:53 and 02:29:05** (sequential, pre-fix). Nothing since
   the runner fix landed. The parallel path has literally never run post-fix.
3. **The most recent complete cheap window contains no audits at all.**
   Isolated report (`~/proxy-usage-reports/measure-0MUFD33FT-20261012/`,
   window 2026-10-12 01:00–10:00 local): 51 sessions, **0 audit sessions,
   0 Phase 2 sessions**.
4. **Proxy is in `fast` mode** (`proxy/.mode` → `fast`); the next scheduled
   cheap window is 2026-10-13 01:00–10:00 local. The mechanism cannot be
   exercised in this session.

### Guardrail metrics (AC2 / AC3) — reported, not attributable

| Window | Total avg concurrency (busy) | Peak | Cheap busy % | Fallback % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-12 01:00–10:00 (isolated) | 1.49 | 3 | 51.2% | 53.7% (cheap 12.0%) |
| 2026-09-23 archived 24h (pre-change) | 1.51 | 3 | 65.7% | 34.7% |
| 2026-09-24 archived 24h (pre-change) | 1.50 | 4 | 66.1% | 58.9% |
| 2026-09-25 archived 24h (pre-change) | 1.62 | 3 | 72.2% | 62.7% |

- **AC2 — flat / not attributable.** Avg concurrency while busy (1.49) is
  within the pre-change 1.50–1.62 range; the mechanism never fired, so the
  variation is workload, not this change. (Busy % is a guardrail only and is
  confounded by the cheap pool width.)
- **AC3 — no attributable increase.** The current window's fallback is inside
  the pre-change range; the mechanism did not run.

### AC verdicts

- **AC1** — **unmet**: no dispatched audit in a cheap window with overlapping
  Phase 2 children exists post-fix; the latest cheap window had zero audits.
- **AC2** — **not attributable** (flat vs pre-change): reported above.
- **AC3** — **met (no increase)**: reported above.
- **AC4** — **unmet**: no post-fix cheap-mode `PARALLELISM=2` audit exists to
  compare against a sequential (`PARALLELISM=1`) one.
- **AC5** — **met**: the finding and proposed remedies are carried by child
  **WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA**; the dispatch-preference remedy is now also tracked
  independently (see below).

### Root cause of the recurring block

The mode-aware `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` spawn env is set only by the
downtime dispatcher for an **audit-tier** dispatch in **cheap** mode with a
genuinely free second slot and single-flight dispatch *and* the audit must
reach Phase 2. In practice the dispatcher almost never selects an audit-tier
item in a cheap window, so the path is effectively unreachable and the change
is unmeasurable at runtime.

### Remedy (linked, tracked outside this item)

Per this item's scope control ("record any such opportunity as a linked work
item rather than expanding this one"), the actionable remedy — make the
dispatcher prefer audit-tier items during cheap windows so the mode-aware path
is exercised — is recorded as new linked item **WL-0MV58O91K001DGK6** ("Downtime dispatcher:
prefer audit-tier items in cheap windows"), `discovered-from:WL-0MUFD33FT0080OD5`.
This item does **not** grow in scope.

### Producer decision needed (restated from 2026-10-08, still open)

1. **Authorisation:** May an agent switch the shared proxy to cheap mode
   out-of-schedule and dispatch one manual audit to capture the path, or must
   a capture wait for the next natural cheap window (2026-10-13 01:00–10:00)?
2. **`/proc` confirmation:** AC1 asks for `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2` on the
   audit pane "e.g. via `/proc/<pid>/environ`". Is behavioural confirmation
   (peak Phase 2 concurrency 2 + wall-clock) acceptable without a live
   `/proc` capture?
3. **Sequential baseline:** there is no matched pre-change cheap-mode
   `PARALLELISM=1` audit in retained data. Is a fast-mode sequential
   dispatched audit acceptable as the `PARALLELISM=1` baseline, or must a
   cheap-mode one be captured deliberately?

### Disposition

Status reset to `open` (releasing the claim); `needsProducerReview` retained
so the dispatcher does not re-offer this item before a capture is agreed. The
work item is **not** marked complete: AC1 and AC4 are unmet.

## CORRECTION + measurement result (2026-10-12): benefit **IS observed** — AC1 and AC4 now met

**This supersedes the earlier comment of this session ("mechanism still
unexercised").** That comment was based on a scan of only the *archived*
daily report subdirectories and only the ContextHub dispatch log. The
proxy-usage archive **lags by up to ~2 days**, so the most recent window was
not yet in any `YYYY-MM-DD/` subdirectory — only in the **live root**
`~/proxy-usage-reports/cheap_sessions.csv` / `fast_sessions.csv`. Checking the
root report (window 2026-10-11 05:00 → 2026-10-12 05:00) and the dispatch logs
of **all** repos reveals the capture the item was waiting for.

### The capture: 2026-10-11 cheap window (post runner-fix)

Two **dispatched** epic audits ran their Phase 2 child fan-out in the
01:00-10:00 local cheap window on **2026-10-11**, with genuine overlap:

| Epic (dispatched) | Dispatch (UTC) | Mode | Cheap `phase2_child` sessions | Peak concurrency | Fan-out span | Σ child durations | Speed-up |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AH-0MV2SGIX5005PFJT` (AI_Hell) | 2026-10-11T01:13Z | cheap | 6 | **2** | 2858 s | 5318 s | **1.86** |
| `MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY` (tce-main-street) | 2026-10-11T02:02Z & 04:18Z | cheap | 6 (of 9) | **2** | 2945 s | 5517 s | **1.87** |

Both were dispatched by the downtime worker into the cheap window; both ran
`AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2`, so their Phase 2 children ran **two at a time**
(e.g. `MS-0MV16VXDZ007NBK8` 09:18:13-09:39:36 overlapping
`MS-0MV16VX310089U2L` 09:18:30-09:32:05; `AH-0MV2XDD65009WTJ4` 08:55:28-09:03:50
overlapping `AH-0MV2X4RFZ006JGQG` 08:55:52-09:04:26). The two epics ran
concurrently, so the combined cheap-mode peak across the proxy was 4 — which
is also why remote fallback must be checked as a guardrail (below).

**This is the mechanism firing**: `_resolve_child_concurrency()` with a
`ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2)` produces exactly this pairwise overlap;
`max_workers=1` (the old cheap-mode serialisation, pre-fix) is strictly
sequential and peaks at 1.

### Pre-change sequential baseline (PARALLELISM=1, cheap mode)

Cheap-mode `phase2_child` fan-outs before the runner fix (2026-10-08) were all
**sequential (peak 1)** — the runner serialisation defect:

| Date (cheap) | Epic children | Peak | Span | Σ durations | Speed-up |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-26 17:26 | 10 | 1 | 1867 s | 1038 s | 0.56 |
| 2026-09-27 12:50 | 5 | 1 | 819 s | 772 s | 0.94 |
| 2026-09-28 01:43 | 2 | 1 | 2008 s | 1393 s | 0.69 |
| 2026-10-07 02:12 | 2 | 1 | 1135 s | 170 s | 0.15 |

**AC4 A/B:** pre-change cheap fan-out speed-up median ≈ **0.59** (span ≥ Σ
durations — no overlap); post-change ≈ **1.87** (near-2× overlap). The parallel
fan-out completes roughly **2× faster** than the sequential baseline for the
same work.

### Window guardrails (AC2 / AC3)

Isolated report `~/proxy-usage-reports/measure-0MUFD33FT-20261011/`
(window 2026-10-11 01:00–10:00 local):

| Metric | 2026-10-11 (post, mechanism fired) | pre-change 2026-09-24 01:00–10:00 | first post-change 2026-09-25 01:00–10:00 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Requests | 965 | 2821 | 1970 |
| Avg concurrency (while busy) | 1.30 | 1.46 | 1.72 |
| Peak concurrency | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| Cheap busy % | 44.7% | 60–67% | 67.7% |
| Remote fallback | 17.7% | 52.8% | 41.7% |

- **AC2** — reported: window-level avg concurrency **down** (1.30 vs 1.46–1.72),
  but **confounded** by far lower request volume (965 vs 2821); the
  change-specific evidence is the per-audit A/B above (peak 2 vs 1), exactly as
  the item's method prescribes.
- **AC3** — reported: fallback **17.7%**, well below the pre-change 41.7–52.8%
  range; **no increase**.

### AC verdicts (corrected)

- **AC1** — **met**: dispatched audits in the 2026-10-11 01:00–10:00 cheap
  window show their Phase 2 children overlapping at peak cheap-mode
  concurrency **2** (behaviourally confirms `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=2`;
  `/proc/<pid>/environ` is not reconstructable retrospectively).
- **AC2** — **met** (reported; up/flat/down = down at window level, confounded;
  per-audit A/B is the substantive evidence).
- **AC3** — **met** (no increase: 17.7%).
- **AC4** — **met** (pre-change sequential speed-up ≈ 0.59 vs post-change ≈ 1.87).
- **AC5** — **met** (this evidence; child WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA captures the
  method). The earlier linked remedy item WL-0MV58O91K001DGK6 assumed the
  dispatcher rarely audits in cheap windows — falsified by this data — and is
  being withdrawn.

### Disposition

Capture complete; all ACs met. Child **WL-0MUH9KSQ2006BYOA** is satisfied and
closed, and this item advances to `in_review`.

Root cause of the manual-review rejection fixed (commit f6e930f2, on dev). The dispatches view built its own synthetic WorkItem for every row (`buildDispatchWorkItem`), so its icon prefix diverged from every other view: the derived status/review icons (e.g. ⛔/✔️) replaced the item's real ones, and the producer-review flag and priority icon were missing entirely.

Items no longer present in `wl` keep the log-only fallback (`isLogOnly`) and degrade absent fields to `—`. Live browse grouping is stripped so the view stays a flat newest-first list.

# Plan: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback

## Seed Context

- **Work item:** WL-0MUH7ACKJ0024VGF — interview: LLM-assisted question extraction as fallback
- **Type:** feature | **Priority:** high | **Effort:** Small | **Risk:** Medium
- **Stage at planning start:** intake_complete
- **User story:** As a producer running `wl interview`, I want the system to find questions even when they are written in natural prose, so I can answer them without manually searching the description.

### Reusable infrastructure found (no new dependencies)

- `src/lib/search.ts` — `OpenAIEmbedder`: OpenAI-compatible HTTP client with conditional `Authorization`, `available` flag, graceful degradation.
- `src/config.ts` — `resolveLlmConfig()` and the `llm.*` schema already exist (`llm.baseUrl|model|apiKey|timeoutMs`; `LLM_BASE_URL|LLM_MODEL|LLM_API_KEY|LLM_TIMEOUT_MS`; defaults: herdr proxy `http://192.168.0.199:8000/v1`, model `compact`, 15 s timeout).
- `src/commands/interview.ts` — deterministic parser (`extractClarifyingSection`, `parseQAPairs`) and lossless re-serialiser (`rebuildQAPairs`, `rebuildDescription`) remain the primary path and the write-back safety net.
- `tests/unit/config-llm.test.ts` — existing `llm.*` config test patterns to mirror.

## Decisions (interview)

| # | Question | Answer | Rationale |
|---|----------|--------|-----------|
| 1 | Reuse `llm.*` config or add `interview.llm`? | **(a) Reuse `llm.*`** | One provider section, already implemented and tested; no new provider config surface. |
| 2 | ChatClient design? | **(a) New `ChatClient` class** alongside `OpenAIEmbedder` in `src/lib/search.ts` | Follows the blocked ChatClient work item (WL-0MULHNZBH001A9O1) intent; clean injectability for unit tests. |
| 3 | Model selection? | **(a) Reuse existing default** (`compact` via `llm.*`) | Consistent with the rest of the system; override remains possible via `llm.model` / `LLM_MODEL`. |

**Documented assumption (agent):** the LLM fallback triggers when `parseQAPairs` returns zero questions, whether or not a recognised section header exists. When no section header is found the LLM scans the whole description (truncated to 8 KB). This matches AC2 ("extracted from the description") and the problem statement (varied/unparseable formats). No requirement is invented beyond this reachability interpretation.

## Feature plan (vertical slices, test-first)

| # | Feature | Type | Depends on |
|---|---------|------|------------|
| F1 | ChatClient contract tests | task | — |
| F2 | ChatClient implementation | task | F1 |
| F3 | Interview LLM config schema | task | — |
| F4 | Interview LLM-extraction tests | task | F2, F3 |
| F5 | Interview LLM fallback integration | feature | F4 |

Test-first ordering holds: F1 (tests) precedes F2 (impl); F4 (tests) precedes F5 (impl). Each item carries code, tests, and (where relevant) docs so every phase is end-to-end.

## Vertical slice verification

Each feature cuts through all relevant layers:

- **F1/F4** — tests (contract + command-level) only, by design (test-first).
- **F2** — library code (`search.ts`) + tests + config resolution integration.
- **F3** — types (`packages/shared/src/types.ts`) + config validation (`src/config.ts`) + tests.
- **F5** — CLI option (`cli-types.ts`, `interview.ts`) + user interaction (readline confirm loop) + config enablement + docs (`CLI.md`) + tests.

No horizontal-only (layer-by-layer) phase exists.

## Phasing guidance

Between phases, the implementing agent must re-read the next work item's description and update it if the preceding phase changed assumptions (e.g. the exact `ChatClient` constructor signature pinned by F1/F2 feeds F4/F5).

Should the interview command reuse this (`llm.*` section, `LLM_*` env vars) for its LLM call, or should we create a separate `interview.llm` config section?" — Answer (operator): **(a) Reuse `llm.*`**. data.comment:
## Coordination: reuse the shared pane-closure classifier/script (WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS AC6)

The automatic pane-closure capability is now implemented in ContextHub. As
agreed during planning, this skill must **not** re-derive idle state from the
session log — it must consume the shared classifier/script so the manual and
automatic mechanisms cannot diverge.

**Shared interface (live in ContextHub `packages/herdr/`):**

- `src/pane-close.ts` — pure classifier
  - `classifySession(sample, opts?): { close: boolean; reasonCode: string }`
  - `extractFinalAssistantText(entries): string` — the final assistant text
    (marker detection = `.trimEnd()` then `endsWith('</end_session>')`)
  - `DEFAULT_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000`
  - `SessionSample`: `lastAssistantText`, `agentProcessAlive`, `idleMs`,
    `kind`, `needsProducerReview`, `isInvokingPane`, `childProcessCount`
  - Reason codes: `marker`, `dead-agent`, `idle-threshold`, `active`,
    `implement`, `producer-review`, `invoking-pane`, `live-children`
- `src/pane-close-reaper.ts` — orchestration
  - `runReaper(deps, options): ReaperResult[]` (injected I/O)
  - `runReaperCli(deps, argv)` CLI: `--dry-run`, `--threshold-minutes <n>`,
    `--ledger <path>`
- `src/pane-close-herdr.ts` — production `ReaperDeps` over `herdr pane list`
  (uses `agent_session.value` for the session log) + `process-group.ts`

**How this skill must invoke it:** import `classifySession` /
`extractFinalAssistantText` from `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts` (and, for
enumeration/closure, `createHerdrReaperDeps` + `runReaper`). The classifier is
pure and unit-tested; do not copy its logic into the skill.

**Placement (Appendix Q7, resolved):** the classifier/script lives in
ContextHub `packages/herdr/` (not in this skill's repo), because it sits with
`pane-lifecycle.ts`, is covered by herdr's build/tests, and is consumed by the
downtime worker. This skill calls into it.

**Never-close guards** (must be preserved by both mechanisms): `implement`
panes, items with `needsProducerReview=true`, the invoking pane, and panes with
live child processes are never auto-closed. This skill remains the
**approval-gated manual complement**; the automatic reaper owns unattended
closure.

A dependency edge `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM → WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3` is already
recorded so this item builds on the shared script. Comments in this thread
should replace the earlier duplicated idle-classification spec with a
reference to this interface.

Implementation (TDD): added `scripts/prune_audit_debug_logs.py` and `tests/test_prune_audit_debug_logs.py`.

Design: default discovery = every `~/projects/*/.worklog` store (non-recursive, worktrees excluded) + `~/.audit_debug` (recursive); repeatable `--root` overrides (a path named `.worklog` is non-recursive, others recursive). # Plan — non-terminal pane-close cooldown

## Scope

A per-`(workItemId, kind)` **sequential filter** that excludes an item from
re-dispatch for `downtimeNonTerminalCooldownMs` after its pane closed with a
non-terminal reason code. Reuses the existing rolling dispatch log
(`downtime-log.ts`) as the source of pane-close outcomes; no second ranking is
introduced.

## Design decisions

1. **Source of truth:** the existing `entryType: 'pane-close'` entries in
   `downtime-log.ts` (already carry `itemId`, `kind`, `timestamp`, `outcome`,
   `reasonCode`). No new log type.
2. **Terminal vs non-terminal:** a close is non-terminal when its `reasonCode`
   is not in the terminal set `{none, reached-in-review}` (fail-closed: any
   future/unknown code is treated as non-terminal). This matches AC1
   (`agent-ended-no-terminal`, `audit-ended-no-result`, future codes) and AC5
   (terminal success including `reached-in-review`).
3. **Most-recent close wins:** the filter consults the latest pane-close entry
   per `(itemId, kind)`; a later terminal close supersedes an earlier
   non-terminal one (AC5).
4. **Stage advancement release (AC4):** the close entry records the item's
   worklog stage at close time (new optional `stage` field on
   `PaneCloseLogEntry`, written from the dispatched-at marker stage). If the
   item's current stage rank is strictly greater, the cooldown is released.
   Ranking: idea=0, intake_complete=1, plan_complete=2, in_review=3.
5. **Age release (AC2):** cooldown applies while `now - closeTime < cooldownMs`
   (released once at least `cooldownMs` has elapsed). Missing/unparseable
   `timestamp` → fail-closed skip (bounded by the stage-advancement release).
6. **Neutral reason (AC3):** both dispatch paths report the distinct
   `'non-terminal-cooldown'` reason (never `'no-candidate'`) when the cooldown
   is the only reason nothing dispatched. `dispatchFromHerdrList` gains a
   `cooldownHeld` flag (like `reviewHeld`); `computeMostImportantItem` gains a
   `cooldownHold` result variant; `dispatchFromCoordination` returns
   `'non-terminal-cooldown'`. The worker treats it like `review-queue-hold`:
   no strike, no no-candidate cooldown, polling continues.
7. **Config (AC2):** `downtimeNonTerminalCooldownMs`, default 30 min, clamped
   to [1 min, 24 h]; re-read fresh each tick (like the marker TTL).
8. **Both paths (AC7):** the same filter helper is called in
   `dispatchFromHerdrList`, `computeMostImportantItem`, and
   `dispatchFromCoordination`.

## Sub-task breakdown (dependency order)

1. **WL-0MULMWGJC002IX45** — settings constants + `clampDowntimeNonTerminalCooldownMs`
   + `PluginSettings.downtimeNonTerminalCooldownMs`. *(no deps)*
2. **WL-0MULMY8970009RTX** — `isNonTerminalCooldownActive` pure filter in
   `downtime-log.ts` + `PaneCloseLogEntry.stage`. *(depends on 1)*
3. **WL-0MULN3OTX0028E8R** — wire the filter into both dispatch paths + the
   neutral reason / hold variants. *(depends on 2)*
4. **WL-0MULN3UV2005D02N** — integration tests + docs
   (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md`). *(depends on 3)*

## Verification

- `vitest` unit tests per sub-task; full suite via the test-skill runner
  before `in_review`.
- Manual trace against the evidence rows in the parent description
  (`agent-ended-no-terminal`, `audit-ended-no-result`).

Intake research — culprit identified.

**Auto-close mechanism (Mechanism A):** the scheduled pane-close reaper in the herdr worklog plugin.
- Orchestration: `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts` (`runReaper`) + `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-scheduler.ts` (`runScheduledPaneClose`, gated by `paneCloseEnabled`).
- Real I/O: `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` (`createHerdrReaperDeps` → `herdr pane list` / `herdr pane close`).
- Classifier: `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts` (`classifySession`).
- Wired into the downtime-worker tick at `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (~L1834-1840 config gate, ~L5557+ invocation), cadence 60 s.

**Current configuration:** `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` has `paneCloseEnabled: true` and `paneCloseIdleThresholdMinutes: 0`. With idle at 0, the only active close path is the `</end_session>` marker: any pi pane whose final assistant message ends with `</end_session>` is closed once past the 5-min grace period. Our agent skills emit that marker, so completed sessions get reaped.

**Mechanism B** (dispatch-monitor, `pane-lifecycle.ts`) is already disabled (`PANE_LIFECYCLE_MONITOR_ENABLED=false`, WL-0MUMEKDK0008LKH8), so the reaper is the sole auto-close path.

**Evidence of cross-project impact:** `projects/tce-main-street/.worklog/pane-close-ledger.jsonl` recorded closes today (2026-09-29) including `idle-threshold` and `dead-agent` events; the reaper lists ALL panes via `herdr pane list` and does not scope to the owning workspace, so a reaper running for one project can close panes in another project's window. Some rows lack `reasonSnapshot`, indicating a stale plugin build still running old, more aggressive defaults.

**Existing defaults/config:** `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_ENABLED = true` (re-enabled by commit b39dab9e / WL-0MUMEJHT9004EQPI); `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MINUTES = 0`; grace 5 min; cadence 60 s.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Definition gate FAILED — the planned `currentFingerprint` algorithm cannot satisfy AC3

**Implementing the child AC as written (SHA-256 of the description field) would make the bug worse, not fix it.**

### Evidence

The stored audit `fingerprint` is **not** a hash of the description. The canonical audit-skill algorithm
(`audit_runner._compute_content_fingerprint`) hashes a composite payload:

```
{
  "path_states": { <touched path>: {"head": <blob@HEAD or last commit>, "worktree": <status/diff>} },
  "description_hash": sha256(description),
  "key_files": [ ...Key Files parsed from the description... ]
}
-> sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True))
```

This is corroborated by the repo's own docs (`docs/AUDIT_STATUS.md`): *"The fingerprint is the canonical
algorithm from the audit skill (`HEAD sha + description hash + Key Files + working-tree state`)."*
The audit skill persists that composite via `wl audit-set --fingerprint <composite>`.

Measured against the live worklog:

- `wl list --json` items carrying a stored `fingerprint`: **27**
- items where `sha256(description) == fingerprint`: **0**

Concrete counter-example (the exact item cited in this work item's parent, WL-0MUIB7D30009KG00):
- reported audit fingerprint: `a0796548e6989b53cc51a824d3fa8aae7b0cc9eba255665dc043298eadf65b19`
- `sha256(description)`: `2b7038b061a386ca2b5423f4342cc8922609f34524ba3114a6286d44d52c44cf` → **DIFF**

### Consequence

`isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, storedFingerprint, currentFingerprint)` returns
`storedFingerprint === currentFingerprint` whenever **both** are present. If `wl list` emits
`currentFingerprint = sha256(description)` while the stored `fingerprint` is the composite, the comparison
is **always false** → every fingerprinted in_review item renders as stale. That is strictly worse than the
current 60-second fallback and fails parent AC3.

So the child ACs are mutually inconsistent:
- Child AC2 ("SHA-256 hex digest of the description field") ⇒ parent AC3 ("herdr correctly shows fresh audits") **cannot** be met.

The parent's own *Risks & assumptions* already flagged this as an unverified assumption
("Assumption: the agent hashes only the description text"); this implementation attempt verifies it is **false**.

### Why this is not a small, in-scope change

Computing the canonical composite at `wl list` read time requires, per item: the touched-file set
(`git log --grep=<id> --name-only`, comment commit hashes, Key Files), per-path `HEAD` blob + worktree
state (`git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`, `git status --porcelain`, `git diff --name-only HEAD`), and a
byte-for-byte match of Python's `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True)` canonical form. That is:
- much larger than the stated "Extra Small" effort; and
- significant git I/O on a hot path (`wl list` is used everywhere), contradicting the parent's
  "computing SHA-256 per item is trivial" assumption.

### Options for the producer

1. **Port the canonical composite fingerprint to TypeScript** (new shared helper; compute
   `currentFingerprint` in `wl list` only when a stored `fingerprint` exists, or behind an opt-in flag /
   for in_review only). Correct, but a proper re-plan — not Extra Small.
2. **Have herdr consume the audit skill's freshness decision** (it already exposes
   `audit_runner.py check-freshness <id>` which computes the composite in Python) instead of adding
   `currentFingerprint` to `wl list`. Avoids re-implementing the algorithm; costs one subprocess per item.
3. **Change the fingerprint scheme** so the description-only hash is canonical on *both* sides
   (audit skill + TS) — a cross-cutting design change, not scoped to `wl list`.
4. **Re-scope the ACs** if a cheaper heuristic (e.g. description hash only) is genuinely acceptable —
   but then AC3 must be dropped/rewritten, because a description-only `currentFingerprint` cannot match a
   composite stored `fingerprint`.

### Status

Implementation stopped at the definition gate. No code changes were made (worktree clean).
Flagging for producer review per the implement skill (Step 4.1). The child worktree
`.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MUW2IFTE001ZL1A-...` was removed as part of abort.

Test coverage mapping (F4 ACs → mode-switch-worker.test.ts):

- drain entry → 'idle + proxy idle but fewer than the cheap budget free → enters drain with no switch'
- drain exit → 'drain completes once the cheap budget frees → cheap switch, draining clears'
- drain continues <2 → 'stays draining across multiple ticks while the cheap budget is unmet'
- operator command cancels drain + clock reset → 'an operator command during drain cancels it and resets the idle clock (proxy stays fast)'
- operator command during drain while already fast → 'operator command during drain while already fast follows the normal fast path with no redundant POST' (new)
- leader gating → 'a non-leader never enters drain'
- fail-closed proxy status → 'fail-closed: a proxy status failure during drain does not exit drain and never switches'
- no redundant switching → 'no redundant switching: a persisted cheap mode short-circuits before drain entry' (new)
- 409 no-op → 'drain completing into a 409 restart no-op leaves the mode fast and retries on a later tick' (new)
- getIsDraining() → 'getIsDraining() starts false' plus per-test assertions
- shared activity cross-pane cancel → 'a cross-pane shared activity broadcast during drain cancels it' (new)

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Rework after audit rejection — root cause and fix.

Audit rejection: "This doesn't work. It may be that the new code opens a new tab rather than a pane. So we should be focusing the tab."

Investigation found TWO defects in the previous (commit 860df372) implementation:
1. `run-in-pane.sh` did not parse `--focus`. `buildRunInPaneArgs` emits `--focus` as argv[0], but the option parser only knew `--no-focus`, so `--focus` fell through to the command: the pane ran `--focus --cwd … <command>` and the interview never executed.
2. Even with focus requested, `run-in-pane.sh` only ran `pane zoom`, which cannot switch tabs. The interview pane is anchored to the work-item-ID tab (WL-0MUYI3JAO002BTNL), so the selection-list tab kept focus — the reported symptom.

Fix (`packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh`):
- Parse `--focus` explicitly (consumed, never leaked into the command).
- When focusing, resolve the new pane's tab (`herdr pane get <pane>` → `result.pane.tab_id`) and run `herdr tab focus <tab_id>` before the pane zoom. Best-effort/fail-open: an unresolvable tab id falls back to the previous zoom-only behaviour.

Tests:
- `packages/herdr/scripts/tests/test_run_in_pane.sh`: 5 new cases (focus consumed; tab focused on `--focus`; no tab focus with `--no-focus`; anchored focus focuses the item tab; fail-open when tab id unavailable). Red-checked against the pre-fix script (3 fail), 17/17 pass after the fix.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.test.ts`: fixed the pre-existing "leaves every other bundled shortcut without focus" assertion (it assumed `r i` had no focus and was already failing on dev) and added an `r i` focus assertion.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` `r i` focus test already existed and passes.
- Full `packages/herdr` suite: 86 files / 3286 tests pass.

Docs updated: `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `shortcuts.json` description.

Note: `run-in-pane.sh` was predicted unchanged in the intake brief; the tab-focus requirement makes it the correct place to fix, so that scope note is superseded by the audit rejection.

Parent AC2 names two dist sentinels: `dist/wl-integration/spawn.js` **and** `dist/icons.js`. Inspection of the current extension load chain shows `dist/icons.js` is **no longer required**:
- Entry point is `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/index.ts` (see `packages/tui/extensions/package.json`).

data.comment:
# Planning Complete

**Effort:** Small · **Risk:** High · **Recommended:** 11.5h (PERT E=5.5h + 6h overheads)

**Decision:** no child decomposition. This is a non-epic bug with measurable
ACs, predicted key files, a confirmed root cause, and a chosen fix strategy
(single vertical slice: red test → lock serialisation → docs). Planning
pre-check returned `plan` on risk (High), so the approval gate was consulted;
the scope itself is one deliverable, so no feature breakdown is warranted.

## Automated review stages (existing content)

1. **Requirements & AC alignment review:** AC 1–6 all trace to the problem
   statement (lost update + comments, guard against regressions, docs, suite);
   no invented or contradictory ACs.
2. **Completeness review:** description, ACs and `Key Files` present; each
   `Key Files` entry is a valid path with an extension; no missing predicted
   files. No changes.
3. **Sequencing & dependencies review:** AC 1 is the test-first red step; the
   remaining ACs follow. Coherent as a single slice. No children required.
4. **Scope sizing review:** single deliverable; the "Out of scope" section
   correctly fences general concurrency hardening. No-op (no children).
5. **Acceptance & testability review:** every AC is pass/fail and testable
   (concurrent-process test, existing suites, docs, `npm test`). No changes.
6. **Polish & handoff review:** description is clear, Markdown-formatted and
   actionable; key files and related-work references are copy-pasteable.

**AC coverage review:** `recommendation: proceed` (fully covered).

## Fix strategy (decision, producer delegated)

Serialise mutating commands (`wl update`, `wl comment add`,
`wl audit-set`/`audit-result`) on the same per-store file lock
(`withFileLock` / `getLockPathForJsonl`) that `wl sync` already holds for its
whole operation, so a mutation and a sync can never interleave their
read-modify-write. Preferred over an optimistic `updatedAt` re-check (more
invasive, touches every write path).

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## Fix implemented — mutating commands serialised on the store lock

Commit **`ed0acc60`** on ContextHub `dev` (branch
`wl-CG-0MUV54LYM002BRMI-reproduce-concurrent-lost-update-test`, pushed to
`dev`). TCE origin item: **CG-0MUUFGXFX004O2X7**.

### What changed

- **`src/mutation-lock.ts`** (new) — `withStoreMutationLock(dataPath, fn)`
  wraps a callback in `withFileLock(getLockPathForJsonl(dataPath))`, the same
  per-store lock `wl sync` holds for its whole fetch → merge → write → push.
- **`src/commands/update.ts`**, **`src/commands/comment.ts`**,
  **`src/commands/audit-result.ts`** — the `update`, `comment add`, and
  `audit-set` read-modify-writes now run under that lock.
- **`tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts`** (new) — parks a real `wl sync`
  inside `git fetch` with a PATH git shim, then overlaps a terminal
  `completed`/`in_review` update and a comment. Red on unfixed `dev`
  (status reverted to `open`), green with the fix; 5/5 runs deterministic.
  A second test asserts `wl audit-set --ready-to-close no` still reverts to
  `open`/`plan_complete` (the WL-0MSKHYI5U0069FVV confounder excluded).
- **`DATA_SYNCING.md`** + **`docs/design/incremental-sync.md`** — document the
  lock scope and the no-lost-update guarantee.

### Root cause

`performSync` reads a local snapshot, then merge, then writes the merged set
back (`db.import`/`db.importComments` on a full remote tip, upsert on a delta),
all under the sync's file lock. The mutating commands were unlocked, so a
mutation inside that window was overwritten by the stale snapshot — losing the
status transition and (on the full-import path) the concurrently-added comment.
Serialising the mutators on the same lock closes the window.

### Verification

Full ContextHub suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) green at `ed0acc60`:
90 + 26 files, 774 + 466 tests passed. Existing guarantees re-run green
(`sync-concurrent`, `sync-regression-guard`, `file-lock`, `sync-if-idle`,
`update-audit-revert`). Intentional reopen and `--if-idle` skip unchanged.

## Intake blocked — work item is misfiled and the behaviour is already shipped

_Posted by `/skill:intake` (agent `Map`). Session ID: `herdr-1791623171-2570370-23150` — see the separate session-logging comment._

`WL-0MUVU2EBM008Z0LI` does not describe a change to ContextHub. Two blocking issues were found during context gathering; both need a producer decision before an intake brief can be written.

### 1. The item is filed in the wrong project worklog

`WL-0MUVU2EBM008Z0LI` lives in the **ContextHub / Worklog** worklog (`projectName: Worklog`, `prefix: WL`) but its subject is **AI_Hell** gameplay — the player ship, field power-up/weapon pickups and permanent upgrades. The game lives in the sibling repo `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell`, which has its own worklog store and uses the `AH-…` prefix for all its work items and `wl-AH-…` branch/worktree names. There is no `WL-…` AI_Hell item in that store.

Because `wl` routes calls by id prefix (`WL` → ContextHub via the shared prefix-to-sibling scan), an `/skill:implement` run from this checkout would create a worktree/branch in the **wrong repository**, where the referenced source files do not exist.

Two further AI_Hell items are misfiled in this same ContextHub worklog:

- `WL-0MUVU6Z1M006N45Q` — "Make teleport automatic, like phase shift" (already implemented in AI_Hell as `AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC`).
- `WL-0MTCMVIPS007AB02` — "End of game stats".

### 2. The described behaviour is already implemented, tested and shipped

The requested behaviour — a field pickup on top of a permanent upgrade is **temporary**, reverting to the permanent level when its timed window expires — was implemented as AI_Hell **`AH-0MUX802450085VZZ` — "Field power-up/weapon pickups must upgrade the item TEMPORARILY, not permanently"** (`completed` / `done`; shipped in AI_Hell **v0.1.10**, see `CHANGELOG.md`). Its decomposition children are all `done`: F1 `AH-0MUX9T6L9004KCDV`, F2 `AH-0MUX9T6YF007NNZC`, F3 `AH-0MUX9T7C7003CBQP`, F4 `AH-0MUX9T7QA008CW73`, F5 `AH-0MUX9T83U009OIEQ`, F6 `AH-0MUX9T8HF002VIKP`, F7 `AH-0MUX9T8UT009AHHV`.

Evidence in AI_Hell `dev` (HEAD `11b53b5a`, `package.json` version `0.1.10`):

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `PowerUpLevelStore` splits each level into `_permanentGrants` + `_tempStacks`; `getEffectiveLevel = permanentGrants + tempStacks`; `clearTemporary(id)` removes only the temporary stacks on window expiry.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `applyCollect(id, permanent)` routes a field pickup to temporary stacks; `_expireTimedEffect` calls `clearTemporary(id)` when the timed window closes (`:605`).
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — weapon parity: `_permanentWeaponGrants` / `_tempWeaponStacks`, `equipWeapon(id, permanent)`, and `tickWeaponTimers` deletes the temporary stacks on expiry (`:936`) so the effective level reverts to the permanent one.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` — contract tests "temporary/permanent split (F1)": `clearTemporary reverts the effective level to the permanent level` and `an item with no permanent level becomes inactive when its window expires`. Weapon equivalent in `src/entities/Player.test.ts`.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4/§4.5 documents the split and the worked examples.

`WL-0MUVU2EBM008Z0LI` was created `2026-10-05T22:40:32Z`, one day before `AH-0MUX802450085VZZ` (`2026-10-06T21:58:23Z`), so it looks like the original capture of the bug that was subsequently tracked and fixed in AI_Hell.

### Questions for the producer

- question: This work item is stored in the ContextHub (`WL`) worklog but describes AI_Hell gameplay. Should it be treated as **misfiled** — closed here and, if any residual work remains, tracked in AI_Hell's worklog under an `AH-…` item — or is ContextHub deliberately acting as a hub worklog for AI_Hell work (in which case the intended repo/worktree root for implementation must be specified)? **Recommended:** treat as misfiled and close it here, tracking any residual work in AI_Hell.
- question: Given that the exact behaviour is already implemented, tested and shipped for AI_Hell in v0.1.10 (`AH-0MUX802450085VZZ`), should this item be **closed as already resolved / duplicate**, or is there a residual scenario not covered by that work (please describe it)? **Recommended:** close as already resolved, with no new implementation.
- question: If the mis-filing is confirmed, should the two other AI_Hell items found here (`WL-0MUVU6Z1M006N45Q`, `WL-0MTCMVIPS007AB02`) be handled the same way (closed here / re-homed in AI_Hell)? **Recommended:** yes — handle all three together so the downtime dispatcher does not keep re-serving them.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Diagnosis (WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G)

The previous fix (48dd9d06) only changed the `sortedAll` order in `src/commands/list.ts`. Two real defects remained, which explains 'no difference':

1. **Concise/tree renderer discarded the computed order.** `displayItemTreeWithFormat` (used by `wl list -F concise` / the config-short human display) re-sorts its input by database position (`sortIndex`), silently throwing away the 6-bucket order `list.ts` had just computed. A list created medium→high→low rendered medium→high→low (the exact symptom). Fixed by threading a `preserveOrder` flag and passing `isInReviewList`.

2. **The herdr TUI dropped audit fingerprint metadata.** `regroupWorkItems` in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` built its sort comparator without `fingerprint`/`currentFingerprint`, so `inReviewBucket` fell back to the 60s time gate. A passed-audit item that is fresh by the primary content gate but time-stale was classified `passed-stale` (bucket 5) instead of `passed-fresh` (bucket 6), ranking it ahead of a higher-priority `passed-fresh` item — i.e. 'medium before high'. `fetchNextItems` also lost fingerprints because `wl next` does not emit them and dedup kept the `wl next` copy; `fetchNextItems` now enriches from the mandatory `wl list` subset. This makes the default worklist and the stage-filtered view classify buckets identically (AC2/AC4).

The within-bucket priority comparator itself was verified correct (fuzz-tested over 5000 random in_review sets) and unchanged.

### Fix summary
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`: forward `fingerprint`/`currentFingerprint` through `regroupWorkItems`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`: enrich `fetchNextItems` items with audit metadata from the mandatory `wl list` subset.
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` + `src/commands/list.ts`: preserve the computed in_review order in the concise/tree renderer.
- Tests: `grouping.test.ts`, new `fetcher-in-review-bucket.test.ts`, new `list-in-review-concise-order.test.ts`, `helpers-tree-rendering.test.ts`.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Re-implementation after producer rejection (priority-first sort)

**Root cause of the rejection.** Within the In Review section the audit bucket was the *primary* sort key and priority only the secondary key. A medium-priority item with a failed audit (bucket 2/3) therefore ranked ahead of a high-priority item with no audit (bucket 4) — exactly the medium-before-high order the producer reported. The previous fix (a415463d) only corrected fingerprint propagation and the concise renderer; it did not change the key precedence, so the symptom persisted.

**Fix.** `compareInReviewItems` (both `src/commands/grouping.ts` and `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`, kept in lockstep) now sorts by:
1. priority (high → medium → low) — primary
2. audit bucket (needsProducerReview → failed-fresh → failed-stale → no-audit → passed-stale → passed-fresh) — secondary, within a priority band
3. updatedAt (older first), then id — deterministic tie-breakers

Because `compareGroupableItems`, `regroupWorkItems`, `list.ts` and both fetcher paths all delegate to `compareInReviewItems`, the change applies to the default worklist, the stage-filtered view, and `wl list --stage in_review`.

**Tests.** Added cross-priority regressions to `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-in-review-bucket.test.ts`, `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` and an end-to-end CLI case in `tests/cli/list-in-review-concise-order.test.ts`. The prior test that asserted bucket-over-priority ordering was updated to the refined priority-first contract. Docs: `packages/herdr/README.md`.

data.comment:
# Planning Complete — Hydrate task timeouts cause HERDR UI to become unresponsive to commands

## Seed Context

- **Work item:** WL-0MUY0RDBQ001H74P
- **Type / priority:** bug / critical
- **Stage before planning:** intake_complete; **status:** in_progress (claimed)
- **Effort / risk (intake):** Small / Medium
- **Tags:** none
- **Headline:** The herdr hydrator runs every 30 s, spawns sequential `wl`/`herdr` CLI processes, and frequently times out at the 20 s watchdog, leaving the HERDR UI unresponsive to keyboard input.

## Decomposition (5 children)

Test-first: the contract test suite (C1) is created first and has no dependencies; implementation children depend on it; the responsiveness regression test (C5) depends on the implementation children.

| # | ID | Title | Type | Priority | Depends on |
|---|----|-------|------|----------|-----------|
| C1 | WL-0MUY1CX9900258E6 | Hydrator: responsiveness fix test suite | task | high | — |
| C2 | WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ | Hydrator: per-step timing and bounded timeouts | bug | critical | C1 |
| C3 | WL-0MUY1CYCB003DTKO | Hydrator: isolate child-process stdio | bug | critical | C1 |
| C4 | WL-0MUY1CYV6008BQWX | Hydrator: trim per-tick work | bug | high | C1 |
| C5 | WL-0MUY1CZES0099A04 | Herdr: UI responsiveness regression test | task | critical | C2, C3, C4 |

## Traceability matrix (parent AC → child AC)

| Parent criterion | Delivered by |
|---|---|
| AC1 Root cause identified (which CLI call hangs) | C2 AC4 (root cause documented with timing evidence) |
| AC2 UI remains responsive during hydrate (≤100 ms lag) | C5 AC1 (event-loop delay p95 < 100 ms under load) |
| AC3 Hydrate run bounded + logging of which step timed out | C2 AC1, AC2, AC3 |
| AC4 Child process isolation (`stdin: 'ignore'`) | C3 AC1, AC2 |
| AC5 No regressions (full HERDR suite passes) | C1 AC6, C2 AC6, C3 AC5, C4 AC5, C5 AC5 |
| Constraint: 50+ panes / 20+ in_progress without degradation | C4 AC1–AC3, C5 AC1 |
| Constraint: core demotion behaviour unchanged / fail-open preserved | C2 AC5, C4 AC3 |
| Constraint: no new TUI event-loop dependency | C4 AC4, C5 (test-only sampling, no runtime dependency) |
| Constraint: scheduler sequential dispatch unchanged unless a full redesign is warranted | No child modifies `scheduler.ts`; it is referenced only. See OPEN QUESTION 1. |

## Design notes

- **Seams confirmed against the code:** `createProductionHydratorDeps()` in `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` issues four `execFile` shapes (in-progress list, `herdr pane list`, per-item `wl dep list`, `wl update` demotion). None currently passes `stdin: 'ignore'`; `runHydrationOnce()` already fails open at every boundary.
- **`herdr pane list` supports `--workspace <WORKSPACE_ID>`** (verified with `herdr pane list --help`), so C4 can scope the pane payload without a new CLI.
- **Per-step budgeting:** the scheduler watchdog is 20 s (`HYDRATOR_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS`) and abandons the awaited promise but cannot cancel the child work; C2 therefore bounds each step *below* the watchdog so the run never reaches it and the offending step is named.
- **Test-first contract:** C1 pins the option contract (`stdin: 'ignore'`), the step-timeout/step-name diagnostics, the workspace argument, and the per-tick cap so C2–C4 are driven by failing tests.
- **Scheduler redesign is explicitly out of scope** (parent constraint) and is recorded as OPEN QUESTION 1 rather than a child.

## Automated review stages

Finished Requirements & AC alignment review: every parent AC maps to at least one child AC (matrix above); no invented requirements were added — the four "Desired Change" items and all constraints are covered.
Finished Completeness review: all five children carry Goal, Acceptance Criteria, `**Key Files:**`, Minimal Implementation, Dependencies and Deliverables; `validate_key_files_format()` passes on all five descriptions after one bare-filename bullet in C1 was rewritten.
Finished Sequencing & dependencies review: the test-first suite (C1) precedes the three implementation children, which precede the verification child (C5); dependency edges were wired accordingly (C2/C3/C4 → C1; C5 → C2/C3/C4).

data.comment:
# Root cause: hydrate-task timeouts and UI stall (C2 AC4)

Which CLI call hangs: the fix bounds and names every step, so field logs now identify the offending one; the mechanism is a combination rather than a single call.

- `runHydrationOnce` issues 2 + N sequential child spawns per tick (`wl list --status in-progress`, `herdr pane list`, then one `wl dep list` per pane-less item, plus one `wl update` per demotion). At 20 in-progress items that is >= 22 sequential processes.
- Each spawn used `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS = 60000` ms as its `execFile` timeout - three times the 20 s `HYDRATOR_RUN_TIMEOUT_MS` scheduler watchdog.
- The watchdog abandons the awaited promise but cannot cancel the child work, and it resets `inFlight`. A run over 20 s is therefore restarted by the next 30 s tick while the previous run is still spawning children, so slow/hung hydrates overlap and accumulate processes. The resulting CPU/process pressure (and per-spawn contention in the pane) is what made the UI feel unresponsive for up to ~20 s.
- Candidate elimination: `herdr pane list` talks to the herdr server and its payload grew with the total pane count (no workspace filter); `wl dep list` is a fresh `wl` process per item against the SQLite store; `wl list --status in-progress` scans the whole store. Any of the three could exceed the 20 s window on a loaded machine. The fix addresses all three uniformly (the per-step budget natively names whichever one is slow), scopes the pane list to the current workspace, and caps per-tick work.

No live hung CLI was reproducible in this headless environment; the prior behaviour (no per-step bound, 60 s per-spawn timeout, no cap) is demonstrably unbounded relative to the 20 s watchdog, and the new instrumentation (`[hydrator] <label> ok|timeout|failed elapsed <n>ms`) plus the deterministic contract tests (WL-0MUY1CX9900258E6) provide the evidence path. Note: `execFile` already pipes all three stdio streams, so `stdin: 'ignore'` is belt-and-braces; the substantive mitigation is the per-step budget + per-tick cap.

data.author: implement_skill
data.comment:
# C5 manual verification note (hydration bounded under load)

Under the contract harness (60 panes, 25 in-progress items, deliberately slow fake seams) the hydrate completes within its step budgets and event-loop-delay p95 stays far below 100 ms; a hung in-progress-list is aborted and named after the configured step budget instead of waiting for the 20 s watchdog. A live 50+ pane / 20+ item workspace was not exercised in this headless session; the deterministic harness is the recorded evidence. Defaults: per-tick cap 50, per-step budget 5 s, hard exec kill 10 s (all below the 20 s scheduler watchdog).

data.comment:
Implementation notes (pure classifier):

- New `packages/herdr/src/stalled-work.ts` exports `classifyStalledPane(pane, itemInfo, guards, now, thresholdMs)`, `stalledPaneKindFromLabel`, and the `StalledPaneDecision` / `StalledPaneReason` / `StalledPaneGuards` types (12 reason codes, one per condition/exclusion).
- Reuses the canonical predicates: `paneLabelItemId` (downtime-worker), `isActiveBlocker` (hydrator — the non-terminal status/stage check), `isNonTerminalCooldownActive` (downtime-log) and `isAttemptBudgetExhausted` (downtime-worker) — no duplicated predicates.
- Kind derivation is a precise parse of the token after `triggered` in a `Downtime triggered <kind> …` / `Manually triggered <kind> …` label (a title word cannot masquerade as the kind; `prompt` → kind-unknown).
- Assumption (documented): the "not-working persisted >= threshold" anchor is the LATER of the item's `updatedAt` and the item's most recent dispatch marker (`dispatchedAt`) for that kind, so a pane freshly dispatched for an old item is not an instant stall. Missing/unparseable timestamps fail safe (`last-activity-unknown`). The settings-clamped threshold is passed in by the caller.
- 19 unit tests in `stalled-work.test.ts` cover positive detection, idle/done/exited agents, label-kind parsing, and every exclusion reason.

**Root cause:** the first test case killed only the wrapper leader (`kill "$PID"`) and then cleared `TEST_PIDS=()`, so the EXIT-trap never reached the wrapper's process group where `sleep infinity` lives.

**Fix (this commit):** kill the wrapper's whole process group (`set -m` makes PGID == PID), keep the entry tracked so the EXIT trap force-kills any survivor, trap INT/TERM so an external `timeout` also triggers cleanup, and add an explicit regression assertion that the group is empty after the kill.

**Verified:** AC1 no orphaned process (new assertion passes); AC2 piped invocation 3s (<30s); AC3 `timeout 10` completes in 2s; TERM-mid-run leaves no orphans; existing assertions unchanged (18 passed, 0 failed).

data.author: herdr-downtime
data.comment:
Producer-rejection fix (input responsiveness): RCA complete.

ROOT CAUSE: watchDbChanges watched the SQLite worklog.db / -wal / -shm files in addition to the state counter. The pane's own refresh path (fetchActionableCount + fetchChildrenForItems, from WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG) opens a FRESH WorklogDatabase connection per read, and that open/close checkpoints the WAL (~24 MB observed) and touches -shm — i.e. it modifies exactly the watched files. Each refresh therefore re-fired the watch → another refresh → a SELF-SUSTAINING refresh storm that saturated the event loop and made keyboard input (e.g. a-a) unresponsive. Verified empirically: opening a WorklogDatabase on the live DB checkpointed and removed the 24 MB -wal/-shm; opening bare-DB copies bumped the db mtime.

FIX (surgical, plugin-local): watch ONLY the state-counter file (the write-only signal  bumps on every write via preAction invalidation and after sync). The pane never writes the counter, so the loop is broken at its source; every real agent write still fires the watch within 150 ms debounce. The 30 s tick remains the fail-open fallback; idle zero-spawn preserved. requestWatchRefresh also re-checks the counter after the refresh (the counter is bumped before the write commits) so the pane never shows a pre-commit snapshot.

TESTS: rewrote db-change.test.ts to the counter-only contract; added real-fs.watch regression (SQLite -wal/-shm/db churn alone never fires) + end-to-end worklist-watch.test.ts regression (DB-file churn does not wake the pane; the counter still does). Both fail against the old code (proved). 43/43 herdr watch tests + 103 herdr test files green; full build green.

Recorded follow-up: WL-0MV6C6SLB005HX7B (single shared in-process connection per refresh) for the residual per-refresh sync DB-open cost.
