data.comment:
**Full breakdown of what the code currently does (producer request 2026-10-17 18:02:31) — verified against the live system.**

## 1. The two consumers of the pane signal

**A. Hydrator (self-healing demotion)** — `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`
- Every 30 s (`HYDRATOR_INTERVAL_MS`) the worklist's `hydrate` scheduler task runs `runHydrationOnce` via `createHydratorRunner`, gated by pane visibility (zero spawns while hidden) and re-invoked immediately on hidden→visible focus-resume.
- Steps, each under a 5 s soft budget (`runStep`): `wl list --status in-progress --json` → `herdr pane list --workspace <HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID>` → per unmatched item `wl dep list <id>` (+ `wl show` per edge for stage) → `wl update --status/--stage` for the demotion.
- Active signal: `isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes, workspaceId)` = `collectPaneWorkItemIds(...)` — a pane whose `label` CONTAINS the exact work-item ID token (regex `[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9A-Z]{6,}`, e.g. `Manually triggered implement Herdr se… - WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ`), scoped to the current workspace.
- Demotion rules (`decideDemotion`): matched pane → untouched; else in_review→`completed`/`in_review`; active outbound blocker→`blocked`; else→`open`/`intake_complete`. Fail-open: any step timeout/error aborts the cycle WITHOUT demoting.
- Production `listActivePanes` runs `herdr pane list [--workspace <id>]` and reuses the shared `parseMachinePaneListOutput` (dispatcher-anchor.ts) which reads `label`/`title` per pane.

**B. Selection-list marker (display)** — `worklist.ts` + `index.ts` + `hydrator.ts`
- `applyActivePaneMarkers(items, listActivePanes, workspaceId)` fetches the workspace panes and `markItemsActiveByPane` stamps `status='in-progress'` on every item whose ID matches a pane title — even when the worklog status is still `open` — so the list reflects pane existence directly. Terminal (`in_review`/`completed`) items are left untouched.
- Applied at: initial render, every `doRefresh` (DB-change gated), every 30 s `active-pane-marker` scheduler task, and hidden→visible focus-resume (`refreshPaneMarkers` — also invoked by the resume-poll). The marker keeps each item's true status in a non-enumerable Symbol and restores it on each re-pass, so a closed pane clears the marker without a `wl` re-fetch.

## 2. Wiring (production)

- Plugin runs `npx tsx src/start.ts` → **source directly (tsx), NOT `dist/`**. Env verified live on the running Work Items pane: `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID=w45`, `HERDR_PANE_ID=w45:pDE`.
- `index.ts` creates `hydratorDeps = createProductionHydratorDeps()` and `hydratorWorkspaceId = process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID ?? undefined`, and injects `applyActivePaneMarkers(items, hydratorDeps.listActivePanes, hydratorWorkspaceId)` into the worklist.
- Every dispatch path titles panes with the ID as a preserved trailing suffix (`pane-title.ts`: `buildManuallyTriggeredPaneTitle`, `buildDowntimePaneTitle`, `buildShellPaneTitle` → `truncatePaneTitlePreservingSuffix`). Verified on live `herdr pane list`.

## 3. Live verification (this session, workspace w45, herdr 0.9.5)

- `herdr pane list --workspace w45` → 4 panes; `parseMachinePaneListOutput` parses all 4; extracted IDs: WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U, WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ, WL-0MVBMLY2Z0032CYR.
- `createProductionHydratorDeps().listActivePanes('w45')` → 4 panes; `collectPaneWorkItemIds` contains all three current in-progress items.
- `runHydrationOnce(productionDeps, 'w45')` → `{ok:true, considered:3, demoted:0, skipped:3}` — every in-progress item has a matching pane, zero demotions (correct).
- Selection-list capture (`herdr pane read` on the live Work Items pane): WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ / WL-0MVBMLY2Z0032CYR / WL-0MV5MYBKJ0033P8U all shown in Groups 1–3 with the in-progress icon, consistent with their open panes.

## 4. Evidence pointing at the break (review window 17:58–18:02)

- The hydrator log shows TWO consecutive `demotion-apply` **timeouts** at 17:58:53 and 17:59:16 (`wl update` exceeded the 5 s step budget — heavily contended `.worklog` writes; `sync.log` is 23 MB + a 105 MB rotation): `[hydrator] demotion-apply timeout elapsed 5001ms`. A demotion timeout ABORTS the whole cycle (fail-open by design), so a stale `in-progress` item with no pane survived through the producer's review at 18:02:31.
- At 18:02:31 the item WL-0MV1BWETT005GSUJ had been `in-progress` for ~17 h (last session ended 2026-10-16 23:52) and — per pane-session timestamps — had NO live pane until the manual re-dispatch at 18:02:34–35. Under the simple pane rule it should have been demoted within one 30 s cadence; the failed `wl update` writes kept it visible as in-progress.
- The w45 "Context Hub" Work Items pane (the view the producer was most likely reviewing) restarted at 18:59 — **after** the review. Any pane open in w45 before that was a process started earlier; tsx loads the code at process start, so a pre-rework process would still be running the rejected TAB-label-matching hydrator (which treats a persistent item-ID **tab** — created at first dispatch and never removed — as "busy", so a closed agent pane never clears the marker). The rework (commit 2a494532, pane-title matching) deployed 2026-10-17 00:39; the other workspace panes restarted 12:32.

## 5. Secondary hygiene finding

- `packages/herdr/dist/` is **stale (2026-10-13)** vs `src/` (2026-10-17): `dist/hydrator.js` still contains the old tab-matching code (`hasItemTab`/`listTabs`) and zero `pane list`/`listActivePanes` references. The worklist pane does not use `dist/` (it runs `tsx src/start.ts`), but the finish step's `npm run build` rebuild has not produced a fresh artifact since before the rework, so any `dist/` consumer (e.g. `worklog-pane-close` bin, `--no-pane` headless paths) is running pre-rework code, and the repo's build output no longer matches source.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
Implementation summary (WL-0MV5638ZS005I5XQ)

**Change:** Added a machine-wide model-cooldown gate to `mode-switch-worker.tick()`. After the leader/proxy-idle gates and before `GET /admin/mode`, the worker reads `readModelCooldowns(coordinationDir, now())` (shared contract WL-0MV563825002R9Y1). While any entry has `cooldownUntil > now` it returns early, holding the proxy fast; the reader returns only active entries, so the hold is bounded by `cooldownUntil` with no latch.

**Decisions/assumptions:**
- Fail-closed: a `null` reader result (unreadable/corrupt signal, unresolvable dir) holds fast and logs the hold. A *missing* file is `[]` (nothing recorded) and does not suppress the switch.
- The gate is skipped when `coordinationDir` is `undefined` (legacy/test default). Production always passes a dir (`index.ts`: `getMachineCoordinationDir() ?? join(targetCwd, '.worklog')`), so production still fail-closes; gating on a defined dir preserves the existing shared-activity/legacy tests.
- Fast path untouched: `onOperatorCommand` never reads the cooldown signal.
- No client drain reintroduced: no slot-count completion gate, no dispatch pause, no unbounded latch.

**Tests:** unit matrix in `mode-switch-worker.test.ts` (active -> hold, expired -> cheap, absent -> cheap, unreadable/corrupt -> fail-closed, no-latch expiry -> cheap, fast-on-command -> fast) and a cross-root integration test in `mode-switch-integration.test.ts` (one machine dir, two roots; a marker for root A suppresses root B's switch, and clearing it resumes the switch). Docs updated in `docs/design/mode-switch-worker.md`.

**Verification:** herdr typecheck clean; `npm run build` clean; 22 test files / 619 tests pass (mode-switch-worker, mode-switch-integration, tests/herdr).

data.comment:
Baseline + verification (WL-0MV563AU2007FM56).

## Regression guard
`packages/herdr/src/drain-regression-guard.test.ts` (3 tests) proves the withdrawn client-side drain (WL-0MUWIHUL2000JEFR) is not reintroduced, behaviourally through the public worker API:
1. No slot-count completion gate — a 3-slot pool with 1 free slot still switches to cheap (the withdrawn `MODE_SWITCH_DRAIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` gate is gone; `MODE_SWITCH_DRAIN_FREE_SLOTS` is no longer exported and the worker exposes no `getIsDraining`).
2. No dispatch pause — a legacy `drainPaused: true` worker config is inert; the worker still dispatches a new pane.
3. No unbounded latch — the cooldown hold ends exactly at `cooldownUntil`.

## AC6 coverage (detection / gating / wake / cross-root / failure paths)
- Detection (exhaustion classification): `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/retry-loop.test.ts` (`recordExhaustionCooldown`: exhaustion writes; plain 5xx and timeout do not) and `model-cooldown-wiring.test.ts` (register-recovery wiring records/clears).
- Gating (cheap-switch hold): `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` `model-cooldown gate` (active hold; expired; absent/empty; unreadable fail-closed + logged; no-latch; fast-on-command unaffected).
- Wake (bounded resume): `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` `bounded model-cooldown wake` (at most ONE due job; earlier failure still one; no new pane).
- Cross-root (two-root integration): `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-integration.test.ts` `cross-root model-cooldown gate (AC4)`.
- Failure paths: unreadable signal (mode-switch-worker gate, fail-closed), unwritable marker (`recordExhaustionCooldown` never throws / returns false), absent Retry-After (bounded default in `resolveRetryDelay`).
- Contract: `packages/shared/src/model-cooldown.test.ts` (34 tests).

Cooldown-related suites run green: 8 files, 304 tests passed.

## AC8 full-suite + baseline
`npm --silent test` (full vitest, `dist/` built):
- Before: 374 files (373 passed / 1 skipped), 8009 tests (8004 passed / 5 skipped), vitest 256.88 s.
- After: 375 files (374 passed / 1 skipped), 8012 tests (8007 passed / 5 skipped), vitest 240.13 s.
- Both green; +3 tests = the regression guard.

Baseline recorded in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` and on the parent WL-0MV54ZP3Y00514Y9.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Manual verification note (WL-0MV5CBQ6L005SPAG) — cold default-view refresh.

Benchmark: `npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts` (1000 root items, 20 expanded parents x 3 children, 2 iterations). Run as an A/B against the same harness at HEAD (5ff1372d) under identical machine load (load average ~45-48 on 16 cores), alternating runs:

- baseline (before): cold 4931 / 5663 / 2329 ms, 25 `wl` spawns, withinTarget=false
- consolidated (after): cold 1402 / 502 / 1551 ms, 3 `wl` spawns, withinTarget=true

Spawn count 25 -> 3 (-88%): one `wl next` + two mandatory-subset `wl list` queries. The review-queue state is deduplicated against the mandatory in_review subset, and the actionable count plus expanded-children reads are served in-process from SQLite. Worst measured cold refresh on the loaded host was 1.55 s (<= 2 s target); the deterministic regression guard is the spawn count.

Semantics: the mandatory critical/in_review subsets stay on the `wl` spawn path so the CLI's git-based `currentFingerprint` audit-freshness enrichment is preserved exactly; the in-process children fast path falls back to `wl list --parent` whenever a matched child carries a stored audit fingerprint (audit dispatch is root-only, so this is rare). A fresh WorklogDatabase handle is opened and closed per read, so no stale cache can be served across a refresh.

  spies, poll `callback`, and redundant query-call assertions already proven

Analysis recorded 2026-10-14T12:05:01Z (pi session herdr-1791969498-1560777-27505).

## Verdict on the claimed intent (CONFIRMED)
The status flip to in_progress is the CAS token from WL-0MSRDEWES0059TZN (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT design point 1): `wl update <id> --status in_progress --if-status <expected> --if-stage <expected>` runs in one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction so exactly one concurrent pane wins. Double-dispatch prevention is its only scheduling purpose. Nothing downstream reads the assignee to make decisions.

## Option A (status-neutral claim via --if-assignee) side-effect analysis
Option A adds --if-assignee to wl update and makes the audit-tier claim write assignee only (keep completed/in_review), CAS-guarded on --if-assignee ''.

CRITICAL problems found:
1. Audit runner success path never clears assignee — audit_runner.py 'yes' verdict sets completed/in_review + needs-producer-review but NO --assignee "". Every herdr-dispatched audit leaves assignee=Map behind. Live DB: 698 items assignee=Map completed/done; 7 in_review items carry an assignee. Under Option A's --if-assignee "" guard those become permanently unclaimable -> review queue stops draining.
2. rollbackClaimWorkItem does not clear assignee either — a failed dispatch strands assignee=Map with the guard failing forever.
3. Sync regression guard fights clearing — assignee is a merge-participating field; 'Map'->'' is refused on other roots without --accept-regressions, so cleared claims resurrect cross-instance (incl. cross-root coordination offers).
4. Every non-empty assignee becomes a dispatch blocker — intake --assignee, implement claims, triage 'set assignee', delegate @github-copilot would all suppress future auto-dispatch unless every session end clears the field.

NON-issues (verified): active-audit serialisation survives (audit runner itself sets in_progress on entry); the pre-flight --force workaround disappears (net improvement); dispatch-log marker exclusion still prevents re-selection.

## New capability enabled by Option A
--if-assignee '' guard means ANY item with a non-empty assignee fails the claim stale at every tier -> assign-to-producer becomes a per-item pause switch for automatic scheduling (@user idea). Requires assignee-clearing discipline across all skills.

## Simpler alternative
Client-side assignee exclusion in the select* functions (mirror the needsProducerReview filter at downtime-worker.ts:6994/3475) instead of a CAS change: zero residue risk, no rollback/sync changes.

## Flag for scheduling hold found
needsProducerReview (migration 20260210-add-needsProducerReview) already blocks auto-dispatch at every tier AND gates release (ship skill check-final-validation.js). Epic WL-0MV7W77AY005MGBL-OptionA will REMOVE this column from the database and replace it with the assignee-based hold.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
**Decision (epic Q1) recorded.** Accepted answer: option (a) — treat `assignee` as a normal, non-regression-guarded merge field so `''` clears propagate cross-root. Rationale: `assignee` is a scheduling hold (assign = hold from auto-dispatch, clear = release); the status-neutral claim (epic Option A) only works if a cleared assignee propagates so the item is re-selectable everywhere. A regression-guarded assignee resurrects stale claims across roots/panes and forces `--accept-regressions` noise on every sync.

**Implementation (src/sync.ts):** removed `assignee` from both `mergeParticipatingFields` lists and added `isEmptyMeaningfulField()` so empty is never treated as an absent/default merge value for `assignee` — empty-vs-non-empty resolves last-writer-wins by `updatedAt` (deterministic tie-break at equal timestamps). `isRegressionDefault` no longer reports `''` as an assignee regression. status/stage/priority regression protection unchanged.

**Tests:** unit coverage in `tests/sync-regression-guard.test.ts` (new Q1(a) block incl. no-weakening assertion for status/stage/priority); end-to-end cross-root coverage in `tests/cli/sync-assignee-clear.test.ts` (two worklog roots, real `wl sync`, remote clear propagates without `--accept-regressions`, stale remote clear does not clobber a newer local hold, status regression still refused).

**Docs:** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` cross-root `assignee` merge rule section; parent epic Appendix Q1 updated to ACCEPTED (a) with a comment on the epic.

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Implementation decisions (Map):

1. `fetchBlockersForItem(id)` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` runs `wl dep list <id> --json`, parses via the shared `parseDepListBlockersOutput()`, enriches each non-terminal edge with its target `stage` via `wl show` (mirroring the hydrator's `listOutboundDeps`), and filters with the shared `isActiveBlocker()`. Fail-open: any failure yields `[]`.
2. Blockers are resolved for the SELECTED item only, cached by item ID in `runWorklistTui`, invalidated on each list refresh; the render path is non-blocking and skips synthetic `isLogDerived`/`isLogOnly` rows.
3. `formatMetadataPanel()` gained a trailing `blockedBy` parameter and appends one `Blocked By  <id> — <title>` row per active blocker (bare ID when the title is empty) after the metadata rows and before the description preview. The detail view is untouched.
4. Discovered pre-existing bug: the `m`/`M` metadata-panel scroll clamp was a no-op because `formatMetadataPanel` always returns exactly `panelRows` padded lines, so `maxScroll` was always 0. The AC requires scrolling to keep working with the extra rows, so extracted `buildMetadataPanelLines()` + `metadataPanelContentHeight()` and clamped against the UNPADDED content height. Test coverage added for this.

## Intake blocked — producer input required

The seed brief ("Whenever the selection list in herdr gets focus it should refresh the view") overlaps almost entirely with **already-completed** work. Research summary:

Code: `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`onPaneFocused` → `doRefresh(true)`; `resume-poll` task).
- **Tab-focus visibility gating is implemented**: `WL-0MSJNJPRM009RM35` / `WL-0MSKUAT5D00443GA` (`visibility.ts` — `HERDR_TAB_ID` + `herdr tab get` → `result.tab.focused`).

So the requested capability appears to already exist. I need to know the **residual gap** before drafting a brief.

### Q1 — Which focus transition is actually in scope?

- **A.** Tab regains focus (hidden → visible) — already implemented and verified.
- **B.** The list pane regains **keyboard** focus inside an **already-visible** tab (multi-pane split: click / focus the list pane while the tab stayed focused). Today this relies on the `pane_focused` event; the `resume-poll` fallback is tab-level only, so if events are unavailable no refresh occurs.
- **C.** Both, including the reliability of the event path (see Q3).

**Recommended:** **B** — because A is already shipped; the only plausible residual gap is pane-level focus within a visible tab when the event path is not delivering.

### Q2 — Is this a defect report or a net-new requirement?

- **B.** Requirement — codify "refresh on focus" (may be satisfied by the completed items above; then close/relate rather than re-implement).

**Recommended:** **A with a repro** — since the implementation exists, a concrete repro is the only way to identify the residual gap. If no repro exists, **B** with an explicit residual-gap statement is next best.

`~/.config/herdr/herdr-server.log` shows `events.subscribe` requests completing with `outcome="stream_closed"` and reconnecting on an ~10 s cadence (`sub-100` … `sub-115` at 2026-10-16T07:15–07:17, matching `MAX_RECONNECT_DELAY_MS = 10_000` in `packages/herdr/src/events.ts`). data.author: Map
data.comment:
## Diagnosis (AC4) — root cause of the repeated `stream_closed` completions

Live read-only probes against the herdr 0.9.5 Unix socket (`~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`) established the server's real contract:

1. **An idle subscription never closes.** A single `events.subscribe` held open for 40 s+ delivered real `pane_focused` events and was never closed — there is **no server idle-timeout** and **no keepalive requirement**.
2. **The server accepts exactly ONE request per connection.** A second frame on an established subscription socket — a second `events.subscribe`, a `ping`, or even `pane.list` — makes the server **reset** the connection (~100 ms), logged as `events.subscribe … outcome="stream_closed"`.
3. **`ping` is a fresh-connection method** (returns `{result:{type:pong,…}}`); a second ping on the same connection is rejected. It is not a stream keepalive.

**Root cause:** `events.ts` resent `events.subscribe` on the live subscription socket (`resendSubscribeRequest`, from `addPaneSubscription`/`removePaneSubscription`). That second request triggered (2). The worklist's startup `syncPaneSubscriptions` re-added panes after each reconnect, killing the fresh connection again — the ratcheting ~10 s loop (`sub-100`…`sub-115`) in the server log. A local reproduction against the live socket confirmed it (health ratcheted to `attempt:8, delayMs:10000`).

**Fix (client-side only, no herdr changes):** every subscription connection is now write-once. Pane-set changes re-establish a **fresh** connection whose single initial request carries the complete set (`restartSubscription`), with `subscriptionVersion` + a single-flight promise coalescing batched/mid-reconnect changes into one rebuild. Backoff resets on every successful subscribe. A new `onReconnected` callback lets `worklist.ts` restore the event path (and stop the resume-poll fallback) after a stream loss; `onError` re-enables the resume-poll fallback while the stream is down.

Post-fix live reproduction: `addPaneSubscription` returns `subscribed`, health stays `active` (paneCount 1→2), no reconnect. Details: `docs/dev/herdr-events-subscribe-reliability.md`.

**Test-suite note:** the canonical runner (`.pi/test-config.json`) covers only `tests/cli` + `tests/unit`; the `packages/herdr` suite (run for AC6/AC8) is `npx vitest run packages/herdr` — 109 files / 3528 tests pass. data.author: Map
data.comment:
**Intake OPEN QUESTIONS (interactive interview round 1)** — Research findings from `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` and `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`:

- The tick resets the idle tracker after EVERY successful dispatch ("require a fresh full idle period before the next dispatch") and the host-wide active-audit marker (WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA) blocks a second audit while one runs. The audit skill's batch drain (SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5) already processes up to `AUDIT_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS` (5) per `batch` run, but herdr seeds a single-item `issue`.
- Production path is coordination mode: the leader dispatches at most one offer from the shared file per tick; each idle instance offers at most one item.

**Q1 (mechanism).** How should "more than one audit per window" work?
(A) Keep exactly one active audit; when depth ≥ threshold, skip the fresh-idle-period reset so the next audit dispatches as soon as the previous audit pane closes and slots are idle again (sequential drain inside a continuous idle window). **Recommended: (A)** — it preserves active-audit single-flight and the host-wide slot, and needs no SorraAgents change.
(B) Dispatch N audit panes in the same tick (relax the host-wide marker for same-batch items; audits serialise only at the runner admission queue).
(C) Keep one dispatch, but have herdr seed the audit skill batch queue with N in_review ids (requires a SorraAgents/audit-skill change, not just herdr).

**Q2 (threshold).** Reuse the existing `browseItemCount` "deep review queue" threshold (`readReviewQueueGate`) as the depth signal, or add a dedicated `downtimeAuditBatchThreshold` setting? **Recommended:** reuse `browseItemCount` (one source of truth for "deep") and add only a small cap (`DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX`, default 2) on audits per window.

**Q3 (second target source).** In coordination mode the leader may see only ONE audit offer. Where should the extra audit target(s) come from? (A) leader re-reads its own Herdr head after the first dispatch (extend the existing own-backlog fallback) — **Recommended**; (B) ask each instance to offer more than one item; (C) apply depth-aware batching to the direct `dispatchDowntimeWork` path only.

These are material to the implementation shape; answers will be recorded in the intake Appendix.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
### Changes made (AC3 triage / AC4 redundancy / AC5 python)

**Root cause.** Per-spawn `tsx` transpilation, not slow test logic. Verified:
`node <precompiled cli>` = **1.1–1.6 s** vs `tsx src/cli.ts` = **2.5–8.0 s**
for the same invocation. Tests that need real process isolation therefore paid
a 5× tax per spawn, and that tax scales with host load (2.81 s idle → 8.0 s at
load 10), which is the source of the 486 → 730 s run-to-run swing.

#### 1. New test helper — `tests/cli/cli-bundle.ts`

Builds `src/cli.ts` **once per test process** with esbuild (the transpiler tsx
already uses) into `.worklog/test-cli-bundles/<pid>/app/src/cli.mjs`, then
tests spawn `node <bundle>` instead of `tsx src/cli.ts`.

- **Behaviourally identical:** same entry file, same command graph, only
  pre-compiled. npm/workspace packages stay external, so `better-sqlite3` and
  `@worklog/shared` resolve exactly as from `src/`.
- **Layout mirrors the repo** (`<dir>/app/src/cli.mjs` + symlinked
  `templates/`, `examples/`, `package.json`), because `src/` derives the
  package root from `import.meta.url`/`../..`; verified that `init` still
  installs the AGENTS template, the example stats plugin and
  `scheduled-prompts.json`.
- **Per-process directory** — parallel vitest workers must not write one
  shared output file (a shared outfile produced truncated bundles and 16
  spurious failures during development).
- **Fail-soft:** if esbuild is unresolvable or the build fails, every helper
  falls back to the original `[node, tsx, src/cli.ts]` invocation (speed lost,
  correctness never).

#### 2. Call sites converted

| Test file | Before | After | Was |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` | 203.2 s | 83.8 s | 60 tsx spawns → 60 node spawns |
| `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts` | 146.2 s | 51.8 s | 30 tsx spawns |
| `tests/cli/init.test.ts` (via `execAsync`) | 109.4 s | 55.6 s | `init` must stay a subprocess (stdin prompts) — now a bundle subprocess |
| `tests/cli/search-fts-freshness.test.ts` | 35.2 s | ~12 s | 10 tsx spawns |
| `tests/cli/doctor-cache.test.ts` | 22.5 s | ~10 s | 8 tsx spawns |
| `tests/cli/update-if-assignee.test.ts` | 18.1 s | ~9 s | tsx spawns |
| `tests/cli/sync-author-gate.test.ts` (`execWithInput`) | 53.0 s | ~22 s | `execWithInput` now rewrites `tsx <cli>` → bundle |
| `tests/cli/sync-assignee-clear.test.ts` (`execWithInput`) | 42.6 s | ~20 s | ditto |
| `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` | 162.9 s | 151.3 s | was `dist/cli.js` → bundle |
| `tests/cli/sync-integration-convergence.test.ts` | 45.5 s | 34.5 s | was `dist/cli.js` → bundle |
| `tests/cli/sync-delta-{pull,push,delete,fallback}.test.ts` | 29.0 s ea. | 22–24 s ea. | was `dist/cli.js` → bundle |

**Correctness bonus on the sync tests.** Those files previously hard-coded
`dist/cli.js` and therefore silently tested whatever build happened to be on
disk. They now run the current `src/` and no longer require a `npm run build`
before the suite (they failed outright in a fresh worktree).

#### 3. Determinism fix — stale `dist/` (AC6)

`tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts` picks `dist/cli.js` when present
(`resolveStartupTarget('auto')`). A `dist/` build older than `src/` makes it
assert against code that no longer exists — observed as a **real intermittent
failure** in this item's first baseline run
(`records --version as a version spawn`, "expected +0 to be 1": the
`recordSpawn('version')` call exists in `src/cli.ts` but not in the stale
build). `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts` now has `isDistFresh()` and `auto` only
uses the build when it is at least as new as every file under `src/`,
otherwise it falls back to `src`. Pre-existing resolution behaviour is
unchanged for a fixture with no `src/`.

#### 4. Reduced excess benchmark iterations

`tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts` — warmup 4 → 2 and bare-node
samples 3 → 2. Warmup only has to reach a served cache hit before sampling
(1–2 invocations do); the gated `runs` (4 per scenario, from the recorded
budget) are unchanged, so the ratchet is identical. 82.4 s → 62.9 s.

#### 5. AC4 — redundancy removal (accounted)

- **Removed** `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts` →
  `a fresh cache dir misses once then hits (no cross-test pollution)`.
  It re-asserted exactly the miss→hit cycle already covered by
  `serves repeat identical reads from cache (AC1)`; every case in the file
  already starts from a fresh temp dir (`setup()`), so the "no cross-test
  pollution" claim added no coverage. Cost: 2 real CLI spawns. **Coverage
  preserved** by the AC1 case.
- A repo-wide duplicate-title audit over the canonical suite found **no**
  duplicated test titles across files (0 duplicates) — the earlier
  deduplication work (WL-0MV4UZ6C4007XDGI) already removed the legacy
  duplicates. Nothing else was deleted.

#### 6. AC3 — every ≥5 s test triaged

All 90 canonical tests ≥5 s fall into exactly one disposition:

| Disposition | Tests | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| **Optimised** (spawn cost removed; assertions unchanged) | 46 | Every test in the converted files listed in §2. The dominant mechanism (tsx transpile per spawn) is gone; each of these tests still asserts the same observable behaviour. |
| **Retained with justification** — must measure `tsx`/build cost itself | 2 | `startup-import-budget` (it *is* the tsx startup benchmark — bundling would defeat its purpose) and `entry-point-split` (asserts the real `dist`-vs-`src` entry-point parity contract, F3). |
| **Retained with justification** — real-git integration, no mockable dependency | ~25 | `sync-vs-mutation` (15), `sync-integration-convergence`, `sync-delta-{pull,push,delete,fallback}`, `sync-author-gate`, `sync-assignee-clear`, `github-push-synced-items`. These drive real bare remotes and real `git` child processes; mocking git would remove the very behaviour under test. They are also the anti-false-confidence anchor required by the brief (keep ≥1 real integration test per subsystem). |
| **Retained with justification** — deterministic parking window | 15 | `sync-vs-mutation`'s `Promise.race([mutation, sleep(3000)])` is the deterministic guard that the mutator *attempted* the store lock while the sync holds it. Shortening it would let the race pass vacuously on buggy code — a coverage loss, not an optimisation. |
| **Retained with justification** — in-process CLI contract tests | ~40 | `close-recursive` (46 tests), `issue-management` (49), `issue-status` (43), `valid-json-output` (38), `json-output-shape` (18): each test drives several full CLI commands through the in-process harness (~200 ms/call: DB open, config load, plugin scan, command registration). The cost is *production* CLI startup, so it cannot be reduced from test code without changing what is being tested. Recorded as a follow-up (§8). |
| **Removed** | 1 | §5 above. |

No test is silently ignored or skipped as a result of this change.

#### 7. AC5 — pytest measured and triaged

`run_tests.py --suite pytest` (equivalent to `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings`):

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Tests | 162 passed, **5 failed** (167) |
| Duration | **101–103 s** |

The 5 failures are **pre-existing and unrelated** — verified by running the
same suite on a clean tree (my changes stashed): *identical* 5 failures,
102.7 s. All are skill-behaviour drift in `tests/skill/heartbeat/` and
`skill/pane-triage/tests/` (`heartbeat.check_queue()` no longer returns
"Held…"), nothing to do with the vitest changes here. Triaged into
**WL-0MVH2T0ZV006KIOU** (`triage.check_or_create.py`).

No Python test is ≥5 s (whole suite is 102 s over 167 tests, dominated by
process spawns of the real `wl` CLI in the heartbeat integration test), so no
pytest optimisation was warranted; the suite is fast relative to the canonical
vitest gates and is untouched.

#### 8. Follow-ups discovered (not this item)

- Dead/invalid vitest config: `singleFork: true` sits at the top level of
  `test` in `vitest.config.ts`, where vitest 4 ignores it (it is a
  `poolOptions.forks.*` option). Harmless today but misleading: the comment
  above it describes behaviour that `isolate: true` + `maxWorkers: 4` already
  provide. Recorded rather than changed to keep this item's blast radius on
  test behaviour.
- In-process CLI harness cost (~200 ms/invocation, ~1200 invocations in the
  canonical suite ≈ 240 s aggregate) is the next largest pool; reducing it
  means changing CLI startup in `src/`, which the brief scopes out unless a
  production optimisation is the proven cause.

data.comment:
### Results (AC2 / AC6) and final verification

#### A/B measurement — back-to-back, matched load (primary evidence)

Baseline and post-change trees measured **adjacently on the same host** so both
see the same conditions (load average **27–30**, i.e. the pessimistic case).
CPU time is the load-independent metric.

| Metric | Baseline (pre-change) | Post-change | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wall clock (`/usr/bin/time -v`) | 1189.5 s | 774.5 s | **−415.0 s (−34.9 %)** |
| CPU (user+system) | 3160.8 s | 2445.5 s | **−715.3 s (−22.6 %)** |
| Result | green | green | — |

#### Mid-load pair (load ~11–14)

| Suite | Baseline | Post-change | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/cli` | 104 files, 868 passed + 4 skipped, **624.03 s** | 104 files, 868 passed + 4 skipped, **426.78 s** | **−31.6 %** |
| `tests/unit` | 43 files, 624 passed, **27.44 s** | 43 files, 624 passed, **29.04 s** | +1.6 s (noise) |
| **Canonical total** | **651.47 s** | **455.82 s** | **−30.0 %** |

Per-test aggregates (`tests/cli`): `tests` **2319.05 s → 1528.78 s** (−34.1 %).

**Reading these numbers.** Wall clock on this shared 16-core host is not a
reliable instrument: six post-change runs of *identical* code measured
462.3 s, 533.8 s, 546.4 s, 560.9 s, 701.8 s and 928.4 s (load 4 → 24). Two
pre-change runs measured 624.0 s and 877.9 s. That is why the adjacent A/B
pair plus the CPU figure are the evidence, and why single-run comparisons are
not quoted as authoritative. AC2's ≥30 % is met on both load-matched pairs
(−34.9 % and −30.0 %).

#### AC6 — determinism (no intermittent timeouts)

Six consecutive labelled runs reviewed; the last **five canonical runs
completed green with zero failures**, at load averages from 3 to 30:

| Run | `tests/cli` | `tests/unit` | Load | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A/B post | 774.5 s (canonical wall) | — | 27–30 | green |
| final #2 | 546.37 s | 30.09 s | 13–18 | green |
| final #3 | 560.87 s | (slot contention, not a failure) | 15–18 | cli green |
| final #4 | 1225.40 s | 87.40 s | 18–24 | cli green, unit failed on the new guard (self-match, fixed) |
| final #5 | 701.75 s | 27.63 s | ~14–24 | **green** |

The pre-change baseline was **not** time-out-stable under the same conditions:
a run at load ~20 failed with `Test timed out in 60000ms` in
`read-cache-e2e > arg variants` (eight ~8 s tsx spawns exceed the 60 s test
budget), while the post-change suite stayed green at load 24–30 because a
spawn now costs ~1.1 s.

Two further timeout classes were removed while verifying:
- `vitest.config.ts` — `hookTimeout: 60000` (default 10 s). Real-git
  `beforeEach` setup in `sync-concurrent.test.ts` exceeded 10 s at load ~20
  and failed as `Hook timed out` with nothing wrong with the code. Same class
  of load-induced flake.
- `tests/unit/no-tsx-cli-spawn.test.ts` — regression guard (AC6): fails if the
  bundle cannot be built, or if any test file outside a documented allowlist
  reintroduces the `tsx src/cli.ts` spawn idiom.

#### Docs updated (AC7)

- `README.md` — new **Test Suite Runtime** subsection under *Vitest
  Configuration*: what dominates runtime, the two rules (prefer the in-process
  harness; use `runCliProcess()`/`cliInvocation()` when a real process is
  unavoidable), when a real `tsx`/`dist` spawn is legitimate, and where the
  baseline lives.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — new section **"Test-suite runtime
  reduction (WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8)"**: root-cause table (per-spawn costs),
  what changed, the A/B + mid-load result tables, the **refreshed post-change
  top-20 slow-test table** (with baseline column), what was removed, the
  full-suite `test:timings` comparison with its load caveat, pytest results,
  reproduce commands and confounders.
- Code comments updated in every touched test file (`cli-bundle.ts` header
  documents the layout/race/fallback rationale; each converted call site says
  why the bundle is used and what is still asserted).

#### Assumptions recorded

1. **`tests/cli` + `tests/unit` is "the canonical suite"** per
   `.pi/test-config.json`; both are included in every measurement.
2. **The pre-compiled bundle is behaviourally equivalent** to
   `tsx src/cli.ts` for these tests: same entry file, same command graph,
   packages kept external, and the bundle directory mirrors the package root
   so `init`'s template/plugin/scheduled-prompt lookups resolve identically
   (verified directly).
3. **`sync-*` integration tests should assert current `src/`, not a build** —
   switching them off hard-coded `dist/cli.js` is a correctness fix as well as
   a speed-up; they no longer require `npm run build` before the suite.
4. **Not changed, deliberately:** worker parallelism (`maxWorkers`,
   `isolate`) — the brief lists parallelisation as out of scope; the dead
   top-level `singleFork` key and the ~200 ms/invocation in-process harness are
   recorded as follow-ups in §8 above rather than touched.

Spec contract pinned for the implementation children (WL-0MVFE1AB0002PEPN, WL-0MVFE1BTB0084T17, WL-0MVFE1DD8000D8T2, WL-0MVFE1EWW004VAW2):

**RED-witness convention.** Every new spec that asserts not-yet-implemented behaviour is committed with `it.fails` (repo TDD pattern, docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher-post-fix-verification.md). The suite is GREEN while the bodies are RED; the implementing child flips each `it.fails` to `it` as its RED→GREEN evidence. Green `it` bodies are regression pins for invariants that must never be relaxed.

**Pinned dispatch-outcome contract.** A successful AUDIT dispatch carries `outcome.auditBatch = { active, depth, cap, remaining }`: `active` true only while batching is engaged (audit-eligible depth >= browseItemCount AND clamped auditBatchMax > 1); `depth` measured from the Herdr head; `cap` = clamped auditBatchMax; `remaining` = continuations still available AFTER this dispatch (0 when off/cap consumed). Non-audit dispatches never carry `auditBatch`.

**Pinned option contract.** `dispatchDowntimeWork` / `dispatchFromCoordination` accept `auditBatchMax` and `auditBatchRemaining` (continuation budget available BEFORE this dispatch; owned by the worker tick).

**Pinned settings contract.** `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = 2`, range [1,5], `clampDowntimeAuditBatchMax` (non-finite -> 2), settings key `downtimeAuditBatchMax` parsed/clamped by loadSettings, `1` = legacy/off.

**Pinned observability contract.** The worker records an `audit-batch-continue` decision via `deps.recordDecision` for batch continuations with `auditBatchDepth` / `auditBatchCap` / `auditBatchRemaining` metadata (existing rate limit applies).

**Pinned coordination contract.** Own-head continuations do NOT release leadership mid-batch (`ownBacklogDispatch` false); the hand-off is surfaced once at batch end (remaining 0); any non-dispatched outcome ends the batch.

## C4 implemented — coordination batch continuation + deferred leadership hand-off

**Session:** herdr-1792441713-1934005-26336 (epic drive; the driven child session for this item timed out at 7200 s with an untouched worktree, so the epic driver completed the leaf workflow in the pre-created worktree).

### Delivered

1. **Leader own-head continuation (AC4).** After the coordination offer scan yields no dispatch, the leader — while a batch is *armed* (`auditBatchRemaining > 0` and clamped `auditBatchMax > 1`) — first runs an **audit-only** continuation over its own Herdr head window + bounded extension (`readOwnHeadWindow` → `getHerdrListHead` + `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`). Exactly one dispatch per invocation; the unchanged all-kinds own-backlog fallback runs when no audit candidate survives.
2. **Same filter chain, factored out (AC2/AC3).** The fallback's sequential filter chain (classify → dispatched-marker id-guard → attempt budget → non-terminal cooldown → code-freeze → audit ≥2 free slots → critical in-flight guard → review-queue hold) moved into one helper, `dispatchFromOwnHead`, used by both the continuation and the fallback — no duplicated gates and no second ranking. Holds reported by the scan are folded into the terminal-reason composition, so a filtered own-head backlog keeps its neutral reason.
3. **Distinct targets (AC3).** Marker exclusion applies exactly as before, plus an explicit **batch-local exclusion set** (`auditBatchDispatchedIds`) owned by the worker tick: `activeAuditBatch.dispatchedIds` accumulates every target dispatched in the window and is passed on each continuation. Any non-`dispatched` outcome for a continuation **ends the batch** — no target hopping.
4. **Deferred leadership hand-off (AC4).** `dispatchFromCoordination` now finalizes every outcome against the leader's own audit depth (`finalizeAuditBatchOutcome`) and raises `ownBacklogDispatch` for a continuation **only when that dispatch ends the batch** (cap reached / depth dropped). Mid-batch continuations leave both `ownBacklogDispatch` and the new `auditBatchContinuation` flag as the only surface, so the worker's existing `releaseLeadership()` step-down fires exactly once, at batch end, with no tick change required.
5. **Surface + plumbing.** New documented `auditBatchContinuation?: boolean` on `DowntimeDispatchOutcome`; new optional `auditBatchDispatchedIds` on the coordination opts; `activeAuditBatch` carries `dispatchedIds`; the legacy path is untouched.

### Tests

- Flipped the three test-first `it.fails` witnesses (committed RED by WL-0MVFE0T0M009ZCPM) to `it`: AC4 continuation/no-mid-batch-handoff, AC6f marker-excluded duplicate target, AC3 claim-failure ends the batch — all green.
- Added `AC3/AC4: the batch-local exclusion set prevents re-selecting an item dispatched in this batch` (no marker present; only the batch-local set excludes the target).
- **Spec correction:** the AC4 witness shifted its own-head fixture *before* the assertion that dispatches the shifted item (off-by-one), so it could never pass; the shift now models the dispatched item leaving the head and runs after each dispatch.
- `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src` (sanctioned herdr package run): **3505 passed, 2 failed** — both failures are **pre-existing at dev HEAD and unrelated** (`worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts` cross-instance late-pane timeout → WL-0MVFX70SB000YRQH; `worklist-blocked-by-cache.test.ts` Blocked By parity → WL-0MVFX6404003TE2E, both completed/in_review).
- Coverage note (AC4 leadership timing): the hand-off decision is entirely driven by the `ownBacklogDispatch` surface, whose mid-batch/batch-end semantics are pinned by the coordination-dispatch specs; `tick()`'s existing step-down path is unchanged.

### Discovered (not fixed here)

- `WL-0MVGJ4WSS005BMSI` — the configured full gate (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`) excludes the herdr package suite, and `run_tests.py --type herdr` is not defined, so herdr verification runs outside the sanctioned runner/cache. (discovered-from this item)

data.author: implement
data.comment:
F1 implemented — spawn records now carry per-process CPU time and peak RSS.

**Code**
- `SpawnRecord` gains `cpuMs` (user+system, ms, from `process.resourceUsage()`) and `maxRssKb` (peak RSS, KiB). `recordSpawn()` appends `<kind>	<ts>	<pid>	<cpuMs>	<maxRssKb>`.
- Legacy 3-field lines still parse: `cpuMs`/`maxRssKb` are `null` (never 0), and blank fields are treated as unknown. If the platform cannot report usage the field is written blank -> parsed as `null`, so aggregation cannot silently under-report.
- New `summariseSpawnRecords(file)` -> `{ total, byKind, cpuSeconds, maxRssKb, missingCpu, missingRss }`.
- `WL_SPAWN_COUNT=1` stderr path now emits `[wl:spawn] <kind> <pid> cpuMs=<n> maxRssKb=<n>`.
- Still best-effort: no throw and no behaviour change with env unset or an unwritable file path (covered by tests).

**Tests** (`tests/spawn-counter.test.ts`): 5-field line shape, live CPU/RSS values, legacy + blank-field back-compat as `null`, unwritable file, stderr path reporting CPU/RSS, and `summariseSpawnRecords` totals/per-kind/peak-RSS/missing counters. `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` untouched and passing (kind counts unaffected).

**Baseline deliverable** — the parent (`WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B`) is `status: open` (mutation invariant: no description/comment on an unclaimed item), so the baseline lives in the repo at `docs/dev/wl-spawn-baseline-2026-10-19.md` for the parent/F10/F11 sessions, and is summarised here. 10 runs each, `node dist/cli.js` from this worktree against the main `.worklog`, `/usr/bin/time -v`:

| Command | p95 wall | median wall | p95 RSS | mean CPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wl --version` | 1.19 s | 1.01 s | 78.9 MB | 1.051 s |
| `wl next --json` | 1.10 s | 1.00 s | 79.2 MB | 1.033 s |
| `wl list --json` | 21.92 s (outlier) | 2.78 s | 257.5 MB | 4.110 s |

`sync` was measured from the main checkout with push excluded (worktrees are blocked by the cross-project sync guard; `--dry-run` primary, `--no-push` real sync as the extreme case). Live instrumentation on this build records ≈1.05–1.18 CPU-s per `wl next --json` process at the record point vs ≈0.43 CPU-s for bare node — the import graph dominates per-spawn cost, which is the AC2 lever.

## F6 implementation summary

**New `src/command-registry.ts`** — the 30 eager `import XCommand` lines in `src/cli-main.ts` are gone:
- `COMMAND_LOADERS`: name → `() => import('./commands/x.js')` (32 names; `audit-show`/`audit-set` share the audit-result module loader and `audit-waive`/`audit-unwaive` the audit-waive loader, so each module's `register()` runs once — no duplicate commands).

data.comment:
## F7 implementation + measured floor (AC1)

**Slimming applied**
1. `--version` now exits **before any fast-path module is imported**: the version check runs first using the dependency-free `argv-normalize` helper, so `--version` loads only `version.ts` + `spawn-counter.ts`. (Bug found and fixed while measuring: the write-completion callback is async, so the original version branch fell through into the heavy graph; it is now a true `if/else` branch.)
2. `extractCommandFromArgv` moved to `src/argv-normalize.ts` (re-exported by `read-cache-cli`) so the fast path can classify the invocation without importing the cache machinery.
3. The read-cache machinery, the worklog resolver and `process-lifecycle` are now **dynamic** imports, loaded only after the `--version` branch: static boot graph **8 → 4 modules** (`cli.ts`, `argv-normalize.ts`, `spawn-counter.ts`, `version.ts`), 3 dynamic entrypoints (`read-cache-cli`, `worklog-paths`, `process-lifecycle`), 8-module runtime union.
4. Worktree registration is unchanged inside a managed worktree but the `process-lifecycle` module is only imported there (cheap path test), so normal invocations skip it.
5. **Ratchet tightened**: the budget now records `fastPathDynamicImports` + `fastPathRuntimeModules` (union of the static graph and every dynamic entrypoint's transitive graph), so moving an import behind `await import()` cannot sidestep the budget. New tests cover the allowlist, a rejected addition, and the no-heavy-modules-on-`--version` rule. Regression policy gains a distinct `rssHeadroomPct` (25 %) and 100 % CPU headroom (tsx CPU varies ~50 % run-to-run; a gate run measured 3226 ms against a 3224 ms limit).

**Measured on the reference host (F2 harness, 12 warm runs, p95)**

| Scenario | dist before F7 | dist after F7 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wl next --json` | 686 ms / 1224 ms CPU / 67.7 MB | **689 ms / 630 ms CPU / 67.8 MB** | CPU −48.5 %, wall flat |
| `wl list --status open --json` | 662 / 624 / 67.6 | **645 / 607 / 67.9** | CPU −2.7 % |
| `wl --version` | 1038 / 557 / 67.2 | **547 / 492 / 60.9** | wall −47 %, CPU −12 %, RSS −9 % |

Against the **pre-split** baseline (F2 capture, before F4): `next` 1316 ms / 1224 CPU / 78.8 MB → **689 / 630 / 67.8** (−47.7 % wall, −48.5 % CPU, −14 % RSS).

**AC1 verdict: not reachable by import slimming alone.** The bare-node floor measured in the same run is **484 ms p95 wall / 458 ms CPU / 61.2 MB** — i.e. AC1's 500 ms leaves ~16 ms over bare node, and 60 MB is *below* the bare-node RSS on this (loaded) host. The fast path is now within ~1.4× of bare node for cache hits and at bare-node level for `--version` (60.9 MB). `ac1Targets.enforced` therefore stays `false`; the measured floor is recorded in `bench/startup-import-budget.json` (`ac1Targets.note`) and an **OPEN QUESTION** is raised on the parent.

## F9 progress + reference-host measurement (AC2)

Implementation landed (opportunistic pruning + config + bare doctor mention + docs + tests). Full suite pending; reference-host evidence captured:

**Before** (`~/.cache/wl/state`, real host): **218,986 counter files / 881 MB** (`du -sh`; ~2.4 MB of actual file bytes — the cost is directory/inode overhead). Dry-run report: 183,823 stale by TTL, 34,163 over the 1,000-file bound.

**One prune run** (`dist/cli.js doctor cache --json --prune`, 40 s wall / 30.7 s sys): removed **217,988** counters (183,823 stale by TTL + 34,165 bound pass LRU; 1 cached entry invalidated), leaving **1,006 files / 30 MB** (bound 1,000 + live counters written within the 30 s live window, never touched by pruning).

Net: **file count 218,986 → 1,006 (-99.5 %); on-disk footprint 881 MB → 30 MB (-96.6 %)**, in a single maintenance command. The 40 s runtime is stat+unlink on 218k files; the opportunistic hook now keeps the dir bounded, so a repeat prune is trivial.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## F9 implementation summary

- **Opportunistic pruning** (`src/read-cache.ts`): `bumpStateCounter` now calls `maybePruneStateDir` through `statePruneDue()` — one `readdir` check per 20 bumps, and a full prune only when the state dir is over the bound. Explicit `maybePruneStateDir`/`wl doctor cache` calls are never rate-limited. Live counters (written within 30 s) are never removed by either pass, so a concurrent writer's cache can only be recomputed, never corrupted.
- **Configurable bound/TTL**: `WL_STATE_MAX_FILES` (default 1000) and `WL_STATE_TTL_MS` (default 7 days), read cheaply per check; documented in `CLI.md` (read-cache env section) and `CONFIG.md` (new 'Read-cache state boundedness' section with Pi-host example).
- **Bare `wl doctor`** reports pending read-cache state: additive `checkId: 'read-cache.state'` finding in JSON, and a text notice (also replacing the misleading 'no issues found' when only cache cleanup is pending).
- **Tests**: 3 new unit tests in `tests/unit/read-cache-prune.test.ts` (direct over-bound prune, bump-triggered opportunistic prune with live-counter survival, healthy under-bound dir untouched) and a new CLI test in `tests/cli/doctor-cache.test.ts` (bare doctor JSON+text flag, cleared after `--prune`). `tests/cli/doctor-upgrade-notice.test.ts` now isolates `WL_CACHE_DIR` so the host's real cache state cannot perturb the upgrade contract.
- **Reference-host measurement** quoted in the previous comment: 218,986 files / 881 MB → 1,006 files / 30 MB in one `wl doctor cache --prune` run (-99.5 % files, -96.6 % footprint).

Full canonical suite green (tests/cli 104 files / 870 tests; tests/unit 43 files / 627 tests).

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## F10 measurement and verdict (AC2)

**Repeatable procedure** (harness added as `bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts`, npm scripts `benchmark:herdr-refresh` / `:json`): 4 panes share one worklog dir (20 seeded items), each pane runs the herdr refresh query set — the four mandatory `wl list` subsets plus `wl next -n 20` — every 5 s for a 30 s cycle, with `WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE` enabled; CPU-seconds are summed from the F1 spawn records.

```sh
# baseline: the pre-F4 build (git worktree at b60faeb1, npm run build)
npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts --json --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5 --cli /tmp/wl-pre-f4/dist/cli.js
# after: current build
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh:json -- --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5
# no-cache (read-work) baseline variant: prepend WL_CACHE_DISABLED=1
```

**Baseline vs after (same host, same workload, 4 panes x 30 s, 120 spawns/cycle)**

| Metric | Pre-F4 baseline | After F4-F7 | Target (0.4x) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spawns / cycle | 120 | 120 | — |
| Spawn kinds | 112 cache-hit + 8 read-work | **120 cache-hit** | all hits |
| **Total CPU-seconds / cycle** | **159.44** | **83.58** | **63.78** |
| CPU-s per spawn | 1.329 | **0.697** | <= 0.53 |
| Peak RSS | 78.8 MB | **68 MB** | — |
| Failures | 0 | 0 | 0 |

**Result: 47.6 % CPU-second reduction — short of the >= 60 % target.**

**Shortfall analysis.** Per-spawn cost fell 1.329 -> 0.697 CPU-s, but the bare-node floor on this host is ~0.46 CPU-s (~66 % of what remains). wl's own work is now ~0.24 CPU-s/spawn. Even a zero-cost `wl` body would cap the reduction at ~65 %, so the target is unreachable by making spawns faster: the remaining lever is **fewer spawns** (five separate `wl` invocations per pane per tick); one consolidated read per tick would cut spawns 5x and take the cycle to ~17 CPU-s (~90 % below baseline).

**Lever decision (AC5):** implementing the consolidated worklist read spans `wl` (new read mode/cache entry) and `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (mandatory-subset semantics) — exceeds this measurement item's scope; filed as **WL-0MVGYLU0S004WZUS** with evidence and acceptance criteria.

**Correctness:** no changes to cache semantics; existing spawn-reduction simulation and fetcher tests pass unchanged (full suite green).

data.comment:
## RCA confirmed (reproduced locally: 1 failure in 5 full-file runs)

The work item hypothesis is correct: **stale frames from an earlier TUI run inside the same file land last**. Reproduced failure output showed:
- `unblocked selections render byte-for-byte without Blocked By rows across refreshes` failing with `Blocked By WL-B2 — Second blocker` — a row only the preceding `re-resolves only when the item's own signature changes` test can produce.
- `the detail view renders Blocked By rows...` failing on a plain **list** frame (no detail view, no `Blocked By`) — the late frame of an earlier list-mode test.

### Mechanism

`watchRefresh()` triggers the production DB-change callback and then waits a fixed `settle(15)` ms. `doRefresh()` is asynchronous and renders at the END of its cycle (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` ~line 6269) and, when a refresh request arrives while one is in flight, schedules a coalesced trailing refresh (`if (refreshPending) { refreshPending = false; void doRefresh(false); }`, ~line 6279). Two/three back-to-back `watchRefresh()` calls therefore leave a refresh cycle (and possibly a trailing refresh) in flight when `quit()` runs. `quit()` only awaits the TUI promise, so that cycle completes AFTER the test ends and its `render()` writes to stdout — recorded by the NEXT test's stdout spy (the mock closes over the reassigned module-level `writes` binding), i.e. attributed to the wrong test.

### Fix (harness only, per the investigation guidance)

Drain until the TUI stops writing instead of assuming a fixed tick:
- new `drainWrites()` helper: wait until no stdout write has occurred for a full quiet window (bounded, throws loudly if it never quiesces);
- `watchRefresh()` drains after triggering the callback (refresh cycles complete before assertions);
- `quit()` drains after the TUI promise resolves, so post-exit renders and coalesced trailing refreshes land in the EXITING test's capture and cannot bleed into the next test.

Production render path is NOT changed; behavioural assertions are untouched.

Session: implement — RED witness + root cause established.

**RED witness (dev HEAD, pre-change):** repeated runs of `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src/worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts` fail intermittently (~40% of runs) with the reported signature — 'timed out after 5000ms waiting for GREEN_CIRCLE after late pane appears; last output showed the item without a green circle'. Additional always-reachable defect: the same command exits 1 even on a fully green run because of UNHANDLED REJECTIONS ('Cannot read properties of null (reading removeListener)', events.ts:368) — 1 per failing run, up to 4 in the original evidence.

**Two confirmed production defects (both fixed in this session):**

1. events.ts — close()/restartSubscription() nulls `this.socket` while a subscribe request is still pending; the settlement handlers then dereferenced `this.socket!` in .then/.catch, throwing an unhandled rejection (Node's default policy would crash the plugin process). Fix: capture the connected socket in a local const and remove listeners from it (safe no-op on a destroyed socket). Deterministic regression test: a stalled mock server (new `respondToSubscribe:false` option on MockHerdrSocket) leaves a subscribe pending; close() must not raise an unhandled rejection. RED confirmed before the fix (rejections[0] = the exact TypeError).

2. worklist.ts refreshPaneMarkersFromEvent — single-flight guard DROPPED a trailing event when a pass was already in flight, so a pane that appeared during that window (pane_agent_detected → operator/hydrator status change) never got its green circle. Fix: mark the refresh pending and re-run the pass after the in-flight one settles (trail-coalescing, mirroring the DB-watch pattern WL-0MTIB7JAN004MQ8N). Deterministic regression test: a controllable applyActivePaneMarkers seam holds the first event-triggered pass; a second status event arrives in that window and must still produce the GREEN_CIRCLE. RED confirmed before the fix.

**Test-harness hardening (hypothesis 2 confirmed as a further race):** the cross-instance test pushed the status event on `mockServer.getFirstClient()`, which can still be the PRE-RESTART handle (the server only removes it on the async socket close); an event pushed there reaches nobody. Replaced with `mockServer.waitForClientSubscribedTo('w5:p55')` (polling, subscription-aware: returns the connection that actually carries the late pane). Also strengthened the cross-instance test per AC2: asserts no GREEN_CIRCLE before the late pane enters the pane list and no RED_CIRCLE.

**Verification:** the file now passes 31 tests (the added 2 regressions + the 5 original + events.test.ts), 5+ consecutive clean runs, stable under 3-parallel-run load. ## Intake complete — RCA & fix brief drafted

**Outcome:** brief drafted (stage `intake_complete`, issue type `bug`); effort **Small** (expected 2.67h), risk **Medium** (7/25), confidence 76% (see effort-and-risk comment).

**Preliminary RCA (code-confirmed):** `_resolvedModel` in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.ts` is set only from the Local Proxy `X-Resolved-Model` response header and reset only on `session_start`. The `model_select` handler updates only `_selectedModel`, so after a mid-session `/model` switch the footer pairs the new alias with the old resolved model — permanently when the switched-to model is a non-proxy provider (`deepseek`/`opencode` in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`), where the header never arrives. This is the mid-session analogue of the already-fixed session-boundary staleness (WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6).

**Mini-reviews:** completeness — ACs, constraints, key files, risks all present, no changes needed; capture fidelity — no interactive answers (automated intake), assumptions documented as OPEN QUESTIONS; related-work & traceability — sibling WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6 + 6 related items linked; risks & assumptions — scope-creep risk recorded (single-slot `onModelChange` and `session_start` alias guard flagged as potential `discovered-from` follow-ups, out of scope); polish & handoff — typo fixed, `(resolving)`/alignment regression constraints tightened.

**Duplicate check:** performed (`wl search` sweep over model/footer/display terms); no fully-overlapping item found — WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6 and WL-0MRO7LWIX001516P are siblings covering session-boundary and `(resolving)` state only.

**OPEN QUESTIONS for the producer (assumptions A1–A3; non-blocking, recommended answers in the Appendix):**
1. What exactly did you observe mid-session — alias updating while the resolved half stayed on the previous model (until next turn), or no change at all? *Recommended:* stale-resolved + non-proxy indefinite staleness (the only code-consistent outcomes).

3. Should invalidation apply on `model_select` with `source: restore` too (consistent with the session-start reset)? *Recommended:* yes.

data.comment:
## TDD red evidence (run via implement.py finish test gate, IMPLEMENT_TEST_COMMAND override)

All 14 new specs **fail against the current implementation** (brother of no production change); the **existing 127 tests keep passing**. Verified with vitest `run` on both files (git state fingerprint cached in the worktree's `.worklog/cache`).

### model-display.test.ts — `mid-session model switch` (11 failing specs)

1. `invalidates the resolved model on a mid-session model_select with source "set"` → `AssertionError: expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be null` (line 420)
2. `... with source "cycle"` → same
3. `... with source "restore"` → same
4. `notifies onModelChange exactly once when a mid-session switch invalidates the resolved model` → `expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be null`
5. `adopts the selected model provider/id immediately for a non-proxy provider (deepseek)` → `expected null to be 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro'`
6. `replaces a stale proxy-resolved value when switching to a non-proxy provider (opencode)` → `expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be 'opencode/big-pickle'`
7. `keeps a Local Proxy selection unresolved until its x-resolved-model header arrives` → `expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be null`
8. `adopts the proxy header after a non-proxy fallback value was displayed` → `expected null to be 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro'`
9. `uses the last selection across consecutive mid-session switches (last-write-wins)` → `expected null to be 'opencode/big-pickle'`
10. `does not throw and degrades safely when model_select has no model` → `expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be null`
11. `does not throw and degrades to (resolving) when the provider is missing` → `expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be null`

### session-health.test.ts — `mid-session model switch — end-to-end Line 3 render` (3 failing specs)

12. `re-renders Line 3 as "<newAlias> → (resolving)" immediately after a mid-session switch` → `expected 'openai/gpt-4' to be null`
13. `renders the non-proxy provider/id fallback instead of a stale value or endless "(resolving)"` → `expected null to be 'deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro'`
14. `right-aligns the longer non-proxy label and keeps it within the width budget` → `expected false to be true` (visible.endsWith('deepseek-v4-pro → deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro'))

### Hand-off notes
- **`it.fails(...)` convention (IMPORTANT for the implement sibling WL-0MVGU7H24009G8II):** these tests are authored with vitest `it.fails(...)` (expected failure) so the suite stays green pre-implementation (repo convention — WL-0MVFE0T0M009ZCPM, WL-0MT1EE3S7005DJ1F). Land the implementation by **flipping `it.fails(` → `it(`** in both files; every test must then pass (an unexpectedly-passing `it.fails` fails the suite). 14 specs to flip: 11 in model-display.test.ts + 3 in session-health.test.ts (the one plain `it` width guard stays as-is).
- **Fixture clarification (assumption, documented):** the pre-existing `model_select sets selectedModel when model id is provided` test used `provider: 'openai'` and asserted `getResolvedModel() === null`. Under the new non-proxy fallback semantics any non-`Local Proxy` provider resolves immediately, so that assertion would no longer hold. Minimal change: fixture now uses `provider: 'Local Proxy'` (assertion unchanged — the test's purpose is the alias-tracking, not provider semantics). No other existing test needed changes.
- Behaviour contract for the implementer (see also sibling item ACs): on any mid-session `model_select` (source set/cycle/restore) invalidate `_resolvedModel` and notify exactly once; non-`Local Proxy` provider → `_resolvedModel = ${provider}/${id}` immediately; `Local Proxy` → keep null until the header arrives; missing model/provider → no throw, degrade to null.

data.comment:
Implementation summary (commit 6b938463, pushed to dev):

**Root cause confirmed as documented:** the failure was a stale `dist/cli.js` (gitignored; predating the `--version` spawn instrumentation in `src/cli.ts`), not a source defect. The `auto` target selected the stale build via `resolveStartupTarget('auto', …)`.

**Findings during implementation:**
1. origin/dev already carried a freshness guard (`isDistFresh`, from WL-0MVF9JJUH0077OB8 commit 1648fa1b), but it was defeated by the build order: `scripts/generate-version.cjs` rewrites `src/version.ts` *after* `tsc`, so a freshly built `dist/cli.js` always appeared stale and `auto` silently fell back to `src` — killing coverage of the built entry across the suite.
2. Fix in `bench/wl-startup-perf.ts`: `newestMtimeMs` accepts a filter; `isDistFresh` excludes generated sources (`src/version.ts`, `.d.ts` compiler output) from the freshness comparison. Fresh build → `auto` selects `dist`; stale build → `auto` falls back to `src`. Both directions verified.
3. Docs (`docs/dev/wl-startup-import-budget.md`): added a “Build-freshness requirement (--target auto)” section covering the guard, the rebuild-after-pull requirement, and the generated-source exclusion (AC3).
4. Tests: new `tests/unit/startup-target-freshness.test.ts` (14 tests) pinning `isDistFresh` / `resolveStartupTarget` / `buildStartupInvocation` contracts (fresh/stale/missing dist, generated-file exclusion, explicit dist throws when missing, invocation shapes).

**Acceptance criteria:** AC1 met — the entry-point-split suite passes (7/7) with the `auto` target. AC2 met — a stale dist can no longer be selected by `auto` (falls back to src); a fresh build reliably selects dist again. AC3 met — docs updated. AC4 met — full suite green: `run_tests.py --scope full` exit 0 at main HEAD (which contains 6b938463); note a bare checkout needs `npm run build` before the suite (tests spawn `dist/cli.js`), consistent with repo convention.

**Commit:** `e740d6d4` — `WL-0MVHSZR9C0012NQY: Implementation complete` (rebased onto dev during push; initial commit `ee6b20c3`).

## What changed

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
  - `LlamaStatus` + `parseLlamaStatus` now read `local_idle_seconds`, `local_last_activity_at` and `local_last_activity_source` (all optional; malformed values degrade to `undefined`, never reject the poll). New exported helper `reportedIdleSeconds()` rejects absent/non-finite/negative ages → `null` (fallback to the local tracker).
  - Tick idle qualification: a usable idle age is AUTHORITATIVE for the DURATION requirement — `>= thresholdMs` is ready on the first poll (global and per-slot modes), `< thresholdMs` refuses even with an older local tracker run, absent → today's tracker behaviour byte-for-byte.
  - Fail-closed preserved: `slots-unavailable` / `capacity-saturated` are evaluated BEFORE the idle age, and `requiredFreeSlots` capacity is unchanged (per-slot mode still requires the CURRENT free-unowned count).
  - Activity outranks the age: `pollShowsLocalActivity()` (busy/owned slot, coarse pre-v2 lease, live contention) disables the idle-age shortcut and falls back to the tracker; an idle-age poll with a live contention waiter resets the idle run immediately.
  - Decision log: `localIdleSeconds` / `localLastActivitySource` on every polled decision entry, plus non-blocking `idle-age-pending` (deferred) and `idle-age-qualified` (admitted) observations. `contentionQueueDepth` is now computed once per tick.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — additive optional log-entry fields.
- Tests: `downtime-worker.idle.test.ts` (+10 tests: AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC6/AC7 incl. global + per-slot first-poll dispatch, short-age deferral, contention/busy-slot/lease activity, absent-field regression, `slots: []`/`slots_stale` fail-closed, decision-log fields) and `downtime-worker.parse.test.ts` (+5 tests: new fields, absent fields, malformed/non-finite/negative degradation, `reportedIdleSeconds`).
- Docs: `packages/herdr/README.md` (new *Proxy-authoritative idle age* section + `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` note), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (new *Idle-age authority* section with the comparison table, fail-closed limits and observability).

## Verification

- `npm run build` (herdr package + root) clean.
- `packages/herdr/src` group: 107 files / 3553 tests pass, including the 15 new tests.
- Full project suite (`npm --silent test -- tests/cli && npm --silent test -- tests/unit`) PASS at the pushed commit `e740d6d4`; recorded in the per-repo test cache (`scope: full`, `success: true`). Note: the first full run in the worktree failed only because `dist/cli.js` was absent (spawn-based CLI tests) — resolved by running the root build in the worktree, no code change needed.

## Assumptions / notes

- Followed the brief: a proxy restart resets `local_idle_seconds` to a small value; the worker then waits one threshold via the local tracker (documented trade-off).
- AC8 mentioned adding idle-signal fixtures to `downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`; a local `idleAgeStatus()` helper in the idle test file was used instead (single consumer, respects the 5-mock-per-test budget) — existing shared fixtures (`makeDeps`, `jsonResponseFixture`) are reused.
- No new settings; `downtimeIdleThresholdMs` remains the user-facing threshold.

data.comment: Implementation decisions: (1) Parser: local_prefills_in_flight / local_max_concurrent_prefills / prefill_gate_waiters are availability-affecting and fail closed on malformed values (poll rejected) like contention_queue_depth; queue_eta_seconds is advisory (malformed degrades to undefined) and prefill_budget_seconds stays advisory, so a missing ETA or budget never blocks. Deferral precedence: gate waiters -> prefill-gate, cap reached -> prefill-cap, then queue_eta_seconds or max per-slot prefill_eta_seconds above prefill_budget_seconds -> prefill-eta (both values must be finite). (3) Tick: gate waiters feed the idle-age activity check and idle-run reset (contention evidence equivalence); the pacing gate sits after slot-owned/contention and before any dispatch, so it can only reduce concurrency; effectiveFreeSlots = min(freeSlots, capacityBudget) is passed to both dispatchFromCoordination and dispatchDowntimeWork (interacts with downtimeRequiredFreeSlots and the per-tier audit >= 2 minimum). (4) Decision header tokens prefill-gate / prefill-cap / prefill-eta are distinct from contention/slot-owner/no-slots; every decision records prefillsInFlight, maxConcurrentPrefills, prefillGateWaiters, prefillBudgetSeconds, queueEtaSeconds and slotPrefillEtaSeconds. (5) No new configuration knob; absent prefill fields restore today's free-slot-only budget byte-for-byte. data.author: pi
data.comment:
**Requirement from llm-proxy-side measurement (2026-10-21): assert "one item per idle window" explicitly.** Session ID: herdr-1792596968-827039-17087

Measured over the llm-proxy log window 2026-10-21 14:56→17:00 (372 contention-queue events, 302 queue waits, 261 fallback-after-queue of which 215 burned the full 120 s budget):

1. **The idle-window race is real but small.** Only 6 of 371 queue events (2%) occurred on a session's *first* request — i.e. a fresh dispatcher launch. The other 365 (98%) are mid-session turns from 29 already-running sessions (median 30 requests/session). So this item is necessary but fixes ~2% of observed queue load; the proxy-side reservation item (llm-manager `LP-0MVICF0FX00CT0ZC`) covers the rest.

2. **Why the current gate leaks despite being correct-looking.** The dispatcher polls every 10 s. Two herdr instances can observe the same idle window within one tick; the proxy has 2 slots so it admits both, the second hits the serialised prefill gate (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`), queues and then falls back remote. In-window evidence: 247 of 325 full-budget losses entered the queue with `saturation=prefill` while `available_slots` was still 2 — i.e. the proxy reported a free slot while the gate was saturated. Gating on `local_prefills_in_flight` (AC2 of this item) is the correct fix for that signal inconsistency.

3. **Requested AC addition (suggested wording):** "At most one new herdr pane is launched per observed idle window: after a dispatch the dispatcher must not launch another pane until the proxy reports `local_prefills_in_flight < local_max_concurrent_prefills` AND a fresh status tick has been observed post-dispatch (no two launches from a single poll result). Tests cover the two-instances-same-tick race, asserting the second instance defers with reason `prefill-gate`."

data.author: implement
data.comment:
## Payload contract (stable — WL-C4 parses this verbatim)

`wl worklist --json` emits:

```jsonc
{
  "success": true,
  "worklogDir": "/abs/path/.worklog",
  "requestedCount": 20,
  "subsets": {
    "critical":        [],  // WorkItem[]: priority critical, status open|in-progress|blocked|completed, ALL parent levels
    "reviewQueue":     [],  // WorkItem[]: status completed|in-progress, stage in_review, root-only
    "inProgressRoots": [],  // WorkItem[]: status in-progress, root-only
    "blockedRoots":    [],  // WorkItem[]: status blocked, root-only
    "browse":          []   // { workItem, reason, group?, groupLabel? }[] — identical to `wl next -n <count> --include-in-progress --include-blocked --no-re-sort --json` .results/.workItems
  }
}
```

- Every subset key is **always present** (empty array, never omitted).
- `workItem` entries carry the same enrichment `wl next`/enrichment path adds: `auditResult`, `auditedAt`, `childCount` (browse items also carry `group`/`groupLabel` when the count is > 1).
- `-n/--number` bounds **only** `browse` (default 20); the four mandatory subsets are unbounded by it.
- Pure read: no `reSort`, never bumps the read-cache state counter (verified by tests).
- Ordering: the four list subsets use the shared hierarchy sortIndex ordering (`createHierarchyOrderComparator`); the review queue therefore uses hierarchy order rather than `wl list --stage in_review`'s 6-bucket order, which needs per-item current content fingerprints (git) that a cacheable pure read must not pay. Browse order is identical to `wl next`.
- `--worklog-dir` is honoured; `worklogDir` in the payload is the resolved worklog dir.

Commit `c8d8197f` on `dev` (branch `wl-WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF-wl-worklist-consolidated-json-read-comma`).

## Measured evidence (same host + build: node v22.22.1, rgardler-AI-Laptop)

### bench/herdr-refresh-cycle.ts (4 panes, 30 s cycle, 5 s tick, 20 seeded items)

| Query set | Spawns / refresh | Spawns / cycle | CPU-s / cycle | p95 spawn wall | p50 | peak RSS |

- Spawn count per refresh: **5 → 1** (80 % fewer), 120 → 24 per cycle — all measured spawns were `cache-hit` (one write-free read populates the shared cache entry every pane reuses).
- CPU per cycle: **0.157×** the same-host legacy cost, **0.075×** the pre-F4 baseline — well below the ≤ 0.4× / ≤ 63.78 CPU-s target.
- p95 per-spawn wall time roughly halved (1227 → 568 ms).

### bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts --json (1000 items, 20 expanded parents, 30 browse)

| Query set | Spawns / refresh | Cold | Warm | within 2 s target |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `legacy` | 5 | 1187.5 ms | 628.8 ms | yes |
| `consolidated` | **1** | **892.9 ms** | **444.9 ms** | yes |

### Reproduce

```sh
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh:json -- --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5 --query-set consolidated
npm run benchmark:herdr-refresh:json -- --items 20 --cycle-seconds 30 --tick-seconds 5 --query-set legacy
npx tsx bench/herdr-refresh-perf.ts --json --query-set consolidated
```

Shortfall: none — the ≤ 0.4× target is met with margin. Residual note: the review-queue subset uses hierarchy ordering rather than `wl list --stage in_review`'s 6-bucket order (that sort needs per-item git fingerprints; the bundle computes `currentFingerprint` only for audited items, so the banner state and membership are identical while the within-subset order can differ).

The parent description already carried a complete brief, constraints, key

design questions this planning session had to resolve and the evidence used.
No interactive producer was available for this downtime-dispatched run, so

OPEN QUESTION.

- **Q1 — Where does "the herdr agent runner" inject `X-Local-Preference` and
  read `X-Local-Route`/`X-Local-Fallback-Reason`?**
  Answer (agent inference): herdr has no HTTP request path for agent turns —
  panes are pi sessions launched by `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` /
  `run-pi-agent.sh`, and pi (provider config in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`,
  provider `Local Proxy`) owns the requests. The established mechanism is a
  pi provider extension: `~/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-sse-signals` already
  overrides the Local Proxy provider's `streamSimple` with a capturing
  `fetch`; this repo ships extensions from `packages/tui/extensions/`
  (`scripts/install-pi-extension.sh`). So: new `local-preference` extension +
  per-spawn env from the runner. Evidence: `proxy-sse-signals/index.ts`,
  `scripts/install-pi-extension.sh`, `packages/shared/src/lease-release.ts`.
- **Q2 — What is the authoritative reservation contract (fields, ticket TTL,
  429 body)?**
  Answer: the parent description's prose contract (`POST
  /llama/local/reserve`, ticket or `429 {reason, retry_after_s}`,
  `X-Local-Reservation`) is the current source of truth. The proxy work item
  llm-manager `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` is **not yet implemented or present in
  llm-manager's worklog** (checked `~/projects/llm-manager` `dev`: no
  `llama/local/reserve` handler; `wl show` returns "not found"), so exact
  field names/TTL cannot be pinned yet. Mitigation recorded in C1: tolerant
  parsing behind one typed accessor; C2 fails open when the endpoint is
  absent. **OPEN QUESTION (proxy side):** confirm field names + ticket TTL
  when `LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL` lands.
- **Q3 — Is the proxy's atomic grant alone enough for the
  one-per-idle-window rule, or does herdr need its own cross-instance lock?**
  Answer (agent inference from the parent AC3 wording + the coordination
  design): the proxy is the arbiter and herdr must not add a second
  distributed lock or lease file (constraint: pacing never raises the budget,
  no second source of truth). The client adds only post-launch suppression on
  its own tick plus a fresh-ticket requirement (C3-AC2), so it is safe even
  if the proxy granted more than one ticket.
- **Q4 — Where should per-turn route evidence be recorded?**
  Answer (agent inference): a bounded JSONL route log next to the existing
  downtime logs (`<cwd>/.worklog/local-route.log`, rolling convention of
  `downtime-dispatches.log`) — per-root, machine-local, gitignored.
  **OPEN QUESTION (producer, low impact):** prefer `~/.pi/agent/logs/`
  instead? C4 implements the proposed location and documents it.
- **Q5 — What is the default per-turn preference for downtime panes?**
  Answer (agent inference from the parent's "work the operator marks
  local-first"): `local-only` for downtime panes, `remote-ok` for
  background/scheduled work, exposed as a knob. **OPEN QUESTION (producer):**
  confirm the default (fail-fast to remote vs wait for local); the knob makes
  either behaviour configurable.
